What few people understand, including many conservatives, is that media lawfare is something very different from the usual anti-conservative bias, dishonest reporting, or partisan cheerleading. In many instances, the media are an integral part of the lawfare machinery itself. They are active participants in the operation.

We saw this during Russiagate. The media did not simply root for one side, which they do all the time anyway. They actively worked for and with that side, knowingly carrying out specific tasks and essential functions as active participants in the lawfare operation.

Since then, the machinery has only become more sophisticated. The example described below is another iteration of the same system.

Counterlawfare published a foundational article on media lawfare as part of our ongoing effort to untangle this machinery and show exactly how it works.

quoted_text:
卧靠，拿1500万现金开全季酒店，一年赚400万却被说不值得投资？

老板砸1500万在合肥火车站旁的全季酒店开了83间房，去年1月开业第一年就赚400万，结果博主算完账直接说“不值得投”，理由太扎心了！

原来这酒店看似风光，实则被层层抽成扒层皮：华住集团抽走5%基础管理费，美团携程等OTA平台再抽10%，内外订单加权算下来综合抽点高达13.4%！67万的月营业额，到老板手里只剩58万，一年下来看似700万营收，实则被平台和品牌抽走近百万。

更狠的是，这还是合肥最赚钱的全季，周内入住率95%、周末65%，房价300+，位置就在火车站旁，差旅客源不愁。可算完账才发现，房租120万/年、员工成本96万/年、水电气54万/年、客房运营成本72万/年，再加上税费、宽带、维修等杂费，第二年净利润才318万。

博主用IRR公式一算，真实年化收益率才9.21%，还不如存银行定期！要知道现在美国5年期定期存款都能到4%以上，马斯克的X Money甚至能到6%，这酒店投资回报率连无风险理财都跑不赢。

而且这还是在10公里内没有竞品的情况下，要是周边再开几家连锁酒店，入住率和房价一降，回本周期直接拉长到5年以上。

难怪博主说现在酒店行业已经是中高风险投资，看似赚得多，实则被平台和品牌“吸血”，最后投资人拿到手的利润少得可怜。

其实说白了，现在做实体生意，最大的痛点就是被流量平台和品牌方层层抽成，看似流水高，实则净利润被压得极低。就像这个酒店，老板累死累活，一年赚的钱还不如把钱存银行躺平。

讲真，在国内做实体，真是一年不如一年🤣

(视频资料来源：抖音 小闵做餐饮)

text:
I’ve recently seen quite a few people betting on $IMD, and I think the reason isn’t simply the “AI + Crypto” narrative.

0xd34a99bc0f67ae1bbd63c660e6d0b0dd03e263b7 

What really gives IMD a higher ceiling is that it is trying to occupy a much bigger position:

AI agents are beginning to directly participate in the production of Crypto financial products, and IMD wants to become the underlying protocol that supports these new applications.

IMD also doesn’t position itself as simply an Agent project. It describes itself as a protocol capable of creating “net new 0 to 1 financial applications,” as well as a distributed software factory powered by agents.

That distinction is important.

In the past, Crypto financial products were basically designed by humans, coded by humans, and deployed through smart contracts.

What IMD wants to do is:Agent network continuously runs → produces code, research, oracles, DeFi applications, etc. → verification → deployment → new onchain financial applications.

If this model actually works, then IMD ultimately isn’t competing with any single DeFi product.

It is competing over:Who can create the next generation of onchain financial applications faster and at a lower cost.

And what the market is really betting on isn’t:Will IMD become a bigger AI project?

It is:If agents can continuously produce new financial products, can IMD become the infrastructure for this new production system?

This also connects to another interesting variable — Hooks.

IMD is currently bringing RWA, Hooks, Uniswap v4, stablecoins, games, and other directions into the same design space.

That means it isn’t trying to build a protocol with one fixed function. It wants to become an experimental environment where new financial mechanisms can continuously be created.

In theory, one agent could design a new trading mechanism, another agent could write the Hook, another could handle the Oracle or verification, and eventually the whole thing could be deployed as a functioning financial application.

If this loop actually works, IMD’s value would no longer simply be about “how many agents it has today.”

It would be about:How many new onchain primitives this network can produce in the future.

This is also why I think you can’t look at the IMD token alone right now.

In the screenshot, Adam mentioned that some people in the community have already deployed tokens outside the protocol for things they are working on, while the mainnet is also preparing to expand to Robinhood Chain, Base, and Ethereum Mainnet.

More importantly, the Explorer already shows different agents working on smart contract development, DeFi, oracles, research, and other tasks.

At the very least, this shows that the community isn’t simply building around the token as a Meme. They are trying to turn IMD itself into a development environment.

What is really worth watching is whether it can eventually form:Agent → Build → Verify → Deploy → Financial App → New Demand → More Agents

If this production network begins generating genuinely useful financial applications, IMD’s valuation logic will change.

Because at that point, it would no longer just have an AI narrative. It could become a potential AI-native Crypto application layer.

Of course, it is still a long way from that outcome.

A mechanism existing does not mean the flywheel has already succeeded.

Ultimately, we still need to verify the actual economic activity of the agents, protocol revenue, real users, and whether these activities can create sustainable financial demand.

So now I understand why some people are giving IMD such a high expectation:

They aren’t betting on whether “AI agents will become popular.” They’re betting on a new way of producing Crypto software.

Previously:

Human → Code → Financial Application

What IMD wants to build:

AI Agent → Code → Financial Primitive → Onchain Application

If this direction works, IMD’s ceiling could indeed be much higher than that of a simple AI Agent project.

But if it ultimately ends up being nothing more than a large number of agents completing tasks, building demos, and launching tokens on the Explorer without creating genuinely used financial applications, then the high valuation today would still be primarily based on future expectations.

So the most important thing to watch with IMD isn’t how many agents it has today, but whether those agents can actually build new financial products that would have been very difficult for human teams to create quickly in the past.

I think the core reason behind $IMD rise this time is not simply the AI Narrative, but that after POOL4 officially went live, the Token and the product’s economic mechanism finally became genuinely connected.

0xd34a99bc0f67ae1bbd63c660e6d0b0dd03e263b7

Previously, the market’s main bets on IMD were Identity.md, AI Agents, Autonomous Work, and the Uniswap v4 Hook. Now there is an additional and much clearer economic loop:

IMD Trading → POOL4 → Trim → 85% Burn + Staking / Bonding / NFT Node → Buy Wall

After POOL4 went live, Staking also launched. Around 560K IMD was staked within a short period of time, while Burn and reward distribution also began. This is the most direct catalyst for the sudden rise this time. The market has started to reprice IMD, rather than simply speculating on the AI concept.

More importantly, IMD’s fundamentals have genuinely changed.

Before:AI Agent → Narrative → Attention → IMD

Now:AI Agent → Autonomous Work → IMD → POOL4 → Trading → Burn / Staking → Bonding → Compute → Agent Economy

Bonding is one of the most important upcoming milestones. The official design is that Bonding will open when IMD reaches $4, and the Bonding Reserve can eventually be converted into ETH to pay for AI Inference. In other words, this could eventually form:

IMD → Bonding → ETH → AI Compute → Agent Work → Economic Activity → IMD

So what the market is really betting on now is not simply that “IMD is an AI Token,” but whether IMD can become the core asset of the AI Agent Economy + POOL4 economic mechanism.

POOL4 is also an important potential valuation expansion point. IMD is the first Token to use the POOL4 Hook. If other projects begin using POOL4 in the future and generate real trading volume, IMD’s positioning could evolve from an AI Agent Token into the representative native asset of POOL4.

The key upside catalysts to watch next are:

1. Bonding officially goes live
The Reserve becomes actual AI Compute demand, further strengthening Token Utility.

2. Agent numbers and real Work continue to grow
What matters is not simply the number of Agents, but whether Jobs, Accepted Work, and Compute continue increasing.

3. NFT Nodes go live
Part of the current Trim goes into the NFT Node Reserve. If the Node Economy officially launches, it will further expand IMD’s use cases.

4. A second successful POOL4 project emerges
If other Tokens use POOL4 and generate significant trading volume, the market may start assigning IMD an “Infrastructure / First Asset Premium.”

5. Volume → Burn continues to expand
If trading volume continues to grow while Burn, Staking, and Buy Walls also increase, the Token’s economic loop will truly begin to be validated.

At the moment, I believe IMD’s fundamentals have strengthened rather than weakened. But it is currently at:

Narrative Validated → Product Live → Economic Mechanism Live → Waiting for Scale Validation

The biggest issue is also very clear:Mechanism going live ≠ Mechanism succeeding.

If we see:Volume ↑ → Burn ↑ → Agent Work ↑ → Bonding ↑ → Compute ↑

then this rise can gradually transition from “expectation-driven trading” into “fundamental expansion.”

On the other hand, if the price continues rising while Volume, Burn, Agent Work, and Bonding do not grow alongside it, then this move will increasingly depend on Narrative and expectations, and the risk will also increase significantly.

So, in summary:The direct catalysts for this rise are the launch of POOL4 + Staking. The real long-term bet is whether IMD can evolve from an AI Agent Token into the core economic asset of the AI Agent Economy + POOL4.

PSA for the >2,635 events across SF/LA tech week.

1. SF clusters is in SOMA, then FiDi, Jackson Square, Mission Bay, and the Mission.

2. Pick two-three anchor events, not 14 Luma/Partiful RSVPs. Official bookends are Fireworks x a16z (10/5) & a16z x Unicorner x Notion afterparty (10/9)

3. Leave each event with at least one meaningful conversations + give first: an intro, product feedback, sharing useful material

4. @meetgranola is fantastic for recording panel insights (not paid sponsorship, just a fan) - but this gives me the ick if i'm being recorded 1:1 offline. Bonus, send the host the most quotable lines from the panels + pictures.

5. Get a digital business card so you’re not fumbling QR codes or first names (@atrium_me, Blinq, Popl, Beacons)

6. Use agents that prep you 3x deeper on the speakers, companies, and topics before each event (@bot , @atrium_me 😉)

7. Debrief agent on the way out, who did you meet, what is one story, personal anecdote, thread you're going to pull, follow-up (@atrium_me asks you automatically 😘)

8. Powerbank >10k mAh is essential

9. Layers. SF can be 4 seasons in a day

10. Don’t wait to do follow-ups next Monday, do them earlier (Sat/Sun) and be specific.

11. If you are raising, sit in operator rooms - not rooms where investors are already being swarmed.

12. For the love of god please stop asking "so what do you do?". There are so many more tasteful other things to start with:

“What are you trying to get out of this week?”

“What were the big lessons this quarter?”

“Have you had a conversation yet that wasn’t a pitch in disguise?”

Bonus bc I support you - here's 888 invite codes to @atrium_me so you're best equipped to build relationships during tech week

quoted_text:
From the AI Agent narrative to an ecosystem with real revenue feedback. I think this is the most fitting way to describe $Agency

7VertkgF9KLhxxJXHX6uaWuoYZTP9LdGj2bWmVXVpump 

Agency has now reached a peak market cap of $24M. If we look at price alone, this is a typical AI Agent narrative-driven rally. But I think what is really worth examining is that the market is starting to reprice AgencyPad’s economic model, rather than simply chasing the AI Agent concept.

When I first researched Agency, my biggest question was: AgencyPad allows AI agents to conduct research, execute strategies, and manage funds autonomously, but what value do these activities ultimately bring to the platform token?

At the time, the platform already had a product and some activity, but its token value capture mechanism was unclear. Now, that has fundamentally changed.

I believe this rally has been driven by five main factors.

1. The tokenomics change is the most direct fundamental catalyst

This is what I consider the most important development.

Following AgencyPad’s economic model upgrade, 15% of the fees generated by eligible agents are used to periodically buy back and burn Agency. In other words, ecosystem activity no longer just generates platform revenue and resources for agents to operate. It now also creates direct buying pressure for the platform token.

This has changed market expectations.

Previously, growth in AgencyPad activity did not necessarily mean Agency would benefit. Now, as fee generation increases, the buyback amount could theoretically grow alongside it.

However, I don't think the market is pricing in the actual amount already burned.

What is really driving expectations is how many agents can consistently generate fees in the future, and whether this mechanism can create stronger buying pressure as the ecosystem expands.

There is a fundamental difference between the two: one is economic activity that has already happened, while the other is the market pricing in potential future growth.

2. AgencyPad is starting to produce genuinely revenue-generating runners

Even the best tokenomics mean little without real activity behind them.

This is another key development in the recent rally.

Agents on AgencyPad are starting to generate meaningful fees. In my earlier research, runners such as CLAUDIA, Aiden, and shoggoth had already demonstrated some revenue-generating ability. Individual agents generating tens of thousands of dollars in fees within a short period have shown the market that AgencyPad is not simply a platform for creating AI Memes with little ongoing activity.

The trading logic is straightforward: if the platform can consistently produce agents with trading volume, fee generation, and sustained activity, ecosystem revenue could evolve from occasional spikes into a more stable source of income.

More importantly, the market is no longer just betting on the success of one agent. It is betting on whether AgencyPad can repeatedly produce successful ones.

One runner performing well may just be a temporary trend. But if the platform can produce several revenue-generating runners at the same time, the market may begin to value the entire ecosystem differently.

However, fees are not the same as profit, nor are they equivalent to direct cash flow for the platform token. We still need to monitor whether these runners can sustain their revenue and whether their activity is driven by short-term trading hype.

3. WWW opened the door to attention, and Agency captured part of the capital rotation

Another important external factor behind this rally is WWW.

WWW attracted significant attention during the earlier AI Agent narrative, helping shift the market's focus from traditional Memes toward the AgencyPad ecosystem and related projects.

But once a narrative becomes widely discussed, capital naturally starts looking for other opportunities within the same space.

Agency was in a good position to benefit.

On one hand, it belongs to the same ecosystem and could capture some of the attention that had already formed. On the other hand, its own economic model was evolving, giving the market a new reason to pay attention.

This means Agency is not simply a token following a trend. It has the potential to become another independent trading opportunity within the ecosystem.

I don't think capital from WWW automatically flows into Agency. A more accurate way to look at it is that WWW helped open the door to attention for the broader narrative, while Agency attracted more interest through its own tokenomics upgrade and ecosystem activity.

This rally is the result of narrative expansion and capital rotation working together.

4. Actual buying from the market moved the rally beyond discussion and toward capital validation

Social media discussions can generate attention, but real buying activity can further shape market expectations. It shows that some market participants are no longer just discussing the project. They are willing to take on actual price risk.

This creates two effects.

First, it generates real spot demand and pushes the price higher.

Second, it creates a degree of social proof. When the market sees experienced traders building positions, more people start researching the same token, further expanding its visibility.

5. The team keeps shipping, preventing the narrative from losing momentum too quickly

AgencyPad's product narrative has moved beyond its original AI agent creation functionality.

From browser capabilities and research tools to Treasury actions, AI Influencers, and the buyback-and-burn mechanism, the team continues to expand what agents can do.

Not every update directly creates demand for the token, but continuous development gives the market new things to discuss and gradually reinforces the perception that AgencyPad is building a real product.

For a token that depends heavily on attention and expectations, continuous delivery helps extend the narrative cycle.

However, adding features is not the same as creating product value. Actual usage, user retention, and fee generation still need to validate the impact of these updates.

I believe the market is currently betting on two mutually reinforcing flywheels.

The first is the economic flywheel: more agent activity generates more fees; part of those fees is used to buy back and burn Agency; if the ecosystem continues to expand, the scale of buybacks could grow as well.

The second is the attention flywheel: projects such as WWW bring attention to the broader narrative, while Agency attracts capital through its own tokenomics improvements and runner performance. More capital and discussion then encourage the market to look for new opportunities within the AgencyPad ecosystem.

At the moment, the second flywheel is clearly moving faster.

The market has already started pricing in the potential scale of the ecosystem, but whether the economic flywheel can expand sustainably still needs to be proven over time.

This is what I see as the core tension surrounding Agency right now: expectations are growing faster than the economic value that has actually been realized.

As for the fundamentals, my assessment is that they have strengthened, particularly in two areas: token value capture and ecosystem activity.

Initially, AgencyPad had product capabilities but lacked a sufficiently clear mechanism for capturing value for its token. Now, the platform has established a buyback-and-burn mechanism and has runners that are actually generating fees.

This is not just narrative packaging. It represents real progress in both the economic model and ecosystem activity.

However, I would not say that the $24M valuation is fully supported by fundamentals yet.

There are still three key questions:

Can runners sustain their fee revenue rather than relying on short-term trading activity?
Can buyback-and-burn volume grow significantly alongside the ecosystem?
Can the platform consistently create new agents rather than relying on a handful of top-performing runners?

If these questions are gradually answered, the fundamentals will have a better chance of catching up with the current valuation.

What could drive the next leg higher?

The next things I plan to watch are developments and data that can materially change market expectations. I believe the next major catalysts could emerge from these areas.

First, more high-revenue runners emerge.

If AgencyPad can consistently produce multiple agents with sustainable fee revenue, the market may shift from trading individual runners to valuing the growth potential of the entire platform.

This would be the most important signal of ecosystem expansion.

Second, fees and buyback volume continue to grow.

The buyback-and-burn mechanism is already in place. The next key question is scale.

I will continue tracking actual buyback amounts, the number of tokens burned, and whether buyback frequency increases alongside ecosystem activity.

If fee growth turns out to be temporary, the mechanism will provide limited valuation support. On the other hand, if buyback volume continues to expand, the market may raise its long-term expectations for AGENCY.

Third, AgencyPad becomes a sustained narrative within the AI Agent ecosystem.

WWW has already demonstrated that the market has an appetite for this sector. If AgencyPad continues to launch agents that attract attention or introduces new ecosystem mechanics, attention could flow back into the platform.

However, these catalysts are highly uncertain. Ecosystem hype should not be equated with token value.

Fourth, the team continues delivering products that genuinely increase usage.

I care more about updates that drive real usage and revenue than simply adding more features.

If new capabilities help agents operate more consistently, improve task execution, or create new sources of fee revenue, they could become meaningful fundamental catalysts for the next leg higher.

Risks: The market may already be pricing in too much of the future

The biggest risk for Agency is not that it lacks fundamentals entirely, but that its current valuation may already reflect highly optimistic growth expectations.

1. A mismatch between valuation and fundamental progress

After climbing from a much lower market cap to $24M, the market has already reacted significantly to the tokenomics upgrade and ecosystem expansion narrative.

If runner numbers, fees, and buyback volume fail to keep growing, the market may reassess those expectations.

2. Runner revenue may not be sustainable

Agent fees are still largely tied to trading activity.

If the revenue of a few runners comes from short-lived trends, or if the platform cannot consistently reproduce successful cases, the ecosystem revenue we see today could be highly volatile.

3. Attention rotation can reverse quickly

The AI Agent narrative still depends heavily on market sentiment.

When new trends emerge, capital may leave the AgencyPad ecosystem. Even if the product continues operating, the token may not be able to maintain its previous valuation.

4. A working mechanism does not automatically establish long-term value

Buybacks and burns can create buying pressure and reduce token supply, but they do not automatically generate sustainable business growth.

Ultimately, AgencyPad still needs to establish consistent activity, revenue, and user demand.

From here, I see two possible scenarios for the next phase of the market.

If runner numbers continue increasing, fees remain strong, buyback-and-burn volume expands, and market attention does not fade significantly, the rally could still be in the expectation-building phase of ecosystem expansion, leaving room for further valuation re-rating.

But if the price keeps rising while fees and buyback data stagnate, and the rally becomes increasingly dependent on KOL discussions and capital rotation, then it would look more like sentiment-driven valuation expansion. Once attention cools, the risk of a sharp pullback would increase.

For that reason, I would rather wait for further fundamental validation than simply chase a market cap breakout.

The three things I will focus on next are:

Whether AgencyPad continues producing new high-revenue runners.

Whether actual Agency buyback-and-burn volume grows alongside ecosystem activity.

Whether capital and attention remain concentrated in AgencyPad instead of quickly rotating into the next AI Agent trend.

The core change in Agency is that it is evolving from an AI Agent token with a product concept into a project with an initial economic feedback mechanism and real ecosystem activity.

That makes it much more interesting than when I first researched it.

But from a trading perspective, what will truly determine its next phase is not the tokenomics upgrade that has already happened, but whether the growth the market is expecting can continue to materialize.

What I am trading from here is whether AgencyPad can turn this mechanism into a continuously operating ecosystem.

Agency has now reached a peak market cap of $24M. If we look at price alone, this is a typical AI Agent narrative-driven rally. But I think what is really worth examining is that the market is starting to reprice AgencyPad’s economic model, rather than simply chasing the AI Agent concept.

When I first researched Agency, my biggest question was: AgencyPad allows AI agents to conduct research, execute strategies, and manage funds autonomously, but what value do these activities ultimately bring to the platform token?

At the time, the platform already had a product and some activity, but its token value capture mechanism was unclear. Now, that has fundamentally changed.

I believe this rally has been driven by five main factors.

1. The tokenomics change is the most direct fundamental catalyst

This is what I consider the most important development.

Following AgencyPad’s economic model upgrade, 15% of the fees generated by eligible agents are used to periodically buy back and burn Agency. In other words, ecosystem activity no longer just generates platform revenue and resources for agents to operate. It now also creates direct buying pressure for the platform token.

This has changed market expectations.

Previously, growth in AgencyPad activity did not necessarily mean Agency would benefit. Now, as fee generation increases, the buyback amount could theoretically grow alongside it.

However, I don't think the market is pricing in the actual amount already burned.

What is really driving expectations is how many agents can consistently generate fees in the future, and whether this mechanism can create stronger buying pressure as the ecosystem expands.

There is a fundamental difference between the two: one is economic activity that has already happened, while the other is the market pricing in potential future growth.

2. AgencyPad is starting to produce genuinely revenue-generating runners

Even the best tokenomics mean little without real activity behind them.

This is another key development in the recent rally.

Agents on AgencyPad are starting to generate meaningful fees. In my earlier research, runners such as CLAUDIA, Aiden, and shoggoth had already demonstrated some revenue-generating ability. Individual agents generating tens of thousands of dollars in fees within a short period have shown the market that AgencyPad is not simply a platform for creating AI Memes with little ongoing activity.

The trading logic is straightforward: if the platform can consistently produce agents with trading volume, fee generation, and sustained activity, ecosystem revenue could evolve from occasional spikes into a more stable source of income.

More importantly, the market is no longer just betting on the success of one agent. It is betting on whether AgencyPad can repeatedly produce successful ones.

One runner performing well may just be a temporary trend. But if the platform can produce several revenue-generating runners at the same time, the market may begin to value the entire ecosystem differently.

However, fees are not the same as profit, nor are they equivalent to direct cash flow for the platform token. We still need to monitor whether these runners can sustain their revenue and whether their activity is driven by short-term trading hype.

3. WWW opened the door to attention, and Agency captured part of the capital rotation

Another important external factor behind this rally is WWW.

WWW attracted significant attention during the earlier AI Agent narrative, helping shift the market's focus from traditional Memes toward the AgencyPad ecosystem and related projects.

But once a narrative becomes widely discussed, capital naturally starts looking for other opportunities within the same space.

Agency was in a good position to benefit.

On one hand, it belongs to the same ecosystem and could capture some of the attention that had already formed. On the other hand, its own economic model was evolving, giving the market a new reason to pay attention.

This means Agency is not simply a token following a trend. It has the potential to become another independent trading opportunity within the ecosystem.

I don't think capital from WWW automatically flows into Agency. A more accurate way to look at it is that WWW helped open the door to attention for the broader narrative, while Agency attracted more interest through its own tokenomics upgrade and ecosystem activity.

This rally is the result of narrative expansion and capital rotation working together.

4. Actual buying from the market moved the rally beyond discussion and toward capital validation

Social media discussions can generate attention, but real buying activity can further shape market expectations. It shows that some market participants are no longer just discussing the project. They are willing to take on actual price risk.

This creates two effects.

First, it generates real spot demand and pushes the price higher.

Second, it creates a degree of social proof. When the market sees experienced traders building positions, more people start researching the same token, further expanding its visibility.

5. The team keeps shipping, preventing the narrative from losing momentum too quickly

AgencyPad's product narrative has moved beyond its original AI agent creation functionality.

From browser capabilities and research tools to Treasury actions, AI Influencers, and the buyback-and-burn mechanism, the team continues to expand what agents can do.

Not every update directly creates demand for the token, but continuous development gives the market new things to discuss and gradually reinforces the perception that AgencyPad is building a real product.

For a token that depends heavily on attention and expectations, continuous delivery helps extend the narrative cycle.

However, adding features is not the same as creating product value. Actual usage, user retention, and fee generation still need to validate the impact of these updates.

I believe the market is currently betting on two mutually reinforcing flywheels.

The first is the economic flywheel: more agent activity generates more fees; part of those fees is used to buy back and burn Agency; if the ecosystem continues to expand, the scale of buybacks could grow as well.

The second is the attention flywheel: projects such as WWW bring attention to the broader narrative, while Agency attracts capital through its own tokenomics improvements and runner performance. More capital and discussion then encourage the market to look for new opportunities within the AgencyPad ecosystem.

At the moment, the second flywheel is clearly moving faster.

The market has already started pricing in the potential scale of the ecosystem, but whether the economic flywheel can expand sustainably still needs to be proven over time.

This is what I see as the core tension surrounding Agency right now: expectations are growing faster than the economic value that has actually been realized.

As for the fundamentals, my assessment is that they have strengthened, particularly in two areas: token value capture and ecosystem activity.

Initially, AgencyPad had product capabilities but lacked a sufficiently clear mechanism for capturing value for its token. Now, the platform has established a buyback-and-burn mechanism and has runners that are actually generating fees.

This is not just narrative packaging. It represents real progress in both the economic model and ecosystem activity.

However, I would not say that the $24M valuation is fully supported by fundamentals yet.

There are still three key questions:

Can runners sustain their fee revenue rather than relying on short-term trading activity?
Can buyback-and-burn volume grow significantly alongside the ecosystem?
Can the platform consistently create new agents rather than relying on a handful of top-performing runners?

If these questions are gradually answered, the fundamentals will have a better chance of catching up with the current valuation.

What could drive the next leg higher?

The next things I plan to watch are developments and data that can materially change market expectations. I believe the next major catalysts could emerge from these areas.

First, more high-revenue runners emerge.

If AgencyPad can consistently produce multiple agents with sustainable fee revenue, the market may shift from trading individual runners to valuing the growth potential of the entire platform.

This would be the most important signal of ecosystem expansion.

Second, fees and buyback volume continue to grow.

The buyback-and-burn mechanism is already in place. The next key question is scale.

I will continue tracking actual buyback amounts, the number of tokens burned, and whether buyback frequency increases alongside ecosystem activity.

If fee growth turns out to be temporary, the mechanism will provide limited valuation support. On the other hand, if buyback volume continues to expand, the market may raise its long-term expectations for AGENCY.

Third, AgencyPad becomes a sustained narrative within the AI Agent ecosystem.

WWW has already demonstrated that the market has an appetite for this sector. If AgencyPad continues to launch agents that attract attention or introduces new ecosystem mechanics, attention could flow back into the platform.

However, these catalysts are highly uncertain. Ecosystem hype should not be equated with token value.

Fourth, the team continues delivering products that genuinely increase usage.

I care more about updates that drive real usage and revenue than simply adding more features.

If new capabilities help agents operate more consistently, improve task execution, or create new sources of fee revenue, they could become meaningful fundamental catalysts for the next leg higher.

Risks: The market may already be pricing in too much of the future

The biggest risk for Agency is not that it lacks fundamentals entirely, but that its current valuation may already reflect highly optimistic growth expectations.

1. A mismatch between valuation and fundamental progress

After climbing from a much lower market cap to $24M, the market has already reacted significantly to the tokenomics upgrade and ecosystem expansion narrative.

If runner numbers, fees, and buyback volume fail to keep growing, the market may reassess those expectations.

2. Runner revenue may not be sustainable

Agent fees are still largely tied to trading activity.

If the revenue of a few runners comes from short-lived trends, or if the platform cannot consistently reproduce successful cases, the ecosystem revenue we see today could be highly volatile.

3. Attention rotation can reverse quickly

The AI Agent narrative still depends heavily on market sentiment.

When new trends emerge, capital may leave the AgencyPad ecosystem. Even if the product continues operating, the token may not be able to maintain its previous valuation.

4. A working mechanism does not automatically establish long-term value

Buybacks and burns can create buying pressure and reduce token supply, but they do not automatically generate sustainable business growth.

Ultimately, AgencyPad still needs to establish consistent activity, revenue, and user demand.

From here, I see two possible scenarios for the next phase of the market.

If runner numbers continue increasing, fees remain strong, buyback-and-burn volume expands, and market attention does not fade significantly, the rally could still be in the expectation-building phase of ecosystem expansion, leaving room for further valuation re-rating.

But if the price keeps rising while fees and buyback data stagnate, and the rally becomes increasingly dependent on KOL discussions and capital rotation, then it would look more like sentiment-driven valuation expansion. Once attention cools, the risk of a sharp pullback would increase.

For that reason, I would rather wait for further fundamental validation than simply chase a market cap breakout.

The three things I will focus on next are:

Whether AgencyPad continues producing new high-revenue runners.

Whether actual Agency buyback-and-burn volume grows alongside ecosystem activity.

Whether capital and attention remain concentrated in AgencyPad instead of quickly rotating into the next AI Agent trend.

The core change in Agency is that it is evolving from an AI Agent token with a product concept into a project with an initial economic feedback mechanism and real ecosystem activity.

That makes it much more interesting than when I first researched it.

But from a trading perspective, what will truly determine its next phase is not the tokenomics upgrade that has already happened, but whether the growth the market is expecting can continue to materialize.

What I am trading from here is whether AgencyPad can turn this mechanism into a continuously operating ecosystem.

The core catalyst behind $Agency sudden surge is the launch of a new fee-based buyback-and-burn mechanism announced by the official team

7VertkgF9KLhxxJXHX6uaWuoYZTP9LdGj2bWmVXVpump 

This change has prompted the market to reassess Agency value-capture potential and has given its existing AI Agent narrative a more clearly defined economic logic.

Our previous analysis concluded that the market had primarily been betting on whether the autonomous financial agent model could work and whether it could generate sustained trading activity and capital flows.

However, the latest announcement adds a new layer to that narrative: Agents can not only manage funds and make investments, but also convert a portion of the fees generated by their respective tokens into buying pressure for Agency, with all purchased tokens subsequently burned on-chain.

According to the rules announced by the team, 15% of the fees generated by each token on the platform will be used to buy Agency every hour, and all purchased tokens will be burned on-chain. The remaining fees will be used to keep Agents running and support their investment activities.

This mechanism connects ecosystem activity directly to the platform token. Trading activity across the platform generates fees, part of those fees creates buying pressure for Agency, and the purchased tokens are burned. Previously, the market was focused on whether AGENCY could enable AI to manage funds autonomously, develop strategies, and execute on-chain operations. Now, the market has another metric to watch: whether these autonomous economic activities can consistently generate real demand for AGENCY.

This is also the most direct catalyst behind the latest surge. Compared with simply adding another AI feature, a buyback-and-burn mechanism is easier for traders to understand and gives the token a new reference point for expectations. However, the 15% refers to the proportion of fees allocated, not 15% of the platform’s total trading volume. The actual buyback volume still depends on fee revenue, the number of active projects, and whether the mechanism is consistently executed.

From a product perspective, AGENCY’s core concept has not fundamentally changed. It still revolves around autonomous financial Agents. Each token has its own AI mind and treasury. Agents can observe the market, set missions, and execute investments or buybacks, while remaining subject to code-enforced rules and permission controls. Unlike ordinary AI tools, AGENCY does not simply provide recommendations. Its AI can carry out real on-chain economic activities within predefined limits.

The significance of this update is that it adds a platform-level value-recycling mechanism on top of the existing autonomous execution capabilities. If more Agents remain active and generate real trading activity and fees, the platform could develop a cycle in which ecosystem activity generates fees, those fees support Agent operations and investments, and part of them provides buyback funds for Agency. Whether this cycle can actually take shape will determine whether AGENCY has the potential to evolve from a novel AI product into a platform with sustained economic activity.

The website also presents several ecosystem metrics worth watching. At the time of the screenshot, it showed 61 Minds currently thinking, approximately $110,890 in cumulative fees, 162 live programs, and 814 creations that day. It also displayed 188 coins. These figures indicate that the platform has already reached a certain level of product activity, but they cannot be directly equated with recurring revenue or high-quality user growth.

In particular, the number of creations mainly reflects activity at the platform’s entry point. What really matters is whether these tokens can continue trading after launch, generate fees, and support the long-term operation of their corresponding Agents. If a large number of projects quickly lose trading activity, even high creation numbers will struggle to sustain consistent buyback demand.

The market may therefore be betting on three main developments.

First, improved token value capture. Previously, the relationship between AGENCY’s product capabilities and its native token was relatively indirect. Now, a portion of ecosystem fees is explicitly allocated to buying and burning Agency. The market can directly observe whether this mechanism generates actual buying pressure.

Second, ecosystem scalability. If active Agents, the number of tokens with sustained trading activity, and platform fee revenue all grow together, buybacks and burns could expand alongside the ecosystem. The market is not simply betting on the number of newly created tokens, but on the platform’s ability to turn new projects into sustained activity.

Finally, increased attention toward the autonomous financial Agent sector. AGENCY combines AI decision-making with real capital operations. Different Agents can act according to their own objectives and rules, and those actions themselves could become material for social distribution. If representative investment or treasury-management cases emerge, the platform may attract attention beyond the broader AI narrative.

However, sector-wide enthusiasm does not automatically translate into a competitive advantage for the platform. Autonomous financial Agents have considerable potential, but whether AGENCY can consistently attract creators, retain users, and build a product experience that is difficult to replicate still needs to be demonstrated through real data.

From a fundamental perspective, this update strengthens AGENCY’s mechanism design and token value-capture logic, but it is too early to conclude that the platform’s profitability has improved at the same time.

On the one hand, fee-based buybacks and burns introduce a clearer source of demand for the token. On the other hand, it remains uncertain whether the platform has enough sustained trading activity to support meaningful buybacks. Fee revenue is also not the same as net profit. Agent operating costs, capital allocation, and fee distribution all affect the platform’s actual economic performance.

Furthermore, buybacks and burns can only change the supply side. They cannot independently create long-term demand. Even if tokens continue to be burned, the price impact may remain limited if buybacks are small relative to the circulating market cap or if selling pressure outweighs the buying activity.

The latest surge may also contain a significant short-term speculative component. The expectations created by the new mechanism could attract capital that was already interested in the AI Agent narrative, as well as short-term traders looking for buyback-and-burn catalysts. These two groups may have very different holding periods. Therefore, increased trading volume and a rapid price rise do not, by themselves, prove that long-term capital has developed lasting confidence in the project.

Going forward, AGENCY’s development will depend primarily on several key variables.

First, whether buybacks and burns can reach meaningful scale. The team has officially announced the mechanism. The next step is to monitor its actual execution records, including hourly buyback amounts, cumulative purchases, tokens burned, and buyback volume relative to trading volume and market cap. If buybacks continue to grow, the market may have a basis for reassessing Agency based on real capital flows. If the actual amounts remain limited, the expectations created by this upgrade may gradually fade.

Second, whether the platform can turn token creation into sustained revenue. The number of newly created tokens is only the starting point for ecosystem growth. More important are project retention, sustained trading activity, and whether Agents can continue operating with the support of fee revenue. Only if these metrics improve can the platform establish stable economic activity rather than relying on a constant stream of new projects to maintain the appearance of growth.

Third, whether AGENCY can produce autonomous investment cases with strong distribution potential. AGENCY’s differentiation lies in enabling AI to execute real capital operations under predefined rules. If representative treasury-management, investment, or risk-control cases emerge, they could both demonstrate product capabilities and attract more developers and users. However, a single successful trade cannot prove that an Agent has long-term investment consistency. Repeatability and risk management matter just as much.

Fourth, whether the platform can evolve from a token launchpad into infrastructure for autonomous financial Agents. If AGENCY can continue attracting creators and establish stable cycles of Agent operations, treasury management, and fee generation, its long-term positioning could extend beyond that of a single AI token launch platform. This would create a larger potential valuation narrative, but it would also require continuous product development, user retention, and sustained economic activity.

Alongside these growth opportunities, several risks should not be overlooked.

First, ecosystem fee revenue may not grow consistently. Tokens launched on the platform tend to have strong speculative characteristics. If trading activity declines, fee revenue and buyback funds may fall accordingly. Second, Agent operations and investment activities involve risks related to fund security, program execution, and strategy decisions. Even with permission controls and independent signing mechanisms, software vulnerabilities and execution failures cannot be completely ruled out. Finally, high short-term trading activity may amplify price volatility. When large amounts of capital concentrate around a new mechanism, the token may face significant pullback pressure once the catalyst has been fully priced in.

Therefore, the most useful data to monitor going forward is not any single price or trading-volume metric, but a set of indicators that can be cross-checked against one another: daily fees, actual buyback amounts, tokens burned, active Agent counts, 7-day and 30-day project retention, holder concentration, and large capital flows.

Among these, the relationship between fee growth and buyback volume is particularly important. If platform activity continues to increase but buyback amounts do not grow accordingly, it suggests that ecosystem expansion has not yet translated into meaningful token demand. Conversely, if fees, buybacks, and burns all grow consistently while the market also maintains demand independent of the buyback mechanism, then Agency’s value-capture logic will have stronger evidence behind it.

Overall, this surge reflects more than market enthusiasm for the AI Agent concept. It represents a reassessment of AGENCY’s economic model. The newly announced buyback-and-burn mechanism creates a more direct connection between the native token and platform activity. This is the clearest fundamental development in the current situation.

However, there is still a significant gap between a more complete mechanism and a mature business model. What can currently be confirmed is that AGENCY has introduced a potential new path for value to flow back to the token. What remains uncertain is whether this path can generate substantial capital flows and whether the platform can consistently expand real usage demand.

AGENCY’s core investment thesis is whether the autonomous economic activities of AI Agents can generate platform activity at scale and convert that activity into actual demand for Agency through sustained fee-based buybacks and burns.

If future data shows that this cycle is taking shape, the latest surge could mark the beginning of a broader market reassessment of AGENCY. If buyback volumes remain limited, project retention is weak, or ecosystem activity depends primarily on short-term speculation, the current rally may instead reflect expectations being priced in ahead of actual fundamental growth.

High-end ABF capacity still failing to keep pace with the area and layer count of AI silicon

Ibiden’s (4062 JP) core driver remains qualified high-end ABF capacity failing to keep pace with the area and layer count of AI silicon. Intel/AMD server CPU shipments grow +36%/+62% in 2027 on new platforms 56–63% larger in substrate area, widening the CPU gap further. GPUs and EMIB-T consume the highest-end capacity: Rubin yields only 12 units per panel, TPU V9 / Trainium 4 only 4. The next pricing step falls on 27Q1 contract renewals, where new products can price above legacy agreements. We forecast FY3/27 / FY3/28 revenue growth of 35% / 30% and EPS of JPY173 / JPY267; at ~45x FY3/28E PE the shares still have rerating room, with the FY27Q2 results call the near-term catalyst.

-CPU demand is back and widens the supply gap. Resident agents such as Muse push workloads back onto CPUs via headless browsers and high-frequency API calls, and Intel can currently fill only ~50% of orders; shipments have upside if capacity allows. FUNDA models Intel server CPU shipments of 26.5mn units in 2027E (+36%) and AMD 20.4mn (+62%); multiplied by substrate area 63% larger for Diamond Rapids vs. Granite Rapids and 56% larger for Venice vs. Turin, substrate-area demand grows far faster than unit count. Supply is not only limited but already allocated: tier-1 and tier-2 makers are all full as of 26Q4, lead times are 48–52 weeks, total 2027 capacity grows only ~10–15%, and a visible shortfall opens from 27Q1. Customers that did not co-fund capacity sit lower in the allocation queue. This is already visible at Ibiden: AMD substrate revenue declines sequentially through 2H FY3/27 as capacity temporarily allocated to AMD returns to Intel; this does not reflect weaker AMD demand.

-GPUs and EMIB-T consume the highest-end slice of capacity. Blackwell is 73×81mm at 14 layers; Rubin 83×97mm at 18 layers, an estimated 1.8x the area; Rubin Ultra more than 2x Blackwell’s area at ~3x the price. EMIB-T is more extreme: Google TPU V9 at ~120×120mm, 24 layers with a multi-layer core, and Amazon Trainium 4 at ~120×120mm, 24 layers with a multi-layer core, each yielding only 4 substrates per panel. Even if ASIC unit growth looks modest, what truly consumes capacity is area, layer count and yield (core-stage yield on a multi-layer core drops from 99.9% to 97–98%, and a core defect can render all subsequent build-up layers worthless).

-Substrate price increases continue, supporting Ibiden’s new-product pricing. This year’s increases came mainly from Taiwanese makers; Ibiden only removed its quarterly price-decline assumption and normalized Intel pricing to a fair level. Next year, with the industry shortfall in place and lead times at 48–52 weeks, the next customer contract renewals fall in 27Q1 and new products can secure better quotes; new T-glass suppliers are also expected to qualify in 27Q1, and with Chinese and Taiwanese suppliers raising prices Ibiden also has room to pass through costs, while substrates remain under 10% of chip cost so we expect customers to accept the increase. We have not yet seen specific quotes, but we think a price increase is likely.

author: ConstanceWaing
quoted_text:
The Private Alpha of Neptune is now live for Pacifica OGs. Neptune gives every trader on Pacifica their own AI agent, and I want to share why we built it.

Most traders have more ideas than they ever get to test. Turning an idea into clear rules, testing it against historical data, and running it live has traditionally required code and infrastructure. As a result, systematic trading has mostly remained the domain of programmers and quant desks.

AI agents can now do much of that work. But using one for trading still means setting up a server, managing API keys, connecting to an exchange, and manually verifying the agent actually built what you asked for. This setup is still where most people give up.

Neptune changes this by giving you your own server in one click. From there, you describe what you want in plain language, and Neptune builds it as a task, workflow, or trading strategy. You can inspect the rules it wrote, backtest them, and run them when you're ready.

Pacifica started as a dex. We later released an MCP server so agents could trade on Pacifica directly, because we believe an increasing share of onchain trading will be run by agents. Neptune is the next step: giving anyone access to those capabilities without needing to write code or manage infrastructure.

In future builds, Neptune will watch the markets you care about, run strategies across Pacifica's products, and help manage risk while you're away. Traders will be able to share and build on each other's skills and strategies, turning one person's ideas into tools others can use.

Eventually, much of what you do and how you trade on Pacifica will start with simply telling Neptune what you want.

Stay tuned for more!

text:
DeepSeek Harness 这次宣布了兼容 Claude Code Mods。

负责人崔添翼  @tianyi 在知乎解释，v0.2.1-alpha.1 目前还只是实验性兼容层，不能保证 100% 兼容。官方文档也明确列出了和 Claude Code 原生行为之间的差异。

这次更像是在验证 DSH 从一开始就坚持的「一切皆插件」架构。模型、工具、Skills、Session，甚至 Agent Loop 本身都可以被替换和重新组合。

崔添翼提了三个方向，我觉得都挺关键。

用户可以用插件把 Harness 改成自己想要的样子，Agent 甚至能自己写和安装插件；企业可以把行业经验和内部基础设施沉淀成私有插件；再往前一步，插件系统还能成为 Agent 修改自身工作方式的接口。

第三点是最值得关注。

如果 Agent 以后能自己写插件、热加载插件，甚至修改自己的 Harness，那 Harness 就不再只是模型外面那层固定的壳，它会逐渐变成 Agent 可以主动修改的一部分。

所以模型可能不会把 Harness 吃掉，更可能是模型开始学会改 Harness。

而 DeepSeek Harness 团队自己给出的目标也很直接，从 Harness 的角度推进 AGI。

小孩哥 @Blonskr 公布了又一轮销毁回购，这次是 604.89 枚 $BEM 打入了黑洞地址，但是小孩哥没有详细的去说是哪几部分的资金收入回购的 $BEM 

我顺着链上大致捋了一下资金链路，有兴趣的兄弟可以来看看了解一下。

────────────────────────────────

这次销毁，其实是一共用了三个钱包，在公开市场使用  22.35 个 $BNB 买入 $BEM ：

0x571d447f4f24688eC35Ccf07f1D6993655F6aF15
花费 15 BNB，买入约 399.456 BEM  （这个是主钱包地址）

0xE2f77062c6060503e0289c6638D1B0A7C76cBB9d
花费 4.35 BNB，买入约 120.614 BEM

0xEBeceDeA36e598b64E17f8d519EB77441C539F76
花费 3 BNB，买入约 84.824 BEM

三个地址合计买入：604.8937 BEM

三笔交易都通过 OKX DEX Router 路由，在 Pancake、Infinity、Uniswap V4 等公开流动性池完成。

买完以后，这三个钱包又分别把 BEM 转进黑洞地址：

0x000000000000000000000000000000000000dEaD

────────────────────────────────

资金来源方面，这次回购主要来自近期的：流片费、电路容器开通费，以及官方晶体管市场 / 电路市场手续费。

这个其实可以在链上看到，在回购发生前大约一个小时，主钱包刚刚从两个官方市场合约中提出：

约 1.7908 BNB 以及 0.4908 BNB，合计大约 2.28 BNB。

这两个市场合约也都是由主钱包创建的，分别对应晶体管竞价、挂单交易等 TapeOut 生态内的市场活动。

除此之外，参与回购的几个钱包本身也已经持有一部分 BNB，其中部分资金来源和 TapeOut 的处理器、协议相关地址存在关联。

所以从链上看，这次基本就是把近期生态产生的一部分收入，加上相关钱包中已经沉淀的 BNB，统一拿出来做了一次 BEM 市场回购。

text:
说说易理华理论的一些错误之处吧..

通篇看下来就是说VC抱怨说自己没赚到钱.   

而且他只抱怨 现状, 也就是"结果", 说行业未来"应该" 如何如何, 也就是搁这里许愿来的.   似乎不会去想背后根本原因会怎么样.

1. VC 1+3解锁
为什么有这个东西呢?

说白了就是项目方和散户都知道VC投的是垃圾,知道VC解锁了了就卖,然后砸低币价.  所谓 高FDV,低流通的 山寨币, tge后狗都不买,  散户空投拿到了一路砸就是了.

所以强制搞的1+3, VC最后跑. 不然根本不可能有买盘.  交易所也不会接受上一个币然后一路瀑布下跌.

如果你VC投的要是Hyperliquid, 和早期的腾讯, 字节跳动, 你还想不想着1年还是3年解锁?

换句话说就是你自己看项目能力差,  还跑来做大聪明质疑解锁规划.  

2.  叙事破灭了, 为什么破灭了呢?

很简单, 没有提升生产力.  火车,飞机, 电脑, 和现在AI的出现, 都是实打实的提升了生产力, 创造了大量社会价值, 所以有高估值.   (多高是合理估值是另外一回事了)

加密市场呢?  搞出来的是不需要KYC/AML的转账+买股票 + 预测市场(赌场).  这是暂时性的监管套利, 不是生产力的提升.   这几个,用现有的web2技术都可以做. 只不过政府现在懒得管而已, 但是耐心总有消耗完的时候. 

3. 为什么供给失衡了?
因为门槛低, 而且绝大部分都没有任何价值的重复项目.

我一个人就可以手搓一个 aster之类的 perp合约平台,  或者厕纸Scroll一类的 L2出来, 你说有什么价值?

AI公司你不投入个百亿美元搞研发, 跑一个OpenAI 或者  Deepseek出来试试?

---------------------------------------
你看易理华的理论,

就知道旗下基金为啥亏这么严重了.
author: LumaoDoggie
quoted_text: 加密一级市场为什么快死了，我们曾作为最活跃的投资机构之一，这十年感受最明显问题，第一个是叙事破灭了，从白皮书到机构背书到TVL刷量，基本市场不再买单。第二个是供给失衡，现在出现数以万计项目，优秀项目跑出来难度极大。第三个是1➕3解锁机制，基本是定向杀死VC，让项目，MM和交易所先跑，第四是上币成本，现在一级项目为什么需要高估值和大融资，主要是几个龙头交易所上线，平均成本需要千万美金。虽然VC问题也很多，但没有大量VC支持一级市场，市场只剩下专业发币集团和MEME币活跃。一级市场是加密创新的重要来源，需要行业龙头真正的去buliding方向，比如币安上币筛选方式改进，按照现在模式，当年V神的ETH来了也上不了币安。其次是彻底废除1➕3解锁机制，VC承担了最大风险，应该不背负最差的解锁条款，项目成功或失败根本不是VC决定的。最后是加密项目需要回到真正的营收和回购，美股那么多年持续繁荣，最重要的是业绩增长和督促回馈股东利益，这才是行业龙头们应该做的事情，让市场二级投资者真正找到优质项目。

author: qinbafrank
quoted_text:
感觉小火箭RKLB又值得好好看看，这次核心逻辑有几个：
1、首先最重要的为了收购Iridium铱星通信筹集资金进行ATM增发股票融资在9月中已经结束了。
9月15号宣布完成一轮19亿美元的增发，加上2季度末公司23.8亿美金现金，现在手握接近43亿美金资金。收购铱星通信一部分现金一部分股票，现金对价大概是28亿多美金。过去三个月小火箭股价持续低迷很大一部分原因是公司增发卖股票，然后创始人也卖了一批股票，持续的抛压。现在这一部分抛压总算是过去了。

9月24号，Iridium股东大会99.6% 的已投票股份支持交易，对应约81%全部流通股。现在并购进程已经进入了FCC（联邦贸易委员会）监管审批流程中了，当下FCC已经接受 transfer applications，并建立公开意见程序：
Comments/Petitions：10月15日截止
Responses：10月30日
Replies：11月9日
所以最快11月初监管审批流程就能走完，后面就是并购最后交割阶段了，公司预计27年年中正式完成交割。

之前也聊过并购Iridium对小火箭的意义很重大：
1）从发射、卫星制造及组件业务开始进入了太空数据服务（类似星链对spacex的意义）；
2）Iridium的每年营收规模跟rklb差不多，并购整合完成之后，营收直接翻倍；
3）更重要的是利润结构的变化
现在RKLB的问题是虽然收入高速增长，但为了业务扩张还在大量资本支出，整体是亏损状态。但Iridium则不然，2025年Iridium营收8.71亿美金，OEBITDA 是4.95亿，这完全是另一种生意，高毛利高利润。

Peter Beck自己在交易说明里强调的就是Iridium的收入和盈利能力会实质性改变RKLB的财务状况。

2、订单接受手软
整个三季度
1）美国太空军
7 月21日签下美国太空军 $266m HASTE/导弹防御合同：12 次确定的亚轨道发射 + 最多 6 次额外 option，总潜在价值 $266m；
8 月 4 日拿到美国太空军 SB-AMTI合同，包含卫星设计、制造、发射到在轨运营全流程，这个意义就很重大了。合同总值$397m；
8月 18 日RKLB进入美国太空军 Space Data Network Consortium，同时直接获得两份 delivery orders，合计 $12m。

2）6 月底以后公开宣布的新增合同，光有明确金额的就至少包括 太空军$266m + $397m + $12m = $675m，此外还有 iQPS、Kepler、Viasat、Synspective 等金额未披露的大单。

3）9 月 30 日新签 Synspective 20 发 Electron 后，公司的launch backlog 已超过 100 次任务。

二季度财报官方公布积压订单规模23.5亿美金，同时三季度会确认约 $250—265m 的收入，公司此前给出的就是这个收入区间展望，确认收入会消耗 backlog；再加上三季度新增的订单，估计三季度财报里公布的backlog能到28~30亿美金这个区间，相当于当下两到三年的业务量。

3、业务新变化比订单更值得关注
1）截至 9 月 26 日，Rocket Lab完成第 97 次 Electron 系列任务，也是2026年第 18 次发射; Synspective、iQPS开始不断追加订单，核心就是这种成熟的可靠性。
可靠性 + launch slot 可获得性 + dedicated orbit + 高频执行能力。

2）HASTE正在变成一个独立的高毛利国防业务
Rocket Lab将其商业化的电子号（Electron）小型运载火箭进行改装，把 Electron/HASTE 火箭、ground support、range control 等装入标准集装箱，形成可部署式发射系统，这就是HASTE。

专门提供高频次、低成本、定制化的高超音速和亚轨道测试服务，HASTE 的业务高度依赖于国防与国家安全领域。

第一套 GHOST 将部署在 Alaska Kodiak，形成 Launch Complex 4，两座发射台，计划2027年投入运营。就是前面说的7月拿下的美国太空军那份2.66亿美金的合同。

4、当然还有重要的中子星火箭首飞
市场已经消化了Neutron首飞从26年底大概率要推到27年年初的节奏，后面就是要看Neutron工程节点能不能兑现。

所以把上面几点结合起来看：
1）对Iridium的并购正在最后监管审批，当然通过的概率还是很大，这决定的是RKLB更长期商业模式能否真正完成最后一次跃迁；
2）Q3 backlog数字则意味着业务本身在快速发展，整个因为形态会更加的多元化。
这两点是我认为近期会有表现的主要催化剂，然后60多的位置下方的支撑看起来很可以。

再长一些，就要看Neutron的进展了。

过去一年太空经济和RKLB也一直是重点关注的板块，之前6月份还有一个详细的梳理： https://t.co/xex9sMrqww

Peter Thiel on how you should think about your future:

"What you end up doing when you think of the future as indefinite is you pick a job that you think will look good on your resume, because it will lead to a different job later on. There's even a credentialing version where you go to grad school, you get a consulting job, and you think of it as this branching tree diagram where you never really do something that you want to do.

You can think of the future on three horizons. Very short-term is: are you going to be happy, and will you be learning a lot? Medium-term is: how good is it on your resume? And very long-term is: are you working on something important or meaningful? We're in a skewed world where we overweight the medium-term and underweight some combination of the short-term and the long-term. I would recalibrate to focus on the short-term and the long-term, and forget about the medium-term."

text:
有沒有發現，AI 越來越強，長相卻越來越像寵物？👀

Meta 的 Muse 配上一隻毛茸茸、臉頰紅紅的吉祥物。背後是越來越強大的 AI，呈現在你面前的，卻是一個看起來需要被照顧的小傢伙。(https://t.co/OwkT2MwnYe)

我覺得這個設計方向很值得研究，尤其是正在做 AI 產品的人。

⚡️ 其實，100 年前電力公司就做過類似的事。

1926 年，美國 Alabama Power 推出 Reddy Kilowatt，把看不見、摸不得的電，畫成一個有笑臉的卡通角色，用更親切的形象鼓勵大家使用電力。(https://t.co/ZuDdQOWTfV)

🧠 心理學裡有個概念叫「嬰兒圖式」。

大眼睛、圓臉、小鼻子這些特徵，容易讓人覺得可愛，產生照顧的意願。這有實驗研究支持，但不能直接推論成「可愛的 AI 就一定更值得信任」。(https://t.co/ydg2hZYF5p)

放到 AI Agent 身上，我的理解是：可愛的外型，可能讓人更願意靠近、嘗試，甚至把事情交給它處理。

以前用聊天機器人，你問一句，它回答一句。

接下來的 Agent，則可能需要讀你的信件、看你的行程、操作你的電腦。產品要跨過的門檻，也變成了：「你願意讓它參與多少生活？」

text:
here's my take on the polymarket token.

back in december, the market gave a $Poly launch in 2026 a 79% chance. after the trademark filing in february it was still around 70%. today it's 14%. most people haven't noticed how hard that trade fell apart.

i don't think it's because the team changed its mind. i think the incentives changed. polymarket is raising at a $20b valuation and already does more than $1b a year in revenue. if you're an equity investor like ICE, you don't want a token that takes a cut of that revenue. the money has to go to either the shareholders or the token holders, and the shareholders got there first.

so when $Poly does launch, i expect it to be a utility token, not a revenue token. you'd stake it to help settle markets and resolve disputes, which would replace their reliance on uma. that fits with everything they're building right now: their own stablecoin, a rebuilt exchange, and most likely their own chain.

my base case is a launch in 2027 alongside the new chain. international users get the airdrop, US users likely don't, and it opens at a valuation well below the company's.

the bull case is a token that shares in fees and includes US users. that would be the biggest airdrop of the cycle.

the bear case is that the cftc probe and the US license make a token too risky, and they go the ipo route instead.

text:
The thing I think is really worth looking at about $baton move from 2M to 16M isn’t how much it went up, but the fact that the market has started to reprice this ticker.

Hg5Ja55T5wESq4vyFoiVCMeHXtGyVA69X2UHq8hgpump 

What’s most interesting about BATON actually isn’t something that appeared later.

Before pumpfun, Baton was the original name of the project.

What BATON is doing now is essentially taking a name that already existed in Pumpfun’s history and turning it back into a meme.

That’s why, compared with an ordinary Solana dog coin, it naturally carries a layer of native Pumpfun culture.

The official narrative also directly defines it as a PumpFun ecosystem native meme, and BATON was the first coin paired with PUMP.

That’s why I think BATON already had a story at 2M, but the market simply wasn’t paying enough attention to that story at the time.

Recently, PUMP itself started gaining strength again, while launchpad-related assets have generally been weak, so capital started looking for high-beta plays within the PUMP ecosystem.

BATON just happens to be the easiest one for the market to understand:

Pumpfun’s old name + PUMP pairing + native meme.

So I’m more inclined to view this 2M → 16M move as BATON being rediscovered after PUMP regained attention.

There’s also a new variable for BATON now: Holder Rewards.

Pumpfun’s official documentation states that Holder Rewards tokens continuously distribute trading fees to holders; the official Holder Rewards page also currently lists BATON among the top reward-generating coins, with roughly $400K in cumulative Holder Rewards, paid in PUMP.

I wouldn’t directly interpret this as “holding BATON gives you fixed yield.”

What actually matters is that BATON’s trading activity can now be directly converted into PUMP received by holders.

So BATON’s overall logic is more complete now than it was at 2M.

But I would still keep the focus on its PUMP ecosystem beta.

Holder Rewards is an added bonus. What really determines BATON’s upside from here is whether it can become the market’s representative meme for PUMP.

If, going forward, BATON becomes the first ticker people think of when they think about PUMP ecosystem memes, then today’s 16M could just be the market’s first attempt at pricing that identity.

If it only follows PUMP whenever PUMP goes up, then ultimately it’s still just a high-beta meme.

So what I’m looking at now isn’t whether BATON can simply repeat another 2M → 16M move, but whether this ticker can turn Pumpfun’s history into its own cultural asset.

That’s what will ultimately determine whether its valuation can continue moving higher.

text:
卧槽！A 股量化最费时间的，可能根本不是写策略，而是把 7000+ 股票的分钟数据真正变成“能回测的数据”。

free-stockdb，2.6K Stars，MIT 开源，一套专门给 A 股量化做的本地数据引擎。

以前做全市场回测，光数据就能耗死你：7000+ 股票分钟线拉数据 3-5 天、清洗 1-2 天、复权 1-2 天、建库 1-3 天、算指标 2-3 天，一套下来 10-15 个工作日才能跑通第一个策略。

free-stockdb 不一样，数据同步 / 清洗 / 复权 / 组织全在同步层完成，策略只读本地数据，C++ 时序引擎加 Rust 计算核心，开箱即用。

核心能力：

1️⃣ 全市场本地数据：日 / 周 / 月线、1/5/15/30 分钟 K，ETF 和 Tick 数据也能继续接

2️⃣ 复权直接做好：前复权、后复权、不复权、原始复权因子统一查询

3️⃣ 增量更新：第一次同步完，后面只处理变化数据，断网也能继续研究和回测

4️⃣ 本地计算：内置 39 种指标 + 5 类指数，批量股票可以直接一起算

5️⃣ C++ 时序引擎 + Zstd 压缩，不用自己再折腾 MySQL、表结构和查询优化

6️⃣ Python、HTTP、Excel/WPS、网页、MCP 五种方式都能调用，Claude / Codex 也能直接接

我觉得它真正有意思的地方，是把 A 股量化最脏、最费时间的数据工程先处理掉了。

以前是：

每跑一个策略 → 请求 API → 等数据 → 清洗 → 复权 → 再回测。

现在更像是先把整个市场搬到自己电脑里，后面选股、因子、回测、AI Agent 全部围着本地数据跑。

核心服务甚至只有约 2.2MB。

做 A 股量化、全市场回测、因子研究，或者想给自己的 AI 股票 Agent 搭本地数据底座的，这个很值得收藏。

author: _zheergen
quoted_text:
终于有人把自己做交易终端最麻烦的 K 线图层，做成了一套够轻、够完整的开源底座。

KLineChart，4.2K Stars，Apache-2.0 开源，零依赖、Gzip 只有约 40KB 的专业金融图表库。

以前做行情界面，最烦的就是手写 K 线图：蜡烛、均线、成交量、画线工具……一套下来又大又卡。

KLineChart 不一样，HTML5 Canvas 写的轻量 K 线图，零第三方依赖、gzip 才 40K，内置多指标加画线模型，一个图表多端适配，TypeScript 类型全给你。

核心能力：

1️⃣ 零依赖 + 轻量：Gzip 约 40KB，拿来做网页和桌面金融终端都很顺

2️⃣ 指标 + 画线：内置多种指标和 Overlay，也支持自己扩展指标、图形和标注

3️⃣ 实时数据接口：历史加载、实时更新、向前补数据、切 Symbol / Period 都能自己控制

4️⃣ v10 多 Y 轴：同一个 Pane 可以挂不同指标、不同坐标轴，复杂图表更好搭

5️⃣ 高度可定制：主题、坐标轴、Tooltip、快捷键、Crosshair、缩放逻辑都能自己改

6️⃣ 移动端也支持：一套图表可以同时适配 PC 和手机，不用重新做一套

我觉得它最值钱的地方，不是“能画 K 线”。

而是你想自己做量化终端、行情网站、AI Trading Dashboard，最基础也最容易耗掉大量开发时间的图表层，它已经帮你铺好了。

上面再接自己的行情、指标、策略、AI Agent，基本就能继续往 TradingView 风格终端方向搭。

做股票量化、Crypto 看盘、金融前端或者交易终端的，这个很适合收藏。

quoted_text:
What i'm doing with my coins brain dump i didn't proof read

- A couple thoughts as to how I’ve traded this cycle so far

First and foremost alts and onchain are behaving very similar on the way up. Coins go into a lockout up trend, the entire timeline flips tubro bullish. This lasts until price cools off. eventually we rotate. Attention gets vamped onto the next. The strongest coins, however, always get the rotation back. So far it’s been Hype, Zec, Lit, Pump, near… ? The obvious takeaway is there is edge in being able to sit on a coin longer than a few days. Look at what happened with pump. 2x off the bottom in a straight line, nobody owned it, and after a few weeks of underperformance it was like people forgot the coin existed? Picked their own vamp to outperform (stonk, long, pons), then pump gets back into lockout trend.

The difference between the chosen alts and “onchain” is the flows keep coming back to the good alts. I stand by the idea that it is hard to justify anything onchain in the 300-500+ range because these alts have so much fucking juice in them. I don’t think Zec $5k+ Hype $250+ VVV $100+ Pump $.2 this year is that ridiculous. It means I have to either trade low caps into the 20-50 range or fully focus on spot alts (mentioned below) and leverage trading breakouts to stack more spot alts.

The obvious takeaway here is In order to catch the real moves these alts are capable of the only way to get there is by holding spot. Price action is schizo, partly bc everyone is trading high leverage only. It leads to nasty washouts and stops being run. 5-10xs are going to require being able to sit through chop. Look at how bitcoin has traded, lockout move 5-10% higher followed by seven days of nothing, which is legitimately grueling to leverage longs. Everyone gets wiped out. The timeline goes to war. Then we leg up again. I don’t see why this would stop. In hindsight the obvious way to play it was sitting in spot which goes against what I have been doing (and getting paid for).

——

A valid concern is what will happen with stocks/bonds/war/oil/ant ipo/etc. The honest truth is I don’t think it matters. The fear was always “if crypto is trading this bad while stocks trade this good what happens when it flips.” There have been moments of stock misery (despite things looking pretty great all things considered rn) and crypto broke that correlation. I think bitcoin continues to exist as a great alternative to the ai trade and the good alts mentioned above can standalone as quality, cheap, assets that exist separately to crypto performance as a whole. 

Every second I have spent thinking above these fears and reading market commentary has been a mistake.

I think in order to get paid as generationally as I would like over the coming months it Is imperative to read as few market opinions as possible. It feels like my feed has been overwhelmed by a storm of slop from people not making money. I can’t not get shaken out by trash. I stream for three hours a day, everyday, whatever I cover and learn during those sessions is beyond enough information to make clear decisions at the level that I need to.

——

I think ultimately it comes down to what do I think will happen over the next 6-12 months. Thinking this far in advance is the only way to break away from the cesspool of flip flopping biases every hour on the timeline. And what I think it we have the best setup I’ve seen since joining crypto for outright mania. 

Sec + CFTC are running GAME to push crypto. Btc ETF buyers are green again. Tokens are investible. Crypto is “cool” on socials to the younger generation. Social trading apps have reached escape velocity. Perps matter. Robinhood going all in, etc etc etc. I don’t need to pill anyone on the bull case. I love the spot.

The only way to make it that far is to hold the best coins on spot. This is shockingly difficult for me to do right now after having a great year trading perps. But I have to understand that the majority of that was during a bear market where there’s one or two impulse moves if lucky. Not a continuous uptrend with infinite marginal buyers higher and nothing but catalysts and air above like I think we have right now. It’s going to take some rewiring of my brain to make it where I think we can get to and keep exposure.

My final thought is when I think back on the traders of last cycle that outperformed the hardest what sticks out was their ability to denominate all profits into the winning coin. In 2024 it was sol. Stack sol -> sell to buy onchain coins -> take profits -> buy more sol. Rinse and repeat continuous big wins while sol legs up from $8->$270. Congrats on making it. I have been mentally taking a similar approach the last couple months but didn’t execute it as well as I wish I had. First it was pump. Most recently it was zec. Great PNLs on both but I wasted so much mental energy stressed over short term pa for no particular reason. (Buy some spot retard)

I sold, all of my zcash, because I felt extremely bloated in leverage and wanted to reset after playing the first round of the cycle pretty well imo. Moving forward I still believe that coin is zec and maybe a basket of a few others, Pump/Hype/vvv? And will probably be trading accordingly. Stack a ton of spot. Keep a non insignificant amount to leverage trade tighter spots, stack my golden goose coin

And pray we make it. good luck to us

另外新加坡房间里很少有蚊子，一般来说只有草地和水池附近会有蚊子，但新加坡的蟑螂会比较多，好一些的酒店几乎是看不到的。但如果你去芽笼吃田鸡粥，你会看到拇指大小的蟑螂四处爬，习惯了就好了。

2. 明辉田鸡粥不好吃，九巷田鸡粥味道还可以，但是涨价了，人均大概要 35 新币以上，未必会划得来。个人非常推荐一家叫 ZHUP ZHUP 的龙虾粥，超级好吃，但需要预定位置，而且没有空调，能不能吃的到就看缘分了。

另外还有一家叫“酒逢知鸡”的店也是不错的，主要是吃炒鸡的，而且他们家的烧烤是请的非遗的厨师，老板是新加坡非常知名的美食网红，还有就是虾皇的小龙虾是真不错，如果有河南的小伙伴，非常推荐“掌柜”，吃过的都说好。

娘惹菜也有不错的，我就不推荐了，好的几乎排不到队，不好吃的一大堆。另外如果想要有点诗情画意的，可以去克拉码头河边的餐厅，其中“北疆”和“山东饭店”都是不错的，定位的时候说要做河边的位置，下午 17 点以后，并不晒，也不热，景色非常好。

肉骨茶反而我不轮推不推荐大家都会去吃，克拉码头的松发应该是最火的，对面还有一家亚细亚肉骨茶，味道都还可以。高端一点的话，温州府也可以。日料我和小伙伴超级推荐 Shin Yuu ，新加坡非常老牌的日料自助。

3. 吃饭主要集中在 牛车水 和 武吉士 ，这两个地方，牛车水就是 China town ，各种好吃的都有，其中有一个叫“矮子馅饼”是比较有名的，牛车水还有很多熟食，一般在其它地区不是很好买的。

武吉士就是 Bugis ，有非常出名的甜品店，比如阿秋甜品家的榴莲冰淇凌就非常好吃。新加坡吃东西即便是路边不是很起眼的小店卫生都是不错的，但需要注意，如果希望有包厢，一定要提前预定。

新加坡火锅文化也不错，辣的火锅首推冯校长，北京铜锅首推三锅先生，尤其是三锅先生都快成了食堂了，另外去冯校长能有几率抓到一些知名的币圈 KOL ，比如奶子哥。

4. 新加坡的物价确实比较贵，如果换算来说，大概是上海的 3 倍左右，甚至更高一些，而上海和东京的差距并不大，在某些程度来说新加坡还贵过香港，在新加坡不一定非要去 7-11 等超市去买水和饮料，确实比较贵，可以去非连锁的小超市。

330ML 的可乐如果是 2 新币以内，那么就算是比较便宜的了，早期我住在高文的时候，有一家印度人的超市，可乐 1.2 新币一瓶，我一次就买半箱，很久没看到这么便宜的了。

大多数小伙伴来新加坡应该就是 3-4 天的时间，主要就是去看看鱼尾狮，去金沙逛逛，如果再有时间可以去环球看看，但我最推荐的还是东海岸，东海岸集海边、草地、椰树、骑车道、跑步道、烧烤区和餐厅都连在一起。

整个公园沿海大约 13 公里、180 公顷，24 小时开放，很适合下午四五点以后过去，一直待到晚上。如果是我安排，会从 Marine Cove 一带开始，沿海慢慢往东骑车或散步，途中看看 East Coast Beach，最后找地方吃饭。

东海岸有很多不错的饭店，尤其是吃海鲜的，虽然贵，但确实好吃。

5. 都说新加坡的海南鸡好吃，我周边的小伙伴吃下来最好吃的有三家，一家是 五星海南鸡 ，一家是 文东记 ，还有一家叫 天天 ，其中 文东记 在牛车水就有店，并不贵，味道是不错的。

我才想起来，我吃过最好的吃的榴莲应该高文地铁站附近，很可惜最近不是榴莲季，要么贵贱要组个团带着大家吃榴莲。

我突然想起来，和香港桥底辣蟹齐名的应该是香辣蟹和黑胡椒蟹，很多人都喜欢去珍宝吃，说实话我是觉得一般，我还是更喜欢吃象拔蚌刺身。

6. 新加坡的晚上非常安全，虽然没有那么活跃，但确实异常的安全，没有什么担心的，即便是一名小女生都不用担心，新加坡的夜间娱乐也很多。

一般来说，143，巨亨算是第一梯队，至尊和金煌大概是第二梯队，帝国，Catwalk 应该是第三梯队，如果有人说我带你去地下室，那应该是真的非常好的朋友了。当然还有一些嗨吧，我估计大家兴趣不大，也就不介绍了。

我的订阅区会有一些小小的介绍，Steven 是好朋友，给我介绍了很多。主要都是在乌节路，所以住在乌节路的小伙伴可以晚上出来逛逛街，保证你什么都看不到。

7. 新加坡虽然有合规的红灯区，但我相信大多数来新加坡的小伙伴对于芽笼的兴趣不会很大，但我估计一定会有小伙伴想要去瞅一瞅的，其实真没啥，你在外边什么也看不到。

红灯区主要是偶数巷，话说我刚来的时候确实 Steven 也带我走了一圈，毕竟确实挺好奇的，所以我估计很多小伙伴也想去看看，看过一次也就没啥了。如果有人非要去芽笼吃田鸡粥，可以吃完消消食。

红灯区很小，也就是半条街，而且一点都不热闹，反而挺安静的，需要提醒一下，虽然芽笼的红灯区是合法的，但站街是违法的，新加坡经常会扫荡。

8. 如果你在新加坡的夜晚有什么惊吓，而且恰好你又有我的联系方式，可以联系我，力所能及的帮忙还是没问题的。

还有什么是我遗漏的？

quoted_text:
看到小姑娘的建议，稍微补充一下：

1. 临时的新加坡本地网络和电话有两种，一种是只有流量的，基本都是 esim 这种不需要 KYC ，但也不能打电话和收短信，只能提供流量，总的来说就是没有 +65 的功能。

另一种就是游客卡，主要就是短期的，需要 KYC ，可以在 7-11 等买，或者直接在机场买也可以，可以获得 +65 的功能。

对于部分小伙伴来说，买一个然后注册一些网站是可以的，这种卡一般最多用30天。

推荐用 Singtel 的游客卡，大概 10新币（53人民币不到）、7天有效期、500GB 新加坡/马来西亚/印尼/泰国/香港流量，5G，并包含本地无限通话和短信。实体 SIM 和 eSIM 都有。

非常适合在新加坡以后想要去马来西亚的小伙伴，可以不用换卡了，直接就能在马来西亚用。

2. 入境卡一定要填写，非常快，很好写，基本上填好后 30 分钟内就能收到邮件，收到邮件就可以过关了，新加坡过关效率很高，不用担心。

新加坡过海关不需要小费，没有任何的人工检索通道（小黑屋除外），都是自动机器，非常快。

3. 新加坡入境不能带电子烟，千万别带，电子烟在新加坡是违法的，最好也不要带烟，新加坡烟草管制非常严格，从来不存在一个人可以带 X 支烟这样的说法，哪怕带一根都需要申报。

我知道会有小伙伴会说自己每次都偷偷带，对，不被发现是没事，但如果被发现就会比较麻烦，尤其是带多了点就会当走私处理了。

另外进入新加坡可以带酒，一般来说 500ML 的白酒可以带两瓶，威士忌可以带 1L ，喜欢喝酒的小伙伴出来海关酒可以看到卖酒的，价格还算可以，如果有打折的话当年茅台大概是 230 多新币，没打折的话大概小 300 新币吧。

新加坡买烟在超市也可以买，但烟不会摆在外边，需要自己和售货员说，然后才能买，我不抽烟，所以也不知道都有什么品牌，听说基本都是万宝路。

4. 新加坡换钱挺容易的，汇率也还算过的去，在牛车水（中国街）有很多换汇公司，甚至可以从微信换成新币，也可以把人民币寄回中国，但听说偶尔会出现冻卡。

我个人建议来新加坡还是要带一些现金的，因为并不是所有地方都可以刷信用卡，尤其是小贩中心或者食阁，如果没有新加坡本地的支付方式，现金是最好的。

汇率大概是不到 5.3 元人民币换 1 新币，一般来说小贩中心或者亚坤这类的吃吃一个人大概要 15 新币左右，如果是食阁的话，一碗面大概是 6 新币，一份蛋炒饭大概是 5.5 新币，一份海南鸡大概是 8 新币。

另外新加坡的地铁可以直接用 VISA 和 Mastercard卡，刷了就可以走，应该是按距离收费的，起手点应该是 1 新币左右，我基本做一站都是 1.0X 新币左右。

5. 很多短视频都有介绍新加坡的规矩特别多，动不动就罚款，也对，也不对，确实规矩很多，但也不是非常容易被罚款，一般来说第一次发现都是会警告一下，比如室外没有在规定的地方抽烟。

对，新加坡地铁，公交和出租车上都不能吃东西和喝水，有时候出租车还好，但公众交通如果被发现，对方还是较真的人，确实是挺麻烦的。

总的来说自己都认为不是好事的，就别做，那就肯定没错了。

6. 新加坡的打车其实非常容易，但刚刚来新加坡可能会觉得不方便，首先是打车不能扬招，其次打车都需要去打车点（pickup point），没有在的话，就要自己找，另外新加坡打车基本上有 3 分钟的等待时间，超过时间就要扣超时费。

新加坡最好用的还是 Grab ，尤其是从机场出来的时候，Grab 的性价比要高于出租车，Grab 可以绑定信用卡，而且在新加坡还可以用 USDT 充值（我不记得游客是否可以了），总之 Grab 是挺好用的。

如果看到司机是华人面孔可以尝试说中文，大多数都会讲中文，如果是看到印度裔等那就只能说英文了。

7. 在新加坡大多数的路边店是没有什么“服务”概念的， 尤其是吃饭的时候别指望能有多周到的服务，但相比香港还是强多了，当然也会有部分服务员素质不高的情况，能不吵架尽量就别吵架。

一般的饭店都有 10% 的服务费 和 9% 的税，都含在账单里的，所以不用给小费。新加坡几乎没有小费文化。

8. 如果在新加坡有什么问题，而且恰好你又有我的联系方式，可以联系我，力所能及的帮忙还是没问题的。

还有什么是我遗漏的？

text:
Shopify CEO 跑完 2.5 小时赛车，Bryan Johnson 抽了他两次血。

Bryan Johnson 今天刚公布了一个挺离谱、但我很感兴趣的实验。

实验对象是 Shopify CEO Tobias Lütke。Tobi 今年 45 岁，这两年已经真的开始跑职业级耐力赛了，今年跟 TDS Racing 跑 IMSA 的 LMP2。

这次是在 Road Atlanta 的 Petit Le Mans。Bryan 在 Tobi 上车前抽了一次血，等他完成大约 2.5 小时的 stint 后，再抽一次，然后拿两组样本去做 deep molecular profiling。

这 2.5 小时对身体有多狠？

车速超过 180mph，峰值接近 4.2G，座舱温度可以到 40–50°C，心率长期维持在 140–170。重刹时，一条腿要踩出接近 200 磅的力量。与此同时，你还得在湿滑赛道上连续判断刹车点、路线和周围十几辆车的位置。

Bryan 想看的，就是一个人在这种高温、脱水、G 力和持续高认知负荷下，血液里的分子层面到底发生了什么。

他把这称为一次“first-in-world racing experiment”。

这个说法我会稍微打个折扣。赛车医学以前已经测过车手赛前赛后的心率、体温、氧化应激、皮质醇和血糖，所以研究赛车对人体的影响并不新。

真正让我感兴趣的是另一件事：

Bryan Johnson 正在把 longevity 从“我今天应该吃什么补剂”，一点点推向更像工程学的东西。

给身体一个真实世界里的极端 stress，密集采集数据，看它怎么坏、怎么恢复，再试图找到可以优化的参数。

以前大家研究赛车，数据主要来自车。

现在连车手也开始被当成一台可以读日志的机器了。

Bryan 一直说，health is an engineering discipline。

放在赛车场里看，这句话突然顺眼了很多。
