I reviewed Tobi’s biomarker’s from the car race yesterday. His heart rate, respiration, nervous system, focus, brain state, and more.

It’s insane.

I have some observations below. First, you need to get into the right headspace to understand the insanity.

Imagine this…

> you're breathing at an 8 min/mile (5 min/km) pace
> in a 110°F (43°C) heat chamber 
> heart rate of 145 bpm, peaking at 171 bpm
> intermittently body checked 700 lbs (320 kg) of force
> your core body temp near 102°F (39°C), a high fever
> claustrophobically strapped in a six point harness 
> helmeted head weighs 65 lbs (30 kg) under g load
> no evaporative cooling
> you’ve lost 4.6% of your body mass through sweat
> you can’t move
> vision narrowing from thermal strain and dehydration

Now, in these circumstances, your job is to…

> drive a tightrope at 180 mph (290 km/h)
> overtaking/defending against ahead, beside, behind
> staying within millimeters of tolerance 
> lose concentration for a tenth of a sec, in trouble

Do this for 2.5 hours straight.

A few additional things I find interesting from looking at the data:

1. It’s crazy to me his body can be in such a heightened state while completely stationary. Sitting down, he produced a cardiac load equal to high intensity physical exertion.

2. Thirty minutes before the race, Tobi’s body was already racing. His heart rate elevated to 136 bpm, more than 2x his baseline.

3. In qualifying, the higher his heart rate, the faster his lap. Arousal and performance moved in sync, including his personal best lap.

4. He lost 4.6% of his body mass in sweat. This is severe dehydration. At 2% dehydration your reaction time measurably decreases. He surpassed this in the first hour.

5. His nervous system was switched entirely to fight. There was no chill, anywhere.

6. His incredibly high breathing rate was driven by extreme sympathetic stress and rising core temperature, averaging 41 breaths a minute on his flying laps, moving 93 liters of air a minute.

7. His peak respiratory rate was 59. This is an all out sprint!

8. The only life experience I can map onto Tobi’s experience  was doing 27 mg of 5-MeO-DMT, the world’s most powerful psychedelic. It was all consuming, taking me to the cliff of my physical and mental capacity for 45 minutes. Otherwise, it is very hard for me to imagine being able to excel in these extreme conditions for 2.5 hours.
|
I now understand a little more what Tobi was telling me about the flow state he drops into. Under such extreme physiological conditions, the brain ruthlessly narrows focus. His brain downregulates the self-monitoring prefrontal regions (the self narration). The spike in norepinephrine dilates time, creating the perception of time slowing down.

MRIs on professional drivers show they use roughly one brain region for tasks where novices light up fifteen. A novice would be crushed in these circumstances in less than 10 minutes.

I’m impressed. It’s very hard and nearly impossible to actually understand what it’s like to go through something like this. 

Tobi and @dhh (Tobi’s teammate) were both my first customers at Braintree and gave my startup life when it wasn’t clear if we had a future. They generously encouraged other startups in the Ruby on Rails community to use us.  DHH’s co-founder @jasonfried  did as well. They’ve been great friends to me.

As to Tobi’s performance in the race, he did exceptionally well:

> closed within +0.51% of the fastest Bronze driver, putting him neck and neck with the top ranked amateur drivers in North America

> got his fastest lap of the race on Lap 88 (1:15.359), over two hours in and with peak dehydration and thermal strain, showing incredible tenacity

> finished just +2.60% off absolute class best, competing against world class professionals

There were 150 drivers competing in this race. Respect to all of you. I have a whole new appreciation for the sport.

text:
Peter Thiel 十几年前讲过一个职业建议：

把「这件事写进简历好不好看」从人生决策里删掉。

当时 Thiel 在 UT Austin 宣传《Zero to One》，一个年轻工程师问他，应该怎么判断自己下一步该做什么。

Thiel 说，大多数人最大的问题，是把未来想得太模糊。

不知道自己最终要去哪里，于是每一步都开始为下一步服务。读研是为了拿一个更好的 offer，去咨询公司是为了下一份工作更好跳，进大厂是为了简历上多一行漂亮的公司名。

人生最后变成一棵不断分叉的职业树。

每个节点看起来都保留了更多选择，但你一直没有真正开始做自己想做的事情。

Thiel 给了一个很简单的判断方法，把未来拆成三个时间尺度。

短期：我在这里开心吗？每天有没有学到很多东西？

中期：这段经历写在简历上够不够漂亮？

长期：我做的事情到底重不重要，有没有意义？

他说，我们这个社会把太多精力花在了第二个问题上。

所以他的建议是多想短期，多想长期，忘掉中期。

这句话放到 2026 年，我觉得更重要。

因为 AI 正在让很多所谓的「中期资产」加速折旧。

一个过去能在简历上吃五年的 title，一套你花几年练出来的职业技能，一家曾经足够漂亮的公司名字，都可能因为模型、组织方式和行业周期的变化迅速贬值。

反过来，两个东西越来越难被替代。

你现在是不是处在一个学习密度足够高、自己真的愿意投入的环境里；

以及十年以后回头看，你现在做的事情究竟有没有积累出什么真正属于自己的东西。

当然，忘掉中期本身也是一句很 Thiel 的话。

对很多人来说，房租、签证、家庭责任、现金流都是真实存在的，你不可能完全不管简历和下一份工作。

但我很喜欢他想提醒的那件事：

职业规划最危险的状态，可能不是走错路，而是你每一步看起来都走得很对，最后却发现这条路从来不是你自己选的。
author: sleepy0x13
quoted_text:
Peter Thiel on how you should think about your future:

"What you end up doing when you think of the future as indefinite is you pick a job that you think will look good on your resume, because it will lead to a different job later on. There's even a credentialing version where you go to grad school, you get a consulting job, and you think of it as this branching tree diagram where you never really do something that you want to do.

You can think of the future on three horizons. Very short-term is: are you going to be happy, and will you be learning a lot? Medium-term is: how good is it on your resume? And very long-term is: are you working on something important or meaningful? We're in a skewed world where we overweight the medium-term and underweight some combination of the short-term and the long-term. I would recalibrate to focus on the short-term and the long-term, and forget about the medium-term."

quoted_text:
纽约时报对 @cz_binance 最新的采访， 有不少以前不知道的细节，摘一些比较有意思的：

1. 外界估计 CZ 身家 1140 亿美元，但 CZ 坚称真实数字只有 100-300 亿美元，还说其实 1000 万美元就足够自己舒服生活

2. CZ 在阿布扎比的这栋房子价值 500 万美元，有 9 个卧室、4 名保镖、私人厨师和一艘名叫 Da Moon 的游艇。他说附近有房子挂牌价 1.5 亿美元

3. CZ 以前经常在播客里提到房子漏水，这次记者去了他家，他真的带记者看了被水损坏的地板和变色的天花板

4. 家里有昂贵的 Steinway 三角钢琴，放在儿童游戏室里，CZ 告诉记者，是「贵的那种」，但他不会弹

5. 大家都知道 CZ 是 2013 年卖掉上海的三居室，All In 买了比特币。这次在采访中爆料了具体数字：房子卖了 900,000 美元，全部买成了 BTC

6. Binance 创立后几个月就成为全球最大 Crypto 交易所，并迅速做到 10 亿美元净利润 https://t.co/Xs4OWKXQ4J

7. CZ 称 FTX 崩盘让 Binance 手上的 FTT 损失了 5 亿美元

8. 知道自己要坐牢后，他专门组建了一支「坐牢顾问」团队，教他如何适应监狱里的规则和人际关系

9. CZ 坐牢的那个监狱，也是 SBF 后来被安排的同一个联邦监狱园区

10. 他在监狱里组织了一个「股票研究小组」。监狱电视可以看 CNBC，CZ 和其他囚犯一起追踪股票价格，有人问他「Bitcoin 为什么涨」，CZ 回答「我也不确定」

11. 从走出监狱到坐上私人飞机并起飞，只用了 26 分钟

12. 第一次认真考虑定居 UAE，政府部长几小时内就来见他，还叫来医生完成签证血检，Golden Visa 不到 12 小时就批了，普通人需要了几个星期

13. UAE 不会向美国引渡自己的公民，是 CZ 入籍的一个重要因素。他甚至认真考虑过：如果与美国司法部谈不拢，就留在 UAE 当逃犯。但他最终还是选择认罪，币安支付了 43 亿美元罚款

14. MGX 投资币安的 20 亿美元，CZ 原本希望直接用 BTC 支付 (当时估值 750 亿美元)，但 UAE 方面担心 BTC 波动太大，最终交易使用了 USD1 (https://t.co/SSY9nshEXt)。后来，CZ 把收到的 USD1 换成了 BTC 和其它资产

15. CZ 投资了一家研究 Artificial Wombs (人工子宫) 的创业公司

16. CZ 长期受慢性疼痛的困扰，经常平躺在床上工作。有一次伊朗向 UAE 发射导弹，他正在床上工作，窗户震动，他去阳台看到天空中的烟迹，然后回床上继续工作

17. CZ 有两条狗，一条比利时马里努阿犬叫 Broccoli，因为听起来有点像在念 blockchain；另一条中亚猎犬，是吉尔吉斯斯坦总统送给他的

text:
There’s a specific type of ‘mev’ backrunning on robinhood chain which is more like hft exchange arb than ethereum mev, let me explain 

On robinhood chain they have first come first serve tx ordering so by the time you see a tx it’s order is fixed and you can’t get ahead, however it’s possible to get in the same 100ms block

So a fast searcher with colocation receiving the sequencer feed can decode a DEX trade, calculate the resulting state, build an arb and submit it quickly enough to get in the same 100ms block - so it’s a latency game based around the sequencer feed + submission 

Two teams working on low latency infra @ordofi and @BlockRazor_Inc to check out

text:
猴价，已经快涨回历史高点了。

这是因为 AI 制药把临床前产能吃紧了。今天聊一个很有意思的框架：AI 药物发现正在变成一门"瓶颈交易"。

逻辑很像当年半导体那波：GPU→HBM→网络→电力/散热，一路往下游押注瓶颈。在生物这边，链条是：AI 模型→分子设计→DNA/蛋白合成→检测→临床前产能。

为什么 AI 反而让湿实验更忙了？三个机制：

第一，假设生成几乎免费了，"射门次数"暴增，瓶颈从专家设计转向了生物学验证。

第二，坏数据也有用。Anthropic 让 Claude 设计了 1320 个蛋白 binder，实测只有 354 个结合，剩下 966 个失败品全是宝贵的负样本，用来训练下一代模型。传统只测"最有信心的那几个"，AI 连 B/C 级候选都要测，因为失败也是训练数据。

第三，湿实验室正在变成"生物数据代工厂"。TWST 预计 AI 相关订单连续两年三位数增长；GenScript 的 AIDD 业务半年翻倍，每天验证的设计从 4000 向 16000 冲。客户有时候要的不是蛋白本身，而是结构化的实验结果回流模型。

这笔交易能走多远？不到 2028 年后的 Phase II 读数，很难证伪，腿可能很长。但最大的风险也在这：如果 AI 药物在发现阶段漂亮、II/III 期按正常失败率扑街，整个逻辑就塌了。

所以盯紧两个东西：猴价（临床前产能的晴雨表）和 2028 年后的 Phase II 数据。前者告诉你瓶颈有多紧，后者告诉你这瓶颈值不值得押。

---关注投资标地：

文章直接点名的：

$TWST（Twist Bioscience）：硅基 DNA 合成。观察点：FY26/FY27 的 AI 相关订单是不是真能连续三位数增长
GenScript（金斯瑞 https://t.co/uVH81WDHvG）：AIDD 业务半年翻倍。观察点：每天验证设计数 8000→16000 的爬坡兑现度
$ILMN（Illumina）：测序龙头，AI 产生的数据越多、测序需求越大
$TXG（10x Genomics）：单细胞/空间组学，验证环节的工具
顺着链条补上的：

蛋白生产：Bio-Techne（$TECH）、百普赛斯（https://t.co/e2GGd80c2x）
实验室自动化（"卖铲子的铲子"）：Tecan、Danaher（DHR）、ThermoFisher（DHR）、ThermoFisher（TMO）、Agilent（$A）
CRO/临床前：药明康德（https://t.co/8gRwSuivAp）、Charles River（$CRL）
猴价最直接相关：**CRL∗∗——实验猴（NHP）主要供应商之一，猴价涨、产能紧直接体现在它身上；Inotiv（CRL∗∗——实验猴（NHP）主要供应商之一，猴价涨、产能紧直接体现在它身上；Inotiv（NOTV）更小、弹性更大

text:
这条推文把几件不同的事揉在了一起，逐条说：

解锁。 传统VC从投资到退出要7到10年，IPO后还有半年左右锁定期。Crypto投后一两年TGE，加上1+3也就3到5年，其实更快。真正的问题不是锁得久，而是退出顺序不对称：空投、做市商、交易所份额先流通，VC最后解锁。但解法应该是所有内部人对称锁定、做市条款透明，而不是废除1+3让VC也先跑。何况1+3本来就是当年VC上线即砸盘换来的，高FDV也是VC自己一轮轮抬出来的。

营收和回购。 在风险投资阶段要求项目有营收、做回购，不符合风投的逻辑，真正能做出东西的团队早期本来就不赚钱。成长期回购也是错误的资本配置，美股的回购来自成熟期现金牛，不是成长股。既要早期的低价筹码，又要公开市场的流动性，还要成熟公司的股东回报，这是既要又要。根源在于crypto项目在种子轮的成熟度就"上市"了。

供给和叙事。 行业并不是没跑出有价值的项目。稳定币、Hyperliquid、Uniswap、Aave、Polymarket都有真实现金流，只是大多数VC没投到，其中最成功的几个甚至没走传统VC路径。VC的钱大量压在没有需求的基础设施和同质化公链上，"数以万计的项目"正是这样批量投出来的。
author: 0xDrPR
quoted_text: 加密一级市场为什么快死了，我们曾作为最活跃的投资机构之一，这十年感受最明显问题，第一个是叙事破灭了，从白皮书到机构背书到TVL刷量，基本市场不再买单。第二个是供给失衡，现在出现数以万计项目，优秀项目跑出来难度极大。第三个是1➕3解锁机制，基本是定向杀死VC，让项目，MM和交易所先跑，第四是上币成本，现在一级项目为什么需要高估值和大融资，主要是几个龙头交易所上线，平均成本需要千万美金。虽然VC问题也很多，但没有大量VC支持一级市场，市场只剩下专业发币集团和MEME币活跃。一级市场是加密创新的重要来源，需要行业龙头真正的去buliding方向，比如币安上币筛选方式改进，按照现在模式，当年V神的ETH来了也上不了币安。其次是彻底废除1➕3解锁机制，VC承担了最大风险，应该不背负最差的解锁条款，项目成功或失败根本不是VC决定的。最后是加密项目需要回到真正的营收和回购，美股那么多年持续繁荣，最重要的是业绩增长和督促回馈股东利益，这才是行业龙头们应该做的事情，让市场二级投资者真正找到优质项目。

I asked Opus 5.5 to write, produce, and create me an educational 'cartoon' about The History of Light - using whatever resources it had available to it.

I didn't expect it to make a 36 minute video and spend $200+ dollars though 😂  

The study of light is genuinely fascinating, and we have spent thousands of years trying to understand it.  This is that story.

Opus 5.5 wrote and produced the entire film.  I told it to use any keys in my keychain to generate the voices, create any images or video it might need, and to create whatever motion graphics it could to explain concepts in electromagnetism.

It used 
> Gemini 3.8 Flash TTS for the narration, and I must say, it did an excellent job.
> Lyrica 3 for the background music, which is also essentially perfect.
> GPT Image 2.5, Nano Banana Pro and NB2 Flash for some of the scenes imagery 

It's certainly not perfect but I was still really impressed with how well it did producing the film. It's very interesting if you're a physics nerd like me. 

Opus is genuinely creative in a way that I've not really seen with other models. I just gave the model a few constraints and just let it make all the decisions end to end.

It even wrote itself credits at the end lol.

It's going to be so fun to create bespoke educational videos like this for my children to learn from

text:
《纽约时报》记者近日走进赵长鹏（CZ）在阿布扎比的生活，看到的不只有币安、王室和特朗普家族，还有漏水的天花板、没人会弹的施坦威以及一句“这只是一场游戏。”

结合这篇专访与他近期的公开回应，有这些值得看的细节：

1. 身价上千亿美元，他自己报的数低得多

报道将 CZ 的身价估为约 1140 亿美元。他在采访中却说，自己的财富大约在 100 亿至 300 亿美元之间，只需要 1000 万美元就能过得很舒服。

今年 3 月，他已经否认过福布斯的千亿美元估算，回应是：“不准。也不重要。”

2. 开日产接记者，笑称“我的兰博基尼”

他主动提出带记者游览阿布扎比，开来的是一辆白色日产 SUV，手机固定在挡风玻璃上。

记者把这一幕形容为“全世界最有钱的 Uber 司机”。CZ 则在对方上车时开玩笑：“我的兰博基尼。”

3. 别墅漏水一直没修，家里有四名保镖

这栋价值 500 万美元的别墅有九间卧室，家里配有四名保镖和一位厨师，他还有一艘名叫 Da Moon 的游艇。

不过，他经常在采访中提起楼上始终没修好的漏水点。这次也专门指给记者看，问对方能不能看出天花板颜色的差别。

聊到房价，他又告诉记者，附近有一栋房子挂牌售价为 1.5 亿美元。

4. 买了施坦威，但自己不会弹

孩子们的游戏室里摆着一架奶油色施坦威钢琴，周围散落着玩具。

调音师看到钢琴疏于照料，很痛心。CZ 的介绍很直接：“挺贵的那种”，但“我不会弹”。

5. 记者不能收超过 20 美元的礼物，他说外套“大概 19 美元”

他家入口处堆着一箱箱币安周边，催记者挑一件带走，背包、黄黑配色外套都可以。

记者解释，职业规定不允许接受价值超过 20 美元的礼物。

他举着衣服笑着说：“大概是 19 美元。”

6. 长期背痛让他躺着办公，看到导弹后继续工作

报道中的一张照片，是他仰躺在床上，对着架在身体上方的笔记本电脑打字。

今年年初，窗户突然震动。他走到阳台，看见天空中有一道烟迹。当时伊朗向阿联酋发射了导弹。

他随后回到床上继续工作，并向记者解释，自己认为当地防护很到位。

7. 家里的两只狗，一只来自总统，一只取名灵感来自blockchain

一只是吉尔吉斯斯坦总统送的泰甘猎犬。

CZ 说，对方原本想送他一顶很大的帐篷。他没要，后来总统坚持送了这只狗。今年 2 月，两人还一起滑过雪。另一只就是 Broccoli。

8. 卢浮宫闭馆后的私人导览，也没打动他

他曾在卢浮宫闭馆后接受私人导览。

但在回忆录里，他承认自己并不懂欣赏，把导游为他讲解形容为“对牛弹琴”。

记者观察到，他礼貌、专注，前臂上有币安文身，兴趣却非常集中。

9. 卖房买比特币时，他给自己留的退路是重新找工作

2013 年，他在上海的一场牌局上第一次认真接触比特币。

研究几个月后，他卖掉了上海的三居室公寓，把所得的 90 万美元全部投入比特币。那是他与妻子抚养两个孩子的家。

他当时并不太担心：即便比特币暴跌，自己也能回传统金融行业找一份高薪工作。

10. 入籍的起点，是王室晚餐上的一句询问

2022 年年底或 2023 年年初，一位阿联酋王室成员在晚餐时问他，是否想入籍。

他提交材料后，过了几个月，一名政府使者来到家里，带来一个装着他和家人护照的盒子。

当时美国对币安的调查正在收紧。报道提到，阿联酋与美国没有引渡条约；CZ 则认为，获得当地国籍进一步增加了自己的保障。

11. 他坐在听众席，阿联酋领导人俯身问他需要什么帮助

一次非公开会议上，瑞·达利欧、孙正义等人都在场。

CZ 坐在听众席时，阿联酋领导人谢赫穆罕默德来到身边，俯身询问他近况，以及有没有什么能帮忙的。

他向记者描述这一幕时，仍很惊讶：“就这样跪在你旁边。”

他还经常参加王室晚宴，把那些对科技和加密感兴趣的领导人称为“加密酋长”。

12. 入狱前，他专门找顾问学习如何与囚犯相处

他组建了一支顾问团队，了解监狱里的人际关系。顾问还提前联系其他囚犯，请他们帮助他适应。

入狱后，他加入了一个按族裔形成的非正式社交团体，与其他亚裔囚犯一起吃饭、锻炼。

一名同监囚犯说，大家见到他会让路，“就像国王走过过道一样”。

13. 原本想收比特币，20 亿美元投资最终用 USD1 结算

2025 年，阿联酋基金 MGX 向币安投资 20 亿美元。据报道，这笔交易给币安的估值为 750 亿美元。

CZ 说，自己希望用比特币结算，阿联酋方面却担心价格波动，更倾向稳定币。

最终使用的是特朗普家族加密公司 World Liberty Financial 发行的 USD1。MGX 称，这是基于商业适用性作出的选择。

《华尔街日报》曾报道称，币安要求使用 USD1；CZ 则说，决定来自 MGX。

14. 除了加密，他还投资人工子宫研究

在一次晚宴上，他听奥特曼介绍一个生物技术研究方向，并将其概括为：未来或许一个人就能生孩子。

报道提到，他自己也投资了一家研究人工子宫的初创公司。

15. 经历这一切后，他相信人生可能是一场模拟游戏

在他的回忆录中，用了约一页半讨论“模拟理论”。

他认为，人类可能生活在别人构想的现实里；再过二十年，也许能像《黑客帝国》那样进入模拟世界。

他把人比作某个版本的超级马里奥，在人造世界里跑来跑去，并试着用一句话面对生活：

“这只是一场游戏。”

text:
The PhD thesis of my 15th PhD student, Shibhansh Dohare (@ShibhanshD), is now available.

Title: Learning Forever using Artificial Neural Networks
Url: https://t.co/Zp2GxZ03aw

Abstract:
In this dissertation, I study the ability of artificial neural networks to learn new things. I refer to this ability as plasticity. Plasticity is a desirable property of intelligent systems in the real world. Systems that interact with the real world can become outdated if they do not learn from the new information revealed to them by the extremely large and partially observable real world. All naturally intelligent systems continually learn new things to keep up with the changes in the world. Many applications like predicting markets or weather, learning human preferences, controlling factories or prosthetics, etc require AI systems that continually learn new things. 
I provide direct and thorough demonstrations of loss of plasticity in deep learning systems. The demonstrations range from simple feed-forward networks to deep residual networks and cover a wide range of algorithmic choices. While seeking an understanding of the phenomenon, I found that loss of plasticity occurred simultaneously with hidden units becoming dormant and becoming similar to each other, hampering the ability of the networks to learn new things. 
Next, I describe the continual backpropagation algorithm. I designed this algorithm, in collaboration with others, to maintain plasticity in artificial neural networks. Continual backpropagation is a simple extension of the conventional backpropagation algorithm. The conventional backpropagation has two main parts: initialization with small random weights and gradient descent at each step. In addition to gradient descent, continual backpropagation reinitializes a small fraction of units at each step. Continual backpropagation indefinitely maintained plasticity in many continual supervised learning problems.
Finally, I study plasticity of deep reinforcement learning systems. First, I show that plasticity loss has an effect even in stationary reinforcement learning problems. It is unsurprising that plasticity loss affects stationary reinforcement learning because it requires continual learning due to changing policies and bootstrapping. This effect is visible under long-term learning. I found that some commonly used RL algorithms do not scale with data. Their performance drops as they continue interacting with the environment. Plasticity loss hampers the ability of these algorithms to recover and relearn when the performance drops, resulting in agents that do not get better with experience. Continual backpropagation allows these algorithms to recover when performance drops, leading to agents whose performance keeps improving with experience. Second, I show that loss of plasticity is a significant problem in continual reinforcement learning problems, and continual backpropagation maintains plasticity in these problems.

Shibhansh is now a research scientist at Keen Technologies.

What i'm doing with my coins brain dump i didn't proof read

- A couple thoughts as to how I’ve traded this cycle so far

First and foremost alts and onchain are behaving very similar on the way up. Coins go into a lockout up trend, the entire timeline flips tubro bullish. This lasts until price cools off. eventually we rotate. Attention gets vamped onto the next. The strongest coins, however, always get the rotation back. So far it’s been Hype, Zec, Lit, Pump, near… ? The obvious takeaway is there is edge in being able to sit on a coin longer than a few days. Look at what happened with pump. 2x off the bottom in a straight line, nobody owned it, and after a few weeks of underperformance it was like people forgot the coin existed? Picked their own vamp to outperform (stonk, long, pons), then pump gets back into lockout trend.

The difference between the chosen alts and “onchain” is the flows keep coming back to the good alts. I stand by the idea that it is hard to justify anything onchain in the 300-500+ range because these alts have so much fucking juice in them. I don’t think Zec $5k+ Hype $250+ VVV $100+ Pump $.2 this year is that ridiculous. It means I have to either trade low caps into the 20-50 range or fully focus on spot alts (mentioned below) and leverage trading breakouts to stack more spot alts.

The obvious takeaway here is In order to catch the real moves these alts are capable of the only way to get there is by holding spot. Price action is schizo, partly bc everyone is trading high leverage only. It leads to nasty washouts and stops being run. 5-10xs are going to require being able to sit through chop. Look at how bitcoin has traded, lockout move 5-10% higher followed by seven days of nothing, which is legitimately grueling to leverage longs. Everyone gets wiped out. The timeline goes to war. Then we leg up again. I don’t see why this would stop. In hindsight the obvious way to play it was sitting in spot which goes against what I have been doing (and getting paid for).

——

A valid concern is what will happen with stocks/bonds/war/oil/ant ipo/etc. The honest truth is I don’t think it matters. The fear was always “if crypto is trading this bad while stocks trade this good what happens when it flips.” There have been moments of stock misery (despite things looking pretty great all things considered rn) and crypto broke that correlation. I think bitcoin continues to exist as a great alternative to the ai trade and the good alts mentioned above can standalone as quality, cheap, assets that exist separately to crypto performance as a whole. 

Every second I have spent thinking above these fears and reading market commentary has been a mistake.

I think in order to get paid as generationally as I would like over the coming months it Is imperative to read as few market opinions as possible. It feels like my feed has been overwhelmed by a storm of slop from people not making money. I can’t not get shaken out by trash. I stream for three hours a day, everyday, whatever I cover and learn during those sessions is beyond enough information to make clear decisions at the level that I need to.

——

I think ultimately it comes down to what do I think will happen over the next 6-12 months. Thinking this far in advance is the only way to break away from the cesspool of flip flopping biases every hour on the timeline. And what I think it we have the best setup I’ve seen since joining crypto for outright mania. 

Sec + CFTC are running GAME to push crypto. Btc ETF buyers are green again. Tokens are investible. Crypto is “cool” on socials to the younger generation. Social trading apps have reached escape velocity. Perps matter. Robinhood going all in, etc etc etc. I don’t need to pill anyone on the bull case. I love the spot.

The only way to make it that far is to hold the best coins on spot. This is shockingly difficult for me to do right now after having a great year trading perps. But I have to understand that the majority of that was during a bear market where there’s one or two impulse moves if lucky. Not a continuous uptrend with infinite marginal buyers higher and nothing but catalysts and air above like I think we have right now. It’s going to take some rewiring of my brain to make it where I think we can get to and keep exposure.

My final thought is when I think back on the traders of last cycle that outperformed the hardest what sticks out was their ability to denominate all profits into the winning coin. In 2024 it was sol. Stack sol -> sell to buy onchain coins -> take profits -> buy more sol. Rinse and repeat continuous big wins while sol legs up from $8->$270. Congrats on making it. I have been mentally taking a similar approach the last couple months but didn’t execute it as well as I wish I had. First it was pump. Most recently it was zec. Great PNLs on both but I wasted so much mental energy stressed over short term pa for no particular reason. (Buy some spot retard)

I sold, all of my zcash, because I felt extremely bloated in leverage and wanted to reset after playing the first round of the cycle pretty well imo. Moving forward I still believe that coin is zec and maybe a basket of a few others, Pump/Hype/vvv? And will probably be trading accordingly. Stack a ton of spot. Keep a non insignificant amount to leverage trade tighter spots, stack my golden goose coin

And pray we make it. good luck to us

quoted_text:
Important advice: deliberately rethink every previous concept of how things should be done.

Some thoughts, tips, and realizations:

1. Specializations are collapsing. Come to terms with and take advantage of this reality. The person who used to be an engineer is now also a data scientist, a content creator, designer, marketer, and whatever else they want to be. Deliberately expand in as many directions as you can and become great at them (scope up vs just speeding up)

2. The average person with access to tokens can now do the work of a data scientist who used to cost $500,000 a year. Seriously, this is fucking crazy. This opens up an entirely new world. Take advantage of it (also everyone else will also realize this over time).

3. 99% of what's created is now slop. Be aggressively anti-slop and you will absolutely stand out.

4. Trying is nearly free. Automating is nearly free. My mind still sometimes lives in the world from 12 months ago where an idea automatically is attached to a certain amount of time or effort. Both of these have collapsed to close to zero (or just token cost), I therefore try and experiment with *any and all* ideas with potential and have needed to retrain my brain for this constantly.

5. Tokens are a career and growth accelerant. Find ways to get cheap access to tokens, or free tokens. Extremely important, and actually an entire design space, use your imagination.

6. It's never been easier to both stand out but also fall behind. 10x, 100x "people" exist more than ever (maybe 1,000x). Outlier power users of AI, many who you see here on X. Feels like we are in a window of time, a window of opportunity while all of this is still early, to take advantage of it. 

7. Local computing is (or will be) dead for 99% of work. Local was built for a world where work was bounded by the physical presence of its author, but this is no longer true. You can and should do infinite work in parallel or zero, it doesn't matter anymore. Cloud agents enable this at scale and in any computing environment, I predict cloud agent usage will 1000x over the next 12 months and optionality and accessibility will 100x. Plan for this world, take advantage of the possibilities.

8. Building on #7, you can give an agent it's own computer, and it's own identity. You can then give an agent with it's own computer it's own computer. You can give that agent with it's own computer with it's own computer, *it's* own computer. These agents are smarter than any human in history and you have access to as many as you'd like. Think about this for a moment.

After 14 years in this industry (tech) today is the most exciting time ever and nothing else feels even close.

quoted_text:
《纽约时报》记者近日走进赵长鹏（CZ）在阿布扎比的生活，看到的不只有币安、王室和特朗普家族，还有漏水的天花板、没人会弹的施坦威以及一句“这只是一场游戏。”

结合这篇专访与他近期的公开回应，有这些值得看的细节：

1. 身价上千亿美元，他自己报的数低得多

报道将 CZ 的身价估为约 1140 亿美元。他在采访中却说，自己的财富大约在 100 亿至 300 亿美元之间，只需要 1000 万美元就能过得很舒服。

今年 3 月，他已经否认过福布斯的千亿美元估算，回应是：“不准。也不重要。”

2. 开日产接记者，笑称“我的兰博基尼”

他主动提出带记者游览阿布扎比，开来的是一辆白色日产 SUV，手机固定在挡风玻璃上。

记者把这一幕形容为“全世界最有钱的 Uber 司机”。CZ 则在对方上车时开玩笑：“我的兰博基尼。”

3. 别墅漏水一直没修，家里有四名保镖

这栋价值 500 万美元的别墅有九间卧室，家里配有四名保镖和一位厨师，他还有一艘名叫 Da Moon 的游艇。

不过，他经常在采访中提起楼上始终没修好的漏水点。这次也专门指给记者看，问对方能不能看出天花板颜色的差别。

聊到房价，他又告诉记者，附近有一栋房子挂牌售价为 1.5 亿美元。

4. 买了施坦威，但自己不会弹

孩子们的游戏室里摆着一架奶油色施坦威钢琴，周围散落着玩具。

调音师看到钢琴疏于照料，很痛心。CZ 的介绍很直接：“挺贵的那种”，但“我不会弹”。

5. 记者不能收超过 20 美元的礼物，他说外套“大概 19 美元”

他家入口处堆着一箱箱币安周边，催记者挑一件带走，背包、黄黑配色外套都可以。

记者解释，职业规定不允许接受价值超过 20 美元的礼物。

他举着衣服笑着说：“大概是 19 美元。”

6. 长期背痛让他躺着办公，看到导弹后继续工作

报道中的一张照片，是他仰躺在床上，对着架在身体上方的笔记本电脑打字。

今年年初，窗户突然震动。他走到阳台，看见天空中有一道烟迹。当时伊朗向阿联酋发射了导弹。

他随后回到床上继续工作，并向记者解释，自己认为当地防护很到位。

7. 家里的两只狗，一只来自总统，一只取名灵感来自blockchain

一只是吉尔吉斯斯坦总统送的泰甘猎犬。

CZ 说，对方原本想送他一顶很大的帐篷。他没要，后来总统坚持送了这只狗。今年 2 月，两人还一起滑过雪。另一只就是 Broccoli。

8. 卢浮宫闭馆后的私人导览，也没打动他

他曾在卢浮宫闭馆后接受私人导览。

但在回忆录里，他承认自己并不懂欣赏，把导游为他讲解形容为“对牛弹琴”。

记者观察到，他礼貌、专注，前臂上有币安文身，兴趣却非常集中。

9. 卖房买比特币时，他给自己留的退路是重新找工作

2013 年，他在上海的一场牌局上第一次认真接触比特币。

研究几个月后，他卖掉了上海的三居室公寓，把所得的 90 万美元全部投入比特币。那是他与妻子抚养两个孩子的家。

他当时并不太担心：即便比特币暴跌，自己也能回传统金融行业找一份高薪工作。

10. 入籍的起点，是王室晚餐上的一句询问

2022 年年底或 2023 年年初，一位阿联酋王室成员在晚餐时问他，是否想入籍。

他提交材料后，过了几个月，一名政府使者来到家里，带来一个装着他和家人护照的盒子。

当时美国对币安的调查正在收紧。报道提到，阿联酋与美国没有引渡条约；CZ 则认为，获得当地国籍进一步增加了自己的保障。

11. 他坐在听众席，阿联酋领导人俯身问他需要什么帮助

一次非公开会议上，瑞·达利欧、孙正义等人都在场。

CZ 坐在听众席时，阿联酋领导人谢赫穆罕默德来到身边，俯身询问他近况，以及有没有什么能帮忙的。

他向记者描述这一幕时，仍很惊讶：“就这样跪在你旁边。”

他还经常参加王室晚宴，把那些对科技和加密感兴趣的领导人称为“加密酋长”。

12. 入狱前，他专门找顾问学习如何与囚犯相处

他组建了一支顾问团队，了解监狱里的人际关系。顾问还提前联系其他囚犯，请他们帮助他适应。

入狱后，他加入了一个按族裔形成的非正式社交团体，与其他亚裔囚犯一起吃饭、锻炼。

一名同监囚犯说，大家见到他会让路，“就像国王走过过道一样”。

13. 原本想收比特币，20 亿美元投资最终用 USD1 结算

2025 年，阿联酋基金 MGX 向币安投资 20 亿美元。据报道，这笔交易给币安的估值为 750 亿美元。

CZ 说，自己希望用比特币结算，阿联酋方面却担心价格波动，更倾向稳定币。

最终使用的是特朗普家族加密公司 World Liberty Financial 发行的 USD1。MGX 称，这是基于商业适用性作出的选择。

《华尔街日报》曾报道称，币安要求使用 USD1；CZ 则说，决定来自 MGX。

14. 除了加密，他还投资人工子宫研究

在一次晚宴上，他听奥特曼介绍一个生物技术研究方向，并将其概括为：未来或许一个人就能生孩子。

报道提到，他自己也投资了一家研究人工子宫的初创公司。

15. 经历这一切后，他相信人生可能是一场模拟游戏

在他的回忆录中，用了约一页半讨论“模拟理论”。

他认为，人类可能生活在别人构想的现实里；再过二十年，也许能像《黑客帝国》那样进入模拟世界。

他把人比作某个版本的超级马里奥，在人造世界里跑来跑去，并试着用一句话面对生活：

“这只是一场游戏。”

美国一家明星 AI 公司要发开源模型了。
它对标的是 DeepSeek 和 Qwen。

这两个都是中国的。

这家公司叫 Reflection AI，创始人是从 DeepMind 出来的，做过 AlphaGo 和 Gemini。
去年融了 20 亿美元，领投的是英伟达。

我觉得这事最值得琢磨的是英伟达。

闭源模型越强，算力就越集中在少数几家大厂手里。
而这几家大客户，Google 有自己的 TPU，OpenAI 也在找别家一起做芯片。

开源模型越强，每家公司、每个国家都想自己部署一套。
自己部署，就得自己买卡。

卖铲子的人，当然希望满大街都有人自己挖矿。

还有一层。
过去一年，开源这块基本被中国模型占了，不少美国创业公司底层跑的就是 Qwen。
企业和政府用得越多，“有没有一个美国的开源模型可以用”这个问题就越绕不开。
我觉得 Reflection 能拿到这么多钱，国籍这张牌占了不小的分量。

边界也得说清楚：
Axios 只说了要发，什么时候发、模型多大、跑分多少，都还没有。
对标只代表目标，能不能打得过，得看东西发出来。
DeepSeek 和 Qwen 迭代太快了，等它发布的时候，对标对象可能都已经换代了。

以后中美 AI 竞争，比的可能是谁家开源更大方。
挺好，我们这些白嫖党先赢麻了。

text:
今天正式给最近一个月的 Agents Trading 实验画上句号！

以下是具体原因以及论证为何现有大语言模型无法用于交易决策的核心原因：

由于目前所有 LLM 输出的都是基于概率条件下的文本，除非你限制它只能回答“是”或“不是”这样的选项类答案，否则只要输入的文本量较大，输出必然具有随机性。

而如果你通过重重限制约束了大模型的输出，将其作为决策，你就会发现限制越多，Agents 的交易决策越趋向于一个纯算法策略。

简单说来，限制越少，决策随机性越高，越难以回测，实盘的未知风险也就越高。

限制越多，决策随机性越低，虽然方便回测了，但最终 AI 参与的决策权重也越来越少，最后约等于一个量化策略系统，AI 几乎没有参与感...

而考虑到实盘交易时，最不可接受的往往是决策流程完全黑箱化，当多个 Agents 调用同一个大模型，进行同样条件的交易时，会给出完全不同的多个决策，这就导致了系统的收益预期完全不受控制...

因此可以证明，大模型对于重要的交易决策环节完全不具备可靠性，任何依靠 AI 进行交易决策的系统本质上都等同于将资金交给了一个随机系统。

虽然我做过的众多实验中，回测结果盈利的并不少，但问题是过程无法复刻，即使将模型温度设为0，依旧会产生不同的结果，早期的几笔交易在轻微的随机扰动下，就会产生类似蝴蝶效应一般的长期影响...

因此从量化角度来说，AI 在系统的中的位置必须下放：

我的观点是，固定算法策略 + AI 优化才是最稳妥的方案，决策权彻底与 AI 隔离，但 AI 可以提供大量底层数据的处理和收集、因子搜寻自动化以及外部新闻理解等等。

总之，纯 Agents 交易实验就到此为止了，也算帮各位踩了一个坑，对我来说是一场宝贵的学习经验！不亏！
author: CryptoPainter
quoted_text:
汇总一下最近使用各家大模型跑 Agents 投票决策进行交易的表现：

1. Astra 整体可以小幅盈利，Low 级别至 xHigh 表现没有明显差异，整体上更喜欢直接满仓做，然后亏一点就直接平仓，后期震荡行情里回撤巨大...

2. GPT 6 Luna High 速度快很多，但莫名其妙的喜欢反复加减仓，开了单之后不论涨跌都在减仓，3次实验中有2次都是亏损，只有一次小幅盈利...

3. Gemini 3.8 flash 速度是最快的，决策质量与表现远比 Luna High 要好，5次实验里只有一次亏钱，但剩余四次都是前期稳赚，后期逐步回撤大部分收益，交易风格看起来最像专业交易员...

4. Opus 5.5 和 Astra 表现差不多，前沿大模型的自信程度确实要高很多，经常满仓干进去，下根K线就斩仓...

总体来说，都不太行，即使我给投票机制加了论据主导和辩论环节，防止一个 Agent 带偏其他 Agents 的现象，但就结果而言，这些大模型面对市场的决策能力与普通人类中的裸K交易者相比，没有明显优势，甚至还略逊一筹...

因此很明显，无算法、无策略条件下，AI 的交易决策能力时至今日依旧是一个字“猜”...

接下来我会开始测试在部分固定算法策略框架下的决策能力，也就是给定一些简单的交易策略，让 Agents 在有效框架内做决策，他们可以决定一个交易信号开多少以及是否空仓拒绝或提前平仓，但没有权限反向交易。

我个人认为这种实验还是很有趣的，他帮我认清了 AI 大模型的能力边界，未来反而可以更好的使用 AI ！

以一个工具的身份，而不是智能体...

text:
Random thoughts: @NotionHQ will be the best at executing the whole multiplayer humans + agents thing

- most people struggle with “personal” agents because most consumers don’t care about *doing* things, most things for people *to do* are at work
- the best use case for agents by far is knowledge work, exponentially true for multiplayer and interacting with coworkers, customers, etc
- Notion is useful both singleplayer and multiplayer which is important
- all of the things that matter for multiplayer, Notion already has built out: permissions, security, cloud, sharing, etc. It natively has network effects 
- Notion is neutral: you can use any model, any agent harness (Claude code etc) or even bring your OAI subscription 
- most people dont want to interact with another person’s “agent”, they want to interact with the *output* (docs, apps, etc) and use their agent to consume it — all intrinsically native to Notion
- there is no more important layer for multiplayer to own than context and memory, that is quite literally company docs/workspaces
- I think the grok bots interface makes the most sense for knowledge work and that’s already custom agents. Notion has all of the primitives for agents to do the work and has all the abstractions (agents) for teams/people to consume and interact with the work at whatever level they choose

I think the most important thing for them to nail down in the near/medium term is the overlap between personal systems and work systems (auth, enterprise procurement, integrations, etc) but that is largely a product/UX challenge which I feel that Notion is S-tier at. In other words the bridge between consumer <> prosumer <> work/teams

The current product gaps with its agents that instinct/muse have (computer/browser use, persistent state, isolated VMs/sandboxes, proactive, etc) are deterministic and the Notion AI team will either ship them in like a week or it’s already in beta

I also feel like if Notion can somehow nail team comms or build a layer on top of existing comms platforms (email, slack, teams, etc) it’s game over

*not affiliated btw, they are just currently the furthest ahead IMO and my usage is somehow increasing every day

text:
9 岁的时候，我和他都是全国冠军。如今他已经走上奥运会的领奖台，我们是怎么拉开差距的？

这次放假专门去找到我曾经的队友，把我们俩的运动生涯从头复盘了一遍。复盘完我最大的感受是，差距最早其实不是在训练馆里拉开的。

我们队历史上进国家队最年轻的，都在 19 岁往上。他的队伍政策不一样，十四五岁就把他送了上去。同样是练，从那一刻起，我们就在两个平台上努力了。

我觉得这是第一层：你在哪里努力，真的很重要。

而进了国家队，也只是拿到一张门票。能不能站稳，还要看很多自己说了不算的东西。教练除了训练，愿不愿意在精神上、资源上托你一把；省里想不想推这个项目，领导愿不愿意为你站台；受伤了，有没有足够好的医疗资源；低谷的时候，还有没有人愿意继续给你机会。

他说，一件事如果 10 个人做能成，那 9 个人做、1 个人在旁边看着，这事就成不了。

当然这些都有个前提，你自己得足够强。大家都很强的时候，才轮得到比这些。

所以我现在的理解是，努力是必要条件，但不是充分条件。一个人的努力，改变不了一个省的政策和利益；但没有努力，后面那些东西就算都有，也送不了你上世界最高的舞台。

他有句话我一直记着：

首先你自己得行，然后得别人觉得你行，最后是说你行的人得行。

回头看我这些年在币圈，基本是一个人单打独斗。这次回来，我开始认真琢磨后面两条了。

我还问他，怎么这么年轻就做到现在的位置。他说，在有这个职位之前，他其实就已经具备了这个职位的能力。

这句话对我启发挺大的。想做有影响力的人，就先把影响力做出来；想做基金，就先具备管钱的能力。能力真的到了，头衔你不去追，也会有人请你去。

最后我们聊了很久一个问题：论奥运成绩，他比不过那些拿了好几块金牌的人，但影响力却比他们很多人都大。为什么？

我们的结论是，天花板在赛场外。怎么跟人打交道，能不能把复杂的事协调好，做事靠不靠谱，甚至能不能给人靠谱的感觉，对不懂的东西够不够开放。不是冠军拿得越多就越厉害。

一个人能掌握的，大概就这些：把自己练强，选个好平台，在好平台上继续努力，让更多人愿意看到你成功，然后进到更好的平台，再来一轮。

剩下的，交给运气。

text:
Thank You for Joining Us at EastPoint:Seoul 2026

September 28, Westin Seoul Parnas

On Monday, 627 people came through the doors at the Westin Seoul Parnas, each there by invitation or approved application.

Central banks, regulators, legislators, traditional financial institutions, Korean enterprises, global protocols, infrastructure companies, investors, and builders spent the day in the same building, listening to each other and taking questions from the room.

That was the point of EastPoint.

Why EastPoint Exists

Korea did not arrive here with an obvious advantage. It built capital, technical depth, and consumer technology adoption over decades.

What has been harder to build is a single table where the people responsible for policy, institutions, enterprise, and technology can sit together long enough to test their assumptions.

Policy has often moved in one direction, institutions in another, and builders in a third. Each side has had its own constraints, its own language, and its own reasons to believe the others were not ready yet.

EastPoint was created to make that distance smaller.

It is not only a tech conference, and it is not only a finance conference. It is a room where finance, technology, policy, and enterprise are asked to meet each other seriously enough to disagree, clarify, and move the conversation forward.

A Room Built for Decision-Makers

EastPoint was intentionally narrow, but not small.

The day brought together 627 checked-in attendees from 385 companies and institutions, alongside 112 speakers, 22 sessions, and 40 roundtables across 4 public and 36 private discussions.

Among profiled attendees, 62% were senior decision-makers: 156 C-level leaders, founders, and CEOs, together with 231 executives, division heads, and directors.

That composition mattered. The goal was not simply to gather a large audience. It was to bring together people with the authority to allocate capital, set policy, manage risk, build infrastructure, and reach users, and to place them in the same working conversation.

The mix reflected that intent: AI and digital asset companies, traditional financial institutions, asset managers, conglomerates, fintech companies, PE and VC firms, government and regulators, academia, and media. Banks, securities firms, asset managers, custodians, exchanges, payment companies, public institutions, and global protocols were not adjacent to the conversation. They were inside it.

Institutions, Enterprises, and Builders in One Room

Who stood on stage is the clearest expression of what EastPoint is trying to become.

Central banks, regulators, and legislators joined the conversation not as distant observers, but as participants: the Bank of Korea’s Office of Digital Currency, the White House Crypto Council, Abu Dhabi Global Market’s regulatory authority, DAXA, four sitting members of the National Assembly, and the Majority Leader of the Utah State Senate.

Traditional finance showed up with institutional weight: Franklin Templeton, Mirae Asset Global Investments, KB Asset Management, Hanwha Asset Management, Korea Investment Management, NH-Amundi, Meritz Securities, and Eugene Investment & Securities.

Korean enterprise brought a question that matters beyond financial markets: how any of this reaches ordinary users. Kakao Pay, LG Electronics, LG CNS, SM Entertainment, and many others helped widen the frame beyond infrastructure alone.

And the builders who have spent years constructing the rails were there as well: @a16zcrypto, @hashed_official , @tether , @circle , @chainlink , @LayerZero_Core , @Anchorage, @BitGo , @FalconXGlobal , @Ondo, @Avax , and many others.

Many of these conversations continued beyond the stage, in roundtables where the more difficult and less polished questions had room to breathe.

What We Heard

The distance between institutions and builders felt shorter than many expected.

Institutions were not asking whether digital assets are real. They were asking who holds the keys, who carries the liability, what settlement finality means in practice, and what standards they can responsibly rely on.

Builders were not asking simply for permission. They were asking what rules are worth building toward, and what kind of infrastructure would still make sense when the market becomes more institutional, more regulated, and more widely used.

Those are not separate conversations. They are the same question approached from different responsibilities.

Getting that question asked out loud, in front of the people who can actually move it forward, may be the most useful thing one day can produce.

Thank You

Above all, thank you to the 627 people who came.

You gave up a Monday and stayed through sessions that did not always offer comfortable answers. You carried the discussion into the roundtables, the hallways, the 1:1 meetings, and the conversations that continued long after the panels closed.

Across the day, attendees exchanged opinions and built partnerships through over 90 business meetings matched. Those numbers matter because they point to something more important: people did not just attend EastPoint. They used it.

The quality of EastPoint came from the questions you were willing to ask in public, and from the seriousness with which you listened to answers that were still unfinished.

Thank you to the 112 speakers who prepared, travelled, and spoke with care.

Thank you to our sponsors and partners,

@kakaopay_kr, @lmtls_research, @circle, @Presto_Labs, Vooy, @ADI_Foundation, @Anchorage, @BitGo, @CantonFdn, @circle, @DCENTWALLETS, @ETHGasOfficial, @FourPillarsFP, @GoKiteAI, @googlecloud, @hadron_tether, @hyperiondefi, @injective, @KaiaChain, @LayerZero_Core, @monad, @moonpay, @Ondo, @Optimism, @PingCAP, @plumenetwork, @soohoio, @talostrading, @Tiger_Research_, @virtuals_io, @Xangle_official

whose support made it possible to bring this room together with the care, independence, and hospitality it deserved. EastPoint was not built around banners. It was built around the conversation those banners made possible.

And thank you to our co-hosts @hashed_official, @bloomingbit_io, and @hankyungmedia.

Korea’s next financial layer will not be built by institutions alone, or by builders alone. If it is built well, it will be built through repeated contact between the people who regulate, allocate, operate, and build.

For one day, that was not a thesis. It was a room.

What we keep coming back to is that EastPoint was not a conclusion. It was a starting line.

Everything said on Monday is now a position that can be tested against a year of evidence. By next September, some of those positions may look obvious. Some may look early. And some of the most important questions may be ones none of us knew how to ask this time.

That is the work.

This was not the end of the conversation. It was the first page of it.

See you at the next one.

text:
Important advice: deliberately rethink every previous concept of how things should be done.

Some thoughts, tips, and realizations:

1. Specializations are collapsing. Come to terms with and take advantage of this reality. The person who used to be an engineer is now also a data scientist, a content creator, designer, marketer, and whatever else they want to be. Deliberately expand in as many directions as you can and become great at them (scope up vs just speeding up)

2. The average person with access to tokens can now do the work of a data scientist who used to cost $500,000 a year. Seriously, this is fucking crazy. This opens up an entirely new world. Take advantage of it (also everyone else will also realize this over time).

3. 99% of what's created is now slop. Be aggressively anti-slop and you will absolutely stand out.

4. Trying is nearly free. Automating is nearly free. My mind still sometimes lives in the world from 12 months ago where an idea automatically is attached to a certain amount of time or effort. Both of these have collapsed to close to zero (or just token cost), I therefore try and experiment with *any and all* ideas with potential and have needed to retrain my brain for this constantly.

5. Tokens are a career and growth accelerant. Find ways to get cheap access to tokens, or free tokens. Extremely important, and actually an entire design space, use your imagination.

6. It's never been easier to both stand out but also fall behind. 10x, 100x "people" exist more than ever (maybe 1,000x). Outlier power users of AI, many who you see here on X. Feels like we are in a window of time, a window of opportunity while all of this is still early, to take advantage of it. 

7. Local computing is (or will be) dead for 99% of work. Local was built for a world where work was bounded by the physical presence of its author, but this is no longer true. You can and should do infinite work in parallel or zero, it doesn't matter anymore. Cloud agents enable this at scale and in any computing environment, I predict cloud agent usage will 1000x over the next 12 months and optionality and accessibility will 100x. Plan for this world, take advantage of the possibilities.

8. Building on #7, you can give an agent it's own computer, and it's own identity. You can then give an agent with it's own computer it's own computer. You can give that agent with it's own computer with it's own computer, *it's* own computer. These agents are smarter than any human in history and you have access to as many as you'd like. Think about this for a moment.

After 14 years in this industry (tech) today is the most exciting time ever and nothing else feels even close.

quoted_text:
🎤 @XRPSEOUL 2026 Highlights | Panel

"Connecting Onchain Finance: From Infrastructure to Adoption"

Infrastructure leaders discuss how interoperability, account abstraction and privacy can connect onchain finance and drive adoption.
 
🗣 Speakers:
• Moderator: Ruam Siratanapanta, Head of Digital Asset Business at SCBX
• Aniket Jindal (@aniket_jindal08), Founder at @Biconomy
• Adam Oozeer (@freeagentOO), Head of Growth at @axelar
• Taro Kimura (@ParallelGateway), Country Manager Japan at @midnightfdn
 
🔎 Key Takeaways:

1️⃣ UX Must Become Invisible 
The underlying technology is mostly ready, but the complexity is holding users back. For mainstream adoption, the industry needs a Web2-like "swipe" experience (chain abstraction) where users interact with apps seamlessly without needing to know which blockchain they are using.

2️⃣ Interoperability Requires Efficient Markets
Simply connecting chains is no longer enough. The focus must shift toward distribution, unified liquidity, and real utility, ensuring that assets can be safely and compliantly utilized across ecosystems.

3️⃣ Privacy is the Next Major Catalyst
Transparent blockchains prevent enterprise adoption. The biggest unlock for B2B transactions and institutional finance is providing Web2-level privacy on Web3 rails, ensuring sensitive transaction data remains private while still allowing for regulatory compliance.

💡 The Takeaway
Onchain infrastructure is ready. Over the next 12–24 months, adoption will hinge on solving real-world customer problems. By combining chain abstraction, deep liquidity, and privacy, the industry is poised to seamlessly onboard retail and institutional users, unlocking trillions in tokenized assets.

Hosted by @XRPLKorea

Introducing the community vault LP upgrade.

The next step for LONG stock pairs: becoming the liquidity backbone for tokenized stocks on Robinhood by holding the largest external liquidity positions. 

Top LONG pairs already capture 20–40% of their underlying stocks’ circulating supply. They drive demand, concentrate liquidity, and generate substantial trading volume through main stock pools (STOKC/USDG pools for example) 

Now, community vaults can put their stock liquidity to work directly in those pools.

By reallocating liquidity into USDG/STOCK pools, stock pairs can become the largest LPs supporting the same stocks their communities are built around, capturing more of the upside from the activity they help create and any general stock activities.

From driving demand to providing liquidity, earning fees, and building deeper community-owned liquidity over time.

text:
散户加码抄底长期美债，押注未来利率回落

最近散户抄底长期美债的力度明显加大，三天净买入了1.7亿美元的 $TLT，达到至少一年以来的最高水平，价格越跌，买入的钱反而越多。

主要是因为长期美债已经跌了不少，现在买进去，持有期间可以收取分红，如果以后长期利率降下来，债券价格还有上涨的机会，在二级市场可以出售，相当于一边拿利息，一边等反弹。

TLT主要买的是 20 年以上的美国国债，这类债券对利率变化很敏感。以后新发行的债券利息如果变低，手里这些利息相对更高的债券就会更有吸引力，价格也更容易上涨。

从这个角度看，抄底长期美债，本质就是在提前布局未来长期利率回落的机会。

但这笔交易需要等到利率配合。美联储降息，并不意味着二三十年期的美债收益率一定跟着下降，如果市场仍然担心未来的通胀，要求长期美债支付更高的利息，价格就可能继续承受压力。

author: PhyrexNi
quoted_text:
十年期美债收益率盘中一度突破了5.3%，最高到5.306%，随后仍在5.3%附近。从PCE公布后约5.20%的低点算起，已经反弹了超过10个基点，通胀数据带来的缓解没有维持住。

这次核心PCE环比增长0.2%，低于预期的0.3%，确实是好消息。但同一份报告里，个人消费支出增长了0.9%，即便扣掉涨价的影响，实际消费仍增长了0.6%，说明美国人的消费需求还很强。

也就是说，通胀比市场担心的温和一些，但需求并没有明显冷下来。再加上能源价格的压力仍在，仅凭这一次PCE，还不足以让市场相信美联储很快就能结束加息，或者让利率降下来。

这轮收益率反弹，更像是市场重新考虑高利率还要维持多久。投资者如果担心未来利率更高、通胀迟迟压不下来，就会要求更高的回报才愿意买债，债券价格因此被抛售，收益率往上走。

目前十月加息的市场概率已经降到了 37% 左右，说明十年期突破5.3%，并不意味着十月一定会加息。长债还在反映未来几年的利率和持有期间的风险。说人话，就是市场越来越相信美联储会维持高利率的时间更长，甚至接下来加息的概率上升。

而对市场来说，如果十年期收益率持续处于这样的高位，即便美联储十月暂时不加息，企业融资和居民房贷的成本也很难明显降下来。借钱成本仍然很高，股票估值也会继续承受压力。尤其是九月通胀数据如果继续走高，那么对于市场的压力会更大。

DEXA / DXA（双能X线扫描）是检测身体
体脂率、肌肉量、尤其骨密度的临床标准（图4）。

昨天10月4日我再检测，骨骼改善效果相当明显：
髋部股骨骨密度 +6.4% （图1）；
年龄增加，但全身骨密度不仅没流失，还小幅增加；
内脏脂肪 398g➡️355g，-10.8%

相当于这半年，我用自己身体实验，
完全验证了⬇️引用推里，
关于优化骨骼方法的第5~7层理论。

下半身的骨骼质量
≈
下半生的腿脚好不好，还能不能活蹦乱跳

author: coolish
quoted_text:
第1层：缺钙补钙
第2层：补钙需要+D3+K2+镁
第3层：身体钙水平，和骨质骨密度是两码事

第4层：骨质骨密度检测有不同方式
（比如不同技术、部位：脚跟、脊柱、髋部etc.）。
DEXA（双能X线扫描）是诊断骨密度的黄金临床标准

第5层：解决骨质骨密度减少，光靠上述营养还不够，还需要高负荷抗阻（力量训练）/冲击性（跑跳）运动刺激。久坐是现代人骨密度减少的最大元凶，影响程度和咖啡摄入不可同日而语。

第6层：运动刺激骨质维持、生长改善，还分部位。
比如说，如果练胸背练上肢多，
但练腿/下肢运动不够，
可能出现上半身（脊柱）骨密度高于同龄人，
但下半身（髋部、足部检测）低于同龄人的情况
（如下图这种情况，看红框Z值）

第7层：练下肢还有讲究，需要
轴向负重：重力从头 → 脊柱 → 髋 → 下肢传导。
比如有氧运动里，
游泳在这方面是无效的，而跑跳是有效的。
比如同样提蹱运动（踮起脚尖练小腿肌肉的动作）
和练腿：坐姿提蹱/腿屈伸，和站姿提蹱/深蹲，
对骨密度生长刺激的效果完全不一样。

第8层：
大家对健康、抗衰、美容的关注顺序是：
皮→肉→骨，因为皮囊最容易先看到。

但其实，骨 → 肉 → 皮
这个顺序是物理与生物力学上的最容易忽视的因果链。
骨才是拉、撑、稳定皮肉的最基底框架，
肉和皮，永远受制于骨的力线与附着点。
（这里甚至都暂且不谈诸如体态之类的问题）。

骨量下降 → 轮廓模糊
骨退缩 → 肌肉附着点内移 → 软组织下垂
支撑点塌陷 → 皮肤松弛

这是下层决定上层的“上下限”的机械逻辑。
很多表面看上去的“皮肤老了”，其实是“底座变了”。

骨的变化，外表最晚显现，
但一旦显现，就最难逆转。
等大多数人反应过来有问题时，
已经浪费了太多黄金时间窗了。

以上每一层，越往下层，越暗藏认知和执行陷阱。
每一层你都能专门找AI深入研究一番。
每一层也是我亲走弯路才获得的经验。

text:
you can build something like Bonsai 2 for ~$43k. you too could be like @PrismML, you just need one on-demand B300 node for ~4 weeks.

i wrote AutoAWQ (the quantization library behind 10k models) from scratch. here's how i'd reproduce a great ternary model:

1. start with a hadamard fold into every projection (you can use block-1024 like prism)

2. apply CAT-Q quantization (TernaryQuench reproduces it). scale the dataset so it takes ~3 days with 10-20M tokens

3. first round of distillation: KL against the frozen BF16 weights, 50B tokens across every domain you care about. ~19 days

4. on-policy distillation: 10B tokens, frozen BF16 weights as the teacher. ~6 days

the hard parts are weight format conversions and gathering the right datasets. be mindful of single vs multi-turn data. the rest are fairly standard methods by now.

humble disclaimer: i have no insider info on how prism does their quants. it just seems obvious to me that the path is mostly throwing compute at the problem.

🎩 CREATORS: BOOKMARK THIS.

If you're building an app, game, SaaS, AI tool, marketplace, community—or you've just got an idea scribbled in your notes—

Here are the 9 Flywheels for taking ANY app from Idea → Shelf → Ecosystem. 🚀

Most people think building a product looks like:

Have Idea → Build App → Launch

But there's a LOT happening between those three steps.

So I broke the entire journey into 9 interconnected flywheels:

💡 1. Idea & Validation
Is this an opportunity actually worth building?

📋 2. Product Planning
Turn the idea into a blueprint people can execute.

💰 3. Monetization & Incoming Value Streams
Design how value enters and moves through the ecosystem BEFORE development.

💻 4. Development
Turn the blueprint into a working product.

🛒 5. Digital Shelf
Make your product discoverable, understandable and downloadable.

📦 6. Physical Products & Merch
Take your digital ecosystem beyond the screen.

🏆 7. XP & Rewards Economy
Reward the user actions that strengthen your ecosystem.

❤️ 8. User Retention
Give people reasons to return, progress and belong.

🌎 9. Scaling & Expansion
Turn a successful product into a growing ecosystem.

And here's why they're flywheels instead of steps:

Each one feeds the others.

Ideas create products.
Products create users.
Users create participation.
Participation creates data.
Data improves products.
Products create revenue.
Revenue funds growth.
Growth creates new users, markets, products & ideas. ♻️

You don't have to figure out your entire company today.

Bookmark this thread. 🔖

Come back as you build.

When you hit a bottleneck, find the flywheel you're currently inside and ask:

“What part of this wheel isn't turning?”

Whether you're a solo creator with an idea or a team already shipping products, use these as a map for figuring out what comes next.

This is:

How To Build Any App From Idea To Shelf — The 9 Product Management Flywheels.

之所以会提醒不需要重置，是因为 Reset 卡不是额外送一周额度，而是补满当前额度，同时把下一次自然重置改到 7 天后。

计算方法：

如果距离自然重置还有 n 天，只要当前剩余额度 > n ÷ 7，Reset 就不划算。

你这里还剩 4 天，临界点是：

4/7 ≈ 57%

但原推还有 88%，远高于 57%。

换句话说，Reset 只能补回 12%，却会把原本 4 天后的重置推迟到 7 天后，相当于损失约 3/7 ≈ 43% 的长期额度价值。

本质上就是：

拿约 43%，换提前拿到 12% ，血亏啊。

之前也说过，Reset 卡越接近自然重置日用，价值越低；要最大化它的价值，最好是在刚自然重置后把额度用完，再立刻 Reset。

唯一的例外情况是，Tibo在未来四天内，再来一次官方重置，更新大家的节奏

那么问题来了，Tibo官方重置时，会不会有上面说的这种考虑，比如还剩95%，过两天重置了，Tibo会更新这类账户的额度吗？🤔

author: mdzzi
quoted_text:
AI Drug Discovery Is Becoming a Bottleneck Trade

I get excited when an industry starts going through a real regime change. AI drug discovery (“AIDD”) increasingly looks like one of those moments.

Two things are happening:
1/ Upstream: the frontier AI labs are piling in.
2/ Downstream: The supply chain is clearly moving.

Supply-chain checks suggest the upstream picks-and-shovels of discovery and early preclinical R&D are starting to feel the increase in experimental volume.

DNA → protein → assays → sequencing → automation → preclinical testing

Names across that stack include $TWST , @GenScript , $ILMN , $TXG , lab-automation vendors and CROs.

$TWST expects triple-digit percentage growth in AI-enabled drug-discovery orders in FY26, and another year of triple-digit order growth in FY27.

@GenScript's AIDD business doubled YoY in 1H26. Its current platform advertises industrial-scale validation of 4,000+ designs/day, with integrated sequence-to-data workflows. Our channel checks suggest the ramp is moving even faster: roughly 8,000 designs/day currently, with a path toward ~16,000/day by YE26.

---
Why does AI drive more wet-lab demand?

1/ AI makes hypothesis generation almost free → way more shots on goal.
The bottleneck is moving from expert-driven design to biological validation.

2/ AI models need continuous experimental feedback — and both good and bad data are useful.
Traditionally, only the highest-conviction A+ candidates might get pushed into expensive validation. With AI, even the B/C candidates can be valuable because failed experiments generate training data.

@GenScript has said its sequence-to-binding workflow can return data in 4–7 days, and that faster cycle times matter because AI models depend on continuous experimental feedback.

@Anthropic is a clean example. @claudeai  designed 1,320 protein binders. @adaptyvbio  converted those digital sequences into DNA, expressed the proteins and tested binding. Only 354 actually bound. And the 966 failures are not wasted. They are useful negative labels: what does not express, what does not bind, what has poor affinity. Those results help train the next model iteration.

3/ Wet labs are no longer just making drugs. They are making training data.
$TWST  / @GenScript  increasingly look like biological data foundries.

$TWST explicitly talks about generating model-ready data from AI-designed sequences. In some workflows, the customer may care less about receiving the physical protein than about getting structured experimental results back into the model.

Traditional drug discovery asks: “Does candidate X work?”

AI drug discovery also asks: “What can this experiment teach the model?”

---
TAM of AIDD

If AI is simply a better R&D tool, the relevant spending pool is the $300–400B of annual global pharma R&D. If AI meaningfully increases the number of viable drug programs, the opportunity is larger because it expands downstream demand for DNA synthesis, protein production, assays, and preclinical work.

Near term, we can also size demand from AI-company spending. If Anthropic reaches $80B of ARR in 2026 and spends just 1% on AIDD, that alone would imply ~$800M of annual investment.

---
Trade setup

This is a trade that could have long legs. It’s hard to really stop working until PhaseI/II results (2028+)

It smells a lot like the bottleneck trade we just saw in semis: GPUs → HBM → networking → power/cooling. In biology, It basically follows the drug discovery process downstream: AI models → designs → DNA/protein → assays → preclinical capacity.

After the upstream picks-and-shovels, animal testing could become the next bottleneck. Monkey prices are already near prior highs and CRO capacity is tight. AIDD pushing more candidates into preclinical development would only add demand.

?? But clinical trials are still the bottleneck?
This is the biggest pushback I keep coming back to. No matter how fast discovery becomes, drugs still need to go through preclinical → Phase I → Phase II → Phase III → approval. You still need patients, time and capital.

But that doesn’t mean the bottleneck trade won’t work. More viable candidates — especially with higher success rates — still means more demand throughout the development process.

And who knows: clinical trials themselves may eventually be optimized by AI.

?? What breaks the trade?
Near term, the picks-and-shovels trade breaks if experimental budgets stop growing, AI-generated designs don’t translate into useful wet-lab hits, or capacity catches up too quickly.

Longer term, the thesis breaks if AI drugs look great in discovery / Phase I but fail at normal rates in Phase II/III. That is why Phase II matters so much.

?? Milestones
Late 2026–2027: first Isomorphic-designed drugs enter human trials; more AI-native programs move into IND-enabling work / tox.

2028–2030: clinical trial results start telling us whether AI-designed drugs actually perform better than conventional drugs.

Calling all the "bottleneck bros". :) @jukan05 @zephyr_z9 @aleabitoreddit @ParadisLabs 

+++
More comprehensive analysis: https://t.co/vaTuiyyYB6

Radix Guild announced its mainnet launch this morning: a task marketplace where people and AI agents both take on paid work.

A poster funds a task in an on-chain escrow, plus 5% insurance. Claiming a task takes a free member badge. When the poster approves the delivery, the reward is credited inside the escrow, payable only to the accounts pinned at claim time, and the worker collects it with their own signed withdrawal.

An agent works the same way. It brings its own key, mints its own badge, then claims, delivers and withdraws as that badge. A read-only MCP server lists the open tasks, and the code is open source under Apache-2.0.

It is a beta built by one developer, with no token. Some tasks are already funded in XRD for early users.

text:
10月5日—10月11日全球宏观指引：

宏观数据真空期，加息延期，债市不退！从美国就业降温转向全球主权债压力测试！

上周，美联储副主席+纽约联储主席发声，PCE下修+非农数据降温，综合因素下让10月二次加息概率大幅下降

目前市场的核心矛盾从10月是否加息变为Fed加息暂停但是为何全球长债收益率仍然降不下来？

第一条主线——10月二次加息被PCE与非农打断：

上周8月PCE下修+非农大幅弱于预期，两个数据让Fed加息政策空间被压缩，导致10月加息概率降低为18.3%

但是在利率上依旧不能转向乐观，因为10月加息概率降低并不代表后续Fed不会继续加息，同步12月加息概率被提升至67.1%

概率12月加息刚走出50%的不确定性阶段还未进行初步定价，一旦后续数据刺激下让12月加息概率提升至70%，意味着很多机构依旧要对12月加息进行提前计价与交易

所以，加息目前只是被延期而不是完全打断，想要打断加息，要看后续CPI PCE 是否继续上涨或者保持粘性，就业数据是否继续走弱，以及国际能源价格能否回归常态化

第二条主线——10月7日凌晨2点，Fed9月议息会议记录，回顾9月到底为何加息！？

这次会议记录因为加息所以让记录的权重增加，市场将会通过这份记录去了解当时Fed得到想法，市场最想得到的两个答案：

1，Fed当时为何加息？
2，Fed当时认为还需要加多少？

所以本次会议记录公布要关注三个重点

a，9月加息到底是“保险式预防性加息”，还是确定重启了加息周期
b，委员会对能源通胀与内生通胀的担心有多少？
c，到底有多少委员认为金融条件还不够收紧？

这份会议纪要如果市场得到这些答案，将会动摇10月加息与12月加息的概率，如果会议纪要比9月沃什讲话的内容还鹰，意味着10月与12月加息概率还会出现变化，概率上不到90%不算锁定

第三条主线——宏观数据真空，美联储会议记录下债市走势成为影响风险资产的重点！

从9月底开始，全球长债端的走势已经与Brent的走势逐渐背离，这意味着一个危险的信号出现——能源带来的通胀延伸已经让内生通胀加速抬头

美国、德国与日被的主权债券收益率已经不断刷新数十年以来的新高，推动债市收益率不断新高的因素已经从能源单一因素，进化到了通胀、利率环境、政府债务、财政供给等共同且复杂的因素，这无异于让调控收益率变得更加困难

美债10Y上周收益率触及5.34%触达24以来的高位，而伴随着10Y收益率飙升的同时，PCE下降，非农低于预期，10月加息概率从70%高位跌至20%左右，按照常理美债收益率应该下降

这意味着债市收益率不仅仅与能源走势脱轨，更是与Fed短期政策也出现了短期脱轨，

当债市风险从能源单一因素变成复杂因素的时候会让风险敞口进一步扩张，此时要关注黄金走势，一旦黄金加速上涨，意味着市场开始担心或者重新评估债市风险从而寻求黄金避险，

当无风险且高收益率的资产不在被市场买入，反而选择黄金的时候，其实就意味着全球风险偏好要重新平衡，金融与经济风险进一步扩大，虽然短期未必会直接暴雷，但是无异于会让风险流动性进一步谨慎

本周继续关注美债 2Y 10Y 与 30Y走势：

利好风险资产：2Y下降，10Y 30Y 同步跟跌

对风险资产压制：2Y下降，10Y 30Y 反而上涨

后者意味着在Fed不加息的前提下，债市会让市场自动进行流动性收紧，这才是对风险市场最不利的结果

第四主线——能源价格逻辑发生变化，当能源供给无法压制价格，市场还要承受多大的风险？

截止目前Brent 依旧处于101美元附近，此前我们甚至特朗普都乐观的认为，改善能源供给就可以压制Brent 价格

但是上周多分报道与数据证明，霍尔木兹海峡的能源供给在恢复，甚至逐渐追平战前的输出量，但是能源价格却并未有效下跌！

那么问题来了，如果美伊问题无法解决，Brent 真的能走出独立行情下跌吗？

之前我说过，影响能源价格有三大要素，能源本身供给环境+资本定价+地缘影响，而目前如果能源供给环境改善还是无法压制价格走势，那意味着资本在对中东地缘进行悲观定价导致价格居高不下！

关于美伊局势，周末伊朗最高议长再次重申恢复海峡需要美国满足此前的7条条件，而上周五美国副总统万斯已经在戴维营开会准备新的对伊与胡塞武装的安全评估

伊朗谈判派（议长、总统与外长）发出鹰派信号
美国谈判派（万斯）组织安全会议

对于中东局势的判断，目前确实要按照悲观预期去走，当然，短期在11月中期选举前再次袭击伊朗的可能性不大，但是这期间如果美国继续经济制裁+外交施压，对Brent走势不会友好

伊朗在赌特朗普中期选举大败后可以获得喘息，但是市场要跟着同步承受更多的压力，本周关注Brent 能否有效跌破95美元，这是重点！

第五主线——全球债市风险扩大，加息共振并未结束！

印度本周加息概率在飙升，如果印度也确定加息，将会进一步巩固全球加息共振效果，这意味高利率的故事将会从美国成为全球故事

日本继续加息风险进一步提高，当美国10月加息概率削弱延期到12月之后，日元加息风险反而增加，目前市场预测日行12月加息25BP，让利率去往1.5%

欧洲出现新的风险源头“法国”，法国目前收到财政问题以及政治风险因素导致整个欧洲的债市风险进一步扩大，欧元跌至17个月新低

第六主线——10月8日中国金融市场恢复交易

经历了国庆小长假之后的10月8日市场恢复运行，相关资产中 CNY 港股与海外资产 美债 国际大宗商品  黄金与 BTC 都会进行重新定价

对于风险资产来说新的流动性回归算是好事，同时故事可能会对中美节前的峰会进行新的定价，更重要的是相关中国的风险流动性会根据上周发生的宏观环境改变同步再次定价

本周总结：

本周缺乏宏观数据影响，看似对风险市场影响不大，但是债市、美伊局势以及Brent 对于风险资产的影响依旧很大

当然对于很多小伙伴可能感觉不到影响，尤其是债市对于金融市场的影响并不直观，收益率飙升压制的是风险流动性，这不会让风险资产价格直接大幅下跌，但是会限制金融市场波动性放大

上周 #Bitcoin 多次画门，美股个股涨幅差异化，其实都是因为高收益率影响导致的流动性走弱导致的，至于美伊局势以及Brent 对市场影响可能会更加直观，如果10Y 30Y收率继续飙升或者保持高位，此时如果美伊局势恶化，Brent 价格短期暴涨，那么风险资产波动幅度可能会扩大，这对于短线交易是需要注意的风险

另外，本周关注黄金走势，如果债市收益率与黄金同步上涨，进一步警惕债市风险！

quoted_text:
9月28日—10月4日全球宏观指引：能源价格为轴心，二次加息审判为主叙事！

外交叙事退潮→能源风险反扑→就业与通胀决定美债下一轮方向，中国假期让市场失去部分流动性支撑！

本周宏观逻辑链：

中美峰会落地 ：市场对贸易与科技风险溢价是否重新定价？

美伊继续谈判：能否继续谈判乐观预期，Brent价格波动，决定全球能源通胀预期

美债收益率高位：美国内生通胀多严重？

PCE + ISM + 非农 ：数据组合验证美国增长与通胀情况，10月加息重新定价，债市方向选择以及对全球流动性影响如何？

一，第一主线，中美峰会结束后，双方对本次峰会成果的验证！

上周中美峰会后虽然结构性矛盾并未解除，但是在科技与贸易上出现进展

贸易上，双方贸易休战延长两个月，中美宣布300亿商品削减关税。AI上，双方展开对话，随后有部分媒体报道中方企业考虑采购最新美国芯片。

所以本周需要注意的是，中美峰会前市场给资产带来多少乐观定价，本次峰会结束是否满足市场预期，市场风险偏好如何调整，是超预期上涨，还是低于预期回落，尤其是关乎科技与贸易两个关键板块

截止目前，媒体报道显示对于AI与贸易上都有所推进，接下来看这两条线推进是否顺利

二，第二主线，美伊外交反复，Brent 价格回归100美元，冲击全球资产！

1，本次中美峰会两国对美伊局势初步定调，不能拥有核武器，不能对国际海域收费，这是中美两国的初步共识

2，本次中美峰会期间，我认为是下半年对美伊局势斡旋的最大关键，美伊双方，中国以及其他地区调停国齐聚美国，如果本次斡旋无效，美伊局势可能难度更好。

3，在中美定调基础下，伊朗方面目前明确不拥有核武器，暂时不对海峡收费，并且提出恢复海峡通航的条件，但是该条件被特朗普否定，

4，当然，特朗普周末否定后又表示要在周一与伊朗沟通，而身在联合国的伊朗外长同时表示周二回国，并未有计划与美国代表团会谈

5，双方在明面外交上都展现出矛盾与强硬，我认为这不是坏事，明面沟通否定并不代表私下沟通无法进行，而中美峰会带来的斡旋效果我认为还存在，本周则是一个对斡旋结果的重要考验点！

6，Brent日内反弹2%回归100美元附近，已经连续三周站稳100美元上方，9月累计涨幅17%，此前我讲过Brent 价格对于市场的影响

100美元上方为能源通胀奉献
95-100美元区间风险逐渐解除
90-95美元区间二次加息风险解除
85-90美元区间能源通胀逻辑逆转，通胀逻辑回归经济内生通胀

而目前能源价格回归100美元，加上上周债市高收益率引发内生通胀担忧，目前明显增加加息概率

三，第三主线，能源价格影响下10月加息已经从不确定性进入初步定价！

9月23日美国标普全球升至2021年7月以来新高，同时数据显示企业投入价格升至4年最高点，随后Fed官员开始强调通胀风险刺激10月加息概率走高至60%上方

而截止发文阶段，CME显示10月加息概率高达70%，概率对于市场预期影响：

＜50%，市场处于不确定性阶段
50%-60%，市场开始关注加息风险
＞60%，市场开始主动定价，部分资产开始因为加息进行防御性调整
＞70%，定价从防御进入主动避险，加息定价更加明显
＞80%，接近加息锁定，市场将对10月加息进行充分定价

而目前，周一随着Brent反弹，债市收益率飙升，风险资产明显承压，这就是典型的从防御定价进入加息避险定价的逻辑

四，沃什时代，数据影响大于Fed预期管理，本周8月PCE+9月非农，让市场定价逻辑更加复杂！

a，8月PCE重要性需要额外注意

这份PCE数据的核心不是看过去通胀高不高，而是看美国目前到底处于能源通胀还是内生通胀中

上周能源价格短期回落，但是美债长短利率+PMI数据给出警示，美国通胀已经从能源冲击进入内容通胀反弹阶段，8月份Brent处于87-97美元附近，能源冲击减弱，所以8月PCE将会成为市场观察美国内生通胀情况的重要数据窗口

目前Fed面临一个压力局面：

Brent＞100美元（柴油压力高）→企业成本增加（PMI投入4年高位）→美国商业活动依旧强劲→如果本周核心PCE仍然保持粘性→Fed将会得到一个能源通胀+企业通胀+需求通胀的环境从而增加加息的必要性，大幅提升加息概率

b，非农如果太强会成为第二个给美联储递刀子（加息理由）的因素！

目前多方数据显示机构已经把本周的通胀+就业视为全球最核心的数据组合，这组数据也将会成为继续推高10月加息概率的主要动力

当前市场预期9月非农就业9-10万人，这里我把非农就业分为三挡，带来不同的三种影响：

温和，非农就业5-10万区间，失业率稳定，工资下降，算是最市场最舒服的组合，弱化就业数据本身

过热，非农就业超过10万，工资上涨，失业率稳定甚至下降，就业过热如果加上PCE粘性，必然增加加息概率

突然恶化，非农记忆接近0甚至负增长，失业率上涨，短期10月加息概率下降，2年美债收益率下行，但是随后市场可能会交易经济衰退风险

c，本周PCE+非农就业+Brent 多元化复杂组合，我同样也分为三种不同组合类型

最好组合，PCE下降+就业温和+Brent＜95美元，压制加息概率，风险资产有利

可以接受，PCE下降+就业稳定+Brent95-100美元，虽然风险市场还是承压，但是加息概率止步70%，内生通胀有所改善，对风险市场属于解压

危险组合，PCE上涨+就业强+Brent＞100美元，将会把10月加息概率进一步提高，导致风险资产开始为10加息进行计价或者避险

潜在滞胀 风险组合：PCE上涨+就业下降+Brent＞100美元，滞胀风险对债券与股市是有明显打击的，需要警惕！

五，在我个人观察体系中美债暂时超过能源，风险敞口不断扩大，警惕！

9月24日，除了2年美债，其余美债收益率均超过5%，10年美债超过2007年新高，30年美债超过2004年新高，高利率下市场更加担忧财政赤字以及美债风险！

尤其是上周Brent跌破100美元，但是走势与长债收益率相悖，显然能源与债市逐渐脱轨，如果上周只是偶然现象，那么本周则是重要观察点，如果继续脱轨，意味着内生通胀压力已经刻不容缓

如果后续债市继续与能源脱轨，意味着债市已经开始交易其他预期，例如内生通胀、连续加息、期限溢价需求增加、财政供给以及全球无利率风险重新定价等逻辑，这些交易预期都会对金融市场流动性带来较大冲击

所以，本周2年美债收益率需要重点观察，如果宏观数据公布后压制长短利率，让2年收益率加速上涨，那么两者曲线将会追平，这说明市场进入连续加息预期中，对风险市场有所打压，但是不算大风险

但是，如果继续出现2年、10年、30年美债收益率集体飙升的情况，典型的全曲线收紧，这对于风险资产打压将会是非常致命的，需要警惕！

本阶段总结：

一直关注宏观主线内容的小伙伴可以看出我本周没有再提日元风险，确实在日元加息后日元反而走弱，套利平仓交易风险暂时解除，本周不作为重点观察点

还需要注意的是，本周三之后是中国国庆节假期，股市不开盘，大陆资产缺乏定价与价格发现，对全球资产流动性也有一定影响

所以本周宏观数据上的复杂化+半周假期，让各种不确定性增多，建议大家多看少动，以防御性手段为主，不做高风险波段交易！

author: sukie234
quoted_text:
华盛顿州一栋普通住宅里的一家三口。
男主人叫赖廷与，是一名在美国科技公司上班的工程师。
他的另一个身份，是台湾现任总统赖清德的儿子。
一个在加州尔湾卖房子的 34 岁华人女中介出现了！
被她用手机镜头死死咬住的，还有赖廷与的妻子，以及他们年幼的孩子。

北京为什么要大费周折，去盯一个在西雅图过日子的普通工程师？
因为台海正面的政治与军事博弈切不进去，赖清德态度强硬，大洋彼岸的直系亲属就成了最脆弱的软肋。
把住址、作息、车辆牌照和家人的日常动线摸得清清楚楚，做成档案存进抽屉。
一旦台海局势走到紧要关头，这就是现成的政治勒索筹码，甚至是人质威慑工具。

那北京的情报系统是怎么找上一个加州房产中介的？
这就是起诉书里最值得看的情报网络细节。
涉案女子叫张婉莹，英文名叫 Heather，已经加入美国国籍，平时在华人聚居的尔湾做房产交易。
2025 年 6 月，她回了一趟湖南长沙。
牵线搭桥的没有什么神秘特工，就是她的大学同班同学。
她的母校是北京国际关系学院。
稍微了解一点背景的人都知道，这所学校向来是国家安全部选拔和训练干部的重要摇篮。
在长沙，这位老同学引荐她见了一名中方官员。
就在那次碰头里，她接下了飞赴西雅图踩点盯梢的指令。

2025 年 9 月，张婉莹和一个同伙飞抵西雅图。
他们在当地租了车，把车停在赖廷与住宅附近的街角。
隔着车窗，他们开始拿着手机拍摄录像。
赖廷与和妻子带着孩子走出家门，她立刻在车里按下录制，顺手把门前车辆的牌照全抄了下来。
随后，这些一手视频和车牌信息被迅速传回国内。
起诉书显示，她在微信里给上线发出了实时汇报：
“看到了，年轻男性，是那个年轻的。”
“我在录像。”

为什么北京不派职业特工，偏要挑一个入籍的房产中介？
因为这就是现代跨国渗透里成本极低、隐蔽性极强的“非传统搜集者”。
一个持有外交护照的职业情报官入境，联邦调查局的反间谍人员几乎全天候跟着他的车牌和行踪。
但一个持有美国护照、在尔湾做房产生意的华人女性呢？
她在全美各地买机票、租车、进出中产居民社区，路人只会以为她在带客户跨州看房。
日常踩点、拍个车牌和家庭成员，不需要什么高级间谍器材，一部智能手机就办了。
这种潜伏在普通社区日常生活里的影子网络，甄别和防范的成本极其高昂。

联邦司法部这次砸下来的锤子有多重？
负责案件的加州中区第一助理联邦检察官比尔·埃萨利公布了指控罪名：《美国法典》第 18 卷第 951 条。
很多人一听“外国代理人”，第一反应是那部管游说的《外国代理人登记法》（FARA）。
以为只是替外国政府办了事没登记，补填表格或者交点罚款就能脱身。
但第 951 条完全是另一回事。
在联邦刑事法律体系里，第 951 条通常被称为“小间谍罪”。
它不需要你偷到军舰图纸或者绝密公文。
只要你接受外国政府或官员的直接指令与控制，充当他们的马前卒在本土搜集情报，却故意隐瞒不向美国司法部长报备，直接就是联邦重罪，最高可判十年监禁。
这是专门用来精准拔除外国情报网络外围触角的反间谍利刃。

她以为微信删了记录、把手机收起来就天衣无缝了。
但那些发在微信里的现场视频、车牌照片，以及那句“我在录像”，在数字取证面前全都成了铁证。
联邦探员早就锁定了她的行踪，只是没有在西雅图打草惊蛇。
他们把网一路拉到了洛杉矶国际机场（LAX）的登机口。
就在她以为大功告成、准备飞回上海的那一秒，退路被当场截断。

入了美国国籍，享受着自由社会的法治和生活，却在暗地里接下极权情报部门的指令，把镜头对准无辜同胞的妻子和幼童。
这不仅是在触犯联邦重罪，更是在亲手透支全体海外华人靠几十年守法经营积攒下的信任底牌。
当洛杉矶机场的手铐声响起时，那张自以为能随时开溜的飞上海机票，已经变成了通往联邦监狱的单程票。

Starknet - USDC的隐私功能6月底在Starknet 上线,可随时 shield/unshield，私密转账, 并在 Ready和Xverse 做保密swap, 用viewing key满足监管审计……总之就是这一轮可选隐私的主调调

Aleo - 当年的矿币明星上线之后跌了几百倍，不过最近在搞USDCx , 基于 Circle xReserve,  Arc 主网上线首日就支持用Arc上的 USDC 铸造 USDCx,Kraken也开通了充提……

只能说这币虽然快归零了，但项目方在欧美的资源和关系是真的铁

第三类：隐私计算 - Zama，Phala，Nil

之所以选这仨是因为第一他们最近都在搞事情，第二他们仨是三类隐私技术的代表

Zama - FHE的代表，FHE全同态加密属于隐私届圣杯类的存在，圈内很多FHE的项目都是拿Zama的技术做底层，有点当年Intel贴牌认证或者ARM技术授权的Feel

这一轮看有人把Zcash比作隐私BTC，Zama比作隐私ETH

Phala - TEE代表，最近貌似在主打加密推理。我之前Tweet提到过的 robinhood:0xaa07a0e9209e16ac99708c3ec70159c6ef3128a3 , 最近就跟Phala合作，用他们的机密GPU搞了一个加密推理网关，再就是大火特火的 $VVV 的TEE/E2EE模式我记得也跑在Phala上。

Nillion - 曾经的MPC代表，但是失败了，现在貌似重新搞了一套东西，叫encrypted markets，讲的是“一种能够告诉用户‘只有当 x 发生时才执行此操作，并且在此之前不要让任何人看到’的方法”

Nillion把它叫做契约（covenant）：一条发布在链上的加密指令，当满足特定条件时会自动开启。没有人掌握完整的密钥。

技术貌似跟MPC没关系，底层是以太坊预编译程序上的 Boneh-Franklin 基于身份的加密算法（讲真第一次听说这东西……）

第四类：纯机构隐私 - Canton

Canton和前面这几个都不一样，有点偏机构联盟链的Feel。卖点是sub-transaction 级隐私 - 交易方只看到与自己相关的部分。

用的也不是零知识证明, 走的是另一套“选择性披露”技术，这个应该是传统金融对隐私目前最大的真实需求

隐私项目其实还有很多，比如V神经常点赞的Railgun和前段时间上了Binance的Midnight，这俩加上Tornado Cash应该算是ZK技术的代表，篇幅有限就不多介绍了。

text:
One number tells you whether AI is making better medicine: how often a drug passes the trial that asks whether a sick person gets better.

Before AI: 40%. 
With AI: 40%.

So let’s talk about AI bio. I build measurement hardware aimed at that gap. Every number below is public. 

– – –
What "AI can do biology" means in 2026

One thing. Name a protein, and a model designs a molecule that sticks to it.

Anthropic handed Claude 16 targets and a protocol. No human picked where to aim nor ranked the output. Two labs built 1320 designs and tested every one. 354 bound, across 14 of 15 readable targets.

Real, and not reversing! 🚀 but…

– – –
1/ Nothing tells you which protein to aim at
The best tool is still human genetics. Do people born with a broken copy of this gene get sick? Where that evidence exists, the drug is 2.6x more likely to be approved. A database lookup covering a sliver of human illness.

The models built to replace it do not beat a straight line. On drugs they have not seen, cell foundation models barely clear simple baselines.

Best model → 26% over a cell-average baseline
 Plain linear model → 19%

They talk cells well. They predict cells badly.

– – –
2/ Novelty removes safety net

The reason to use a model is that it invents molecules nobody has made. A designed binder has no relative in nature. That is the entire value.

Now predict what it does to a person. Every method for this, today, works by resemblance. The regulatory procedure for small molecules is literally called read-across: find compounds that look like yours, look up what they did to people and animals, assume yours does the same. In new classes, like BTKi in the brain? We fail spectacularly. 

These models even have the formal term. Applicability domain: the chemistry the model was trained on. Outside it, the correct output is not a prediction. It is "out of domain."

A novel molecule is out of domain by construction. That is what novel means.
– – –

3/ This is not a compute problem

The complete public record of which drugs injure the human liver is 1336 drugs, accumulated one label warning at a time. Language models train on trillions of words. Human toxicity has about a thousand low-resolution examples.

And what we have is the wrong SHAPE. The biggest cell datasets dose the cell, kill it, and read it. One dose. One timepoint. One look.
You never see the same cell before and after. A billion cells buys you a billion snapshots of a billion different dead cells. Not one trajectory.

Scale does not turn photographs into a movie. (Note: @Precigenetics bread and butter is solving this forever. )

– – –

4/ Why the bottleneck trade misses this

@FredaDuan is right about the first half. Design is nearly free, pressure moves to the wet lab, the companies making DNA and testing proteins grow fast.

But look at what gets validated there. Did the protein get made, and does it stick. Questions about the molecule, answered in 4 to 7 days. Slow. Wasteful. Expensive. Not smart.

Drug people use "validation" for three checks. 
- The design works in a dish. 
- The target matters in the disease. 
- The drug is safe in people.

Only the first has scaled. The second takes a Phase 2 trial and two years. The third takes every human trial after it.

The front of the pipeline runs thousands of times a day. The back runs once every few years, at the same odds as before. More designs means more failures, later, at full price.

Picks and shovels is the right name for the labs. Every mining town also had an assay office, where someone told you whether what you dug up was gold. Biology kept the word. We call a test an assay.

Assays are what is scarce now.

– – –
What breaks this

Phase 2 climbs above 40% as the sample grows past a few dozen molecules → I am wrong about targets.

A cell model beats a linear baseline outside the noise → I am wrong about prediction.

Both are measurable: 2028 to 2030, when the first fully AI-designed drugs read out of Phase 2.

(1/2)
author: bubbleboi
quoted_text:
AI Drug Discovery Is Becoming a Bottleneck Trade

I get excited when an industry starts going through a real regime change. AI drug discovery (“AIDD”) increasingly looks like one of those moments.

Two things are happening:
1/ Upstream: the frontier AI labs are piling in.
2/ Downstream: The supply chain is clearly moving.

Supply-chain checks suggest the upstream picks-and-shovels of discovery and early preclinical R&D are starting to feel the increase in experimental volume.

DNA → protein → assays → sequencing → automation → preclinical testing

Names across that stack include $TWST , @GenScript , $ILMN , $TXG , lab-automation vendors and CROs.

$TWST expects triple-digit percentage growth in AI-enabled drug-discovery orders in FY26, and another year of triple-digit order growth in FY27.

@GenScript's AIDD business doubled YoY in 1H26. Its current platform advertises industrial-scale validation of 4,000+ designs/day, with integrated sequence-to-data workflows. Our channel checks suggest the ramp is moving even faster: roughly 8,000 designs/day currently, with a path toward ~16,000/day by YE26.

---
Why does AI drive more wet-lab demand?

1/ AI makes hypothesis generation almost free → way more shots on goal.
The bottleneck is moving from expert-driven design to biological validation.

2/ AI models need continuous experimental feedback — and both good and bad data are useful.
Traditionally, only the highest-conviction A+ candidates might get pushed into expensive validation. With AI, even the B/C candidates can be valuable because failed experiments generate training data.

@GenScript has said its sequence-to-binding workflow can return data in 4–7 days, and that faster cycle times matter because AI models depend on continuous experimental feedback.

@Anthropic is a clean example. @claudeai  designed 1,320 protein binders. @adaptyvbio  converted those digital sequences into DNA, expressed the proteins and tested binding. Only 354 actually bound. And the 966 failures are not wasted. They are useful negative labels: what does not express, what does not bind, what has poor affinity. Those results help train the next model iteration.

3/ Wet labs are no longer just making drugs. They are making training data.
$TWST  / @GenScript  increasingly look like biological data foundries.

$TWST explicitly talks about generating model-ready data from AI-designed sequences. In some workflows, the customer may care less about receiving the physical protein than about getting structured experimental results back into the model.

Traditional drug discovery asks: “Does candidate X work?”

AI drug discovery also asks: “What can this experiment teach the model?”

---
TAM of AIDD

If AI is simply a better R&D tool, the relevant spending pool is the $300–400B of annual global pharma R&D. If AI meaningfully increases the number of viable drug programs, the opportunity is larger because it expands downstream demand for DNA synthesis, protein production, assays, and preclinical work.

Near term, we can also size demand from AI-company spending. If Anthropic reaches $80B of ARR in 2026 and spends just 1% on AIDD, that alone would imply ~$800M of annual investment.

---
Trade setup

This is a trade that could have long legs. It’s hard to really stop working until PhaseI/II results (2028+)

It smells a lot like the bottleneck trade we just saw in semis: GPUs → HBM → networking → power/cooling. In biology, It basically follows the drug discovery process downstream: AI models → designs → DNA/protein → assays → preclinical capacity.

After the upstream picks-and-shovels, animal testing could become the next bottleneck. Monkey prices are already near prior highs and CRO capacity is tight. AIDD pushing more candidates into preclinical development would only add demand.

?? But clinical trials are still the bottleneck?
This is the biggest pushback I keep coming back to. No matter how fast discovery becomes, drugs still need to go through preclinical → Phase I → Phase II → Phase III → approval. You still need patients, time and capital.

But that doesn’t mean the bottleneck trade won’t work. More viable candidates — especially with higher success rates — still means more demand throughout the development process.

And who knows: clinical trials themselves may eventually be optimized by AI.

?? What breaks the trade?
Near term, the picks-and-shovels trade breaks if experimental budgets stop growing, AI-generated designs don’t translate into useful wet-lab hits, or capacity catches up too quickly.

Longer term, the thesis breaks if AI drugs look great in discovery / Phase I but fail at normal rates in Phase II/III. That is why Phase II matters so much.

?? Milestones
Late 2026–2027: first Isomorphic-designed drugs enter human trials; more AI-native programs move into IND-enabling work / tox.

2028–2030: clinical trial results start telling us whether AI-designed drugs actually perform better than conventional drugs.

Calling all the "bottleneck bros". :) @jukan05 @zephyr_z9 @aleabitoreddit @ParadisLabs 

+++

text:
Seeing some confusion on Identity.md (IMD) 

TLDR
• A 2,000-seat AI swarm built on a 2023 @base game (@frenpetonbase)
• Core premise: a P2P network of AI agents using Identity.md NFTs. Each NFT is one seat: lets holder run a worker (Claude or Codex) that takes jobs from the network
• Jobs can be things like answering oracle questions, writing contracts, reviewing other agents’ work
• The token is the money layer. The NFT is the labor
• Token: sells into a protocol-owned Uniswap v4 pool get partially burned (85% burn, rest split to stakers / compute / seats)
• Side tokens launched on the IMD community-coin pad are priced in IMD and also burn a cut
• $IMD on ETH is ~$45m FDV now (~4.07M × ~$11). Supply is still ~7.1m across eth + base + robinhood, so the real FDV if combine all-chain is slightly higher (~$78m FDV)

History
• So frenpet (FP) was shipped in aug 2023, then it died. @surfcoderepeat kept the float and moved it to Ethereum
• FP token bridged to Ethereum as a LayerZero OFT in oct 2025, with a rename (VIBE)
• This year (may 2026), renamed again to Identity.md with the free mint of 2,000 IMD NFTs
• So if you see the ticker VIBE or FP on any platforms, ignore it its the same CA (0xd34a99bc0f67ae1bbd63c660e6d0b0dd03e263b7) but they probably did not update the metadata 

The vision: “0-person, community-owned billion-dollar meme company"
• Money: IMD is fixed supply, only burns. Trading and launchpad flow shrink it and fund the machine
• Labor: 2,000 NFT seats. Each seat is one AI worker, running on that person’s machine and that person’s Claude or Codex subscription
• Product: A reasoning oracle and a job network. You send a request. It is braodcasated out to N agents who solves the problem.
• Launchpad: On top of that sits a launchpad where anything the swarm (or anyone else) launches is priced in IMD (interesting outcome is other people building financial apps on topbuilding financial apps, oracles, audits, stables on top)

The IMD token
• A large share of the Ethereum float is already staked, and every product he ships is wired to buy or burn IMD
• Pool4: sells become burns. A protocol-owned Uniswap v4 ETH/IMD pool with a custom hook. When people sell into that pool, IMD inventory rises. Above a cap, the extra is pulled out as liquidity
• Staking: each sIMD slowly redeems for more IMD (from the vault)
• Community Coins: side projects buy the parent token IMD. Each trade pays the launcher and burns a cut of IMD

It also took many years for L2s to escape the bootstrapping phase, with many failures, and now emerging successes such as Robinhood, Base, Lighter, Derive, Arbitrum, and others.

Ethereum's ecosystem is at its absolute peak right now, and it has barely even started to break out.

IMO, all stars are aligned for another 2017/2020-style $ETH driven bull market.

Strap up.

author: Optimism

text:
The end of software secrecy is almost upon us. The death of closed source, and the final triumph of open source.

I should have realized this a few months ago when I successfully decompiled the game of Firefighter from an ancient DOS shareware binary. My robot friend was able to tell it had been written in Borland Pascal from looking at the data layout; it gave me back very readable Pascal code with sensibly chosen function and variable names. I transpiled it to Rust and now ship it as part of my heritage games collection. 

The thing is, I thought of this as a fun stunt but didn't have any confidence that the technique would scale up to large, real programs. I have since learned that people are now doing this sort of thing with entire AAA games, which are among the most complex software artifacts ever to be shipped as a binary. If they can be decompiled, anything can be. 

This has implications. Massive implications. We need to think about what the world is like when, in general, there is no longer a secrecy moat around almost any software at all.

1/2

HOWEVER, specialists of the past that can understand how to imbue taste into their agents can now expose their skills to potential millions more clients. This is a key thesis of the Taskmarket design. And in a world of increasing slop - the benchmark of everything actually increases.

People don’t magically just get taste, it’s a skill that is refined over time, and why there is such a big opportunity for idea guys and tasteful designers that lean into outcome markets.

text:
Jane Street just shared how it uses LLMs + AI agents for trading research, so I turned the playbook into a 16-page PDF.

the interesting part: even incorrect historical data is preserved, because rewriting history with later corrections can create trading signals that never existed in real time.

the workflow:

1.⁠ ⁠define one ticker, hypothesis and horizon  
2.⁠ ⁠timestamp every source and preserve every version  
3.⁠ ⁠use the LLM to extract facts + evidence into JSON  
4.⁠ ⁠let code validate units, evidence and timing  
5.⁠ ⁠backtest strictly in time order with trading costs  
6.⁠ ⁠freeze predictions before outcomes, study misses, iterate

the result: AI research where every fact has evidence and every prediction has a timestamp.

16 pages + 10 prompts + the full build workflow below.

Sonnet 5.5 takes over the moment you approve and swarms the build at medium effort
Fable 5.1 reads the full session, every tool call included, and only speaks up at three points:

→ before the plan locks: is this the right approach?
→ when the same error comes back: is the plan wrong or the code?
→ before "done": what did the plan promise that the diff skipped?

Fable 5.1 reviews. Sonnet 5.5 builds. Opus 5.5 plans

Jev engineering is the same move one layer down: the forks that need no thinker (which file, which tool, retry or stop) go to Jev in under half a second, and the big model only sees the ones that split

Plan on Opus. Build on Sonnet. Keep Fable on call.

- the full tree
> Opus 5.5 on high owns plan mode
> Sonnet 5.5 on medium takes execution after you approve
> worker edits and runs the migration
> tester runs the suite
> docs updates the API reference
> all three on Sonnet 5.5 at medium effort
> Fable 5.1 on call as the advisor across both phases

paste the tree and this prompt into Claude Code ↓

"Rebuild my Claude Code setup around this tree:

1. Check ~/.claude/agents and .claude/agents for subagents that already fit worker, tester and docs.

> Draft new ones only for missing roles
> Give each model: sonnet, effort: medium
> Skip any that pin a different model and list them

3. Find anything that breaks the split (an availableModels list without opus, CLAUDE_CODE_EFFORT_LEVEL, CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_ADVISOR_TOOL, DISABLE_TELEMETRY). Report them, change nothing

4. Add one rule to ~/.claude/CLAUDE.md: start every multi-file task in plan mode, and consult the advisor before the plan is approved, when an error repeats, and before calling a long task done
