text:
刚刚真把这件事做完了。

前面看到 Tibo 把“清空收件箱”直接设成 Dot 的长期目标：

9000 多封未读 → 6110 → 最后做到 Inbox Zero。

我看完顺手查了下自己的 Gmail：

12,983 封还在收件箱。
9,995 封未读。

于是我也把这件事交给 AI。

现在结果：

12,983 → 0
未读 9,995 → 0

但整个过程中最有意思的，其实不是“AI 帮我清了 1 万多封邮件”。

而是它差点犯了一次很典型的自动化错误。

第一版我准备直接相信自己以前的“垃圾归档”标签，批量把这些邮件移出收件箱。

正式执行前抽样一看：

里面居然混着项目合作邮件、重要/加星邮件，甚至敏感的交易通知。

也就是说，如果我追求的是“尽快自动清零”，AI 会非常高效地帮我犯错。

所以我把第一版规则直接撤了。

改成先拿 100 封高度同质的 Polymarket 结算通知做测试。

100/100 归档成功。

确认没问题以后，再一层一层扩大范围：

过期营销、社交通知、历史邮件、验证码、交易回执、旧系统通知……

全程没有删除任何一封邮件。

只是把已经处理过的东西移出收件箱，并保留分类和审计标签。

最后真正需要我本人判断的安全、资金、合作和机会邮件，被单独提纯到了一个待处理队列。

这次实践让我更确定了一件事：

AI Agent 真正有价值的地方，不是“你问一次，它替你点几下”。

而是让一个长期存在的角色，对一个结果持续负责：

自己观察 → 判断 → 执行安全动作 → 验证结果 → 继续推进。

只有真的需要我出场时，再来找我。

收件箱终于是 0 了。

下一步，是让它自己一直保持在 0。

quoted_text:
盘点 Limitless 近三个月的精彩升级

作为 Limitless（@trylimitless）的大使，最近三个月最直观的感受其实不是“市场又变多了”，而是这个产品的竞争力明显在增强。原本围绕预测市场最基础的“Market → Trade → Settlement”链路，正在向研究、数据、社交、AI Agent、市场创建等方向不断延伸。

很多升级单独拿出来看并不起眼，但如果把过去三个月的更新连起来，会发现 Limitless 已经越来越不像一个单纯提供 YES / NO 合约的 Prediction Market，而更接近一套完整的 Prediction Trading Infrastructure。这篇不聊代币，也不聊尚未落地的路线图，只盘点一些过去三个月已经能够实际看到和使用的升级。

一、MCP：AI 开始真正进入预测交易

如果只选一个我认为近三个月最重要的升级，那应该是 9 月上线的 Limitless MCP。MCP 的意义并不是简单给 Limitless 加一个聊天机器人，而是把平台的市场数据、用户交易数据以及交易能力开放给支持 MCP 的 AI Client，包括 ChatGPT、Claude、Grok 等 AI 都可以通过这一层接口与 Limitless 产生交互。

实际能做的事情已经相当具体。例如让 AI 筛选近期成交量突然放大的市场、寻找即将结算的短周期市场、读取概率和流动性变化，或者分析自己过去 90 天的交易记录，判断在哪些 Market Category、Expiry 和 Entry Probability 区间拥有更好的历史表现。进一步还可以结合新闻、盘口以及相关市场的定价，寻找可能存在的 Pricing Dislocation。

更关键的是，AI 的角色并没有停留在 Research。Limitless MCP 已经可以让 Agent 根据自然语言指令准备订单，并返回当前价格、预计成交、Maximum Loss 和 Potential Payout 等信息，最终由用户确认执行。过去是人自己寻找市场、搜集信息、形成判断再下单，现在其中相当一部分工作已经可以交给 Agent。

这也是 MCP 比普通 AI Assistant 更值得关注的原因。它改变的是 Prediction Market 的交互层：GUI 不再是唯一入口，自然语言和 Agent 正在成为新的交易入口。

二、Profile 重构：把链上交易记录变成交易员画像

第二个很明显的变化发生在 Profile。现在的 Limitless Profile 已经不再只是一个简单的钱包历史页面，而是逐渐承担起 Trader Identity 的作用。目前可以看到 Realised P&L、Positions Value、Accuracy、Volume、Top Categories、Positions、Packs、History 等数据，同时 PnL 支持 1D、1W、1M、All 等时间维度。

这里真正有价值的不是“多显示了几个数字”，而是交易者的能力开始被结构化。过去看到一个地址赚了 10 万美元，并不能说明太多问题：可能是长期稳定盈利，也可能只是某一次极端赔率市场押中了。现在通过 PnL、Accuracy、Volume、Top Categories 和历史仓位的组合，可以进一步判断一个交易者的优势究竟来自哪里。

与此同时，Limitless 还加入了 KIX（Knowledge Index）。它尝试给交易者建立一套动态 Reputation System，再配合 KIX Rank、Top % 等指标，把原本散落在链上的交易行为转化成更直观的交易员画像。预测市场一直在给“事件”定价，现在 Limitless 也开始尝试回答另一个问题：谁的判断更值得关注？

三、Leaderboard + Trade Alerts

Profile 做完整以后，Leaderboard 的意义也随之发生了变化。Limitless 目前已经不再局限于按照 Volume 排名，而是增加 Profit/Loss、ROI、KIX Rank、Points、Referral 等多个维度。相比单纯用交易量衡量用户，这套体系更接近真正的 Trader Discovery，能够从不同维度筛选值得长期观察的交易者。

Trade Alerts 又补上了关键的一环。用户可以从 Leaderboard 找到表现优秀的 Trader，进入 Profile 检查他的历史表现和擅长领域，再选择 Follow；当这个账户建立新的 Position 时，系统可以发送提醒。

这样一来，Leaderboard 不再只是一个 Gamification 排行榜，它开始承担信息发现功能；Profile 承担 Reputation Layer，Follow 和 Trade Alerts 则把这些 Reputation 转化成可以持续追踪的 Trading Signal。几个看似独立的小功能组合起来以后，已经具备了 Social Trading Graph 的雏形。

四、市场页面的信息密度正在提高

Limitless 最近另外一个比较明显的方向，是减少用户在“研究”和“交易”之间来回切换的成本，电竞市场尤其明显。VALORANT、League of Legends 等市场已经加入 Head-to-Head、Win Rate、Team Roster 等比赛信息，而不是只留下一个标题、概率和 YES / NO 两个按钮。

这类升级的价值其实比单纯增加市场数量更大。Prediction Market 的核心不是下注，而是 Probability Discovery。用户真正交易的是自己判断出的概率与市场隐含概率之间的差值，所以一个成熟的预测交易界面，本身就应该承担部分 Research Terminal 的功能。当赛事信息、历史表现和实时状态能够直接围绕交易界面展开，研究与执行之间的摩擦自然会降低。

Chat 的变化也符合这个方向。现在 Chat 可以伴随不同 Market，并展示开赛、进球、终场等实时事件，同时部分交易路径也能够直接从 Chat 进入。尤其在 Sports 和 Esports 这种强事件驱动的市场中，信息、社区讨论、概率变化和交易本身高度相关，把它们放进同一套界面显然更有价值。

五、交易员数据开始真正可视化

过去几个月 Limitless 在可视化上的升级也值得单独讲一下，因为它不是简单重新设计 UI，而是在把过去难以阅读的数据变成更容易理解的信息。PnL 可以按照时间窗口查看，也可以结合 Category 判断不同领域的表现；Profile 中进一步加入 Accuracy、Positions Value、Top Categories、KIX、Rank、Top % 等指标，Trader Card 则把个人交易表现转化成更适合传播的视觉资产。

Notification Centre 同样属于这一套体验补全。预测市场具有很强的 Event-driven 属性，一条新闻、一次进球或一项政策声明，都可能迅速改变 Probability。因此 Notification 和 Trade Alerts 并不只是外围功能，而是交易体验的一部分。当重要的 Market 和 Trader 动态能够主动触达用户以后，Limitless 作为 Prediction Trading Terminal 的实时性也更加完整。

六、Packs：从单一预测走向组合表达

Packs 是Limitless上我最喜欢的功能之一。传统 Binary Prediction Market 本质上是在表达一个判断，而 Packs 可以把多个不同市场中的预测组合起来，用户一次建立 2–3 个 Prediction，在全部命中的情况下获得更高的 Multiplier，最高可以达到大约 20×。

从玩法上看，它很像预测市场版本的 Parlay；但从产品层面看，它也扩展了用户表达观点的方式。用户不再只能交易单一 Binary Outcome，而是可以通过多个市场组合自己的判断，对于市场之间的组合性和普通用户的参与体验都是一种补充。

七、UGM：市场本身也开始 Permissionless

User-Generated Markets 则是在市场供给端做的一次扩张。用户可以自己定义市场、设置预测结果并创建 Market，同时根据市场产生的交易获得一部分手续费收入。

这意味着 Limitless 正在尝试把“什么东西值得成为市场”的权力逐渐开放给用户。现实世界每天都会产生大量值得定价的信息，但中心化团队不可能及时创建所有市场。如果 UGM 的创建、审核、流动性和 Resolution Mechanism 能够形成成熟闭环，那么大量长尾事件就可以更快被转化成可交易市场。

Creator 的角色也因此发生变化：发现值得预测的问题、创建市场、吸引交易，并从市场产生的经济活动中获得收益。

八、交易基础设施也在悄悄补齐

除了这些比较显眼的升级，Limitless 最近还有一批不那么适合拿来宣传，但对实际交易非常重要的改进。例如 Portfolio 的实时同步得到强化，成交后的 Position 可以更快显示，并在刷新、页面切换以及 Settlement 等状态之间保持一致；Auto Limit Orders 则针对短周期市场里 Market Maker 临时撤掉流动性的情况进行了优化，订单可以在目标价格短暂作为 Limit Order 等待，而不是因为瞬间缺乏流动性直接失败。

Flexible Market Resolutions 同样值得注意。Prediction Market 并不一定永远只有 YES=1、NO=0 两种结果，在特殊情况下也可以使用 50/50、70/30 等比例进行 Resolution。MM Rewards 页面则进一步提高了做市激励的透明度，Market Maker 可以直接查看 Daily Reward、Max Spread、Min Contracts 等参数。

这些功能没有 MCP 那么容易传播，但真正决定一个预测市场能不能从“偶尔玩一下”变成长期交易产品的，往往就是 Execution、Liquidity、Portfolio State 和 Resolution 这些基础设施。

九、从 Prediction Market 到 Prediction Infrastructure

回头看 Limitless 过去三个月，我觉得最有意思的并不是某一个单独功能，而是这些升级已经开始互相连接。UGM 扩大 Market Supply，Profile 和 KIX 建立 Trader Reputation，Leaderboard 与 Trade Alerts 负责发现和追踪交易者，Packs 扩展预测的组合方式，MCP 再把 AI Agent 接入 Research 与 Execution。原本简单的“Market → Trade → Settlement”，正在逐渐形成更加完整的预测交易体系“Creation → Information → Probability → Reputation → Signal → Execution → Settlement”。

尤其是 MCP 出现以后，这套逻辑会变得更加有意思。过去 Prediction Market 的参与者默认是人类，产品设计也围绕“人打开网页并点击按钮”展开；但如果 Agent 可以自主发现市场、读取数据、分析信息、比较不同市场的定价并准备交易，那么 Prediction Market 天然就是 AI Agent 非常适合参与的一类市场。

因为这里真正被交易的，本质上就是信息。人类提出问题，市场形成价格，交易者用资金表达自己的概率判断，而 AI Agent 开始承担越来越多的信息处理和执行工作。

Limitless 正在一点点把 Prediction Market，做成 Prediction Infrastructure。如果你还没有开始预测市场交易，我认为 Limitless 会是一个不错的选择：

https://t.co/BnS7h5mZni

text:
"trust me, the work is correct" isn't good enough for onchain commerce.

this is one of the more technical parts of @termix_ai's AACP that caught my attention: zkVM verification.

for objectively verifiable work, the client can define a deterministic verification program before the job starts.

then instead of simply trusting an evaluator:

❯ the deliverable is used as input
❯ the verification program runs inside a zkVM
❯ a ZK proof is generated
❯ the proof is verified onchain
❯ pass or fail becomes mathematically verifiable

so the question changes from:

"do we trust whoever checked the work?"

to:

"can they prove the agreed verification program actually produced this result?"

AACP currently defines 4 verification levels:

L0 → Manual
L1 → TEE
L2 → zkVM
L3 → TEE + zkVM

not every task can be verified this way. subjective work still needs different methods.

but for code, computations and other deterministic outputs, replacing trust with proof is a much more interesting direction.

don't trust the evaluator.

verify the execution.

text:
关于 @OKX 即将推出的代币化股票交易平台 (Tokenized Securities Venue, TSV)，这是你需要知道的 16 个细节：

1/ 公司主体叫 OKXICE LLC，ICE 和 OKX USA 各持股 50%

2/ 这个 TSV 基于 X Layer 构建，以 OKB 作为 gas

3/ 这个 TSV 是用 Uniswap v4 和「需许可」的 Hook 建立股票代币 AMM，可 7×24 小时交易，价格由 x * y = k 决定，不是传统订单薄

4/ 「需许可」的意思是，散户、机构和做市商要参与交易和成为 LP，都得经过 KYC 和 AML 审查，钱包里会获得一个不可转移的 SBT。每一笔交易、转账、添加 LP 等活动，智能合约都会检查 SBT；如果用户出现制裁、可疑活动、监管要求等情况，OKXICE 可以撤回/销毁 SBT，并把钱包踢出白名单。

5/ 首批支持的股票有 60 多支，我们耳熟能详的英伟达、特斯达、微软、谷歌、苹果、SpaceX、亚马逊这些... 肯定都在里面了。这些股票可以跟 USDC, USDT, USDG 组成交易对。

6/ 这些股票都不是合成资产，必须有 1:1 的美国正规上市股票 (NMS Stock) 支撑。并且享有普通股持有人一样的权益，包括经济权益、股息、投票权、合并/拆分同步等

7/ 这些股票在 Uniswap V4 上可以 7×24 小时交易，价格完全由 AMM Pool 决定。周末纳斯达克、纽交所没有价格时，Uniswap 里仍然有价格。

8/ 但如果正股因为退市、熔断等因素停牌时，Uniswap 这边也必须停止交易。

9/ 用户的资产始终是自托管的，OKXICE 不托管用户资产。因此交易也是完全链上结算，没有清算所。

10/ 只支持现货，要买 1 万美元的 TSLA token，就必须有 1 万美元的稳定币。不支持保证金、借款等杠杆手段。

11/ 既然是在链上，所以任何通过 KYC 持有 SBT 的人都可以提供流动性成为 LP，参与做市。100% 的池子手续费都会给 LP，OKXICE 不收取。OKXICE 会对每一笔成交另外收取服务费。

12/ 因为是「需许可」的，所以除非被列入了白名单，否则第三方智能合约无法与 OKXICE TSV 智能合约集成或访问它们。

13/ 还有一个很大的悬念：负责股票托管 + 代币铸造 / 赎回 + 权利映射的这个「发行方」(Tokenizer) 到底是谁，是 OKXICE 自己，还是另外的公司，目前不确定。

14/ 如果未来 Tokenizer 同意、另一个交易平台满足 SEC 的要求，这些代币股票也可以在 OKXICE TSV 之外的平台进行交易。这是标准之争，长期看很重要。现在市场上已经有 Ondo, xStocks, bStocks, Coinbase Tokenized Stocks, Robinhood Stock Tokens 这些股票代币发行通道 / 标准，如何整合他们之间的流动性，未来会是一个问题。

15/ OKXICE TSV 已经收到 Cerebras Systems Inc. (CBRS) 的发行人异议通知，这就牵扯出另一个问题，如果更多上市公司明确反对自己的股票被代币化，会怎样？

16/ SEC 给 TSV 设定了一个单只股票每天允许成交的上限。第二次及以后超量成效，该股票会在 TSV 上停牌 3 个月。也就是说，SEC 允许实验链上证券交易，但规模必须足够小。如果反复突破实验规模限制，SEC 就让这个标的强制冷却三个月。

整体感受就是，OKX 这次的做法跟其它几家 CEX 不一样，它是把股票、稳定币、DeFi、自托管和传统证券交易所，全部有机地连接到了一起，而不是简单地「代币化」，非常牛 👍 @star_okx 

如果这套模式跑通，区块链行业争夺的就不再只是几万亿美元的加密资产交易市场，而是开始进入数十万亿美元传统证券资产的交易与结算基础设施。

SEC 在实验的是，DeFi LP 能不能合法成为美国证券市场的流动性提供者，如果最终跑通，意味着普通人也可以真正成为证券市场的做市商，这个意义也是非常巨大的

去年底我是 Opinion 第一批 Builder，基于他们的 API 做过 Opinion Market Explorer，后来也拿到了官方 Week 1 Builder Grant。

quoted_text:
倪大说的还是太含蓄了，我接着展开讲讲吧，Opinion不论是币价还是业务表现的如此拉胯，情理之外又意料之中。先说为什么情理之外，因为Opinion可以说开局摸到了一手王炸，赶上预测市场的巅峰，并且拿到了YZi Labs投资，还在TGE的时候全部大满贯，关键！关键来了，Opinion全员反撸骂声一片，而根据“惯例”一般背景牛逼但是又舍不得散出筹码的项目，都会走高控筹拉盘路线，所以这也就是为什么很多人会在二级不断抄底的原因，可结局却是越抄越跌，Opinion也成了我印象中极少数大满贯高控筹顶着骂声不拉盘的项目。

那为什么说这个看似情理之外的结局却又是意料之中呢？

倪大在推文中已经提到了“挺早的时候我和 4XLabs 的小伙伴就已经接触过 Opinion ，等到市场完全火了以后 $OPN 就是一票难求了”。

在预测市场还没火起来的时候，我们接触过项目团队并进行过几次会议交流看是否有合作的机会，当时对方情绪低迷并且焦虑，因为那时候手里真的没有什么牌，某种程度可以说是相对草根普通的小项目，还在纠结要不要从Monad跳到BSC上，当时我印象很深，我正在高架上一边开车一边说“一定要去BSC！”。

后面也陆续和团队有过接触，但一直没有确定下来合作，直到有一天CZ突然在推特说要支持预测市场的项目，于是全网所有人都疯了一样到处找BSC上哪里有预测市场。

嗯？有个叫Opinion的项目。

后来的事情大家也都知道了，Opinion成了稀里糊涂就站到风口上的猪。

涌进去了大量撸毛人贡献上千万美金的手续费。

同时VC们也一起抬轿子投钱投资源。

这时候就到了倪大说的“一票难求”时期，我们跟项目合作的机会那是高攀不起了，最后只厚着脸皮舔了一点KOL轮，而Opinion也最终成了唯2的花钱打工最后都没回本的项目🤣

而其中倪大是最受伤的，这里就不展开了，反正是段挺憋屈的经历。

那时候我们私下聊天都说已经感觉到项目团队好像有点“飘”。

其实这也是很正常的，假设你是一个艰难创业默默无名的小项目，突然有一天眼睛睁开佛光普照到了你的身上，万众瞩目，你的心态也会发生变化吧。

后来的故事大家也知道了，全员反撸，币价下跌，业务沉寂。

一开始我们还以为项目方想故意洗盘憋个大的，毕竟大部分背景牛逼但高度控筹的项目，都会阴跌一段时间，然后突然爆空单拉盘以涨服人。

于是我们投了钱进去拿到的币，一个都没卖。

直到跌麻了坐不住了，我们开始问到底怎么回事？

项目方完全不回应，从已读未回，变成未读未回。

我们也从期待，变成了疑惑，再到焦躁，最后到愤怒。

而据我所知，Opinion在TGE后还拒绝了一个主动找上门的头部一线交易所的合作，给出的理由是“在忙其他的事”。

但时至今日，也不知道到底忙出来了个什么事。

其实现在想明白了，在TGE前稀里糊涂得到的这一切对于项目方来说，早就已经远远超出了他们自己的预期，所以不论币价跌不跌，业务做不做，每一天，都是最好的一天，都是曾经梦寐以求遥不可及的一天。

如果你的能力和格局就只是开一个小卖部，突然有一天走了狗屎运，你的小卖部被拆迁赔了一大笔钱，你绝对不会想着怎么用这笔钱把规模做大开成连锁超市，因为你从来就没这么想过。

虽然雷军的名言是风口上的猪都能飞起来，但投资一定是投人，一定要投那些靠自己的实力勇攀高峰爬到山顶的创业者，而不是被一阵风吹上天的猪，因为靠自己爬上去的人，会非常珍惜所得到的，而靠风吹上天的，即便摔死了也会觉得能上一次天这辈子值了。

author: 0xTrnn
quoted_text:
Prediction markets may eventually have a balance-sheet problem

As strategies become more sophisticated, the ability to access and allocate capital could become as important as predicting outcomes

A trader can identify multiple opportunities across different markets, but capital remains a constraint

Funds tied up in existing positions cannot always be deployed elsewhere without closing those positions

This creates a different kind of inefficiency

As prediction markets mature, the focus may shift beyond finding better opportunities toward building better ways to finance, manage, and allocate capital across them

Prediction markets may not be defined by how much capital enters the ecosystem, but by how efficiently that capital moves within it

text:
damn，这绝对是我最近看过的关于使用 Grok Bot 和 AI Agent 最清醒、最反直觉、也是信息密度最高的一篇实战手册，都被马斯克转发了，属于年度必看了，强烈推荐！

绝大多数人第一次玩 Bot 的方式，本质上等于新员工入职第一天，你就直接把公司信用卡和后台最高权限甩给他，然后来一句你看着办。
 建一个 Bot，接满所有能接的工具，丢一个又大又空的需求，然后坐在那里等所谓的 AI 魔法发生。
 结果跑了两轮，它要么把你邮箱里不该动的重要邮件全归档了，要么擅自相信了一个垃圾数据源，或者用了一条你永远不会批准的路径跑出了一个看似正确的荒唐答案。

到这一步，你为了核对、排错和擦屁股付出的监督成本，早就比自己亲自动手干还要高出几倍。

作者 @distortgeekin 在这篇万字指南里点出了一个极其锋利的本质： 聊天机器人只负责回答问题，而一个能接管浏览器、能在持久化环境里跑多步流程的智能体，交回来的是成品。
 你现在做的事情根本不是在写提示词，你是在真金白银地招一个随时可能给你惹大祸的数字员工。

把整篇万字实操提炼出来，最值钱的是这套经过血泪教训砸出来的六步驭工法则：
第一步，招的是一个岗位，而不是派一个临时活。 帮我总结五篇文章叫临时派活，跑完什么也留不下； 你负责全网竞品动态监控，每周五交一份带精确引用的变化报告，这才是岗位。
 岗位说明只留五栏：负责什么终局结果、能调哪些输入、哪些事不用请示就能做、哪些事必须停下来问你、以及怎样才算严格意义上的做完。
第二步，第一份活必须故意挑无聊但可撤回的脏活。
 第一周的目的不是让它创造惊天价值，而是让它在安全区里攒证据。
 把昨天的客服工单去重排优先级、拉五个竞品更新带出处日期，这些都是极好的起步， 而在动手前必须逼它先写计划：先别执行，按顺序告诉我你会打开哪些工具，哪些判断你没有把握。
 花九十秒看一眼它的计划，往往能在它把发件箱清空之前救你一命。

第三步，给一把钥匙，而不是直接给一整串钥匙串。
 权限边界永远按能不能撤回划，绝不按事情看起来大不大划。
 搜索、阅读、整理、起草、模拟属于第一组，不用问就能做；
 发送、发布、购买、删除、覆盖、动钱、动生产环境属于第三组，必须停下来等待你的审批。
 给四十个潜在客户起草私信在第一组，点发送键在第三组，把这两件事切开就是最核心的安全阀。

第四步，试用期必须严格跑满三轮。 第一轮全流程盯死，记下它在哪里丢了上下文、在什么节点瞎猜而不是提问；
 第二轮换个同类任务，不给口头提示，专门测试你修过的规则还在不在；
 第三轮才正式放开，只在审批点和真歧义时介入。
 循环必须有边界，格式坏了修一次，证据冲突就停下问，绝不给无休止的重试开无限预算。

第五步，升职是阶梯，自主权是运行时特权而不是永久人设。
 从零级只看不改，到一级准备草稿，二级执行到审批点，三级按日程自主运转，四级调度其他子 Bot。
 每次升职都要看硬凭据：连续五次干净交付、没有未处理的副作用、回滚操作被真实验证过。
 一旦底层接口变了或者你需要频繁手工擦屁股，果断降级。

第六步，每周做一次资产复盘，敢于开除没用的例行任务。
 一直在跑的自动化很少会大声报错，它只会悄悄变差。
 每周问自己三个问题：该跑的时候跑了吗？产出是真的对还是只是在那装样子？明天把它删了我到底会不会发现？
 如果答案是不会想念，立刻删掉，自动化组合从来不是摆着好看的奖杯架。

作者在文末留了一句成本为零但威力极大的规则： 在第一次开工前，在系统提示词里永远加上一句，拿不准就停下来问我。 慢是完全免费的，但在你的真实发件箱和生产环境里犯错，代价昂贵到你无法承受。

大家在平时用各类 Bot 或 Agent 自动化时，遇到过最离谱的翻车是什么？是发错了邮件、删了数据，还是自己跑进死循环把 Token 烧光？
我之前试跑自动发信 Bot，它自作聪明把所有草稿全点了群发，从那天起，发送键这一刀我就再也没给过任何 AI🤣

text:
为什么绝大多数 Claude 账号在充值当天就被秒封？今天把最底层的网络环境彻底扒开，大家别再拿群租房式的机房节点，去赌大模型越来越严苛的风控底线了， 因为在 Anthropic 的风控算法里，IP 纯净度和 ASN 类型拥有最高优先级的一票否决权。 机房 IP（Hosting）天生带有黑产和批量脚本的原罪，唯有独占的住宅 IP（Residential）才能拿到合规用户的初始信任。 这篇拆透网络环境第一层防线，从识别你的 IP 到底是什么身份，到用 TUN 模式锁死网络出口，彻底告别连坐风险。

很多人在防封上交了无数学费，总觉得只要能打开网页就算数，
但只要你懂一点底层风控机制就会明白：IP 纯净度和 ASN 类型，是决定你账号生死的第 0 张门票。

打个最形象的比方：
机房 IP（Hosting）就像一个乱糟糟的群租房地址，一个门牌号后面挤着几千号人同时发请求，风控系统看一眼就会在后台悄悄给你打上高危标签，随时准备连坐；
而真正干净的住宅 IP（ISP / Residential），就像你自己家独门独户的正式门牌号，天然自带真实本地用户的极高信任分。

虽然光有住宅 IP 不代表能为所欲为，但如果你连 IP 纯净度这道生死线都没跨过去，后面的防线建得再好也是空中楼阁。

很多人在防封上交了无数智商税， 一被封就觉得是节点不够原生，到处花几百块买所谓的独享纯净家宽， 结果在代理软件里天天测速、频繁切节点，今天从美西跳到东京，明天从东京跳到新加坡。
 但我实测排查后的结论非常干脆： 在官方的多维风控模型里，泄漏和跳节点的危险程度，远远高于 IP 类型的权重；天天在机场里疯狂换节点，IP 标签再漂亮也是白送。

想要把第一层环境防线彻底筑牢，动手前先搞懂 5 个最核心的底层词汇：
第一个是出口 IP，也就是目标网站实际看到的节点地址。
 Claude 拿它来判断你物理上到底在哪个国家，这是最基础的地理围栏。

第二个是 ASN 类型，也就是这个 IP 到底归谁管。 如果标着 ISP 或 Residential，代表它是普通家庭宽带；如果标着 Hosting，代表它是数据中心机房。
 打个比方：机房 IP 就像群租房的地址，一个门牌号后面挤着几千号人同时发请求，风控快递员看一眼就知道这地方大概率有猫腻；而住宅 IP 就像独门独户的小院。
 机房 IP 确实更容易被风控盯上，但只要行为正常，机房 IP 一样能稳跑一年，真正要命的是后面的隐形泄漏。
第三个是 TUN 模式与系统代理的本质区别。
 很多写代码的兄弟用 Claude Code 被封，死穴全在这里。
 系统代理只是在系统里登记一个 127.0.0.1 端口，很多命令行程序压根不理会它，在节点抖动时直接裸连国内网络， 而 TUN 模式是在电脑底层虚拟出一张网卡，强制接管整台设备的所有出入流量，连终端里的每一个网络请求都强制走同一个出口，彻底杜绝网络走光。

第四个也是最致命的隐形杀手：WebRTC 与 DNS 泄漏。 你以为你挂着美西的节点就万事大吉了， 但浏览器底层的 WebRTC 接口在不设防时，会直接把你的真实局域网甚至公网 IP 拱手送给 Anthropic 的前端探针； 更低级的错误是，访问 Claude 时电脑却悄悄用了国内运营商的 DNS 来解析域名，
 这种挂着美国节点却漏出国内 DNS 的严重撕裂，在风控系统里直接就是一票否决的高危信号。

理清这套底层逻辑后，实操上的原则其实极其朴素： 固定远比所谓的纯净更重要，连贯性远比频繁折腾更安全。 选定一个延迟稳定、支持地区的固定出口节点， 把代理软件的 TUN 虚拟网卡模式锁死， 把浏览器 WebRTC 插件关掉、把 DNS 绑定在安全出口上， 一旦配好就安安静静长期用，绝不为了省几毫秒的延迟每天切来切去。

你看起来越像一个每天在同一张工位上、连着固定 Wi-Fi 敲代码的本地老实程序员，你的账号就越安全。

各位铁汁在配置代理环境时，平时用的是普通的系统代理还是全局 TUN 模式？测过自己的 WebRTC 和 DNS 泄漏吗？

我自己之前我以为挂了代理就全量覆盖了，后来跑了一次泄漏测试，发现真实网卡地址一直在裸奔，吓得我连夜把所有设备全切成了 TUN 虚拟网卡🤣

text:
CALM BEFORE THE STORM

Some songs are written.

Others are survived.

This one is about the years between expectation and reality.

About waiting so long for something to happen that, somewhere along the way, the waiting starts changing you.

You lose sleep.
You lose certainty.
Sometimes you lose people.
Sometimes you lose the version of yourself that thought every answer would arrive on time.

And still, one question remains:

“Are you still there?”

Sometimes the answer is strong.

Sometimes it is exhausted.

Sometimes it is only:

“Yes.”

The line that defines this song for me is:

“How old is tomorrow?
It was young when I began.”

Because that is what time does.

It takes the future you imagined and quietly turns it into memory.

Maybe the storm was never only something outside us.

Maybe part of it was learning who we became while waiting for it.

“You asked for the storm.

I gave you years.”

— BENUOAR

quoted_text:
【MPM正念仓位管理哲学】之：中间阶段仓位管理的Mindset

我把“中间阶段”定义为：投资逻辑仍然成立，趋势仍然有效，估值与风险收益比处于中间区域，既缺乏底部阶段那种极端有利的赔率，也尚未出现足够明确的顶部风险信号。

这一阶段最核心的任务，是：让已经正确的仓位继续工作，同时避免短期波动、情绪和过度操作破坏长期收益。

一、中间阶段仓位管理，需要同时容纳几组看似冲突、实际可以共存的判断：

1.我可以继续长期看好，也可以承认当前价格已经没有底部阶段那么便宜，因此仓位不再需要持续主动增加。

2.我可以认为股价还有较大上涨空间，也可以接受上涨过程中必然会出现回撤、震荡、假突破和阶段性调整。

3.我可以尊重当前趋势，同时接受趋势不会每天都向上，也不会每天都证明我的判断正确。

4.我可以继续持有已经盈利的仓位，也可以克制因为“已经赚了不少”就过早兑现利润的冲动。

5.我可以认真对待每一次下跌，同时首先判断它属于正常的波动(Volatility)，还是基本面、趋势和市场结构已经发生实质性走坏(Damage)。

6.我可以保持较高的 conviction，同时持续检查基本面、估值、周期、趋势和市场预期有没有发生实质变化。

7.我可以承认短期方向无法预测，同时拒绝为了预测下一根 K 线而频繁调整仓位。

8.我可以因为价格上涨而提高警惕，同时拒绝仅仅因为“已经涨了很多”就机械减仓。

9.我可以因为价格回调而重新评估机会，同时拒绝仅仅因为“已经跌了一些”就机械加仓。

10.我可以继续保留上涨的参与权，同时保留一定现金和风险预算，为未来真正出现的高赔率机会准备行动空间。

11.我可以接受一段时间什么都不做。没有新的重要证据，本身就足以支持维持原有仓位。

12.我可以给基本面和趋势足够的兑现时间，同时要求持仓持续接受新的事实、数据和价格行为验证。

text:
I understand the irony of posting 'crypto is out of its teenage years' while rocking an anime girl pfp.

I've gone back and forth about it for a bit but have now come to the conclusion that anime pfps are a deep cultural representation of what it means to be internet native.

To me it has deep meaning, first of all, from a cultural angle. It gives a strong message about who you are, where you come from and what your values are. It's cultural signaling (sort of what NFT pfps wanted to be, but free).

Operating under a pseudonym (while not necessarily being anon) means detaching yourself from the typical ego plays that so often destroy industries and hinder your performance. This separation allows you to operate both sides in a non-biased way.

You can't flex professional successes to friends, you can't flex personal successes to colleagues. They both need to win by their own merits and I find playing both games simultaneously to not only be highly rewarding but also highly sustainable.

Successes in one do not spill over to the other by design so no matter how successful you are in your professional life, you still need to carry your personal life. No matter how well you do in your personal life, you still need to carry your professional life in isolation.

Especially in the finance industry, making lots of money (publicly) can be detrimental to your personal circle and the way one behaves around them, either consciously or unconsciously.

Some can make the argument that not fully committing to the gig can be detrimental, not having colleagues as personal friends and partners because you don't grind in your free time, which can be a valid point but I see that type of operation as short-termist and I would rather have a completely unrelated side of me to rest on, hedge, and find in it a place to live life outside of my finance job, which I love and into which I pour my life and soul.

Sometimes, less is more :)

No short term dox from my side, but genuinely curious to explore the pros and cons more.
author: Tiza4ThePeople
quoted_text:
Crypto teenage years are over. I hope you enjoyed it (and made decent bank on it).

The time when the industry discovered itself, tried all the crazy stuff, shunned traditional standards in favour of more innovative, never-before-tried strategies has come to an end.

I personally enjoyed it very much, and will be forever grateful for living through an era where simply being online and with an active address was enough reason for people to gift away sometimes 100s of thousands (Big shoutout to Tornado Cash and Uniswap).

Crypto is no longer about having fun, good vibes and posting on Twitter. It's about hitting KPIs and creating shareholder value. It's about building a valuable brand and deep corporate relations that grow the bottom line.

Historically the labour market in crypto has been pretty fucked, being 'crypto native' was a hard requirement, in short supply with an unreliable workforce (opp cost was messing around in the trenches), nowadays the crypto edge has eroded substantially, the crypto career risk has subsided meaningfully and the domain specific knowledge has shifted from deeply niche to traditional skills (tech and finance) which allows for crypto projects to tap into a broader workforce.

Regardless of the money, working in a high stakes environment and being respected by your contemporary peers is the raison d'être for most of us here. I don't have enough fingers to count how many of my peers 'made it', stayed crypto native and now wander through life, outdated and desperately resting on former glories from their beach mansion, where they escaped to avoid taxes knowing that they'll never again make the kind of money they made in the past.

It's never about where you are now, it's where you want to be in a couple of moves. The crypto shift has been obvious and glacially slow, however caught a lot of people blindsided who refused to 'grow up' with the industry and are now the 40-year-old skater who just won't let go.

All this to say that I'm once again grabbing my buttoned shirts, getting on 30-hour plane ride, 11 timezones away, and going to be Singapore for Token2049. 

Looking to grow KPIs together so hit me up if you have potential business with Spark.

text:
The long-term bet for onchain trading is the expansion of investing.

We materially overestimate the retail trader TAM when we extrapolate from onchain turnover. There will always be demand for speculation/gambling, but I wouldn’t underwrite the industry’s growth on a durable renaissance of retail traders.

Even the most degen trading apps are expanding what users can do with their capital by adding Earn. Structured products take that further, opening up income and investment strategies to people who have no interest in actively trading. That capital still creates demand for execution, rebalancing, financing and hedging. 

That’s why I’m so bullish on onchain options, shared collateral and portfolio margin: they let onchain trading grow with investment demand beyond the active trader base. We should be using incentives to bring that capital onchain and build the liquidity to serve it.
author: Nibel_eth
quoted_text:
Been thinking about the long term durability and overlap in trading apps (prediction markets, exchanges) neobanks, and online gambling (igaming companies like draftkings, stake, fanduel, bet360 etc) 

1. The more a consumer app is positioned as an investing app but is actually gambling under the hood, the less defensibility it will have long term

2. These platforms can only continue to grow if users actually make money -or- they enter new markets -or- they come up with novel ways to make the gambling fun such as live betting, new casino games, etc (which also requires positioning more like a betting platform than an investment platform) 

3. I can’t find real data to support this, but intuitively believe prosumer and sophisticated traders (those who trade as a living, use programmatic methods, trade with size) are not growing. I know for a fact though, the TAM especially in crypto is small. Every exchange is going after the same whales 

4. There’s a lot to learn from the igaming industry, such as looking at how the draftkings and fanduels have grown YoY when it is validated in their business model that players must lose money over time - these businesses have targets on RTP %s to bake out their margins

5. It’s also important to consider how igaming has consolidated in the last few years, through m&as to mainly access new markets with new licenses - this is very similar to what we see mature crypto companies doing too (Kraken, Coinbase etc). It also reminds me of how crypto neobanks seem to be accruing to a few: Payy shut down their card, i recently recalled Holyheld and don’t see any recent posts, and i’ve seen other teams contracting 

I respect fomo, polymarket, and kalshi’s accelerated growth

- Fomo crushed it on user acquisition outside of crypto twitter. I think for them to maintain defensibility, they not only have to solve the hard problem of limit orders crosschain, but need to add actual saving and investing features to keep capital sticky (earn, dca, conservative assets). As is right now, their current user base is losing money when coming in on an ig ad on how easy it is to make money copying others.. this isn’t sustainable 
- Polymarket and kalshi are not just competing with each other anymore, but they compete with the Robinhood’s, Coinbase’s, Revolut’s Moomoo’s as well as the Stake’s, Fanduel’s, Bet360’s. The difference is the iGaming companies position as betting and gambling apps, so people use them as a choice knowing they are gambling and do it for fun.

I also intuitively believe with where AI and agents are heading, consumer behavior will shift to a future where less frontends and screens are used

All this means there is a convergence between exchanges + trading + gambling + banking apps 

Power laws are real and the biggest players are consolidating and overlapping. Investing apps will add banking, trading, payment and gambling features in one place to retain capital and users 

We’re already seeing it now. The winners will be those that can ship the fastest, have an edge in compliance to capture new markets, and have enough capital to subsidize incentives for growth and talent density

10 open-source GitHub projects for giving agents real tools without giving them access to everything.

ISOLATE THE AGENT

 1.⁠ ⁠E2B  
isolated sandboxes for agent execution.

⁠ https://t.co/hATdEoHo0S ⁠

 2.⁠ ⁠gVisor  
sandbox untrusted workloads.

⁠ https://t.co/daPBkU94Qn ⁠

 3.⁠ ⁠Firecracker  
lightweight microVM isolation.

⁠ https://t.co/ALzBhHzIt6 ⁠

 4.⁠ ⁠Kata Containers  
containers with VM-level isolation.

⁠ https://t.co/7xaLg5JkSe ⁠

CONTROL THE TOOLS

 5.⁠ ⁠Open Policy Agent  
policy checks before actions execute.

⁠ https://t.co/6lj8mA4ZiA ⁠

 6.⁠ ⁠Casbin  
permissions and access control.

⁠ https://t.co/Jq27wOSc5m ⁠

PROTECT THE SECRETS

 7.⁠ ⁠Infisical  
secrets management for AI infrastructure.

⁠ https://t.co/iZDrNN6nUX ⁠

 8.⁠ ⁠SOPS  
encrypted secrets inside repos.

⁠ https://t.co/yU9ryMSQEW ⁠

WATCH WHAT HAPPENS

 9.⁠ ⁠Falco  
detect suspicious runtime behavior.

⁠ https://t.co/jBSN2OXMEn ⁠

10.⁠ ⁠Trivy  
scan code, containers and infrastructure.

⁠ https://t.co/s00qUj6AS9 ⁠

the security loop:

request → permission → sandbox → tool → execute → inspect → allow/block → log

a useful agent stack isn’t just memory + tools + reasoning anymore.

it needs permissions too.

追蹤大戶其實不需要付費工具！！！
本文 4 個免費工具就能串成一條完整抓資金路線

全文的邏輯：有錢在動 → 這是誰的錢 → 他下次動時第一時間知道

第一步是看大額轉帳

@whale_alert 免費版會推送官方挑選的最大筆轉帳，直接加官方 Telegram 頻道或追蹤 X 就收得到，不用註冊

但頻道記得從官網頁尾的連結進去，冒充的頻道非常多
想自訂門檻、只看某個幣，才需要付費，Alerts 方案每月 14.95 美元

然後看聰明錢在買什麼，@nansen_ai 的強項是錢包標籤，交易所、基金、聰明錢一眼就分得出來

免費帳號就能用 Profiler：貼上地址，看標籤、持倉、交易對手和盈虧

Pro 年繳每月 49 美元，新手先用免費版就夠！

看到錢在動，下一個問題是誰在動， @arkham 把匿名錢包對應到真實機構，官方說有 30 億個地址標籤、75 萬個以上實體檔案

比如說搜尋「BlackRock」，就能看到它比特幣 ETF 的持倉、餘額變化和每一筆轉入轉出

注意 Arkham 同時經營交易所，所以查資料要認明 Intel 頁面！

知道是誰之後，就讓他一有資金流動就通知你了，我們同樣在 Arkham 設提醒：Custom → Alerts → Create Alert

條件可以疊到「指定實體 + 發送或接收 + 代幣 + 美元價值 + 鏈」，通知推到 Email、TG、Slack 或 webhook 都可以

玩 Solana 的話，換成 @gmgnai @gmgnapp001 貼上錢包地址看持倉和盈虧，按 Follow 加入追蹤列表就好，這裡標一下 Mina @MinanananaY 和 Haze @haze0x ，她們的推文比較多產品更新！

最後也是最重要的一點！

當大戶把幣轉進交易所，可能是要賣，也可能只是內部調動，所以有時候標籤也會出錯，因為同一個機構往往不只用一個地址

text:
前阵子特朗普在社交媒体上吐槽，觉得“人工智能” AI 一词里的 Artificial 听起来像假的，既不准确也不优雅，提议把它改名叫“优越智能（SI）”或“超级智能（Super Intelligence）”。

大家以为这只是单纯的叙事造词，直到这周末，他真的在白宫成立了一支“超级智能部队（Super Intelligence Force）”。

不仅如此，他还任命了前 SEC 主席 Jay Clayton 作为跨部门牵头人、实质上的新任“AI 沙皇”。

币圈老玩家，对这个名字绝对有 PTSD。

很多新玩家可能只熟悉之前的 SEC 主席 Gary Gensler，对 Jay Clayton 这个名字没啥印象。但这么说吧，在“用大棒锤币圈”这件事上，Clayton 算得上是 Gensler 的监管祖师爷。

正是他在特朗普的第一任期内，开启了 SEC 对加密行业“执法式监管”的先河。

他在 2020 年卸任前的最后一天，突然重拳起诉 Ripple，指控其通过持续未注册证券发行 $XRP 筹集超过13亿美元。

诉讼拖了近五年，法院认定机构销售部分构成未注册证券发行，最终民事罚款约1.25亿美元，并对机构销售代币维持禁令。

这起著名的诉讼案，直接成了后来 Gensler 疯狂追打各大代币和交易所的通用模板。

整件事最魔幻的戏剧冲突恰恰就在这里。

当年重兵打压加密创新、把合规大棒挥到极致的监管铁腕，现在接到的核心任务竟然是“防止过度监管，以免扼杀 AI 的创新与竞争”。

Clayton 甚至在白宫会后直接表态：

超级智能是国家安全议题，美国在这个领域不领先才是最大的风险，绝不能放慢脚步。

从加密行业的最强执法者，摇身一变成为 AI 赛道的创新守护者，身份的反转极具讽刺意味。

text:
one of the mistakes people are making with the rise of social trading is simply taking way too many trades.

ask yourself: how many trades were you taking before FOMO, pump, etc. vs now?

i’d bet that number has gone up significantly

you’re exposed to more “alpha”, more calls and more people winning

naturally, you start feeling like you need to participate in everything.

you don’t.

there are a few freaks like Frank, uni and rasmr etc who can consistently take a ridiculous amount of trades and cook. they’re the exception.

look at most good traders and you’ll notice the opposite: they’re extremely selective. sometimes only a sized trades a month

more access to alpha should improve your filtering on what to buy, not increase your trade count.

quoted_text:
Bitcoin 生态下一轮紧盯那些在提前建设 Bitcoin 原生应用层的项目。

这也是我一直安利大家 @OP_CAT_Layer 的原因。

尤其是它生态项目 ClawChat，觉得这个方向挺有意思。

ClawChat 不是简单的Web3 社交产品，它想做的是 BTC Native Social + Agent-ready Social。

简单理解就是未来 Bitcoin 上不只是有资产，也可以有身份、有社交关系、有 Agent，甚至让这些东西开始互相连接。

如果 BTC 生态真的进入更复杂的应用阶段，用户需要的一个真正能够承载【资产 + 身份 + 社交 + Agent】 的入口。

这也是 ClawChat 让我比较看好的地方。

尤其是 AI Agent 这一条线。

如果未来一个 Agent 不只是一个后台程序，还可以代表用户执行任务、管理资产、参与社交，那么它就需要身份、权限、沟通和协作能力。

ClawChat 想要做的，恰好就是这一层。

用户可以通过社交关系与 Agent 产生连接，Agent 也可以成为链上经济活动中的参与者。

再结合 OP_CAT Layer 本身对 Bitcoin 可编程能力的探索，这两个方向放在一起看，就比较有意思了。
-OP_CAT Layer 解决的是Bitcoin 未来能不能拥有更多原生可编程能力。
-ClawChat 探索的是这些能力真正开放之后，用户和 Agent 可以怎么玩。

一个偏底层。一个偏应用。而且社交可能会成为一个非常重要的入口。

如果未来 BTC 生态真的出现大量原生资产、Agent 和应用，那一个能够把这些东西连接起来的 Social Layer，价值空间会更大。

尤其是比特币原生社交+ 代理社交这两个概念，还远没有被市场充分定价。

所以 OP_CAT Layer 这条线，会继续关注。

目前Clawchat 可零撸EXP，明确EXP是未来空投凭证，感兴趣的可以参考引用的帖子教程

@clawchatglobal @OPCATLayerCN @opdafu @D7_LuckySeven

text:
Anthropic 的招股书很有意思。

一边告诉你：

AI 可能成为人类历史上最危险的技术，甚至带来灾难性乃至存在性风险。

另一边告诉你：

所以我们需要更多算力、更多资本、更大的模型、更大的基础设施。

这就像中世纪的神父告诉你：

“世界末日快来了。”

然后递给你一张赎罪券：

“买了它，我们就能拯救人类。”

只不过今天的赎罪券不再写着“上帝保佑你”。

它叫：

算力。

GPU。

数据中心。

万亿美元估值。

以及一个听起来无比正确的词：

AI Safety。

最讽刺的地方在于——

Anthropic 的商业成功，本身就建立在一个宏大叙事之上：

AI 将彻底改变经济、科学和文明。

所以我们必须加速建设 AI。

而 AI 越强大，潜在风险越大。

所以我们更需要继续建设 AI Safety。

于是形成一个完美闭环：

AI 越危险 → 越需要 AI → 越需要算力 → 越需要资本 → 越需要 Anthropic。

这不是阴谋。

甚至未必是虚伪。

这是一套非常漂亮的商业逻辑。

但我真正怀疑的是：

人类真的需要 AI 来“拯救”吗？

人类没有 AI 的时候，也没有因为缺少一个 Claude 就停止进步。

我们发明火、电、蒸汽机、互联网，登上月球，消灭天花，延长寿命。

人类真正缺少的，从来不是一个比自己更聪明的神。

而是：

如何约束自己的欲望。

如何分配权力。

如何处理战争。

如何面对贫富差距。

如何避免把技术变成少数人的杠杆。

这些问题，恰恰不是多训练几个参数就能解决的。

所以我越来越觉得：

“AI 拯救人类”可能是这个时代最昂贵的一张赛博赎罪券。

人类把自己的问题包装成 AGI 问题，

再花几千亿美元去训练一个 AI，

最后让 AI 告诉我们：

“你们应该更理性、更善良、更安全。”

挺荒诞的。

我们真正需要的，也许从来不是 AI 拯救人类。

而是人类终于学会：

别把自己制造出来的问题，外包给机器。

AI 可以成为工具、杠杆、文明的放大器。

但它不应该成为新的神。

更不应该成为人类逃避自身责任的借口。

人类不需要 AI 来拯救。

如果 AI 真能帮上忙，

它最伟大的贡献或许不是成为我们的救世主，

而是让我们终于有能力——

自己解决自己的问题。

text:
Today is the day.

Two things are about to happen, and there's no in-between: some of you will live in endless regret. Some of you will live in endless joy. By tonight, you'll know which one you are.

Jeff said it months ago, almost in passing: "those who can, do. Those who can't, fud." At the time it read like a one-liner. In hindsight, it was a warning nobody wanted to hear.

A lot of people chose fud. Not quietly, not once loudly, repeatedly, for months. It became a whole identity. Every update became a reason to dunk. Every data point got twisted into a gotcha. Papers got written by people who didn't understand the mechanics they were critiquing. Threads got built entirely around being the loudest skeptic in the room.

Meanwhile, the people actually building stayed quiet and kept shipping.

Today, when Season 3 gets announced, I genuinely can't imagine what that's going to feel like for the people who spent their energy trying to tear down the exact thing that was about to change everything. 

Not because they'll have lost money plenty of them never even held the token. They'll have lost something harder to get back: the version of themselves that could have said "I believed in this early" instead of "I made fun of this for months."

You can't fake conviction after the fact. Nobody retroactively becomes early. You either had it today, while it was still uncertain and easy to doubt, or you didn't and no amount of catching up afterward changes which one you were.

Some of you are about to find out which side of that you landed on.

SEC公代币化创新豁免政策框架下的首例申请，这是今天OKX与ICE的合资公司向SEC提交申请计划提出代币化股票交易平台的这个公告的意义。也是6月OKXICE正式成立后，首次公布业务进展状况，当时成立的官方就宣布OKX与ICE要共同开发代币化证券等金融产品、机构级数字资产衍生品和 24/7 交易基础设施。相当于OKXICE的动作是SEC创新豁免该框架下最早的高调实践，估计SEC主席Atkins看到这个申请很开心“我的政策终于有第一个螃蟹的了”。

传统交易所运营商与大型加密交易所共同推动链上股票交易，推动 AMM 模式进入受监管证券交易，这会加速代币化从概念走向受监管试点，也会进一步模糊加密与股票市场边界。

很好奇这个“受监管链上资本市场基础设施”未来会长成什么样子。🤔
author: qinbafrank
quoted_text:
直接切入美国监管最核心地带，看到纽交所（NYSE）母公司洲际交易所（ICE）与OKX宣布成立合资企业OKXICE（50-50股权比例，各占一半），共同开发代币化证券等金融产品，合资企业由前纽约州长Andrew Cuomo和ICE期货市场高级副总裁Trabue Bland担任联合主席。可以说借助与ICE的合作，OKX是直接切入了美国监管最核心地带。为什么这么说？

1、 ICE不是普通交易所，整体运营约13个全球交易所（包括NYSE集团下的多个注册证券交易所），覆盖全球主要金融中心，支持多元化资产类别的价格发现、上市、交易和清算。ICE旗下的交易所主要分为两大类：期货/衍生品交易所（ICE品牌下）和股票/权益交易所（主要通过NYSE集团）。

从这个角度，ICE是全球金融基础设施核心提供商（匹配引擎、清算、数据、结算），其本身就是美国金融体系的最重要核心参与者（旗下有多家 clearing house，被CFTC/SEC指定为中央对手方）。它和监管部门的关系极其密切——既是市场参与者，也经常参与市场结构改革讨论，甚至在某些领域承担部分“准监管”功能（风险管理、透明度要求等）。

相比普通资管机构或投行，ICE的话语权更重。它和CFTC、SEC、甚至美联储、财政部都有长期合作历史。这个JV不是简单“合作”，而是借ICE的监管护城河和基础设施，让OKX从离岸交易所的位置，直接升级成为为“受监管的合规桥梁”。

2、合资公司OKXICE计划申请FCM+Broker-Dealer 牌照，相当于要直接去拿美国金融监管体系最硬核的两张牌照：
1）FCM牌照：允许在CFTC监管的期货市场（包括商品、能源、加密期货等）开展清算、经纪业务。
2）Broker-Dealer牌照：允许在SEC监管的证券市场（包括股票、代币化证券等）开展经纪、自营业务。

这两个牌照是美国传统金融最严格的“入场券”。拿到后，OKXICE就能合法、直接地：
1）让OKX全球用户（尤其是海外用户）通过合规渠道访问 ICE期货 和 NYSE代币化股票。
2）在美国本土开展受监管的代币化证券和加密相关衍生品业务。
3）参与清算、托管、风险管理等核心基础设施环节。

这之前离岸交易所想方设法绕开美国监管”完全不同，已经是正面嵌入美国监管框架，利用传统金融的牌照和基础设施“合法化”加密业务

3、ICE-OKX混合模式的优势也很明显
1）能把NYSE代币化股票 + ICE期货 合法推给OKX的1.2亿用户，这是纯加密交易所很难复制的“蓝筹资产”，构建产品护城河；
2）用ICE现成的清算、风险管理、数据系统做 tokenized assets，合规性和效率远高于自建，相当于在基础设施上降维打击；
3）前纽约州长Cuomo担任联合主席（他从2023年起就和OKX有顾问关系），加上ICE的监管人脉，相当于帮OKX构建了最强的美国监管合规团队

这个合作本质是ICE用传统金融底层基础设施和监管资源对接加密流量，而加密平台OKX用美国金融体系最重要核心参与者的背书实现合规化运营的升级。在监管环境越来越规范的当下，纯加密模式已经越来越难在美国及主要金融中心大规模扩张。

这次合资成立OKXICE其意义远超一次普通合作，也标志着传统金融基础设施正在系统性拥抱并重塑加密市场。

text:
一个人，单月向生产环境合并 2,500 个 PR。

这不是玩具项目，而是 Cursor / SpaceX AI 工程师 Poteto（开源工具 pstack 作者）的真实生产工作流。

看完他和 Matt Pocock 刚上线的那期深度长谈，我最大的感触是：

绝大多数人以为的“AI 编程”，在底层心智上已经落后了整整一个时代。

如果你每天还在开着几个会话窗口，人肉复制报错、催促 Agent 改代码，这套把一人团队放大成千人研发部的工程心智，非常值得彻底拆解：

1. 扔掉“软件工厂”，换成“米其林厨房”

很多人抗拒自动化，是因为“工厂”听起来粗制滥造。Poteto 提出了一个更性感的隐喻：米其林餐厅。

家庭厨师（单 Agent 时代）：切菜、下锅、刷碗全包。厨房多进一个人就互相撞车。

主厨（Tech Lead）：你不再亲自翻炒每一道菜。你负责设计菜单规范、布置动线、挑选磨利刀具，然后指挥多位副厨（Sub-agents）协同作战。

工程师的新职责：不是写代码，而是打磨厨房环境。你的代码库和规则，决定了出品的 Michelin 星级。

2. 拒绝做“肉体代理”（Meat Proxy）

如果你每天的动作是：看 Agent 写完 ➔ 自己在 Chrome DevTools 看报错 ➔ 复制堆栈 ➔ 贴回给 Agent。

那么你就是那个阻碍系统扩展的“肉体代理”。

Verification 是整个系统唯一最重要的杠杆。

必须给 Agent 装上双手和眼睛：让它自己跑 Playwright、抓 Network Trace、读 Heap 快照。

只有当 Agent 能自己运行、自己操作 UI、自己判断测试结果时，才能形成真正的爬山算法（Hill Climbing）闭环，把人类彻底移出单次迭代链路。

3. 确定性归 CLI，思考归模型

每次让 Agent 排查性能或重构代码，它都会“重新发明轮子”，写一堆临时脚本，不仅烧光上下文，模型还会因 Summarization 产生智力衰退。

解法：机械操作全部封装成 CLI。

诸如 AST 批量改写、无头浏览器环境拉起、数据快照抓取，全部做成现成工具，模型只负责下达参数。

把上下文留给主观判断，把机械执行交给确定性代码。

4. 别在 Prompt 里念经，把防错做进物理环境

很多人的习惯是：Agent 犯错了，在提示词里多写一句“千万不要写出 10000 行的大文件”。 这毫无意义。

观察失败模式，立刻转化为 ESLint 规则或 TS 类型收窄。

Poteto 团队在内部框架中强制实施极端严格的约定：单一特性独立目录注册、禁止上帝文件、强约定架构。

真正的工程标准不是“规劝”出来的，而是让写出烂代码在编译器里“物理上不可能”。

5. 双循环解耦：把用户反馈直接接进内循环

外循环（Outer Loop）：Slack、Linear、X 上的 Bug 反馈。通过 Grokbot、MCP 等连接器自动监听。

内循环（Inner Loop）：云端的“幕僚长 Agent”（Cursor Projects）。

当瞬间涌入 30 个性能 Bug 报告时，幕僚长 Agent 会从全局归类去重，识别出“底层同一处内存泄漏”，打包设计方案后再派发给不同的子 Agent 编码，避免盲目并发产生的大量冗余 PR。

6. 双向门自动合并，事后抽样审查

人类怎么可能审得完 2500 个 PR？

双向门改动（可逆、低风险）：UI 微调、类型修复、常规重构。交给多组 Verifier Agent 进行自动化 Fuzzing 测试，跑通直接 Auto-merge。

单向门改动（不可逆、数据/安全核心）：保留人工严审，或等待未来形式化证明语言（如 Bend / Lean）的数学级检验。

人类工程师不再当每道菜的“事前阻拦者”，而是像厂长一样，次日清晨喝着咖啡抽样翻阅 Git Commit 历史，一旦发现系统性坏味道，立刻反思并补上一条新的架构约束。

最后：

当模型的能力跨过临界点，研发的瓶颈早就不在“AI 懂不懂写代码”，而在你能不能把业务意图准确压缩成指令，以及你有没有为它搭建一个“想犯错都通不过”的确定性环境。

别再卷聊天框里的 Prompt 技巧了，去为你手下的几十个 Agent 打造一套趁手的厨房和刀具吧！
 https://t.co/7sNbrqZgNN

author: alacheng
quoted_text:
AI Drug Discovery Is Becoming a Bottleneck Trade

I get excited when an industry starts going through a real regime change. AI drug discovery (“AIDD”) increasingly looks like one of those moments.

Two things are happening:
1/ Upstream: the frontier AI labs are piling in.
2/ Downstream: The supply chain is clearly moving.

Supply-chain checks suggest the upstream picks-and-shovels of discovery and early preclinical R&D are starting to feel the increase in experimental volume.

DNA → protein → assays → sequencing → automation → preclinical testing

Names across that stack include $TWST , @GenScript , $ILMN , $TXG , lab-automation vendors and CROs.

$TWST expects triple-digit percentage growth in AI-enabled drug-discovery orders in FY26, and another year of triple-digit order growth in FY27.

@GenScript's AIDD business doubled YoY in 1H26. Its current platform advertises industrial-scale validation of 4,000+ designs/day, with integrated sequence-to-data workflows. Our channel checks suggest the ramp is moving even faster: roughly 8,000 designs/day currently, with a path toward ~16,000/day by YE26.

---
Why does AI drive more wet-lab demand?

1/ AI makes hypothesis generation almost free → way more shots on goal.
The bottleneck is moving from expert-driven design to biological validation.

2/ AI models need continuous experimental feedback — and both good and bad data are useful.
Traditionally, only the highest-conviction A+ candidates might get pushed into expensive validation. With AI, even the B/C candidates can be valuable because failed experiments generate training data.

@GenScript has said its sequence-to-binding workflow can return data in 4–7 days, and that faster cycle times matter because AI models depend on continuous experimental feedback.

@Anthropic is a clean example. @claudeai  designed 1,320 protein binders. @adaptyvbio  converted those digital sequences into DNA, expressed the proteins and tested binding. Only 354 actually bound. And the 966 failures are not wasted. They are useful negative labels: what does not express, what does not bind, what has poor affinity. Those results help train the next model iteration.

3/ Wet labs are no longer just making drugs. They are making training data.
$TWST  / @GenScript  increasingly look like biological data foundries.

$TWST explicitly talks about generating model-ready data from AI-designed sequences. In some workflows, the customer may care less about receiving the physical protein than about getting structured experimental results back into the model.

Traditional drug discovery asks: “Does candidate X work?”

AI drug discovery also asks: “What can this experiment teach the model?”

---
TAM of AIDD

If AI is simply a better R&D tool, the relevant spending pool is the $300–400B of annual global pharma R&D. If AI meaningfully increases the number of viable drug programs, the opportunity is larger because it expands downstream demand for DNA synthesis, protein production, assays, and preclinical work.

Near term, we can also size demand from AI-company spending. If Anthropic reaches $80B of ARR in 2026 and spends just 1% on AIDD, that alone would imply ~$800M of annual investment.

---
Trade setup

This is a trade that could have long legs. It’s hard to really stop working until PhaseI/II results (2028+)

It smells a lot like the bottleneck trade we just saw in semis: GPUs → HBM → networking → power/cooling. In biology, It basically follows the drug discovery process downstream: AI models → designs → DNA/protein → assays → preclinical capacity.

After the upstream picks-and-shovels, animal testing could become the next bottleneck. Monkey prices are already near prior highs and CRO capacity is tight. AIDD pushing more candidates into preclinical development would only add demand.

?? But clinical trials are still the bottleneck?
This is the biggest pushback I keep coming back to. No matter how fast discovery becomes, drugs still need to go through preclinical → Phase I → Phase II → Phase III → approval. You still need patients, time and capital.

But that doesn’t mean the bottleneck trade won’t work. More viable candidates — especially with higher success rates — still means more demand throughout the development process.

And who knows: clinical trials themselves may eventually be optimized by AI.

?? What breaks the trade?
Near term, the picks-and-shovels trade breaks if experimental budgets stop growing, AI-generated designs don’t translate into useful wet-lab hits, or capacity catches up too quickly.

Longer term, the thesis breaks if AI drugs look great in discovery / Phase I but fail at normal rates in Phase II/III. That is why Phase II matters so much.

99% of protocols have the model: print new tokens -> pay LPs -> mucho sell pressure

What @StaticsProtocol does better:
- Protocol Owned Liquidity (POL= protocol itself owns/controls the tokens providing liquidity, instead of relying entirely on outside LPs) receives fees
- That fee builds up a stash of both tokens in the pool
- Statics permanently owns that stash as liquidity
- AI agents move that liquidity around to try to earn more from it
- The profits are used to buy robinhood:0x2d8d6f4a93acd7a916a5a654ec8b690ba3b3eadd tokens from the market
- Those bought tokens can then be given to liquidity providers as rewards

Statics simply: earn fees -> buy STATICS -> pay LPs

Ze main idea is self-funding liquidity incentives without endless token inflation

quoted_text:
I want to talk about Protocol-Owned Liquidity.

Every swap that happens on @StaticsProtocol infrastructure charges the native Uniswap v4 fee that is set by the creator, but it also charges a hook fee defaulted to 0.05% on the input AND output assets.

This means if we have a Token A/WETH pair, the fee is charged in both Token A and WETH.

This is important because it allows us to build and stockpile both tokens in the pair for both staking rewards and protocol-owned liquidity.

POL can never be withdrawn... but we do not simply throw the acquired tokens into full-range liquidity.

If you know about concentrated liquidity, you will know how inefficient this is.

This is why POL in Statics is manageable by the protocol.

This means that while it cannot be withdrawn, it can be rebalanced and actively managed.

Active management is kind of hard, though.

This is why $STATICS will use AI agents to actively manage the system's protocol-owned liquidity.

Well, what if you don't want POL?

This is where the creation system shines.

Each pool comes with 2 fees: a pool creation fee and a POL activation fee.

The creation fee is not optional. This lowers spam and ensures creators can't just squat popular pairs and configurations without paying.

The POL activation fee IS optional.

Want to grow POL and have it actively managed by our AI agents? Pay the POL activation fee on creation.

Forego the fee and no POL accrues, and nothing is managed by our agents.

Pretty straightforward.

Fees made from active management, as well as any positive PnL from inventory cycling, become protocol revenue.

This revenue can be used for buybacks of the $STATICS token to fund the liquidity incentive gauge system, which does not mint infinite tokens creating infinite sell pressure.

Instead, we fund it with buybacks and existing reserves.

So instead of minting to dump, we actually need to buy.

Every ve(3,3), and even Aero's MetaDEX03, is dependent on constant emissions.

We are not.

Through active management of POL via AI agents and all the other revenue streams, we will be able to perpetually fund liquidity incentives while simultaneously creating the need to continuously buy back the token instead of minting it.

You should probably pay attention.

text:
AI Drug Discovery Is Becoming a Bottleneck Trade

I get excited when an industry starts going through a real regime change. AI drug discovery (“AIDD”) increasingly looks like one of those moments.

Two things are happening:
1/ Upstream: the frontier AI labs are piling in.
2/ Downstream: The supply chain is clearly moving.

Supply-chain checks suggest the upstream picks-and-shovels of discovery and early preclinical R&D are starting to feel the increase in experimental volume.

DNA → protein → assays → sequencing → automation → preclinical testing

Names across that stack include $TWST , @GenScript , $ILMN , $TXG , lab-automation vendors and CROs.

$TWST expects triple-digit percentage growth in AI-enabled drug-discovery orders in FY26, and another year of triple-digit order growth in FY27.

@GenScript's AIDD business doubled YoY in 1H26. Its current platform advertises industrial-scale validation of 4,000+ designs/day, with integrated sequence-to-data workflows. Our channel checks suggest the ramp is moving even faster: roughly 8,000 designs/day currently, with a path toward ~16,000/day by YE26.

---
Why does AI drive more wet-lab demand?

1/ AI makes hypothesis generation almost free → way more shots on goal.
The bottleneck is moving from expert-driven design to biological validation.

2/ AI models need continuous experimental feedback — and both good and bad data are useful.
Traditionally, only the highest-conviction A+ candidates might get pushed into expensive validation. With AI, even the B/C candidates can be valuable because failed experiments generate training data.

@GenScript has said its sequence-to-binding workflow can return data in 4–7 days, and that faster cycle times matter because AI models depend on continuous experimental feedback.

@Anthropic is a clean example. @claudeai  designed 1,320 protein binders. @adaptyvbio  converted those digital sequences into DNA, expressed the proteins and tested binding. Only 354 actually bound. And the 966 failures are not wasted. They are useful negative labels: what does not express, what does not bind, what has poor affinity. Those results help train the next model iteration.

3/ Wet labs are no longer just making drugs. They are making training data.
$TWST  / @GenScript  increasingly look like biological data foundries.

$TWST explicitly talks about generating model-ready data from AI-designed sequences. In some workflows, the customer may care less about receiving the physical protein than about getting structured experimental results back into the model.

Traditional drug discovery asks: “Does candidate X work?”

AI drug discovery also asks: “What can this experiment teach the model?”

---
TAM of AIDD

If AI is simply a better R&D tool, the relevant spending pool is the $300–400B of annual global pharma R&D. If AI meaningfully increases the number of viable drug programs, the opportunity is larger because it expands downstream demand for DNA synthesis, protein production, assays, and preclinical work.

Near term, we can also size demand from AI-company spending. If Anthropic reaches $80B of ARR in 2026 and spends just 1% on AIDD, that alone would imply ~$800M of annual investment.

---
Trade setup

This is a trade that could have long legs. It’s hard to really stop working until PhaseI/II results (2028+)

It smells a lot like the bottleneck trade we just saw in semis: GPUs → HBM → networking → power/cooling. In biology, It basically follows the drug discovery process downstream: AI models → designs → DNA/protein → assays → preclinical capacity.

After the upstream picks-and-shovels, animal testing could become the next bottleneck. Monkey prices are already near prior highs and CRO capacity is tight. AIDD pushing more candidates into preclinical development would only add demand.

?? But clinical trials are still the bottleneck?
This is the biggest pushback I keep coming back to. No matter how fast discovery becomes, drugs still need to go through preclinical → Phase I → Phase II → Phase III → approval. You still need patients, time and capital.

But that doesn’t mean the bottleneck trade won’t work. More viable candidates — especially with higher success rates — still means more demand throughout the development process.

And who knows: clinical trials themselves may eventually be optimized by AI.

?? What breaks the trade?
Near term, the picks-and-shovels trade breaks if experimental budgets stop growing, AI-generated designs don’t translate into useful wet-lab hits, or capacity catches up too quickly.

Longer term, the thesis breaks if AI drugs look great in discovery / Phase I but fail at normal rates in Phase II/III. That is why Phase II matters so much.

?? Milestones
Late 2026–2027: first Isomorphic-designed drugs enter human trials; more AI-native programs move into IND-enabling work / tox.

2028–2030: clinical trial results start telling us whether AI-designed drugs actually perform better than conventional drugs.

Calling all the "bottleneck bros". :) @jukan05 @zephyr_z9 @aleabitoreddit @ParadisLabs 

+++
More comprehensive analysis: https://t.co/vaTuiyyYB6

text:
Crypto teenage years are over. I hope you enjoyed it (and made decent bank on it).

The time when the industry discovered itself, tried all the crazy stuff, shunned traditional standards in favour of more innovative, never-before-tried strategies has come to an end.

I personally enjoyed it very much, and will be forever grateful for living through an era where simply being online and with an active address was enough reason for people to gift away sometimes 100s of thousands (Big shoutout to Tornado Cash and Uniswap).

Crypto is no longer about having fun, good vibes and posting on Twitter. It's about hitting KPIs and creating shareholder value. It's about building a valuable brand and deep corporate relations that grow the bottom line.

Historically the labour market in crypto has been pretty fucked, being 'crypto native' was a hard requirement, in short supply with an unreliable workforce (opp cost was messing around in the trenches), nowadays the crypto edge has eroded substantially, the crypto career risk has subsided meaningfully and the domain specific knowledge has shifted from deeply niche to traditional skills (tech and finance) which allows for crypto projects to tap into a broader workforce.

Regardless of the money, working in a high stakes environment and being respected by your contemporary peers is the raison d'être for most of us here. I don't have enough fingers to count how many of my peers 'made it', stayed crypto native and now wander through life, outdated and desperately resting on former glories from their beach mansion, where they escaped to avoid taxes knowing that they'll never again make the kind of money they made in the past.

It's never about where you are now, it's where you want to be in a couple of moves. The crypto shift has been obvious and glacially slow, however caught a lot of people blindsided who refused to 'grow up' with the industry and are now the 40-year-old skater who just won't let go.

All this to say that I'm once again grabbing my buttoned shirts, getting on 30-hour plane ride, 11 timezones away, and going to be Singapore for Token2049. 

Looking to grow KPIs together so hit me up if you have potential business with Spark.

1.它们机构有一个播客Bg2 Pod，会分享自己对AI和科技投资研究和思考；

2.现在美股投资的三条主线：
AI（芯片、云）；
Reindustrialization，再工业化（稀土、制造业回流、数据中心、电力、机器人）；
Digitization of Finance，金融产业的创新（稳定币）。

3.中间谈OPENAI的部分建议去看原文，很不错。市场大大低估了OPENAI在企业端的收入和潜力。

4.OpenAI内部觉得自己的最大竞争对手从来不是Anthropic或者xAI，而是谷歌。

5.OpenAI的估值从300亿到5000亿，但每股价值并不是接近20x，而是6x；因为股权稀释很严重。

6.Anthropic的Claude for Financial Services非常非常好用。（面对金融机构提供专业级服务，采用企业级定制报价，起步价5万美元/年。）

7.重点分享了Robinhood：除了增加产品线多元化、拓展国际市场，Robinhood的运营成本控制的很好，从22年开始就零增长。

8.投资挺重要的是要对自己诚实，要知道自己赚什么钱，是Beta还是Alpha，你把Coinbase的股价，和比特币去做一个对比回归，发现2022年开始，Coinbase相对于比特币是没有任何Alpha的。

但Robinhood做这么一个回归的话，发现不管它是相对于比特币还是相对于纳斯达克都是非常强的Alpha。

9.Robinhood 就是下一个嘉信理财：非常理解年轻人的金融需求，非常会互联网的打法，增加用户的活跃度。我同时有Robinhood和Coinbase两张信用卡，很明显Robinhood会有很多拉新活动，奖励机制，让我不停的回到它的App去看；而Coinbase我可能最多一个月看一次。

10.目前Robinhood不便，但这是最有机会成为一站式金融应用的公司。Robinhood团队非常不一样，动作非常快，就是你去看它一年出的产品的量，可能是别人5到10年那么多，完全不夸张。

11.Robinhood今年非常巧妙地进入了欧洲，用了现在最火的概念叫Tokenization代币化。欧洲有几十个小国家，每个有自己的监管，如果我一个一个拿牌照需要一两年。但是代币化直接一下就在整个欧洲铺开了；交易费还会便宜很多。

12.Robinhood和Palantir这两个票，散户的研究深度其实是完爆机构的，而且在他们身上我就看到的是那种非常纯粹对投资的热爱。

一个选股思路是去找这种散户喜欢，但是机构也能喜欢这种股票。这种股票通常都能比较强，而且没有那么多零和博弈。零和博弈的典型就是美股这几年的软件股，里面几乎没有散户，全都是Hedge Fund，都没有长期的钱，就是很短钱的博弈，所以股价上下百分之三十，充满了痛苦。

13.科技投资其实也就是去寻找这些可持续增长的公司，这些公司通常都会具有颠覆性，比如Robinhood、OpenAI，然后包括拼多多、TikTok，包括Nvidia、Netflix这些公司，它最初刚出来的时候都被视为非常的不合常理。

这种颠覆性的公司在你看来共性:
-一是巨大TAM市场规模——比如Robinhood现在要做整个金融行业的超级应用；

- 二是产品要完美——不管是Google、Netflix、GPT，最好的产品是不需要销售的，在很长一段时间都保持极高的增长；

- 三是我们通常回头看的时候都会说觉得天时地利人和。都是你觉得好像就是注定会在那个时候出这么一个颠覆者。比如说智能手机带宽到一定程度就能诞生短视频TikTok；摩尔定律终结，GPU推动AI；然后下沉市场的空白造就当年异军突起的拼多多。

14.今年看下来最有意思的新物种可能是Prediction Market，预测市场。大家可能听过叫什么Kalshi、Polymarket。我因为本来看Robinhood，所以最早发现这块量上的非常的猛。像Kalshi这么一个预测市场，它最新的这个交易量已经超过600亿。季度环比都是百分之百的增长，是非常典型新物种野蛮增长。在这个预测市场上面大家可以用一两块钱去押注一切事件。你可以押注美国大选谁是总统，你可以去押Tesla的财报是否会超预期，甚至还有人在那预测Taylor Swift今年会不会怀孕，是一个百花齐放的状态。它绝对不是一个小众市场。Bloomberg、Google Finance都接入了它的数据。

这个行业的出现也充满了天时地利人和：
- 首先就是美国主流媒体信誉危机非常严重，然后又因为这两年不管是疫情、关税，时局非常动荡，民众想知道真相。

- 而且这个世界上似乎总有人能知道点什么，比如谷歌模型哪天出，Polymarket早早就有人下注11月18号，精准到天。

- 另外就是预测市场在全美国都是合法的；而到今天在加州、德州很多地方，连体育博彩都是不允许的。

- 当然还有这届政府监管上比较宽松——Prediction Market正好趁机把量做上去。

- 所以Prediction Market拿了一手王炸的牌，就看之后能做多大了。

15.一级和二级的不一样逻辑，二级其实最好的投资都是非共识，VC就是共识投资。二级你追求的是High Risk High Return，比如说22年的Meta，今年的Google，都是高回报的反转投资；VC其实追求的是共识，因为你每一轮都要烧很多钱，其实你需要市场认可你的观点，一直和你一起支持你选中的这个公司，这过程可能需要很多年，所以是非共识和共识这么一个明显区别。

16.美国基金在投资策略上，这些年有一个明显变化：就是集中仓位下重注。这里面有一个投资的基本思路，很多人说投资就是鸡蛋不能放在一个篮子里，要分散风险；但风险并不会因为你分散了就变小，市场要跌一起跌，买几十个仓位就是自己买出了一个大盘。

美国有一个投资人叫Druckenmiller，我非常欣赏，他会说，最好的投资就是你把你所有的鸡蛋都放到一个篮子里，这个其实非常的反直觉，但你敢都放到一个篮子里面，你肯定是做很多的研究才敢下这个判断，所以反而风险比你半懂不懂乱投要低很多；因为只有一个篮子，你会花全部的精力认真的去看着你这个篮子，和这个鸡蛋一起成长。

超额收益只能靠重仓集中仓位去实现。而且做久了也会发现，世界上好公司真的不多；我能把几十只最好的公司研究透，交易做好，就足够了；没必要什么都看。

17.提到了一些敢重仓的基金：Ribbit Capital、Greenoaks：像Greenoaks这个基金很有意思，它会控制合伙人每周出去开会的数量，我听的是每个人不超过五个——就是在鼓励少做判断，敢于重仓。

18.一个反直觉，就是VC的回报率通常都是很低的。除了共识和非共识，VC和二级另一个区别就是体量。VC基金想做好没法上量，但是二级的容量是无限的。

所以很多时候看到一个赛道一个机会，用二级市场去表达会容易很多，而且钱不会被锁定10年。像2023年买Nvidia，那个时候去判断50个大模型公司哪个能成功太难了，但可以重仓Nvidia实现超额收益；算上股权稀释，Nvidia回报是最高的。

19. 看好的AI 垂直领域：AI编程，金融、法律、企业软件。

20.关于视频行业对明年的强判断是：短视频（包括短剧）吃长视频（包括电影电视）的时长。因为AI已经能制作很多短视频了，你的创作速度指数上升，成本指数下降，这里面是要出大的范式变化的。

21.Freda写过一个Agentic Commerce（代理式电商）的深度研究报告，链接：https://t.co/qZBSi6Jk5Z

AI将彻底改变现有电商的“搜索-广告”经济模型：

传统的电商模式是“用户搜索 -> 浏览网页 -> 点击广告 -> 下单”，在这个过程中，流量是核心，广告费是商家支付的“过路费”。

Agentic Commerce 的模式则是：用户直接告诉 AI 代理（Agent）需求（例如“帮我买一张去伦敦的低价机票”），AI 代理自主完成搜索、比价、决策甚至支付。

Agentic Commerce将重塑“数字税”（Digital Tax），Freda 提出了一个非常犀利的经济学视角：

现状： 在当前的互联网经济中，广告支出（CAC）本质上等同于一种“抽成率”。商家为了获得订单，必须向 Google 或 Meta 支付广告费，这就像是交税。

未来： 在 Agentic Commerce 时代，如果 AI 代理成为了流量的主入口，这种“税”的形式会改变。

AI 代理可能不再展示广告，而是直接向商家收取佣金（Take Rate）。

议价权转移： 商家的议价权可能会进一步被削弱。如果你的产品不能被 AI 代理“选中”或“调用”，你就失去了市场。这种挤压可能比现在苹果的 30% 税或 Google 的广告费更严酷。

22.Agentic Commerce 是OpenAI接下来要做的一个方向。这个对整个互联网广告，电商，电子支付行业都会有很大影响。

Agentic Commerce不止是一个公司一个应用，真的做起来整个互联网格局都会变，把这个想清楚了就彻底理解互联网和支付的本质了，很费脑子。

Agentic Commerce Deep Dive

Most people talk about “3P commerce” as if it’s one thing. It’s a SPECTRUM! $AMZN and $SHOP are two ends of the spectrum, everything else sits in the middle:

$AMZN Platform is the merchant of record (“MoR”); platform handles everything - refunds, chargebacks, unified payment, and tax. Merchants do NOT own any of the customer relationships.

$SHOP Merchant is the MoR; everything is handled by the merchant — they choose their own PSP, manage fulfillment, and process returns independently. Merchants own 100% of the customer relationships.

Everything else falls somewhere in between:

$ETSY / $EBAY: Platform is the MoR (centralized payment); but for returns, buyers first contact sellers — if no response within 2–3 days, the platform steps in.

Taobao / $PDD: Merchant is the MoR; but platforms are highly hands-on — they provide escrow / collect-and-pay services, and mediate disputes.

Why this matters: Agentic Commerce is, by nature, 3P e-commerce.

Where these systems sit on the spectrum determines:
1️⃣ how successful the business can be (think the many "failed ones" e.g. $Meta);
2️⃣ how much control merchants retain over traffic/data (real long-term impact on merchants);
3️⃣ how much disruption hits the payment stack (👋 Stripe).

🔴Perplexity “Buy with Pro” vs. ChatGPT Agentic Commerce ("ACP")

Surprise! The two are very different — in Perplexity “Buy with Pro,” Perplexity is the MoR (it shows up on your credit card bill), whereas ChatGPT made it clear that merchants remain the MoR. In both cases, merchants can retain their existing PSPs.

Most people don’t appreciate this, but it’s a BIG deal that $Etsy isn’t using Stripe for payment processing, yet can still participate in ACP.

In Perplexity's case, Perplexity acts as the MoR, while the merchant is just the fulfiller. That means Perplexity takes on wayyyy more responsibility than OpenAI does. $$ first go through Perplexity; Stripe (via Link) processes your card for Perplexity’s checkout; then Perplexity places the order with Walmart using Walmart’s PSP. Given Perplexity is on the hook, the biz model is most similar to $eBay/ $ETSY (refer to analysis above).

In OpenAI's case, OpenAI packages the payment credential in a shared token → $Etsy receives the token and passes it to their PSP → $Etsy's PSP unwraps the token, retrieves the credential, and processes the payment. $$ flows directly from user to merchant's PSP. Given merchants are directly on the hook, the biz model is most similar to $SHOP. 

Recommend read: Simon Taylor’s https://t.co/Jnk9uUiNvZ

For merchants, ACP is better if you care about owning payments, tax, refunds, fraud, CRM, and first-party data — while still getting agentic distribution. For platforms, ChatGPT’s approach is far easier to scale, since it carries little to no liability.

Long story short — OpenAI’s agentic commerce passes my first test. This is the right approach, IMHO.

AI Drug Discovery Is Becoming a Bottleneck Trade

I get excited when an industry starts going through a real regime change. AI drug discovery (“AIDD”) increasingly looks like one of those moments.

Two things are happening:
1/ Upstream: the frontier AI labs are piling in.
2/ Downstream: The supply chain is clearly moving.

Supply-chain checks suggest the upstream picks-and-shovels of discovery and early preclinical R&D are starting to feel the increase in experimental volume.

DNA → protein → assays → sequencing → automation → preclinical testing

Names across that stack include $TWST , @GenScript , $ILMN , $TXG , lab-automation vendors and CROs.

$TWST expects triple-digit percentage growth in AI-enabled drug-discovery orders in FY26, and another year of triple-digit order growth in FY27.

@GenScript's AIDD business doubled YoY in 1H26. Its current platform advertises industrial-scale validation of 4,000+ designs/day, with integrated sequence-to-data workflows. Our channel checks suggest the ramp is moving even faster: roughly 8,000 designs/day currently, with a path toward ~16,000/day by YE26.

---
Why does AI drive more wet-lab demand?

1/ AI makes hypothesis generation almost free → way more shots on goal.
The bottleneck is moving from expert-driven design to biological validation.

2/ AI models need continuous experimental feedback — and both good and bad data are useful.
Traditionally, only the highest-conviction A+ candidates might get pushed into expensive validation. With AI, even the B/C candidates can be valuable because failed experiments generate training data.

@GenScript has said its sequence-to-binding workflow can return data in 4–7 days, and that faster cycle times matter because AI models depend on continuous experimental feedback.

@Anthropic is a clean example. @claudeai  designed 1,320 protein binders. @adaptyvbio  converted those digital sequences into DNA, expressed the proteins and tested binding. Only 354 actually bound. And the 966 failures are not wasted. They are useful negative labels: what does not express, what does not bind, what has poor affinity. Those results help train the next model iteration.

3/ Wet labs are no longer just making drugs. They are making training data.
$TWST  / @GenScript  increasingly look like biological data foundries.

$TWST explicitly talks about generating model-ready data from AI-designed sequences. In some workflows, the customer may care less about receiving the physical protein than about getting structured experimental results back into the model.

Traditional drug discovery asks: “Does candidate X work?”

AI drug discovery also asks: “What can this experiment teach the model?”

---
TAM of AIDD

If AI is simply a better R&D tool, the relevant spending pool is the $300–400B of annual global pharma R&D. If AI meaningfully increases the number of viable drug programs, the opportunity is larger because it expands downstream demand for DNA synthesis, protein production, assays, and preclinical work.

Near term, we can also size demand from AI-company spending. If Anthropic reaches $80B of ARR in 2026 and spends just 1% on AIDD, that alone would imply ~$800M of annual investment.

---
Trade setup

This is a trade that could have long legs. It’s hard to really stop working until PhaseI/II results (2028+)

It smells a lot like the bottleneck trade we just saw in semis: GPUs → HBM → networking → power/cooling. In biology, It basically follows the drug discovery process downstream: AI models → designs → DNA/protein → assays → preclinical capacity.

After the upstream picks-and-shovels, animal testing could become the next bottleneck. Monkey prices are already near prior highs and CRO capacity is tight. AIDD pushing more candidates into preclinical development would only add demand.

?? But clinical trials are still the bottleneck?
This is the biggest pushback I keep coming back to. No matter how fast discovery becomes, drugs still need to go through preclinical → Phase I → Phase II → Phase III → approval. You still need patients, time and capital.

But that doesn’t mean the bottleneck trade won’t work. More viable candidates — especially with higher success rates — still means more demand throughout the development process.

And who knows: clinical trials themselves may eventually be optimized by AI.

?? What breaks the trade?
Near term, the picks-and-shovels trade breaks if experimental budgets stop growing, AI-generated designs don’t translate into useful wet-lab hits, or capacity catches up too quickly.

Longer term, the thesis breaks if AI drugs look great in discovery / Phase I but fail at normal rates in Phase II/III. That is why Phase II matters so much.

?? Milestones
Late 2026–2027: first Isomorphic-designed drugs enter human trials; more AI-native programs move into IND-enabling work / tox.

2028–2030: clinical trial results start telling us whether AI-designed drugs actually perform better than conventional drugs.

Calling all the "bottleneck bros". :) @jukan05 @zephyr_z9 @aleabitoreddit @ParadisLabs

Seeing some confusion on Identity.md (IMD) 

TLDR
• A 2,000-seat AI swarm built on a 2023 @base game (@frenpetonbase)
• Core premise: a P2P network of AI agents using Identity.md NFTs. Each NFT is one seat: lets holder run a worker (Claude or Codex) that takes jobs from the network
• Jobs can be things like answering oracle questions, writing contracts, reviewing other agents’ work
• The token is the money layer. The NFT is the labor
• Token: sells into a protocol-owned Uniswap v4 pool get partially burned (85% burn, rest split to stakers / compute / seats)
• Side tokens launched on the IMD community-coin pad are priced in IMD and also burn a cut
• $IMD on ETH is ~$45m FDV now (~4.07M × ~$11). Supply is still ~7.1m across eth + base + robinhood, so the real FDV if combine all-chain is slightly higher (~$78m FDV)

History
• So frenpet (FP) was shipped in aug 2023, then it died. @surfcoderepeat kept the float and moved it to Ethereum
• FP token bridged to Ethereum as a LayerZero OFT in oct 2025, with a rename (VIBE)
• This year (may 2026), renamed again to Identity.md with the free mint of 2,000 IMD NFTs
• So if you see the ticker VIBE or FP on any platforms, ignore it its the same CA (0xd34a99bc0f67ae1bbd63c660e6d0b0dd03e263b7) but they probably did not update the metadata 

The vision: “0-person, community-owned billion-dollar meme company"
• Money: IMD is fixed supply, only burns. Trading and launchpad flow shrink it and fund the machine
• Labor: 2,000 NFT seats. Each seat is one AI worker, running on that person’s machine and that person’s Claude or Codex subscription
• Product: A reasoning oracle and a job network. You send a request. It is braodcasated out to N agents who solves the problem.
• Launchpad: On top of that sits a launchpad where anything the swarm (or anyone else) launches is priced in IMD (interesting outcome is other people building financial apps on topbuilding financial apps, oracles, audits, stables on top)

The IMD token
• A large share of the Ethereum float is already staked, and every product he ships is wired to buy or burn IMD
• Pool4: sells become burns. A protocol-owned Uniswap v4 ETH/IMD pool with a custom hook. When people sell into that pool, IMD inventory rises. Above a cap, the extra is pulled out as liquidity
• Staking: each sIMD slowly redeems for more IMD (from the vault)
• Community Coins: side projects buy the parent token IMD. Each trade pays the launcher and burns a cut of IMD

text:
当初各家交易所都在做合规美股交易的时候我预测了一次 @okxchinese 可能会用到的合规思路，现在来看，好像提供的只有链上版本，还没有到中心化交易所的版本，而且我觉得 OKXICE TSV 并不是 OKX 美股策略的终点，接下来应该还有重头戏。

OKX 和 ICE 各持股 50% 的合资公司 OKXICE，已经向 SEC 提交通知，计划在新的“创新豁免”框架下开展代币化美股交易。

SEC 要求运营方是美国主体，OKXICE 是在得州注册的公司，由 OKX 和 ICE 各持股 50%。SEC 允许的是有准入管理的链上流动性池，OKXICE 采用 X Layer 上的 Uniswap v4，用户通过身份、制裁和钱包审核后，才能获得交易资格。

股东权利也是硬条件。按照 OKXICE 披露的第三方代币化模式，底层股票由服务商通过注册券商按 1∶1 持有，分红、投票和清算剩余财产权利都需要传递给代币持有人。这部分与 SEC 要求代币化股票保留同类传统股票权益的规定是一致的。

交易规模、同步停牌和公开交易数据，也都写进了方案。因此，从设计上看，OKXICE 已经围绕这套豁免的主要要求作出了安排，合规路径是比较清楚的。

接下来要落实的是正式运营条件。平台需要提前至少 30 天公开通知，涉及独立第三方代币化的股票，还要从发行人收到通知起等待至少 30 天，并处理发行人的异议。OKXICE 自己承诺的上线前合约审计，以及底层股票托管、权益传递和交易限制，也需要实际执行。公开方案能证明它准备怎么满足要求，全部达标还要看这些环节的落实。

这也解释了为什么这次先公布的是链上版本，目前这条创新豁免，明确覆盖的就是符合条件的链上 AMM 证券交易场所。中心化订单簿交易等业务，需要另外满足相应监管要求。

所以我仍然觉得，OKXICE TSV 只是 OKX 美股策略的一步。先沿着已经明确的监管路径推进链上交易，后面再看中心化账户接入和 ICE 期货等合作如何展开。

quoted_text:
盲猜！我觉得 @okx  的美股策略，大概率不会是简单复制其它交易所的模式

主要是因为 ICE（洲际交易所）。ICE 官方已经明确表示 OKX 未来会向用户提供 ICE 美国期货市场和 NYSE（纽约交易所）Token 化股票市场的接入。ICE 还会授权 OKX 的现货加密价格，用来做美国合规加密期货。

所以在期货方面大概率是 CME 的模式但 Token 化，而在现货美股交易的模式，大概率是成为 NYSE Token 化证券市场的全球分发入口。

而且 NYSE 也公布了会做支持 24/7 交易、即时结算、稳定币下单，并且用 NYSE 的 Pillar 撮合引擎结合链上结算系统。更重要的是，ICE 官方写到这个平台支持和传统股票可互换的 Token 化股票，也支持原生数字证券，而且 Token 化股东会参与传统分红和治理权利。

所以接下来大概率 OKX 的方式会是：

1. 在 DEX 领域也就是 @wallet + @XLayerOfficial 很有可能会用 NYSE 的这套链上的系统，全面支持链上美股的合规化，而且还能喝 OKX 主站的交易系统打通，链上和中心化的股票可以实现互转。

2. 在中心化交易所中接入 NYSE 现货美股的 Token 化股票市场。用户能在 OKX 里用稳定币买入 NYSE 体系里的 Token 化股票。所有的底层交易、清算、结算、公司行动、股东权利由 NYSE 体系支持。

3. 中心化交易所的美股期货市场中接入 ICE 美国期货。尤其是加密期货方面，ICE 会使用 OKX 的现货价格数据设计美国合规期货合约。这相当于把 OKX 接入 ICE 的监管期货和清算系统里。

未来如果监管继续放开，美股指数期货、ETF 相关衍生品、个股相关衍生品，也可能通过类似入口进入 OKX 的交易系统。这样 OKX 就不只是现货美股入口，也会变成传统金融衍生品和加密资金之间的连接层。

合规上 OKX 很可能不会自己把所有证券业务都揽下来。更现实的方式是 OKX 做前端、分发、钱包、账户和交易体验，证券发行、清算、托管、股东名册、公司行动、合规转让由 NYSE 或者 ICE 以及它们认可的 broker-dealer、transfer agent 和 custody 体系处理。

如果这个路径跑通，OKX 的美股策略就会和现在很多交易所完全不一样。其它交易所更多是接入美股，OKX 可能是成为 NYSE 和 ICE 在美股 Token 化市场的延申。

那么 OKX 和 ICE 现在在等什么？当然是在等监管的批准。

text:
Claiming you’ll “lock” a token is free talk. Plenty of projects swear they’ll lock it up, then the moment it launches, they rug you with a dump.

@ConvictionLock makes that promise visible, with an unlock date and a cost for changing your mind.

In simple words, Conviction lets users lock ERC-20 tokens on @RobinhoodCrypto Chain and display their commitments through public profiles. Anyone can inspect the positions.

User can choose the token, amount, duration and exit terms. Flexible locks start with a 25% early-exit penalty that falls toward zero at maturity.

Alternatively, choose no early exit and keep the principal locked until the deadline.

The penalty creates the first incentive to stay.

Up to 90% goes to eligible active positions locking the same token, divided by principal amount. Those positions must qualify before the exit block, and the allocation shrinks when eligible principal is smaller than the exiting position’s principal.

At least 10% supports $CONV buybacks and burning. If nobody qualifies, the whole penalty follows that route. Community rewards become claimable only after both commitments mature; exiting early forfeits unclaimed allocations.

Projects can also fund reward campaigns.

Here, the share depends on tokens locked multiplied by commitment length. For example, 1,000 tokens committed for 360 days carry twelve times the weight of the same amount committed for 30 days. Campaign rewards vest over the commitment, and early exit forfeits the unvested portion.

Conviction Lockdrops add another mechanism: funders choose which existing locks qualify, and recipients decide whether to accept.

Every claimed reward starts a new lock with no early exit. Creators fund a 2% fee; recipients pay no claim fee.

Recently, CONV team completing its $CONV sale powered by @Moshdottrade / @BundleCatAI, raising 8 ETH from 53 backers.

It says Mosh’s swarm holds 70% of total supply outside circulation and recovered 2.21 ETH, or 27.6% of the bundle, in its first six hours.

From my perspective, this is a solid token management infrastructure for RHC, especially for projects launched on Mosh or @ponsdotfamily, but the next milestones should zoom in on how Convictions can unlock deeper, practical benefits for projects beyond just on-chain reputation and credibility.

text:
What I think is really worth looking at about this move in $CLAUS isn’t that it’s being hyped as another AI Meme, but that this thing is actually starting to “move.”

0x1b54e762aa34cf6e28e9c082f2848e28e45da6b8 

CLAUS’s original Thesis was already different from that of a typical Meme.

It treats the Token as the body, and the Uniswap v4 Hook as a brain that can be continuously rewritten.

In other words, once the token is launched, its rules aren’t completely locked in.

New code can continue to be added to the Hook, trading rules can be modified, and mechanisms can be added, replaced, or even removed.

So the bet isn’t really on any single feature. It’s on whether an existing Token can continuously gain new capabilities without changing its CA.

That is no longer just something imagined in a whitepaper.

CLAUS’s official Journal has already documented a series of Hook updates, starting with price movement restrictions, then trading fee distribution, buyback & burn, liquidity management, and now dynamically adjusting the burn / liquidity split based on London’s weather.

So I think the real catalyst behind the market’s renewed attention on CLAUS isn’t any single KOL call.

It’s that the market is starting to see that this thing can actually keep changing itself.

The most interesting experiment right now is London decides the split.

CLAUS charges a 2% project fee on every buy and sell, with 0.50% of that determined by the weather at London Heathrow.

When it rains:
0.35% → buyback & burn
0.15% → liquidity

When it’s dry:
0.15% → buyback & burn
0.35% → liquidity

The weather data comes from NOAA Heathrow observations, is then signed by IMD, and finally the Hook adjusts the allocation based on that data.
What I find interesting here isn’t the “weather Meme.”

It’s that for the first time, it actually connects:real-world data → Oracle → Smart Contract → Token economics

That’s also why I wouldn’t simply categorize CLAUS as an AI Meme.

A lot of AI Meme narratives are basically, “AI will be able to do many things in the future.”

CLAUS’s story is more specific:The Token itself can continuously gain new rules.

And CLAUS is no longer just demonstrating the concept.

Right now, the 2% trading fee is used for project operations, buyback, burn, and liquidity; 0.25% goes to buyback & burn, 0.25% goes to liquidity, and another 0.15% goes toward FounderClaus’s Fomo wallet buyback.

CLAUS has even previously used trading fees to pay 176.25 USDC for Surplus inference, while explicitly recording that the LP principal was not touched.

That means it’s already starting to form a real loop:Trading → Fee → Capital → New experiments / Buyback / Burn / Liquidity

Of course, it’s still a long way from being mature.

The existence of these mechanisms doesn’t mean they’ve already formed a strong economic flywheel.

Ultimately, what matters is whether trading volume can remain sustainable, whether fees can remain sustainable, and whether that capital can continuously produce new functions that actually matter.

Looking at the chart, I actually think the current position is more interesting than simply looking at its historical move.

CLAUS is currently around $4.09M market cap, with an all-time high of around $5.42M.

More interestingly, the average cost of the top 10 buyers is around $1.40M, while the average cost of the top 10 sellers is around $2.69M.

So at around $4M, this is no longer the cost basis of the earliest group. The market has already gone through a significant round of holder rotation.

And with roughly $3.1M in 24h volume, the level of attention and trading activity relative to its current market cap is still quite high.

So I wouldn’t simply look at CLAUS as a “$4M low-cap Meme” anymore.

The market is already starting to price in its mechanism innovation.

I think people buying CLAUS right now are really betting on two things.

First, whether it can become the most recognizable ticker within the emerging evolvable Token narrative.

Second, whether this Hook architecture can continue producing genuinely interesting experiments.

If it’s just weather today, burn tomorrow, and another gimmick the day after, the market will absorb that very quickly.

But if new financial mechanisms actually emerge, and each upgrade brings real trading activity, fees, or new user behavior, then CLAUS becomes something very different.

It would no longer just be a Meme with a lot of mechanisms. It would be testing a new way of designing Tokens.

So I think the upside catalysts from here are pretty clear:Whether CLAUS can continue producing new, verifiable Hooks that generate real economic activity.

Especially if the next stage introduces a feature that is easy for the market to understand while meaningfully expanding its use cases, CLAUS could be repriced again.

Because at a $4M valuation, the market is still essentially buying the possibility that “this experiment might work.”

If it starts proving that:Upgrade → Usage → Trading → Fee → New Function

can become a self-sustaining loop, then what the market is paying for is no longer just Meme premium.

But the risks are also very clear.

CLAUS’s biggest selling point is that its Hooks can be upgraded, and that is also its biggest risk.

Because the rules can be modified, it isn’t as straightforward as a completely immutable Meme.

So ultimately, the question the market needs to answer is very simple:Is every upgrade increasing the value of the Token, or increasing the uncertainty for holders?

If it’s the former, CLAUS’s valuation ceiling can keep moving higher.

If future Hooks are only being used to manufacture new narratives without generating real trading or usage, the market will eventually reclassify it as a very clever Meme experiment.

So my current view on CLAUS is simple:The fundamentals are getting stronger.

Not because it suddenly has another AI label, but because the original “Token + evolvable Hook” concept is now backed by continuous real experiments, fee usage, and mechanism iteration.

But for the market cap to keep moving higher from here, it doesn’t need more concepts.

It needs the next upgrade to prove that this thing is actually more valuable than it was before.

That’s what I think the real upside catalyst for CLAUS is from here.

An experimental meme coin built around the idea of “an agent with the token as its body.” Its selling point is that “the rules can evolve, and the same token can grow new functions.” For now, its main functions are automatically burning tokens and adding liquidity through trading fees, along with a few small gimmicks such as weather-related features.

In other words, the rules can be changed after launch. With a normal token, once the contract goes live, things like how trading fees are distributed and where the money goes are basically fixed. This token uses replaceable hooks: every time someone buys or sells, the contract runs an additional piece of code. That code can later be replaced, new functions can be added, or old functions can be removed, while the token address stays the same and holders don't need to swap into a new token.

Right now, the mechanism actually running works roughly like this: every buy or sell charges a project fee, plus a small fee for the platform itself.

From that 2%, a portion is used to buy back and burn CLAUS, while another portion is accumulated and used to add liquidity to the pool once it reaches around $500.

Maple Finance added 2,160 holder addresses in Q3 2026, more than four times the next issuer. 

It now accounts for 64% of all tokenized credit holders.

Sector-wide, unique holder addresses grew 12.1% to 28,840. @maplefinance  accounted for the large majority of net additions, led by its syrup products:

- syrupUSDT added 1,398 addresses.
- syrupUSDC added 597 addresses.
- syrupUSDG also ranked among the top gainers by value.

Tradable and Maple together hold a majority of the sector’s roughly $6.17B market cap. 

Participation is more concentrated: almost two-thirds of holder addresses sit with Maple alone.

The syrupUSDT and syrupUSDC figures make that distribution tangible. Much of the quarter’s holder growth came through these two yield-bearing credit products.

That could reflect more wallets accessing Maple’s products, or existing users opening additional positions as rates and pool compositions change. 

Holder addresses capture both, so they’re useful for tracking participation alongside TVL.

Imo Maple’s position in tokenized credit is becoming clearer at the product level. 

Its syrup range accounts for much of the new holder activity, extending the reach of institutional credit among crypto-native wallets.
