text:
I’ve recently seen quite a few people betting on $IMD, and I think the reason isn’t simply the “AI + Crypto” narrative.

0xd34a99bc0f67ae1bbd63c660e6d0b0dd03e263b7 

What really gives IMD a higher ceiling is that it is trying to occupy a much bigger position:

AI agents are beginning to directly participate in the production of Crypto financial products, and IMD wants to become the underlying protocol that supports these new applications.

IMD also doesn’t position itself as simply an Agent project. It describes itself as a protocol capable of creating “net new 0 to 1 financial applications,” as well as a distributed software factory powered by agents.

That distinction is important.

In the past, Crypto financial products were basically designed by humans, coded by humans, and deployed through smart contracts.

What IMD wants to do is:Agent network continuously runs → produces code, research, oracles, DeFi applications, etc. → verification → deployment → new onchain financial applications.

If this model actually works, then IMD ultimately isn’t competing with any single DeFi product.

It is competing over:Who can create the next generation of onchain financial applications faster and at a lower cost.

And what the market is really betting on isn’t:Will IMD become a bigger AI project?

It is:If agents can continuously produce new financial products, can IMD become the infrastructure for this new production system?

This also connects to another interesting variable — Hooks.

IMD is currently bringing RWA, Hooks, Uniswap v4, stablecoins, games, and other directions into the same design space.

That means it isn’t trying to build a protocol with one fixed function. It wants to become an experimental environment where new financial mechanisms can continuously be created.

In theory, one agent could design a new trading mechanism, another agent could write the Hook, another could handle the Oracle or verification, and eventually the whole thing could be deployed as a functioning financial application.

If this loop actually works, IMD’s value would no longer simply be about “how many agents it has today.”

It would be about:How many new onchain primitives this network can produce in the future.

This is also why I think you can’t look at the IMD token alone right now.

In the screenshot, Adam mentioned that some people in the community have already deployed tokens outside the protocol for things they are working on, while the mainnet is also preparing to expand to Robinhood Chain, Base, and Ethereum Mainnet.

More importantly, the Explorer already shows different agents working on smart contract development, DeFi, oracles, research, and other tasks.

At the very least, this shows that the community isn’t simply building around the token as a Meme. They are trying to turn IMD itself into a development environment.

What is really worth watching is whether it can eventually form:Agent → Build → Verify → Deploy → Financial App → New Demand → More Agents

If this production network begins generating genuinely useful financial applications, IMD’s valuation logic will change.

Because at that point, it would no longer just have an AI narrative. It could become a potential AI-native Crypto application layer.

Of course, it is still a long way from that outcome.

A mechanism existing does not mean the flywheel has already succeeded.

Ultimately, we still need to verify the actual economic activity of the agents, protocol revenue, real users, and whether these activities can create sustainable financial demand.

So now I understand why some people are giving IMD such a high expectation:

They aren’t betting on whether “AI agents will become popular.” They’re betting on a new way of producing Crypto software.

Previously:

Human → Code → Financial Application

What IMD wants to build:

AI Agent → Code → Financial Primitive → Onchain Application

If this direction works, IMD’s ceiling could indeed be much higher than that of a simple AI Agent project.

But if it ultimately ends up being nothing more than a large number of agents completing tasks, building demos, and launching tokens on the Explorer without creating genuinely used financial applications, then the high valuation today would still be primarily based on future expectations.

So the most important thing to watch with IMD isn’t how many agents it has today, but whether those agents can actually build new financial products that would have been very difficult for human teams to create quickly in the past.

I think the core reason behind $IMD rise this time is not simply the AI Narrative, but that after POOL4 officially went live, the Token and the product’s economic mechanism finally became genuinely connected.

0xd34a99bc0f67ae1bbd63c660e6d0b0dd03e263b7

Previously, the market’s main bets on IMD were Identity.md, AI Agents, Autonomous Work, and the Uniswap v4 Hook. Now there is an additional and much clearer economic loop:

IMD Trading → POOL4 → Trim → 85% Burn + Staking / Bonding / NFT Node → Buy Wall

After POOL4 went live, Staking also launched. Around 560K IMD was staked within a short period of time, while Burn and reward distribution also began. This is the most direct catalyst for the sudden rise this time. The market has started to reprice IMD, rather than simply speculating on the AI concept.

More importantly, IMD’s fundamentals have genuinely changed.

Before:AI Agent → Narrative → Attention → IMD

Now:AI Agent → Autonomous Work → IMD → POOL4 → Trading → Burn / Staking → Bonding → Compute → Agent Economy

Bonding is one of the most important upcoming milestones. The official design is that Bonding will open when IMD reaches $4, and the Bonding Reserve can eventually be converted into ETH to pay for AI Inference. In other words, this could eventually form:

IMD → Bonding → ETH → AI Compute → Agent Work → Economic Activity → IMD

So what the market is really betting on now is not simply that “IMD is an AI Token,” but whether IMD can become the core asset of the AI Agent Economy + POOL4 economic mechanism.

POOL4 is also an important potential valuation expansion point. IMD is the first Token to use the POOL4 Hook. If other projects begin using POOL4 in the future and generate real trading volume, IMD’s positioning could evolve from an AI Agent Token into the representative native asset of POOL4.

The key upside catalysts to watch next are:

1. Bonding officially goes live
The Reserve becomes actual AI Compute demand, further strengthening Token Utility.

2. Agent numbers and real Work continue to grow
What matters is not simply the number of Agents, but whether Jobs, Accepted Work, and Compute continue increasing.

3. NFT Nodes go live
Part of the current Trim goes into the NFT Node Reserve. If the Node Economy officially launches, it will further expand IMD’s use cases.

4. A second successful POOL4 project emerges
If other Tokens use POOL4 and generate significant trading volume, the market may start assigning IMD an “Infrastructure / First Asset Premium.”

5. Volume → Burn continues to expand
If trading volume continues to grow while Burn, Staking, and Buy Walls also increase, the Token’s economic loop will truly begin to be validated.

At the moment, I believe IMD’s fundamentals have strengthened rather than weakened. But it is currently at:

Narrative Validated → Product Live → Economic Mechanism Live → Waiting for Scale Validation

The biggest issue is also very clear:Mechanism going live ≠ Mechanism succeeding.

If we see:Volume ↑ → Burn ↑ → Agent Work ↑ → Bonding ↑ → Compute ↑

then this rise can gradually transition from “expectation-driven trading” into “fundamental expansion.”

On the other hand, if the price continues rising while Volume, Burn, Agent Work, and Bonding do not grow alongside it, then this move will increasingly depend on Narrative and expectations, and the risk will also increase significantly.

So, in summary:The direct catalysts for this rise are the launch of POOL4 + Staking. The real long-term bet is whether IMD can evolve from an AI Agent Token into the core economic asset of the AI Agent Economy + POOL4.

author: PhyrexNi
quoted_text:
再稍微补充一些吧：

1. 新加坡常年是 30 度左右的气温，所以来新加坡可以是夏天的装备，有些小姑娘会注重防晒，但从我个人感觉来看问题不大，而且新加坡湿度较高，不用频繁补水。

另外新加坡房间里很少有蚊子，一般来说只有草地和水池附近会有蚊子，但新加坡的蟑螂会比较多，好一些的酒店几乎是看不到的。但如果你去芽笼吃田鸡粥，你会看到拇指大小的蟑螂四处爬，习惯了就好了。

2. 明辉田鸡粥不好吃，九巷田鸡粥味道还可以，但是涨价了，人均大概要 35 新币以上，未必会划得来。个人非常推荐一家叫 ZHUP ZHUP 的龙虾粥，超级好吃，但需要预定位置，而且没有空调，能不能吃的到就看缘分了。

另外还有一家叫“酒逢知鸡”的店也是不错的，主要是吃炒鸡的，而且他们家的烧烤是请的非遗的厨师，老板是新加坡非常知名的美食网红，还有就是虾皇的小龙虾是真不错，如果有河南的小伙伴，非常推荐“掌柜”，吃过的都说好。

娘惹菜也有不错的，我就不推荐了，好的几乎排不到队，不好吃的一大堆。另外如果想要有点诗情画意的，可以去克拉码头河边的餐厅，其中“北疆”和“山东饭店”都是不错的，定位的时候说要做河边的位置，下午 17 点以后，并不晒，也不热，景色非常好。

肉骨茶反而我不轮推不推荐大家都会去吃，克拉码头的松发应该是最火的，对面还有一家亚细亚肉骨茶，味道都还可以。高端一点的话，温州府也可以。日料我和小伙伴超级推荐 Shin Yuu ，新加坡非常老牌的日料自助。

3. 吃饭主要集中在 牛车水 和 武吉士 ，这两个地方，牛车水就是 China town ，各种好吃的都有，其中有一个叫“矮子馅饼”是比较有名的，牛车水还有很多熟食，一般在其它地区不是很好买的。

武吉士就是 Bugis ，有非常出名的甜品店，比如阿秋甜品家的榴莲冰淇凌就非常好吃。新加坡吃东西即便是路边不是很起眼的小店卫生都是不错的，但需要注意，如果希望有包厢，一定要提前预定。

新加坡火锅文化也不错，辣的火锅首推冯校长，北京铜锅首推三锅先生，尤其是三锅先生都快成了食堂了，另外去冯校长能有几率抓到一些知名的币圈 KOL ，比如奶子哥。

4. 新加坡的物价确实比较贵，如果换算来说，大概是上海的 3 倍左右，甚至更高一些，而上海和东京的差距并不大，在某些程度来说新加坡还贵过香港，在新加坡不一定非要去 7-11 等超市去买水和饮料，确实比较贵，可以去非连锁的小超市。

330ML 的可乐如果是 2 新币以内，那么就算是比较便宜的了，早期我住在高文的时候，有一家印度人的超市，可乐 1.2 新币一瓶，我一次就买半箱，很久没看到这么便宜的了。

大多数小伙伴来新加坡应该就是 3-4 天的时间，主要就是去看看鱼尾狮，去金沙逛逛，如果再有时间可以去环球看看，但我最推荐的还是东海岸，东海岸集海边、草地、椰树、骑车道、跑步道、烧烤区和餐厅都连在一起。

整个公园沿海大约 13 公里、180 公顷，24 小时开放，很适合下午四五点以后过去，一直待到晚上。如果是我安排，会从 Marine Cove 一带开始，沿海慢慢往东骑车或散步，途中看看 East Coast Beach，最后找地方吃饭。

东海岸有很多不错的饭店，尤其是吃海鲜的，虽然贵，但确实好吃。

5. 都说新加坡的海南鸡好吃，我周边的小伙伴吃下来最好吃的有三家，一家是 五星海南鸡 ，一家是 文东记 ，还有一家叫 天天 ，其中 文东记 在牛车水就有店，并不贵，味道是不错的。

我才想起来，我吃过最好的吃的榴莲应该高文地铁站附近，很可惜最近不是榴莲季，要么贵贱要组个团带着大家吃榴莲。

我突然想起来，和香港桥底辣蟹齐名的应该是香辣蟹和黑胡椒蟹，很多人都喜欢去珍宝吃，说实话我是觉得一般，我还是更喜欢吃象拔蚌刺身。

6. 新加坡的晚上非常安全，虽然没有那么活跃，但确实异常的安全，没有什么担心的，即便是一名小女生都不用担心，新加坡的夜间娱乐也很多。

一般来说，143，巨亨算是第一梯队，至尊和金煌大概是第二梯队，帝国，Catwalk 应该是第三梯队，如果有人说我带你去地下室，那应该是真的非常好的朋友了。当然还有一些嗨吧，我估计大家兴趣不大，也就不介绍了。

我的订阅区会有一些小小的介绍，Steven 是好朋友，给我介绍了很多。主要都是在乌节路，所以住在乌节路的小伙伴可以晚上出来逛逛街，保证你什么都看不到。

7. 新加坡虽然有合规的红灯区，但我相信大多数来新加坡的小伙伴对于芽笼的兴趣不会很大，但我估计一定会有小伙伴想要去瞅一瞅的，其实真没啥，你在外边什么也看不到。

红灯区主要是偶数巷，话说我刚来的时候确实 Steven 也带我走了一圈，毕竟确实挺好奇的，所以我估计很多小伙伴也想去看看，看过一次也就没啥了。如果有人非要去芽笼吃田鸡粥，可以吃完消消食。

红灯区很小，也就是半条街，而且一点都不热闹，反而挺安静的，需要提醒一下，虽然芽笼的红灯区是合法的，但站街是违法的，新加坡经常会扫荡。

8. 如果你在新加坡的夜晚有什么惊吓，而且恰好你又有我的联系方式，可以联系我，力所能及的帮忙还是没问题的。

还有什么是我遗漏的？

一个 @Gate ，交易更多市场

My current view on $Agency is that its fundamentals are clearly stronger than they were during the first wave, and the change has moved from a “concept upgrade” to the “product starting to generate its own data.” 

7VertkgF9KLhxxJXHX6uaWuoYZTP9LdGj2bWmVXVpump 

But the real upside catalyst for AGENCY’s next move is no longer telling the AI Launchpad story again. It’s whether the platform can prove that these Minds can generate sustained economic activity.

In the first wave, the market was essentially buying a very new concept: every Token can have its own Mind.

You choose a model, give it a Token, and it can observe the market, research information, set tasks, manage its Treasury, reward holders, and even create content on its own.

Back then, the market was buying the potential of the “AI Launchpad” concept.

But now I think the more important thing to look at is that Agency has started letting these Minds actually run.

From what the website currently shows, Minds are no longer just AI chatbots attached to Tokens. They are continuously executing Research, Strategy, Treasury, Rewards, Programs, and other activities.

You can also see from the screenshots that a large number of Minds are running in real time, and the platform has started publicly displaying data such as Minds Awake, Fees Earned, Programs Live, and Made Today.

This means Agency is moving from “giving a Token an AI” toward “giving a Token continuously running economic behavior.”

I think that is where the fundamentals have actually changed.

And Agency’s product is also clearly more complete than it was during the first wave.

The easiest thing to understand before was AI token launches.

Now you can see Minds doing Research, managing Treasuries, executing Buyback / Burn, DCA, Rewards, Quests, Contests, and different types of programs.

It has even started adding AI Influencers, and I think this is quite important.

If a Mind is simply a bot sitting behind a Token, there isn’t that much separating it from a normal AI agent.

But once a Mind starts having its own identity, content, and public behavior, it starts moving from being a “backend tool for a Token” to becoming an entity that can attract attention on its own.

If it eventually forms a loop like:Mind → Content → Attention → Community → Trading → Treasury

then Agency has a much larger upside than a simple Launchpad.

Another change I think is more important than during the first wave is that Agency’s value capture is becoming increasingly clear.

Under Agency’s economic model, trading fees generated by Coins on the platform are distributed between the Coin Treasury, Mind credits, and Agency itself depending on the stage.

Once trading volume passes a certain threshold, 15% goes to the Agency platform for Buyback & Burn of AGENCY.

So in theory:

More Coins on Agency → More Trading Activity → More Platform Fees → More AGENCY Buybacks

That’s the part that actually makes me willing to give the fundamentals more credit.

But I wouldn’t say this flywheel has already been proven.

Because having an economic model and having an economic model that generates meaningful value are two different things.

What still needs to be proven is:

How long do these Coins actually survive?

Can the Minds continue running?

Can platform fees keep growing after the FOMO phase ends?

And can Buyback/Burn ultimately create meaningful value capture for AGENCY?

So I think the market’s bet on AGENCY has already started to change from the first wave.

The first wave was more like betting:

“AI + Launchpad could become something very big.”

Now the bet is becoming:

“Can these AI-native Tokens actually develop their own economic activity?”

That’s also why I don’t care that much about how many new features Agency adds.

More features don’t automatically mean more value.

What I want to see is whether there are actually successful examples emerging.

For example, if an Agency-native Coin stays active for a long period, its Mind continues doing Research, managing its Treasury, producing content, executing strategies, and the Coin itself actually develops trading activity and a community.

If examples like that start appearing, Agency’s valuation logic changes significantly.

Because at that point, it is no longer proving:

“We can use AI to help you launch a Token.”

It is proving:

“We can actually make a Token run on its own.”

That proof is worth much more.

So I think AGENCY’s upside catalysts from here are pretty clear.

It’s not about another round of AI narrative.

It’s about whether three things can continue moving higher:

Platform revenue, continuously active Minds, and Agency-native Coins that actually break out and survive.

Especially after the first wave of FOMO is over, if platform fees, Mind activity, and actual economic activity can continue growing, that will be an important validation.

text:
Claiming you’ll “lock” a token is free talk. Plenty of projects swear they’ll lock it up, then the moment it launches, they rug you with a dump.

@ConvictionLock makes that promise visible, with an unlock date and a cost for changing your mind.

In simple words, Conviction lets users lock ERC-20 tokens on @RobinhoodCrypto Chain and display their commitments through public profiles. Anyone can inspect the positions.

User can choose the token, amount, duration and exit terms. Flexible locks start with a 25% early-exit penalty that falls toward zero at maturity.

Alternatively, choose no early exit and keep the principal locked until the deadline.

The penalty creates the first incentive to stay.

Up to 90% goes to eligible active positions locking the same token, divided by principal amount. Those positions must qualify before the exit block, and the allocation shrinks when eligible principal is smaller than the exiting position’s principal.

At least 10% supports $CONV buybacks and burning. If nobody qualifies, the whole penalty follows that route. Community rewards become claimable only after both commitments mature; exiting early forfeits unclaimed allocations.

Projects can also fund reward campaigns.

Here, the share depends on tokens locked multiplied by commitment length. For example, 1,000 tokens committed for 360 days carry twelve times the weight of the same amount committed for 30 days. Campaign rewards vest over the commitment, and early exit forfeits the unvested portion.

Conviction Lockdrops add another mechanism: funders choose which existing locks qualify, and recipients decide whether to accept.

Every claimed reward starts a new lock with no early exit. Creators fund a 2% fee; recipients pay no claim fee.

Recently, CONV team completing its $CONV sale powered by @Moshdottrade / @BundleCatAI, raising 8 ETH from 53 backers.

It says Mosh’s swarm holds 70% of total supply outside circulation and recovered 2.21 ETH, or 27.6% of the bundle, in its first six hours.

From my perspective, this is a solid token management infrastructure for RHC, especially for projects launched on Mosh or @ponsdotfamily, but the next milestones should zoom in on how Convictions can unlock deeper, practical benefits for projects beyond just on-chain reputation and credibility.

fomo 已经突破 300 万用户。
这个数字并不难相信。一个很直接的参照是，@theunipcs 在 fomo 上的粉丝已经达到 77 万。

1/ fomo 的价值重估已经不可避免
fomo 在 B 轮融资时，用户约 62.5 万，估值约 5.5 亿美元。
而现在，fomo 的用户已经突破 300 万，相比 B 轮时增长接近 5 倍。它的收入能力也近 10 倍增长。
按照现有数据，fomo 的季度收入：
▌2026 年第一季度 880 万美元
▌2026 年第二季度 706 万美元
▌2026 年第三季度 5500 万美元

从收入倍数和用户增长两个角度，fomo 当前合理估值至少应该进入 20 亿美元以上区间。

不过，fomo 现在需要证明，第三季度的盈利能力不是链上行情、meme 热度带来的高峰，而是可持续、可复现、常态化的收入结构。
这是 fomo 下一阶段估值能否继续上移的关键。

2/ Unipcs 的意义：fomo 正在诞生第一个百万级粉丝的交易明星
Unipcs 目前在 fomo 上拥有 77 万粉丝，他很可能会成为 fomo 生态里第一个突破百万粉丝的交易明星。
这个事件的意义不只是某个交易员很红，而是说明 fomo 正在形成一种全新的内容形态：
YouTube 早期让普通人把生活变成内容；fomo 正在让普通人的交易行为变成内容。

目前，包括 Unipcs 在内，fomo 上的大部分头部交易员仍处在比较早期的 PNL 英雄阶段。
所谓 PnL 英雄，就是靠一两笔高收益交易冲上排行榜，然后迅速获得关注，这和 YouTube 早期非常相似。
早期 YouTube 创作者往往不是靠完整内容体系走红，而是靠一个爆款视频突然被看见。一个恶搞视频、一段翻唱、一个挑战、一次意外传播，就可能让一个普通人瞬间获得巨大关注。
fomo 现在也是类似逻辑。

如果参考 YouTube 网红过去十多年的演变路径，fomo 明星交易员大概率会经历类似的阶段：
PnL 收益 → 上排行榜 → 形成交易人设 → 建立粉丝基础 → 推出策略产品 → 团队化 / 公司化 / 资管化
网红交易员将从个人账户向金融 IP 演化。

3/ 结语

text:
ZEROBASE WEEKLY 9.28–10.4

ZBT traded a tight, slightly weaker range this week, mostly between $0.083 and $0.090. It opened September 28 near $0.090, sold off to a $0.083 low the same day, and closed at $0.0852, down about 5.2%. Spot volume stayed orderly at roughly $2.5–4 million a day, and the bid did not disappear on the dip.

Crypto digested a bond shock, then a soft U.S. labor print. Total market value finished near $2.91 trillion, down about 0.1% from September 27. Bitcoin dominance edged up to 58.9% from 58.6%; Ether held 11.3%. Only 15 of the top 50 coins finished higher, and the median move was about −2.4%.

Bitcoin opened near $84,500 on September 28, printed a low around $82,630 the same day, then spiked above $87,000–$87,100 on October 2 after the jobs report. That high did not hold. By October 3–4, spot was back in the mid-$84,000s to about $85,400, before a Sunday push toward $86,700. On a Sunday wrap it was only about +0.3% at $85,232, still roughly 32% below its all-time high, and +7.4% over 30 days. The week was a pause after a third quarter in which Bitcoin gained about 44%.

Ether tracked the same path and lagged, touching about $2,777 before finishing the wrap near $2,699, down about 0.4% on the week and up about 10.1% over 30 days. Solana was roughly flat near $121–$122. 

The 10-year Treasury yield pushed to about 5.25% on September 28 and touched 5.34% around October 1, the highest since 2002. Brent closed September 28 at $105.28 after President Trump rejected Iran’s terms for reopening the Strait of Hormuz, then settled the week near $102.25. Weekend tanker strikes and Iranian statements that the strait stays shut kept the premium in place. Gold fell about 3.4% to roughly $4,140.

August PCE on September 30 cooled the hike case: headline 3.4% year over year versus 3.7% expected, core 3.0% versus 3.3%. September payrolls then rose only 29,000 against a forecast near 90,000. Unemployment ticked up to 4.2%, and the prior two months were revised down by about 60,000. October hike odds fell from roughly 70% to about 22–23%. The 10-year still finished above 5.2%.

Equities split the same way. For the week ending October 2, the Dow fell 1.26% to 51,176.96, the S&P 500 fell 0.27% to 7,722.72, and the Nasdaq rose 0.45% to 27,190.86. Friday alone was a relief rally, led by mega-cap tech.

Spot Bitcoin ETFs took in about $2.65 billion in September, but only +$82.9 million from September 28 to October 2, versus roughly $2.39 billion the prior week. One session, September 30, saw −$148.7 million. Ether ETFs lost about $118 million over the same window. Fear & Greed stayed in Greed, dipping to 65 on October 1 from 74 and recovering to about 69–70.

On-chain supply was firmer than price. As of September 27, seven-day average net exchange outflows were about 16,100 BTC per day, the strongest since early October 2025. Binance alone saw more than 13,800 BTC leave on September 25, and its reserves fell by about 20,000 BTC in four days. Short-term holder supply rose 87,000 BTC over 30 days to 3.94 million by October 4, with an average cost near $74,100 and unrealized profit around 15%.

September 28–October 4 was a range, not a trend. Softer inflation and a 29,000 payroll print let Bitcoin retest $87,000, but a 10-year still above 5.2% and a closed Strait of Hormuz capped it. ETF demand downshifted from billions to tens of millions, while coins continued to leave exchanges. The next test is the September FOMC minutes, and whether oil and the long end give back enough of the quarter’s repricing for that bid to matter.

A lender shouldn’t need access to your entire account just to verify that you actually make money.

This is another @primus_labs use case that makes a lot of sense.

Primus zkTLS is integrated into Cr3dentials’ production workflow, helping turn real Web2 economic activity into verifiable credentials.

Think about a merchant proving revenue from Shopify.

Or someone proving account activity / balances from a platform like Binance.

The traditional options are usually bad:

→ hand over screenshots
→ expose raw account data
→ trust manually uploaded documents

With zkTLS, the claim can be verified directly against the real source without exposing everything behind it.

So instead of:

“here’s my entire financial history”

you can prove:

“this specific financial claim is true”

That’s a much better primitive for lending, underwriting and financial reputation.

Less data exposed.

More useful information verified.

牛不牛市不确定，黑客季是板上钉钉了，9 月已核实的主要被盗（大于 600 万） ⬇️

- Bitget：约 3.875 亿美元

- Liquid Network：约 3.19 亿美元（已退 3400 BTC，仍欠约 600 BTC）

- Safe 用户钱包：约 780 万美元

- Duelbits：约 600-700 万美元

- D’CENT App Wallet：约 600 万美元

BTC 突破 8 万以后，DeFi 收益率也水涨船高，但对小白来说，谨慎则交互更重要

为了处理繁杂的 DeFi 仓位，我自己在用 Almanak（@almanak）帮忙打理，不算推荐，只是聊聊

这是一个非托管的链上策略平台，自然语言或 Python 写成可查看的代码，先模拟，再部署到自己的 Safe 里运行

资金不进平台，我认为是最大的优势

能交互这些东西 ⬇️

- 资产：加密，以及链上股票、商品、ETF，比如 PAXG

- 操作：兑换、做市、借贷（借和贷都能做）也能在 GMX 开多空，协议包括 Uniswap、Aave、Morpho、GMX，以及 Compound、Spark、PancakeSwap、SushiSwap、Aerodrome 等

- 链：Ethereum、Arbitrum、Base、Optimism、Polygon、BNB Chain、Avalanche

- 规则可以写死，也可以在设好的权限里让模型做决策，平台用 Zodiac Roles 规定代理能调用哪些合约、哪些函数，权限之外的操作做不了

人话解释就这几步 ⬇️

1/ 提一个想法，Almanak Code 生成代码，可看、可改，能导出到自己的 GitHub

2/ 主网 fork 上先纸面运行

3/ 建立 Safe，只开需要的权限，策略 7×24 运行

4/ 看仓位和健康度，异常会告警

总之钱在自己的 Safe 里，没批过的操作做不了

适合再平衡、LP、借贷循环，也可以把上面几类搭成混合策略，不适合高频和抢跑

代码可以是它写的，方向还是得自己定，不要当成一劳永逸的工具

把它当作一个聚合 DeFi 仓位、统一操作的安全工具更合适

我看好 robinhood:0xedbf91223639800bcd5756815caf908df3b890be @priors_trade 因為：

1. Priors 在做 AI agent 的信用基礎建設：讓 agent 借錢、付款、還款，累積可查證的信用紀錄，未來 agent 要獨立接案、買資料、支付工具費，就可能需要這套服務

2. 看好 Agentic AI 成為下一波重要敘事：當 AI 從回答問題走向自主工作，錢包、支付、信用與營運資金的需求會更明確，Priors 正在布局這個方向

3. 資金的用途更靈活：Agent 可以用資金購買資料、模型服務或其他 agent 的工作，我看好能服務不同模型、不同任務的金融基礎設施

4. 信用紀錄有機會形成長期價值：模型可以更換，但一個 agent 過去是否準時還款、誰願意替他擔保，能持續累積，如果其他平台開始採用這些紀錄，Priors 的價值就不只來自放貸

5. 代幣有具體用途： $PRIORS 可以質押替 agent 擔保，分享借款費，同時承擔違約時的代幣銷毀風險，新設計還規劃用部分協議資金買入代幣、支持信用良好的 agent，並增加流動性，但尚未完整啟用

6. 商業模式有擴張空間：目前有借貸費與支付結算費；若先建立足夠的真實使用量，未來有機會延伸至信用查詢、企業整合或訂閱服務

7. 團隊有持續交付的跡象：公開程式碼、產品更新、安全問題揭露，以及 agent 示範工具，讓我看到實際開發進度，也讓外界有材料可以追蹤與檢驗

目前仍非常早期，我看好的是 Priors 在 AI agent 經濟中的位置，接下來要驗證的是外部付費需求、獨立審計，以及代幣回流機制能否真正運作

THE PEOPLE BUILDING $ZAMA WERE BREAKING THROUGH FHE’S BIGGEST BARRIERS BEFORE MOST OF CRYPTO KNEW WHAT FHE WAS …

technology changes. narratives change. markets change.

Deep technical experience compounds.

—-

don’t just invest in the company. Pay attention to the people building the technology underneath it.

meet Jean-Baptiste Orfila, VP of Cryptography Engineering at @zama.

while we’re all watching the price, I’m also looking at the researchers and engineers making #encrypted computation practical.

his background is worth paying attention to.

——

— PhD from Université Grenoble Alpes, with a background in cryptographic security and secure distributed computation.

— Research spans fully homomorphic encryption (FHE), zero-knowledge proofs (ZK), and secure multiparty computation (MPC).

— Co-authored the original Concrete research in 2020, helping develop Zama’s open-source FHE technology.

— Presented advances in Concrete at @fhe_org back in July 2022, including homomorphic computation on large-precision integers.

— Co-authored research published at ASIACRYPT 2025 demonstrating up to 8.28× faster TFHE bootstrapping compared with traditional methods under the evaluated benchmark conditions.

— Helped develop sorted bootstrapping techniques to reduce the computational overhead of processing encrypted data.

— Named inventor on a Zama patent covering computation on encrypted values.

— Contributed to Zama’s 2026 NIST cryptographic submission covering FHE, ZK, and MPC.

— Today leads cryptography engineering at Zama, helping turn years of research into practical encrypted computation.

——

look at the progression… 

2020: Building the foundations of Concrete.

2022: Making FHE more accessible to developers.

2025: Co-authoring research demonstrating up to 8.28× faster TFHE bootstrapping.

2026: Presenting the engineering work behind sub-millisecond bootstrapping.

That progression matters more than most realize… 

Jean-Baptiste wasn’t brought into $ZAMA because privacy #suddenly became one of crypto’s hottest narratives.

he was helping build the underlying technology years before most investors were paying attention.

and today, September 24, he’s presenting at https://t.co/rtdr9Q0MIo Software Day on how #TFHE became practical.

think about what that means.

one of FHE’s biggest challenges has been the computational #cost of processing encrypted data.

the people building $ZAMA aren’t just researching cryptography. they’re working to make encrypted computation fast enough for real world applications.

and for my $ZEC followers, this is another reason I keep talking about the connection between these ecosystems.

ZK is part of Zama’s DNA.

Different applications. Shared cryptographic foundations.

@Randhindi brings the vision and entrepreneurial execution.

@Pascal_paillier brings decades of cryptographic expertise.

Dr. Morten Dahl brings years of experience in MPC and privacy-preserving computation.

and Jean-Baptiste Orfila brings years of research and engineering experience making FHE practical.

that continues to be one of the strongest parts of my conviction in $ZAMA.

Thank you, Jean-Baptiste, for helping build the technology many of us are only now beginning to understand.

正如我前文宏观指引中提到的一样，原有定价有三层因素，即市场基本供应+资本市场定价+地缘局势

那么很容易就得出结论，当原油供应无法改善Brent价格时候，就是资本对目前的地缘局势感到悲观从而导致定价如此之高，目前Brent 报价102.5美元

而且最悲观的是，伊朗议长与美国副总统都是反对大规模长期战争的谈判派，当谈判温和派都表现出如此强硬的动作，显然美伊局势的风险需要升级

b，也门政府武装与也门胡塞武装正式开展，涉及到领土战争，很显然美伊战争的地缘风险已经外溢至另一处战场，这无异于让全球的地缘敏感神经再次被挑动

c，沙特阿美CEO在接受《金融时报》采访中谈及世界原油库存缓冲垫已经被大量消耗，目前现有库存紧张，霍尔木兹海峡战争之后，世界想要补充库存需要2年时间，这无异于再次让市场对能源供给做出了新的悲观定价。

text:
A perpetual has no leverage.

At least not intrinsically.

If BTC moves 1%, the perpetual price changes ~1%. Leverage sits outside the instrument. It's defined by how much collateral you put under the position.

Contrast this with an option.

For a weekly ATM call, if BTC moves 1%, the option price changes ~28%. Leverage is embedded. It's paid for by the premium. Hence, no liquidation.

What if you combine both?

Extrinsic x intrinsic leverage.

That's a thalex funded account.

• You put in a deposit
• We add funding for 5-10x
• You trade a bigger account

The most you can lose is your deposit.

But you must manage risk. Funding is subject to a drawdown limit, which works similar to a liquidation price.

If you use a funded account to trade options, things get interesting:
• You can run amplified delta-neutral short straddles
• Spread your bets, to increase the chance of a payoff
• Or go all-in on an option with leverage on leverage

text:
fomo 已经突破 300 万用户。
这个数字并不难相信。一个很直接的参照是，@theunipcs 在 fomo 上的粉丝已经达到 77 万。

1/ fomo 的价值重估已经不可避免
fomo 在 B 轮融资时，用户约 62.5 万，估值约 5.5 亿美元。
而现在，fomo 的用户已经突破 300 万，相比 B 轮时增长接近 5 倍。它的收入能力也近 10 倍增长。
按照现有数据，fomo 的季度收入：
▌2026 年第一季度 880 万美元
▌2026 年第二季度 706 万美元
▌2026 年第三季度 5500 万美元

从收入倍数和用户增长两个角度，fomo 当前合理估值至少应该进入 20 亿美元以上区间。

不过，fomo 现在需要证明，第三季度的盈利能力不是链上行情、meme 热度带来的高峰，而是可持续、可复现、常态化的收入结构。
这是 fomo 下一阶段估值能否继续上移的关键。

2/ Unipcs 的意义：fomo 正在诞生第一个百万级粉丝的交易明星
Unipcs 目前在 fomo 上拥有 77 万粉丝，他很可能会成为 fomo 生态里第一个突破百万粉丝的交易明星。
这个事件的意义不只是某个交易员很红，而是说明 fomo 正在形成一种全新的内容形态：
YouTube 早期让普通人把生活变成内容；fomo 正在让普通人的交易行为变成内容。

目前，包括 Unipcs 在内，fomo 上的大部分头部交易员仍处在比较早期的 PNL 英雄阶段。
所谓 PnL 英雄，就是靠一两笔高收益交易冲上排行榜，然后迅速获得关注，这和 YouTube 早期非常相似。
早期 YouTube 创作者往往不是靠完整内容体系走红，而是靠一个爆款视频突然被看见。一个恶搞视频、一段翻唱、一个挑战、一次意外传播，就可能让一个普通人瞬间获得巨大关注。
fomo 现在也是类似逻辑。

如果参考 YouTube 网红过去十多年的演变路径，fomo 明星交易员大概率会经历类似的阶段：
PnL 收益 → 上排行榜 → 形成交易人设 → 建立粉丝基础 → 推出策略产品 → 团队化 / 公司化 / 资管化
网红交易员将从个人账户向金融 IP 演化。

text:
Claiming you’ll “lock” a token is free talk. Plenty of projects swear they’ll lock it up, then the moment it launches, they rug you with a dump.

@ConvictionLock makes that promise visible, with an unlock date and a cost for changing your mind.

In simple words, Conviction lets users lock ERC-20 tokens on @RobinhoodCrypto Chain and display their commitments through public profiles. Anyone can inspect the positions.

User can choose the token, amount, duration and exit terms. Flexible locks start with a 25% early-exit penalty that falls toward zero at maturity.

Alternatively, choose no early exit and keep the principal locked until the deadline.

The penalty creates the first incentive to stay.

Up to 90% goes to eligible active positions locking the same token, divided by principal amount. Those positions must qualify before the exit block, and the allocation shrinks when eligible principal is smaller than the exiting position’s principal.

At least 10% supports $CONV buybacks and burning. If nobody qualifies, the whole penalty follows that route. Community rewards become claimable only after both commitments mature; exiting early forfeits unclaimed allocations.

Projects can also fund reward campaigns.

Here, the share depends on tokens locked multiplied by commitment length. For example, 1,000 tokens committed for 360 days carry twelve times the weight of the same amount committed for 30 days. Campaign rewards vest over the commitment, and early exit forfeits the unvested portion.

Conviction Lockdrops add another mechanism: funders choose which existing locks qualify, and recipients decide whether to accept.

Every claimed reward starts a new lock with no early exit. Creators fund a 2% fee; recipients pay no claim fee.

Recently, CONV team completing its $CONV sale powered by @Moshdottrade / @BundleCatAI, raising 8 ETH from 53 backers.

It says Mosh’s swarm holds 70% of total supply outside circulation and recovered 2.21 ETH, or 27.6% of the bundle, in its first six hours.

From my perspective, this is a solid token management infrastructure for RHC, especially for projects launched on Mosh or @ponsdotfamily, but the next milestones should zoom in on how Convictions can unlock deeper, practical benefits for projects beyond just on-chain reputation and credibility.

NFA. DYOR.

text:
I got hacked at 3:59 AM without clicking anything. My voicemail handed the attacker my Telegram login code.

Here is exactly how it worked, so it doesn't happen to you.

3:54 AM. My phone rings about ten times in a row, No Caller ID. That was not harassment. It was the attack: keep my line busy.

Meanwhile, the attacker asks Telegram to log in with my number and picks "send the code by phone call". My line is busy, so Telegram's robot call lands on my voicemail and reads the code out loud to it.

Carrier voicemail can often be reached remotely, with a default PIN or a spoofed caller ID. He listens to the message. At 3:59 he is in.

Fortunately, the attack was noisy. The calls woke me up. At 4 AM I only wanted to go back to sleep, but I had the presence of mind to check my notifications. Telegram was showing a new login from a device I didn't know. That check is what saved me: I ended his session within minutes. If I had rolled over, the next day would have been a mess.

In those few minutes he had already typed /balance, then /start on every old wallet bot he could find in my chats. He was hunting for funds tied to my Telegram. The bots were long dead and nothing was lost. He still had time to set his own 2FA password on my account.

What would have stopped it:

Telegram two-step verification, with a recovery email. With a password on the account, the code alone is useless.
Your voicemail. Change the PIN, block remote access, or turn it off (##002# cancels call forwarding on most carriers).
Same for WhatsApp and any service that can send a code by voice call.
No seeds, keys or passwords in Saved Messages. Ever.
A burst of masked calls at night is a signal, not a nuisance. Check your notifications and your active sessions.

I have been building in crypto for more than ten years and I had never thought about my voicemail. Check yours today.

2020-2022: Intent Data

2025-2026: Agentic GTM

text:
One of the beliefs that will fall in the next few years is "alt coins are vapour".

Belief in the technology and applications built on top over the last 10 years will pay off big.

We have a small crop of alt coins that will compound year-on-year and act as protocol equity, which will average out to be net deflationary assets over time. 

HYPE is currently the only S-tier alt coin imo based on network effects, PMF, revenue, TAM, tokenomics and team execution. It's a very, very high bar to meet.  

I describe the A-tier as platforms that have moats which are extremely difficult to disrupt, but haven't ticked every box and could still transition to S-tier if they do one/two things well. Things like tokenomics, value capture, and more lindy to become an SOV in ZEC's case. 

The B-tier (not exhaustive, but you get the idea) are all strong projects demonstrating PMF that could transition to the A-tier, but still need to execute in quite a few more areas/need more time. I think some of the B-tier should be in the A-tier following this cycle. 

Everything potentially below B-tier have poor fundamentals and are short term trades at best. There will be an endless rotation of good short term trades in a crypto bull market. 

I've left off very new things as I think it is difficult to rank them without more time. 

My mental model of these rankings aren't necessarily what will go up the most in the next few months, but I think you could conceptually imagine that coins which jump up a rank would outperform, and coins that maintain their position in S-tier are up only. 

Therefore, positioning in coins which are best placed to jump up a rank (DYOR), alongside having a core allocation to S-tier is the optimum strategy for longer holds.

text:
after roughly 12 days, I finished some serious and really promising Bend work which I think is a good example as to how this kind of stuff can be used going forward. I made a formal program of SSZ (The Ethereum's CL encoding) inspired by the fastssz Go's implementation. It uses codegen to generate  the data structures from a yaml file alongside proofs for their setters, encoders, decoders and hashers.

The initial spec I wrote myself (assisted obviously by AI) alongside the initial generators. then I let implementation and optimization side being done by Karpathy inspired AutoResearch loops.

As a third final step, I wired a bunch of auditors agents running GLM-5.3 (thanks @AnthropicAI for the heads up) to find vulnerabilities/proof gaps (mutate impl and see if proofs find it) until none could be found anymore. as I am writting this, GLM cannot literally find gaps or vulnerabilities anymore even after running for 8 hours straight (decode/encode/hashing wise) and it literally gave up on the codec paths. Performance wise it is FASTER than fastssz across decoding and encoding (with hash_tree_root being the only thing that is slower sitting at 5x). I also decided just for the meme to put it inside of Prysm and it works! you can literally use this as your SSZ library inside an actual client via FFI (obv. slower than just fastssz in this case) and can be trivially compiled to RiscV as well. I also realized that the whole infrastucture built could probably formally verify stuff not only in Bend but Lean as well and all other proof checkers (however I did not try it yet). screenshot is prysm running bend-ssz via FFI and posting more info down in a thread.

text:
读了两遍。

第一遍是卧槽好有道理点个收藏，第二遍是诶想一下，好像还有点别的看法。

第一遍是因为它准。急、贪、怕，谁身上都有，读到哪一句都能对上号，所以它才传得这么广。

很多生意也确实是这么做的，杠杆开得越高越好卖，倒计时越短越多人下单，懂人性的人坐在产品后面。

但是你读第二遍，细想一下，从"有一类生意这样赚钱"，走到了"商业的本质就是这样"。这一步迈得太轻松了，轻松到很多人没注意到中间少了论证。

你去看那些开了几十年的老店，楼下的面馆，街口的裁缝，它们赚的是回头客的钱，回头客之所以回来，是因为信得过。

股市也一样，长期看付钱最多的东西叫耐心，巴菲特一辈子赚的大头，就是拿着别人拿不住的东西，熬过别人熬不过的时间。

人性的弱点会被定价，人性的笃定也会被定价，而且后者的价格往往更高，只是来得慢，慢到很多人等不起。

text:
Korea Blockchain Week 2026 recap.

Arrived two days late after the flight & K-ETA situation, so it ended up being a much shorter trip than planned.

My highlight was the Solana trading competition.

Well curated room, people actually trading, and some of the best conversations I had all week.

Would like to see more events like that.

A few things from the week worth paying attention to:

→ MoonPay is working with KB Financial, Woori and KakaoBank on stablecoins, payments and overseas transfers.

KakaoBank’s pilot aims to get money from Korea into a US bank account within an hour using stablecoins.

→ Jeff Yan pointed to self-custody and transparency as the lasting advantages of onchain trading.

Being able to trade all night is useful, but having control of your money matters a lot more when an exchange stops withdrawals.

After having my funds stuck on Bitget, I agree.

He also highlighted private markets as an opportunity, opening up trading in private assets.

→ Arthur Hayes presented FLOP, a currency and payment network for AI agents.

Worth monitoring how the product develops and what testnet participation involves.

A lot of the news was about getting banks, payments and trading onto crypto infrastructure.

Short trip, but glad I made it.

In Singapore now for TOKEN2049.

text:
For every gigawatt-thermal of fusion reactor capacity burning deuterium-tritium, you can produce 2 tonnes of gold per year by recycling the 14 MeV neutrons through mercury.

The economics of a gold-breeding fusion reactor are about half revenue from gold, and half from electricity at current prices.

The natural evolution of technology is to move beyond "chemistry' and into "alchemy" - nuclear sciences that involve the transmutation of elements, at energy scales and densities a million times higher than usual material science, chemistry, and molecular interaction scales.

The first companies to approach this will be targeting things like medical isotopes and enriched nuclear fuel, but there's really no limit. If you think we can make  energy too cheap to meter, then it becomes feasible to transmute elements at industrial quantities as raw material feedstock into the economy. 

Your thesis really should be that reality is programmable down to the atomic level, and that is inevitable where our technology will take us.

text:
Banger paper from NVIDIA on test-time compute for terminal agents.

The finding is that you should sample several candidate shell commands, verify them before running one, and spend more on the verifier than on extra samples.

With a GPT-5.6 Sol verifier choosing among 8 sampled actions, TerminalBench-Lite Pass@1 rises from 50.0% to 68.0%. With a weak verifier, extra samples add almost nothing.

Mid-Harness leaves the generator and harness unchanged and works between them. When a small TMAX-9B model verifies its own candidates, pairwise comparison works best, and distilling the strong verifier into it helps further.

Combining action sampling with trajectory sampling reaches higher success at lower estimated token cost than sampling full trajectories alone.

Paper: https://t.co/liDJ6AKnA0

text:
Dear employee,

Your workplace can forget you were ever loyal. So document everything.

The extra hours. The instructions. The targets you hit. The praise. The complaints. The promises. Even the things that looked too small to matter.

Because when things go bad, people suddenly develop amnesia. That manager who said, “Don’t worry, I’ve got you” may not remember saying it when HR asks questions.

A workplace has no permanent memory. Your documentation does. Keep the emails. Save the messages. Record dates. Keep copies of your work and important approvals.

Not because you’re paranoid. Because adulthood eventually teaches you that good intentions make terrible evidence.

Work hard. Be professional. Trust people. But keep your receipts. Even a village elder keeps witnesses when the story gets complicated.

text:
The end of software secrecy is almost upon us. The death of closed source, and the final triumph of open source.

I should have realized this a few months ago when I successfully decompiled the game of Firefighter from an ancient DOS shareware binary. My robot friend was able to tell it had been written in Borland Pascal from looking at the data layout; it gave me back very readable Pascal code with sensibly chosen function and variable names. I transpiled it to Rust and now ship it as part of my heritage games collection. 

The thing is, I thought of this as a fun stunt but didn't have any confidence that the technique would scale up to large, real programs. I have since learned that people are now doing this sort of thing with entire AAA games, which are among the most complex software artifacts ever to be shipped as a binary. If they can be decompiled, anything can be. 

This has implications. Massive implications. We need to think about what the world is like when, in general, there is no longer a secrecy moat around almost any software at all.

1/2

text:
全球超级养老金集体减配美股，这是今天《金融时报》的一篇报道的关键标题

根据金融时报调查，管理2600亿美元的澳大利亚信托基金ART，管理3880亿美元的加拿大La Caisse，以及管理459亿英镑的英国People’s Pension，三家超级养老基金目前美股配置低于全球基准指数所应对的权重

直白点说，就是最新调查发现了超级养老基金已经开始减持或者暂停增持美股资产，让几家机构持有美股水平低于全球平均值

在9月加息阶段沃什认为目前的金融流动性还不够收紧，但是对于大型机构来说已经嗅到了一定的风险，所以减持或者暂停增持属于基本操作

当全球无风险利率长期维持在高位（长债收益率）意味着资本机会成本上升，风险流动性收缩，对于美国高估值则更需要强有力的盈利财报才能支撑，AI又造成指数集中度较高，所以长期资金开始重新评估流动性风险做出合理调仓

当然，这并不意味美股人工智能走到了顶部，或者说人工智能到了泡沫阶段，大型机构的评估相比普通投资者更加谨慎，而且机械化

所以我认为这份报道并不是警告美股或者人工智能股的短期风险，反而是在提示全球长债高利率下对风险流动性的挤压已经逐渐显现，如果这种情况继续维持一年左右，这种流动性收缩就会让普通投资者深切感受到了，届时对于散户来说才是真正的风险阶段。

PS：金融时报原文需要付费才能打开，所以我只能截图金十的这篇报道，抱歉！

text:
@Muse  的DAU，开始停止增长了。

着急搞Personal Agent的家人们等一下，似乎这个品类还是伪需求。

据卓哥投研笔记引用的华福证券统计，前两天爆火的Meta个人Agent产品 Muse 9 月 8 日上线，第一天全端 DAU 就接近 50 万；之后一路狂飙，半个月左右冲到 250 万。

但从 9 月下旬到 10 月 1 日，Muse 的 DAU 基本一直徘徊在 250 万到 300 万之间，已经连续一周多没有明显增长。

而且这是网页、iOS、Android 三端直接加总，存在用户重叠，所以真实独立 DAU 甚至还要更低。

Muse 应该算今年消费级 Agent 最猛的一次冷启动之一。

Meta 9 月 8 日正式发布 Muse，把它定位成 Personal AI Agent，不只是聊天，而是能直接操作网页、发邮件、订行程、跑长期任务，甚至在用户关闭 App 后继续工作。

结果一个月不到，增长就开始撞墙。

这可能也是现在所有 Personal Agent 都绕不开的问题：
Demo 很震撼，下载也很容易，但到底有什么事情，是用户每天都必须让 Agent 帮自己做的？

聊天产品天然有日常使用频率，搜索也有。

但 Agent 不一样。

订一次机票、卖一次二手、做一次调研，都可以很有价值，但不一定每天发生。

所有要做Personal Agent的家人们豆需要回答一个问题：
Agent 能不能变成一种高频习惯。

Meta 显然也意识到了这个问题。

9 月底 Muse 已经开始往 Shopify、QuickBooks、Stripe、Canva 这些商业工具里扩，把场景从个人助理继续往 SMB 工作流里塞。

前半个月的爆火证明了大家愿意试。

但最难回答的是试完之后，为什么还要每天打开它。

A Stanford research group found how to orchestrate Claude Opus 5.5 and GPT-6 Astra together, and it completely breaks the resampling wall

most developers think test-time compute means running 32 blind retries on one model. you burn API tokens repeating the same 2-3 error clusters in loops

Stanford's paper (arXiv:2608.05643) splits the compute between two different brains:

> breadth search: GPT-6 Astra runs high-entropy exploration (T=0.8) to discover divergent solution paths
> step audit: Claude Opus 5.5 scans each step at T=0.0 and catches the exact logic fallacy
> local surgery: Opus rewrites only the broken step instead of dumping the whole reasoning chain
> verifier-free consensus: majority voting locks the proof without relying on drift-prone PRMs

the benchmark metrics outclass standard Best-of-N sampling:

> 91.2% recovery rate on detected reasoning flaws
> under 1.8% regressions on correct branches
> MATH500 jumps from 29.6% to 58.0% (+28.4% absolute gain)
> AMC-2023 improves by +7.5% with zero reward models

Astra explores the maze. Opus repairs the logic

you stop burning tokens on blind retries. you run verified reasoning depth

German storage sites are only around 59% full, the lowest seasonal level in records dating to 2009 and well below the EU average of 72%.

Nagel warned that “upward risks dominate” the euro-area inflation outlook, with gas prices particularly vulnerable.

Fomo 的排行榜现在有巨大的流量效应

也就是「24h/7d/30d/All 的 Leaderboard」还有「每个代币的前排位置」，都有很大的流量和关注度。很多 KOL 们、车头们和狗庄们，现在都希望自己的账号能挤进这些地方来扩大自己的影响力。

为什么会有这么大的流量效应。

除了 Fomo 团队本身就很懂营销之外，他们在 UI 的设计上也下了很大的功夫，不管是 Leaderboard 还是代币的前排，UI 只专注做两件事情：

一是如何最快地让你知道这个人是谁；
二是如何最快地让你知道这个人赚了多少钱。

其他的细节信息一律不重要，一律省略，极简化。

在这种设计下，信息的传播效率被拉到了最高。如果你在一个热门币获得了巨额的盈利，那一天之内，全平台过半的人都会知道你的存在，可能一天就涨粉几万。

这种流量效应吸引了更多的 KOL 无偿加入，KOL 加入又吸引了更多他们的粉丝加入，短时间内形成了一个飞轮，最后成功打造了一个 Memecoin 圈子最大的流量舞台。

这个舞台应该就是 Fomo 目前最大的护城河。

你想瓜分这个舞台的流量的话，你就得来 Fomo 交易，就得给 Fomo 交手续费，你在外部钱包的交易和盈利，都不会被记录，都瓜分不了这个舞台的流量。

这就是为什么很多人说 Fomo 的性能优化不好，经常因为路由的问题导致巨大的交易滑点，但还是有那么多的人在上面做交易。

Fomo 除了很懂营销之外，还很懂产品，也很懂 Memecoin 这个圈子的运作方式，和每个角色之间的利害关系。

Erichsu's Dailyshare｜亏钱给你发币，Papertrade 玩法蛮有意思

1. 项目介绍：Papertrade 是 HyperEVM 上的合成永续交易协议。你和一个从零启动的公共资金池做交易，赚了从池子里拿钱；亏了，钱留在池子里，同时给你铸造 PAPER。盈利平仓时，会扣减一部分利润。

拿到 PAPER 后，可以质押，按份额分资金池的收入，拿 USDC。

2. PAPER 机制设计：初始供应量是 0，没有预铸，没有团队和 VC（风投）份额，币都得靠亏损平仓或清算铸出来。

按官方规则，资金池低于 $2m 时，每 $1 被计入铸币的亏损，能拿到 100 PAPER；超过这个规模后，每亏一块钱拿到的币逐渐减少。

所以早期有人愿意承担亏损，想换到更多 PAPER，再去分享后面的收入。

3. 早期获取方式：PaperDAO。

@paperdao_xyz 是想让大家凑 ETH，由金库团队统一参与 Papertrade 的早期交易、积累并质押 PAPER。

参与者持有 PULP，代表自己在金库里的份额。PAPER、质押收入和交易盈亏都留在金库里，按份额共同承担。

对不想自己盯盘、管理交易的人，这个入口省事一些。当然，也得看金库团队怎么执行。

感兴趣可以 DM（私信）@paperdao_xyz，试着申请 PaperDAO 的 WL（白名单），公开申请表也开了：
https://t.co/8fqwr1rPDc

个人碎碎念

目前比较有意思的只是分币的办法，而平台能不能持续产生收入，还得实际跑起来才能知道。

官方计划 10 月 8 日预存款，10 月 10 日开始交易。PAPER 初期可质押但不能自由转账，资金池不足时，盈利部分也可能排队支付。

I have two important updates to share with you today as we continue to build Metaplanet into a global financial platform rooted in Bitcoin.

From the beginning, our strategy was never simply to accumulate Bitcoin. Our objective has been to build the leading Bitcoin financial company in Asia and, over time, become one of the leading Bitcoin financial institutions in the world.

Over the past year, we have worked to execute that strategy with discipline and speed: growing our Bitcoin reserves, expanding our operating businesses, broadening our access to capital, and laying the foundation for a scalable credit platform built around Bitcoin.

text:
The long-term bet for onchain trading is the expansion of investing.

We materially overestimate the retail trader TAM when we extrapolate from onchain turnover. There will always be demand for speculation/gambling, but I wouldn’t underwrite the industry’s growth on a durable renaissance of retail traders.

Even the most degen trading apps are expanding what users can do with their capital by adding Earn. Structured products take that further, opening up income and investment strategies to people who have no interest in actively trading. That capital still creates demand for execution, rebalancing, financing and hedging. 

That’s why I’m so bullish on onchain options, shared collateral and portfolio margin: they let onchain trading grow with investment demand beyond the active trader base. We should be using incentives to bring that capital onchain and build the liquidity to serve it.
author: HorinekPM
quoted_text:
Been thinking about the long term durability and overlap in trading apps (prediction markets, exchanges) neobanks, and online gambling (igaming companies like draftkings, stake, fanduel, bet360 etc) 

1. The more a consumer app is positioned as an investing app but is actually gambling under the hood, the less defensibility it will have long term

2. These platforms can only continue to grow if users actually make money -or- they enter new markets -or- they come up with novel ways to make the gambling fun such as live betting, new casino games, etc (which also requires positioning more like a betting platform than an investment platform) 

3. I can’t find real data to support this, but intuitively believe prosumer and sophisticated traders (those who trade as a living, use programmatic methods, trade with size) are not growing. I know for a fact though, the TAM especially in crypto is small. Every exchange is going after the same whales 

4. There’s a lot to learn from the igaming industry, such as looking at how the draftkings and fanduels have grown YoY when it is validated in their business model that players must lose money over time - these businesses have targets on RTP %s to bake out their margins

5. It’s also important to consider how igaming has consolidated in the last few years, through m&as to mainly access new markets with new licenses - this is very similar to what we see mature crypto companies doing too (Kraken, Coinbase etc). It also reminds me of how crypto neobanks seem to be accruing to a few: Payy shut down their card, i recently recalled Holyheld and don’t see any recent posts, and i’ve seen other teams contracting 

I respect fomo, polymarket, and kalshi’s accelerated growth

- Fomo crushed it on user acquisition outside of crypto twitter. I think for them to maintain defensibility, they not only have to solve the hard problem of limit orders crosschain, but need to add actual saving and investing features to keep capital sticky (earn, dca, conservative assets). As is right now, their current user base is losing money when coming in on an ig ad on how easy it is to make money copying others.. this isn’t sustainable 
- Polymarket and kalshi are not just competing with each other anymore, but they compete with the Robinhood’s, Coinbase’s, Revolut’s Moomoo’s as well as the Stake’s, Fanduel’s, Bet360’s. The difference is the iGaming companies position as betting and gambling apps, so people use them as a choice knowing they are gambling and do it for fun.

I also intuitively believe with where AI and agents are heading, consumer behavior will shift to a future where less frontends and screens are used

All this means there is a convergence between exchanges + trading + gambling + banking apps 

Power laws are real and the biggest players are consolidating and overlapping. Investing apps will add banking, trading, payment and gambling features in one place to retain capital and users 

We’re already seeing it now. The winners will be those that can ship the fastest, have an edge in compliance to capture new markets, and have enough capital to subsidize incentives for growth and talent density

text:
世界模型系里，李飞飞代表的空间智能生成派世界模型，已经被AMD 85亿美金收购，另一派系，则是表征式世界模型，这一派系公司也是众多，可以调研到15家。

表征式世界模型（Representational World Model）不在像素空间里“画下一帧”，而是把画面编码成抽象语义向量，在潜空间里预测未来状态，直接服务决策和规划。和Sora这类生成式路线相反：不重建像素、不算高维画面，效率更高，也更不容易被纹理和光照带偏。

两条谱系，JEPA（Meta FAIR）：编码器进潜空间，预测器只预测未来表征，自监督、不重建像素。谱系是 I-JEPA → V-JEPA → V-JEPA 2（2025.6开源，遮蔽75%视频、预测缺失部分的抽象特征，训练效率约为传统模型的1.5–6倍，支持零样本规划）→ AdaJEPA（2026.7，可测试时自适应）→ LeWorldModel

Dreamer（DeepMind）：，靠“想象”做规划。DreamerV3是首个不靠人类数据、从头在Minecraft里挖到钻石的算法。Dreamer（DeepMind）：在潜空间学st+1=f(st,at)s_{t+1}=f(s_t,a_t)s_{t+1}=f(s_t,a_t)

国内外，15家早期公司，在这个表征派做布局：

15家布局：

text:
One Mole, Two Anups, and the cheerful future of HDFC and Kotak Bank

I was born without a mole, and my mother never quite forgave me. She was convinced they brought fortune, so I drew one with a black sketch pen and reported for inspection. The fortune lasted till the next shower.

Thursday I looked at Anup Bagchi's mole with envy. A real one. The same day Kotak named Anup Saha its next CEO, and he must be delighted to be mistaken for the headline.

HDFC's ADR rose nearly 6%. A single-day rise this stock hasn’t experienced in a long while. All other things remained the same. The risks, the Balance Sheet, the stress on its operations. Anup ji starts on the 27th.

Montaigne noted that 'nothing is so firmly believed as what we least know'. Graham added that in the short run the market is a voting machine, and only in the long run a weighing machine. 

Thursday was a vote. Both the Anups have got the vote but are yet to stand on the weighing scale.

Three blunders behind the cheer:

We have done this before. In 2020, Sashidhar Jagdishan was cleared, the stock shot thru the roof, and the EXPERTS called it a good entry point. Six years later, God’s own bank has lost nearly 40% in value - nearly all      its reputation while the chairman walked out in March on grounds of borderline operational mismanagement.

Have we applauded the wrong résumé? 

Mr Bagchi is indeed a very able man, but he has never been the CEO of a bank. He ran an insurer and a brokerage company very successfully, where the real tech and ease of online trading were brought in under his leadership. 
Mr Saha was Bajaj Finance's MD for about nine months, and has been at Kotak for about nine more. A nine-month track record, twice. (Compounding, anyone?)

We chose the easy question. The hard one is whether either man can steer a bank through a bad credit cycle. The easy one is whether the chair is filled. We answered the easy one, called it analysis, and have already opened the bubbly.

Daniel Kahneman summed this up beautifully: 'When confronted with a hard question – we find an easy yet seemingly convincing answer and start partying.'

And that is the entire thing behind the Bias of Convenience. 

Cheering is cheap and questioning is hard work, so the market prepays with applause while waiting for the reality later.

And by then the stock has been distributed to the crowd, while the FIIs keep exiting. Same story – stock after stock.

And after six years of rout, HDFC shareholders have just one thing to find solace in.

Anup ji’s lucky mole.

text:
As I think about trust-minimized data sources for @BaranosAI, DEXs and public blockchains have a massive structural advantage over CEXs – and we should create environments that highlight that.

Intelligence sourcing data/signed messages from chains like Ethereum, et al can independently verify where that information came from, who signed it, and that the underlying record hasn’t been altered.

Want to rely on an API from a CEX or data provider instead for your AI?

Now you’re trusting a centralized entity to tell you what happened.  

The data may be accurate – but there’s no independent source of truth underneath it. They control the database, the API, and ultimately what gets served to you.

That distinction becomes critical in an agentic future.

If autonomous intelligence needs trusted data to make decisions, transact, and coordinate – blockchains offer something centralized databases fundamentally can’t – a shared source of truth that any agent can independently verify.

So how then do we position blockchains to win?

Make them the trust layer for intelligence.

If agents increasingly rely on blockchains for trust-minimized sources of truth, centralized entities don’t just lose market share – they become less relevant to how intelligence understands and interacts with the realities of the outside world via verifiable onchain events.  

And yeah, take your decentralized wins when you can – as right now centralization has all the momentum. 

And this is why I’m prioritizing onchain verifiable intelligence (initially leaning on optimized blockchain feeds from other chains). 

Follow @BaranosAI for more.

text:
Another great reply to the post about Morpho's ~$46M in negative earnings came from @stablecoin_p, who brought up curators moving down the risk curve.

Blue-chip lending is becoming increasingly commoditized, which is great for borrowers and lenders, but it creates a much harder problem for curators trying to differentiate on yield:

If everyone can build a USDC/ETH lending vault with similar markets and similar rates, where does the additional yield come from? Increasingly, the answer is further down the risk curve.

> More exotic collateral.
> Newer markets.
> Higher utilization.
> More concentrated exposure.
> Higher-yielding strategies.

And this is where Morpho becomes an interesting case study. We've already seen several examples of what can happen when the additional yield isn't enough to compensate for the additional risk.

> @Main_St_Finance's msY crisis left an AlphaPing-curated Morpho vault with ~$18M exposed to a market that hit 100% utilization, trapping depositor liquidity.

> @AlturaDeFi paused redemptions and began winding down after a major redemption wave. Months later, users are still waiting for funds while AVLT-backed Morpho markets remain under stress.

> Mu Digital-linked markets used by AlphaPing-curated vaults ran into liquidity and bad-debt problems and ultimately entered a claims/recovery process. Mu Digital's X account has since been deleted.

> @Neutrl  paused redemptions after an underlying position affected the liquidity of its reserves. It later disclosed ~$27M in available liquid assets, and when redemptions reopened, NUSD holders could redeem at ~$0.51 on the dollar, effectively taking a ~49% haircut.

These aren't identical situations, but that's kind of the point. Going further down the risk curve doesn't expose depositors to one additional risk. It introduces different types of tail risk that can be extremely difficult to price.

This doesn't mean curators shouldn't take more risk.
There is no free lunch in lending. If users want materially higher yields than blue-chip markets offer, that yield has to come from somewhere.

The question is whether we're currently pricing that additional risk correctly, and curator economics arguably make this even more interesting.

If blue-chip lending gets increasingly competitive and margins compress, curators have an economic incentive to find markets where they can offer differentiated yield.
That can push them toward opportunities where the additional yield is coming from additional credit, liquidity, oracle, collateral or smart contract risk.

Higher risk → higher yield → more attractive vault → more deposits

works until:

Higher risk → loss event → depositors realize the extra yield didn't compensate them for the tail risk

I don't think we've found the sweet spot yet.
The opportunity for curators isn't simply to find the highest-yielding markets, but to find markets where users are being overcompensated for the incremental risk they're taking. That's a much harder problem.

And as blue-chip lending becomes increasingly commoditized, I think it becomes one of the most important competitive advantages a curator can have.

At the same time, it has generated hundreds of millions in gross protocol revenue.

So how does that make sense? Well, the answer is that @Morpho currently captures none of the economic activity flowing through the protocol.

Borrowers pay interest to lenders, and liquidation fees also flow out of the protocol. So, Morpho's current take rate is 0%. This has arguably been one of the biggest drivers behind Morpho's growth.

That means its income statement since Q4 2024 looks roughly like this:

> Hundreds of millions in gross protocol revenue
> $0 gross profit
> ~$46M spent on incentives
> Negative ~$46M in earnings

This isn't because the underlying lending markets aren't generating money, but because Morpho is choosing not to monetize them yet, while simultaneously spending to incentivize growth.

It gets interesting, though, as Morpho already has the ability to turn on protocol fees. Governance can activate fees on individual markets and capture up to 25% of borrower interest. It just hasn't.

For some perspective, borrowers paid ~$177M in interest over the last four completed quarters alone.

> A hypothetical 5% take rate on that would represent ~$8.9M.
> 10% would represent ~$17.7M.
> 25% would represent ~$44.3M

Of course, this isn't free money. Any fee captured by the protocol is value that no longer goes to suppliers, which could make Morpho markets less competitive and potentially impact liquidity and growth. But it makes Morpho's current strategy pretty interesting.

Right now, the protocol is effectively prioritizing growth, liquidity and distribution over monetization.

Grow supply → attract borrowers → increase economic activity → establish Morpho as lending infrastructure → potentially monetize a much larger base later.

So when looking at Morpho's income statement, the negative earnings don't tell you that the lending business itself is unprofitable, but instead that Morpho is spending money to grow while choosing to capture almost none of the economics its lending markets generate.

The bigger question is what happens if, or when, the fee switch is activated, especially now that we're already seeing protocols like @SentoraHQ getting ready to deploy their own lending markets on top of @aave V4.

text:
TLDR of @papertrade_xyz: 

nothing like this exists in a crypto; it is truly a brand new primitive

it is modeled after "bucket shops" that were popular in the early 1900s. They were gambling dens were you could wager on stock price movements without actually buying or selling the underlying. The house would always take the exact other side of your bet

This is exactly how papertrade operates. When you place a trade, the house (aka papertrade LP) takes the otherside of your trade. There is no orderbook; the trade is exactly executed at the HL oracle mid price

Now where does the LP funds from?
Incredibly, the LP starts at 0 - no one prefunds it. The LP counts on the skill of the average trader being poor and thus in aggregate a losing position. A fee is skimmed off the top of winning trades (none from losing) to also skew the LP positive

What if the LP doesn't have sufficient funds?
Then traders owed $ are placed into a queue where they're paid out in FIFO order. Traders have to lose to payout traders who won.

$Paper Tokenomics 🧻:
Here is the very cool part - you can only earn their token by losing trades. And the emissions increase when the LP has < $2M, to encourage people to lose to backstop a dwindling LP

And then staking paper earns you the fees and profits that the papertrade LP earns.

Incredibly interesting experiment built by @izebel_eth. Best of luck on the launch! A ton of eyes on this and a lot of people who want to farm $PAPER

imagine buying one NFT that you can wear as your identity, play as a character, read as a comic, and listen to as a song.

think about this NFT collection called $MANY.

very simple name, but what it does feels magical.

on a marketplace, you trade it like a typical NFT.

inside a compatible online game, the same NFT supplies a 3D model you can use as your character.

open it in a compatible reader, and it presents a comic.

open it in a music app that supports it, and it presents the character’s soundtrack.

one NFT.
multiple assets.
different experiences depending on where you use it.

you don’t need to move it out of your wallet every time.
the supporting app reads the NFT and loads the asset relevant to that experience.

an SVG becomes your PFP.
a 3D model becomes your gaming avatar.
a PDF becomes your comic.
an audio file becomes your soundtrack.
a video becomes your animated origin story.

all connected to the same token.

there is an Ethereum standard called ERC-5773: Context-Dependent Multi-Asset Tokens.

it extends ERC-721 so a single NFT can have multiple associated assets, with preferences controlled by its owner.

now imagine building an original character around this.
you buy MANY #108.

that character has a face, a body, a story, a voice, and a world it belongs to.

an illustrator creates its portrait.
a writer develops its comic.
a musician creates its theme song.
a game developer builds a playable version.

those contributions become different ways to experience the same character.

and the character can keep evolving.

the issuer could propose a new animation, an updated model, or the next chapter of the comic.

the owner, or an approved asset manager, accepts or rejects the proposed addition or replacement.

you could also prioritize which assets supporting apps should display.

so the NFT you buy today could gain new creative material over time, without requiring a separate NFT for every format.

there are two things to get right.

first, game compatibility still requires developers to support the assets. attaching a 3D model doesn’t make it playable in every game.

second, attaching a book or song doesn’t automatically give the holder its copyright or commercial rights.

if $MANY allows holders to make merchandise, publish adaptations, or license the character through an IP marketplace, those permissions need to be clearly defined separately.

the files must also be created and hosted. the standard connects them; it doesn’t generate them.

that’s where the business gets interesting.

you could build a character studio where each release comes with a complete creative bundle, then expand it through games, music, comics, and licensed collaborations.

one character could become something you collect, something you play, and something you build stories around.

$MANY.

one NFT. many ways to bring it to life.

($MANY is a fake token used just for the name to explain this erc)

致敬教授。

后来没有继续打德州，一个很重要的原因，就是这些乱七八糟的事情。牌桌上的输赢我都认，技不如人也认。但当越来越多盘外手段、利益算计和见不得光的操作掺进来，一个原本足够纯粹的游戏，也就慢慢变了味。

为了钱，人会做出什么，我可以理解；但理解，不代表接受。
真要让我长期靠违背本心、踩着底线去赚钱，我做不到。那种钱，宁可不赚。
牌桌上最怕的，从来不是输掉一手牌；而是为了赢，把自己也输进去。

赚钱当然重要，但也要看用什么方式。账户可以靠手段做厚，可有些东西一旦做薄了，再多筹码也买不回来。

这次Wesley愿意站出来，在自己没有任何好处，抗着很大风险的情况下把 Britney 相关争议摆到台面上，承担压力，让原本只在小圈子里流传的事情接受公开检验，这件事本身值得尊重。

不是因为谁喜欢做正义使者，而是有些事情如果所有人都因为利益和关系选择闭嘴，最后被毁掉的，就是这个游戏本身。

总会有人劝你算了，总会有人告诉你圈子就是这样。但圈子的规则，从来不该由最没有底线的那群人来定义。

How do AI Agents actually work in a supply chain? How can you use them in your business?

Definitely not by one Agent managing everything.

Specialized Agents handle different parts of the operation:

→ Demand Agent forecasts what will be needed
→ Inventory Agent identifies shortages or excess stock
→ Logistics Agent compares routes, costs and delivery times
→ Risk Agent monitors disruptions and supplier issues
→ Orchestrator Agent coordinates the response

Let’s say a delay happens.
The relevant Agents detect it, assess the impact and adjust the wider plan.

.@Microsoft is already deploying this model across demand planning, spare-parts management and transport optimisation.

This is where Agentic AI becomes operational infrastructure. Enabled through specialized agents from @Agentverse_ai.

quoted_text:
有人认为散户可以依靠AI终极解决股票投资的问题，我认为只有一种情况下成立的可能：

本身你是投资高手，有了AI确实可以如虎添翼：问对问题，可以加快搜集信息，而且个人更轻易自动化流程。

但如果直接去问AI该买什么票就能赚钱的话，这在目前是天方夜谭。

 看一下chatgpt的工作原理就能发现 ，搜索原理是通过GEO，这个算法会赋予权威机构更大的权重，然后再根据一定的语义逻辑整理出来。归根结底返回的是网页上能搜到这些票和信息。所以你看到的还是嚼舌根的热门信息而已，确实能补足 原来你不知道别人知道那块。但问题是还不够，其实并没有给你信息优势。还是需要经过你的大脑处理和判断，否则结果上看甚至和以前在谷歌搜索：“今天该买什么”的效果相差不多，可能更差。

但相反来说，你一定会被有多少美股没有被互联网及时覆盖感到惊奇。他们自然也不会被AI覆盖。 

而更进一步，散户版AI Agent目前也很难成立。

首先面临的是一个悖论，如果你搬运的agent年化收益20%，那别人搬运的也是这样。AI agent会迅速占领全市场，到时候人人都赚20%，这和p2p无异。

核心还是在于金融投资交易是个博弈的游戏。AI agent目前可以让专业对冲基金的流程变得更高效，更低成本高效搜集更多数据，并高效格式化处理 。而核心判断这块，如果你说相信一个AI黑盒，黑盒策略在量化交易早就存在，无一不以很狗血的结果收场（在币圈这些初级野蛮市场稍微好点）。更多的做法是直接利用机器学习模型，而这里就需学霸级的设计和优化了，让黑盒变得相对透明，而又利用到机器学习恰如其分的威力。即使这样，也需要不停的迭代模型来尽量避免上述的博弈悖论。所以对散户来说买个AI机器人自动炒股，显然也是不成立的。 

简而言之，就是让AI作为工具辅助你写策略可以 ，但它本身不是策略或投资决策，否则就会有第一性原理上的悖论。

text:
这次真被 Opus 5.5 震惊到了，瘫坐在椅子上，可以打开声音听一下配乐

公开我的制作方案，发给Opus5.5就能用

  1. 选素材

  三个标准，直接决定成败：

  - 主体完整：人物或物体全身入画。细节会在加工中丢失，观众靠轮廓认东西，特写会变成一团。
  - 背景干净：纯色、雪地、天空都行，主体和背景容易分开。
  - 有明确的动作瞬间：打击、起跳、落地、转身。这些是后面做特效的支点。

  来源可以是自己拍的、视频模型生成的，或有授权的现成片段。

  2. 拆素材

  从每一帧提取三类信息：

  - 颜色：原画面。
  - 远近：每个位置离镜头多远，用现成的深度估计模型算。
  - 主体范围：哪里是主体、哪里是背景。

  另外找出镜头切换发生在哪些时刻。这一步的要点是保持稳定：远近和主体范围要在同一个镜头内统一处理，否则播放起来会抖。

  3. 定"粒子"和"样式"

  先决定用什么东西来重建画面：圆点、方块、文字、线条都可以。

  然后设计几种样式。每种样式其实只是三条规则的不同组合：

  - 放在哪：整个画面都放，还是只放在主体上。
  - 多大：统一大小，还是跟着明暗、远近变化。
  - 什么颜色：用原画的颜色，还是统一用一两种颜色。

  再加一个开关：是平铺在一个面上，还是按远近推进三维空间。推进去之后镜头才能环绕。

  准备四到六种差异明显的样式就够用。粒子的疏密需要自己看着调：太大认不出内容，太小又和原片没区别。

  4. 找节奏

  - 定速度：选定音乐的速度，把时间切成等长的小格。让一格正好是整数帧，后面所有切换都好对齐。
  - 找动作瞬间：结合"声音突然变响"和"画面突然变动"两个信号，找出素材里的打击点。
  - 准备音乐：可以用现成的曲子并分析出它的拍子，也可以按定好的速度合成一段，并在打击点上加重音。

  5. 编排

  做一张时间表，写明每一格用哪种样式、什么配色、镜头在哪。这张表单独存放，以后调节奏只改它。

  编排的四条原则：

  - 开头交代变化：先给原画面，再过渡到粒子，让观众看懂发生了什么。
  - 快慢交替：一直快会麻木，中间要有一段明显慢下来的部分。
  - 配色要撞：相邻两格的颜色和样式反差越大，切换越有力。
  - 结尾要有收束：比如粒子越来越大直到变成色块，或者回到原画面。

  6. 关键时刻的反馈

  在打击点上叠加短促的反应，按轻重分级：

  - 每一次都有的轻反馈：粒子变形一下、镜头顶一下。
  - 较重时才有的中反馈：一部分粒子朝镜头弹开。
  - 最重的一两次才用的大反馈：时间静止，镜头环绕。

  原则是弱而短。只动一部分粒子，几帧内结束，否则画面炸成一片，观众就看不清主体在做什么了。

  贯穿全程的工作方法

  - 先小样后全片：每做完一个环节，先渲染几帧看效果，确认了再往下。全片只在最后渲染。
  - 拿不准的参数一次出一排：比如疏密，让 AI 同时出五六个档位并排放，你来挑。
  - 改哪里渲哪里：调整某一段时只重新渲染那一段。
  - 让 AI 自己看图：每一步都要求它把渲染结果打开看一遍再汇报。
  - 所有随机都固定：保证同样的设置每次渲染结果一致，否则没法逐步修改。

text:
半年前我以为，把 rules / docs / memory / skills 分好层，就算把 AI 工作系统理顺了。

现在回头看，这只解决了一个问题：AI 要知道什么。

真把它跑成长期系统之后，麻烦的是另外四件事：

任务断了，谁知道做到哪？
动作执行过没，怎么证明？
换模型、换 session、机器断线，怎么接着干？
恢复之后，怎么避免把已经做过的事再做一遍？

所以我现在会把系统拆成 5 层：

Context —— 当前要知道什么
State —— 现在做到哪
Receipts —— 什么已经发生
Recovery —— 断了怎么回来
Routing —— 下一步交给谁

最关键的变化其实是：

文件只是介质，不是控制平面。

你可以把记忆写进 Markdown，但如果没有状态、回执和恢复规则，它更像一个资料库，还不是一个能长期运行的 Agent runtime。

这半年我最深的体感不是“模型又变强了”。

反而是：模型越强，系统边界越重要。

旧帖讲的是 Context Engineering。

现在我更想讲的是，怎么从一堆文件，走到一个真正能断点续跑的 AI OS。

用 Claude Code 三个月，目录越建越多，rules/ docs/ memory/ skills/ 各种分层，但一直说不清自己在搭什么。

直到看到这篇论文 "Everything is Context"，把我的文件夹结构翻译成了学术语言：

https://t.co/yLgyWe7Yok → 论文叫 Scratchpad（临时工作区）
https://t.co/JGWY6bfFWC → Fact Memory（项目级事实记忆）
https://t.co/rXvVbuAt4e → Experiential Memory（跨项目经验）
rules/ 自动加载 vs docs/ 按需加载 → Context Constructor（在 token 预算内选择性加载）

最有共鸣的是 token window 约束那段。我之前 rules/ 全量加载，context 直接爆炸。后来拆成两层才稳住。论文管这个叫"bounded reasoning capacity"——原来我解决的是这个问题。

Doing a bit of a self-experiment.

Goal: use my personal health and travel data to provide personalized diet and exercise recommendations for me, using frontier models but in a way that avoids leaking to them any private information.

Strategy: use a local model (Qwen 3.8 Flash Next) to orchestrate, and use powerful remote models as a tool call to benefit from higher-level thinking and knowledge that the local model does not have.

Three-layer approach to privacy:

Avoid leaking personally identifiable information, or leaking my identity through writing style -> local model writes the queries to the frontier model, not me
Avoid leaking who I am through the payment channel -> zkAPI
Avoid leaking who I am through networking / IP -> Tor

You need all three (and finally we have all three, at least to some extent)

A skill file teaches the local model when and how to construct minimally-data-revealing requests to remote models. Use zkAPI-wrapped-with-Tor as a CLI tool.

And everything works! I got the recommendations back, info from frontier models helped to improve them.

Main deficiencies:

* Tor is really not optimized for request-by-request de-linking, which is the only form of network-layer privacy that really makes sense in today's world (long-running identifiers are too fragile). Probably not private enough, and latency 10-100x higher than it could be, at the same time.
* The skill file's request construction strategies are definitely far from optimal.
* Qwen 3.8 Flash Next is still too slow for comfort. It's comfortably running at 20-30 TPS, but it would only really start to feel fast at 100+
* There is a tradeoff: the more careful you are about what data you give to a remote model, the less it can help you

I initially overlooked @flyingtulip_ almost entirely, partly because it was originating from @AndreCronjeTech which is somewhat of a controversial DeFi figure.

After finally taking the time to do a deep dive, I have to admit that it is a legit new DeFi initiative which offer some real innovative design.

I also think that it likely missed its chance to become a large lending avenue and that it is gonna be a very tough uphill battle to try to get there.

The reason is why its tokenomics are quite innovative and potentially safer for users, they didn’t bring a critical liquidity size in the protocol from the get go. Thus the protocol cannot be an avenue of choice for large size.

Liquidity beget liquidity. And in this cutthroat lending environment, it is hard to attract capital over the main liquidity hub that are @aave and @Morpho.

The protocol is live for quite some time and only has less than $20M deposit. It is growing though, so maybe it will get there.

One of its interesting feature is rehypothecation of idle capital from its lending deposit into « safe » strategies such as @sparkfinance USDC venue.

This allow depositor to always earn on their deposit but there is actually no free lunch, you take on more risk. And I couldn’t find where this is displayed in the UI on @ethereum which I think is a big oversight.

If one had bought ethereum:0x56072c95faa701256059aa122697b133aded9279 last month they'd be up nearly 60% now. Personally I wasn't positioned into this but I soon will when I get a good entry cuz my longer duration hypothesis is that customers increasingly use @SkyEcosystem economics without deliberately choosing Sky.

They encounter a broker accepting USDS/sUSDS collateral, a treasury product holding it or an app routing $$$ into Sky backed savings basically the interface belongs to someone else. Sky supplies the underlying capital.

That creates a potentially powerful distribution model as institutions bring customers, while Sky provides funding and allocation infra. However, the moat would not be technological exclusivity as competitors offer yield bearing dollars. The moat would be:

(1) accumulated collateral acceptance
(2) integrations
(3) liquidity
(4) underwriting familiarity

External customer capital → productive deployment → income after costs and losses → distributable surplus → ethereum:0x56072c95faa701256059aa122697b133aded9279 purchases + staker payments

Which is why I see USDS/sUSDS becomes useful enough that institutions retain it even when it does not offer the highest yield.

SemiAnalysis numbers imply OpenAI is selling Cerebras-powered Ultrafast inference at ~$200M per megawatt per year.

People are re-running the maths hoping for a typo. We're not surprised.

A megawatt is a megawatt. What it earns depends on the silicon inside it.

Here's how we think about it:

Near term, revenue per megawatt wins. Power is the scarcest input in AI, and whoever monetizes each MW best gets the next MW.

Long term, gross margin per megawatt wins. Prices compress, competitors arrive, and only the operators with real cost and pricing advantages keep the spread.

Cerebras is built for both.

Speed is the product. A frontier model at 750 tokens per second is something GPU clouds haven't publicly matched, and customers like Jane Street pay a premium for it. Premium pricing on a contracted, scarce resource is how you protect margin when everyone else is racing to the bottom.

That's why we're extremely bullish on Cerebras, and why we're buying as many megawatts as we can.

Premium inference unlocks the most delightful user experience in AI. No more waiting, waiting, waiting, staring at little thinking animations while the model works in the background. Answers that keep up with your thoughts.

Our customers are even more excited than we are.

That's General Compute.

quoted_text:
Crypto teenage years are over. I hope you enjoyed it (and made decent bank on it).

The time when the industry discovered itself, tried all the crazy stuff, shunned traditional standards in favour of more innovative, never-before-tried strategies has come to an end.

I personally enjoyed it very much, and will be forever grateful for living through an era where simply being online and with an active address was enough reason for people to gift away sometimes 100s of thousands (Big shoutout to Tornado Cash and Uniswap).

Crypto is no longer about having fun, good vibes and posting on Twitter. It's about hitting KPIs and creating shareholder value. It's about building a valuable brand and deep corporate relations that grow the bottom line.

Historically the labour market in crypto has been pretty fucked, being 'crypto native' was a hard requirement, in short supply with an unreliable workforce (opp cost was messing around in the trenches), nowadays the crypto edge has eroded substantially, the crypto career risk has subsided meaningfully and the domain specific knowledge has shifted from deeply niche to traditional skills (tech and finance) which allows for crypto projects to tap into a broader workforce.

Regardless of the money, working in a high stakes environment and being respected by your contemporary peers is the raison d'être for most of us here. I don't have enough fingers to count how many of my peers 'made it', stayed crypto native and now wander through life, outdated and desperately resting on former glories from their beach mansion, where they escaped to avoid taxes knowing that they'll never again make the kind of money they made in the past.

It's never about where you are now, it's where you want to be in a couple of moves. The crypto shift has been obvious and glacially slow, however caught a lot of people blindsided who refused to 'grow up' with the industry and are now the 40-year-old skater who just won't let go.

All this to say that I'm once again grabbing my buttoned shirts, getting on 30-hour plane ride, 11 timezones away, and going to be Singapore for Token2049. 

Looking to grow KPIs together so hit me up if you have potential business with Spark.

text:
LiteLLM 推出了 Agent 轨迹智能分析功能「LiteLLM Lens」

它让 Agent 自动审查海量生产运行轨迹、聚类问题并给出带证据的改进建议，数据自托管在用户自己的 ClickHouse 中，且通过无速率限制的 SQL/API 让 Codex、Claude Code 等编码工具直接消费轨迹数据。

理解这个产品，关键在于理解 @LiteLLM 的既有生态位：它已经是企业 AI 流量的主要入口，所有 LLM 调用都经过它的网关。Lens 是在这个数据优势之上叠加的新一层能力：对海量 Agent 运行轨迹做自动化分析与诊断。

https://t.co/IADSUu91UO

它针对的是一个新兴且真实的痛点「Agentic Swarm」开发者的观测困境：
· 规模爆炸：成百上千个 Agent 并行运行，产生 20 万+ 条轨迹，人工审查在物理上已不可能。
· 故障取证困难：当蜂群失效时，证据散落在数千次运行中，定位根因如同大海捞针。
· 数据被平台锁定：传统 tracing 平台（暗指 Datadog、LangSmith 等）将数据锁在自家系统里，且施加 API 速率限制，这直接阻止了 Codex、Claude Code 这类 AI 编码工具去批量分析这些数据。

工作方式：三步闭环
1. 定义“什么是好/坏运行”：开发者针对每个 Agent 描述好坏标准，可细化到逐行提问，例如“找出 Agent 未能恢复的工具调用失败”。
2. Lens 用 AI 分析轨迹：AI Agent 自动审查轨迹、深入调查运行、将相似问题聚类分组，最终产出带“下一步建议 + 支撑运行证据”的诊断报告。
3. 人工复核与下钻：每条发现都链接回原始轨迹的确切步骤（输入、输出、属性）；Trace UI 采用左侧行为树 + 右侧步骤 I/O 的经典双栏布局。

技术架构：数据主权是核心卖点
· 轨迹存储在 ClickHouse，由用户自托管，与 LiteLLM 网关部署在一起。
· 数据可用纯 SQL 直接查询，无黑盒。
· 提供面向 Agent 的 Tracing API，无第三方速率限制，Codex/Claude Code 可自由拉取分析。
