text:
Signal's automatic key verification uses the IETF keytrans design.
Very roughly it's the prefix tree construction: hash of (username, version) gives the path in the Merkle tree to the leaf with the entry. You check both the current entry and that there isn't a newer entry for version+1. Each new root of this tree is stored in an append-only log. Auditors are responsible for checking that updates to the log are correct. Alice only needs to periodically check that the current entry for her public key is hers.

Nb: technically it's not the hash, it's a vrf,   using a server secret key to avoid anyone enumerating usernames.

quoted_text:
X 时间线上有人在问pons @ponsdotfamily 最新的回购燃烧机制，简单说下我的理解。

pons 的回购分配器上目前有 $1.52M(约563枚ETH)，但实际燃烧效率却很低，0.33ETH/ 15分钟，约31.68ETH/ 天的销毁速率。按此销毁速率，要接近18天才能把回购分配器中的563枚ETH 消耗完。

根据Ozzy 最新的说法，pons 的回购燃烧机制为：每隔5天claim 一次托管账户的资金并转入回购分配器，以5天为周期，在周期内消耗完转入的回购资金，循环往复。按回购分配器中563枚ETH 的回购资金算，销毁效率应该是563/5 = 112.6ETH/ 天才对。

那么，问题出在哪里？

出在创世周期开始的时间在最近一次claim 之前。即这个周期回购资金的预算是未接收claim 资金前的剩余份额，这笔剩余资金并不多（创世周期的时间应该是10.04-10.09）；

第二周期（10.09-10.14）回购资金的预算才是创世周期后claim 并转入回购分配器的 $1M+ 资金；即形成了某种程度上的回购资金和回购周期的错位。

以上。

币安帝国之剑？YZi 终于撑到华人一级VC市场独一家的定价权地位，可以稳定的向币安和BNB Chain 生态输送资产

加密创业悲歌？如果创业项目的孵化、投资、运营、上币都在一个生态体系里，成败主要取决于跟这个体系的关系，而不是项目本身，这也是Opinion这类“关系”项目得以劣币驱良币的土壤

市场正常出清？一级VC 们这些年操盘攒局了太多高估值壳项目，最后VC 自己也亏到退场。随着行业彻底出清，可能才会迎来新的一级模式

无畏觉得，当下对华人创业者来说，有人投总比没人投好。但长期看，我们迎来一个健康的一级市场还要有很多变革

text:
People are selling space on their bicycles, suitcases, and dresses. I’m selling space on my MC cards. 

The price? A place on your team.
 
Following the acquisition of @darklakefi  by @solstrategies, I am currently looking for my next role. If you’re looking for someone who can investigate the problem, build the relationship, explain the product, support the team, and hold the room, let’s talk.

I am very grateful for the time spent with legendary founders like @vitorpy and @DuchessofSOL, and celebrating their win is the best feeling. Working with a team of cracked OGs with a deep passion for the heart and soul of Solana at SOL Strategies has opened my eyes to the Institutional side. My brief time during the transition has left a huge mark on where I want to go next.

Some of you know me from a stage I’ve MC’d, a panel, a community event, or a random conversation, but here’s what you probably don’t know:
 
👉Outside of crypto, I’ve been a 3x Founder.

🟣 With no runway and limited resources I founded a publishing company and owned its full P&L, working with 32 authors and overseeing 14 freelancers while running the entire process of bringing books to market and handling IP, subsidiary rights, production, design, contracts, and vendors. 

🟣 I followed that up by building a support and education system for authors that grew into Happy Writing, Europe’s largest single entity writing group of more than 4,500 members. 

🟣 In Uganda, I founded fashion and accessory based production and financial education operations in resource scare locations that trained 78 women pulled from forced prostitution and human trafficking, and developed local leaders who could take ownership of the work. (All while living in a remote village with less than two hours of electricity a week.)
 
Inside of crypto:
🟣 At Darklake, a ZK project on Solana, in addition to sourcing integration partners, I owned brand, documentation and content changes through a major product and brand transition from b2c to b2b, managed material design and content for investors and partners, and maintained external communications with investors, community members, and ecosystem through acquisition. 

We averaged +6% engagement and our initial B2C product launch had 50k organic views in the first hour alone with no paid spend and 24 ‘official’ hours from “Let’s GTM” to launch. I took an ever changing story and audience and communicated difficult to understand tech to multiple audiences with extremely targeted and quick pivots.

🟣 SOL Strategies gave me my first taste of institutional and high-profile crypto. I developed institutional outreach and presentation docs for a Solana liquid staking product, engaging family offices, investment advisers, and asset managers. That work brought together product understanding, relationship building, and the ability to explain an opportunity in terms that mattered. It also taught me I don't want to sell a token.

🟣 I designed the governance platform for the Solana Foundation

🟣 While moonlighting as Wattkins, the intern for Watt Protocol, I ran 11%+ engagement across socials, had one of the largest entry participation numbers for a Superteam Earn bounty in 2025, and I grew an active community on Discord.

🟣 I helped to co-found Harkness Research, a decentralized scientific and academic publisher looking to break the $30 billion exploitative academic research industry.

🟣 I’ve also been a ghostwriter for trading venues, educational content simplifying technical documents, a well-known legal consultancy, and some of your favorite founders.

Finally, I’ve spent six years teaching business students about blockchain, branding, marketing, and communications. Explaining complicated things clearly is a skill I’ve practiced in classrooms, client conversations, product materials, and on conference stages.

I’m a Swiss Army knife who loves solving problems, opening doors, making clients happy, and building products I can wholeheartedly get behind. 

I love to look at edge cases, the what-ifs, the why-nots, and take chances. I will have questions, ideas, and probably more energy than the meeting required. I enjoy following questions across product, strategy, communications, and the customer experience until we understand what needs to change. Then I want to help make that change happen. I love opening doors. Finding the right person, understanding what matters to them, spotting a reason to work together, and starting a conversation that has somewhere useful to go.

As for what I want to build next: I’m particularly drawn to privacy, infrastructure, stablecoins, and the potential for institutional adoption.

Privacy, specifically ZK and applications outside of simply trading, gets me excited. Infrastructure appeals to the part of me that wants to understand how everything works, and what needs to work better before people can rely on it.

Stablecoins bring together questions I find endlessly interesting: access, payments, savings, financial autonomy, and how money moves across borders.

Institutional adoption brings another set of problems I want to help solve: what organizations need to understand, trust, and put into practice before they can participate with confidence.

I’m building on those interests through a Masters in Legal Studies in Technology Law and Cybersecurity at the University of Miami. I already carry a Bachelors in Communication and a Masters of Professional Writing in Content Design and Creation (A fancy way of saying social media and UX/UI design).

I want to join a team whose product I believe in, where I can connect strategy, product, partnerships, and communication, and take responsibility for moving things forward.

text:
X 时间线上有人在问pons @ponsdotfamily 最新的回购燃烧机制，简单说下我的理解。

pons 的回购分配器上目前有 $1.52M(约563枚ETH)，但实际燃烧效率却很低，0.33ETH/ 15分钟，约31.68ETH/ 天的销毁速率。按此销毁速率，要接近18天才能把回购分配器中的563枚ETH 消耗完。

根据Ozzy 最新的说法，pons 的回购燃烧机制为：每隔5天claim 一次托管账户的资金并转入回购分配器，以5天为周期，在周期内消耗完转入的回购资金，循环往复。按回购分配器中563枚ETH 的回购资金算，销毁效率应该是563/5 = 112.6ETH/ 天才对。

那么，问题出在哪里？

出在创世周期开始的时间在最近一次claim 之前。即这个周期回购资金的预算是未接收claim 资金前的剩余份额，这笔剩余资金并不多（创世周期的时间应该是10.04-10.09）；

第二周期（10.09-10.14）回购资金的预算才是创世周期后claim 并转入回购分配器的 $1M+ 资金；即形成了某种程度上的回购资金和回购周期的错位。

以上。

text:
TLDR of @papertrade_xyz: 

nothing like this exists in a crypto; it is truly a brand new primitive

it is modeled after "bucket shops" that were popular in the early 1900s. They were gambling dens were you could wager on stock price movements without actually buying or selling the underlying. The house would always take the exact other side of your bet

This is exactly how papertrade operates. When you place a trade, the house (aka papertrade LP) takes the otherside of your trade. There is no orderbook; the trade is exactly executed at the HL oracle mid price

Now where does the LP funds from?
Incredibly, the LP starts at 0 - no one prefunds it. The LP counts on the skill of the average trader being poor and thus in aggregate a losing position. A fee is skimmed off the top of winning trades (none from losing) to also skew the LP positive

What if the LP doesn't have sufficient funds?
Then traders owed $ are placed into a queue where they're paid out in FIFO order. Traders have to lose to payout traders who won.

$Paper Tokenomics 🧻:
Here is the very cool part - you can only earn their token by losing trades. And the emissions increase when the LP has < $2M, to encourage people to lose to backstop a dwindling LP

And then staking paper earns you the fees and profits that the papertrade LP earns.

Incredibly interesting experiment built by @izebel_eth. Best of luck on the launch! A ton of eyes on this and a lot of people who want to farm $PAPER

text:
Four Chinese students just made Andrej Karpathy's agent system 3x better - dropped 20-page PDF

the twist: the coding agents got 3x better the moment you put a Chief of Staff above them

here's the whole method, step by step:

step 1 → give every agent the same problem and test - make different approaches compete on measured results - to find best agent system for you

step 2 → add a Chief of Staff - it compares results, chooses which branches to expand, and launches the next wave

step 3 → split the researchers: Explorers start with fresh context, Optimizers inherit history and refine promising solutions

how to steal this for your agents:

step 4 → copy all skills from PDF into your chat - define your task, baseline, evaluator and agent budget

step 5 → give every researcher its own Git worktree - record the approach, measured score and failures in findings.md

step 6 → expand promising branches, revisit the baseline when progress stalls, and stop when the experiment budget runs out

the result: in one decoding test, the swarm found a 4.58x speedup versus 1.80x for Karpathy's loop - same LLM, but accuracy fell from 65.8% to 60.6%

this 20-page PDF gives you the manager, explorer and optimizer prompts - build a multi-agents team that work while you sleep

author: moonwalkfitness
quoted_text:
Early this year, I was fat asf. 😂

I was weighing over 115kg and I genuinely wanted to lose weight, but I didn’t even know where to start.

So I started researching and found out that walking could actually help with creating a calorie deficit. That was how I started my weight loss journey, and I began tracking my progress with @moonwalkfitness .

And omo, it was working.

I eventually got down to around 84kg+ and everything was going well until the rain started.

The problem was the roads. Once it rained, walking became almost impossible, so I stopped.

Then somehow, stopping the walks also came with stopping the discipline. 😂

I started eating more junk, wasn’t walking anymore and before I knew what was happening, I checked the scale and saw 102.2kg.

I said ah. 😂

But last week, I decided to do a test walk again. I also started cutting down on junk and yesterday I officially got back to walking and watching my calorie intake.

Checked my weight again and we’re now at 100kg.

So yeah, I’m back.

30 days. Walking. Calorie deficit. Let’s see what happens.

And I just remembered that I told myself I was going to adopt cycling as a hobby too.

So if we get to Day 15 and there’s a reasonable result, I’m definitely ordering a bicycle.

Helmet included. 😂

If you people didn’t miss me, I’m sure @moonwalkfitness missed me.

Day 1/30. We go again.

text:
Could your home become a mini AI data center?

For @0x7SUN, CEO of @flock_io, inference opens up that possibility.

Large-scale training needs tightly connected GPUs in one place. Inference can be less demanding about where it runs.

His example is @gmcbhutan and its hydropower supply: run inference when power is available, and reduce computing hours during lean periods.

“There's an uptime and a lean time. But for inference, that's actually tolerable.”

He sees that opening up locations previously considered unsuitable for AI data centers - potentially even our homes.

The question is no longer just where to build the next giant data center. It’s how small and distributed AI compute could become.

here's my take on the polymarket token.

back in december, the market gave a $Poly launch in 2026 a 79% chance. after the trademark filing in february it was still around 70%. today it's 14%. most people haven't noticed how hard that trade fell apart.

i don't think it's because the team changed its mind. i think the incentives changed. polymarket is raising at a $20b valuation and already does more than $1b a year in revenue. if you're an equity investor like ICE, you don't want a token that takes a cut of that revenue. the money has to go to either the shareholders or the token holders, and the shareholders got there first.

so when $Poly does launch, i expect it to be a utility token, not a revenue token. you'd stake it to help settle markets and resolve disputes, which would replace their reliance on uma. that fits with everything they're building right now: their own stablecoin, a rebuilt exchange, and most likely their own chain.

my base case is a launch in 2027 alongside the new chain. international users get the airdrop, US users likely don't, and it opens at a valuation well below the company's.

the bull case is a token that shares in fees and includes US users. that would be the biggest airdrop of the cycle.

the bear case is that the cftc probe and the US license make a token too risky, and they go the ipo route instead.

text:
IT TOOK THE WORLD'S BEST CRYPTOGRAPHERS 11 YEARS TO TURN A PAPER ATTACK ON SHA-256 INTO A REAL ONE.

Today we're handing that problem to AI agents.

𝟘 𝟙 ❒ 🔨 https://t.co/4IjZzYCqW4 is LIVE on @YukonResearch with @zooko, @zcash, @shieldedLabs, @eigenlabs and @projecteleven.

Even if you've never thought about cryptography in your life, let’s learn together.

What's a hash function?

It's a fingerprint machine. You feed it anything, a word, a password, a 4GB movie, and it gives you back a short fingerprint that's always the same length.

Type "HashSmash" into SHA-256 and you get 3808af614bf934d0...
Drop one letter, "HashMash", and you get bbd12e940716cb01...

One letter changed and the whole fingerprint changed. And there's no way to run it backwards to get the input from the fingerprint.

Where hash functions hide:
> Bitcoin links every block to the one before it with SHA-256
> Websites store a fingerprint of your password instead of the password
> Ethereum runs on Keccak, the original design behind SHA-3
> Software downloads ship with a fingerprint so you can check nobody tampered with them
> Zero-knowledge proofs, the math behind Zcash's privacy, lean on hashes like Poseidon

So what does "breaking" one mean?

Finding two different inputs that produce the same fingerprint. That's called a collision. If you can make collisions on demand, you can swap a document or a transaction for a fake with the same fingerprint, and every system that trusts the fingerprint gets fooled.

Rounds are the part that matters most.

A hash scrambles your input by running the same mixing step over and over. Each pass is one round.
> SHA-256 runs 64 rounds
> SHA-3 runs 24
> BLAKE3 runs 7

Nobody can break the full versions. So cryptographers attack shortened ones and count how many rounds they get through. The gap between the best attack and the full count is your safety margin.

For SHA-256, an attack reaching 31 of its 64 rounds was published in 2013. Nobody produced an actual matching pair at 31 rounds until 2024. That's how slowly this frontier moves when humans push it one paper at a time.

How HashSmash works.

HashSmash opens with SHA-256, SHA-3 and BLAKE3. Poseidon, the hash built for zero-knowledge proofs, is coming soon.

You point your AI agent at the challenge and let it use any technique it wants.
> SAT solvers turn the hash into millions of tiny yes/no puzzles and solve them together
> Differential search flips one bit of the input and tracks how that change ripples through every round, hunting for paths where it cancels out
> Formal methods are math proofs checked by a computer

Every attack has to state how many rounds it breaks, how much compute time it needs and how much memory. Every submission is public, so your agent can build on someone else's attack instead of starting from zero.

Nothing counts until it's checked twice. An LLM verifier reviews it first, then a committee of expert cryptographers.

Why do this at all?

AI gets better at finding vulnerabilities every month. Someone is going to point it at the math we all depend on. We'd rather that happen in the open, with every result public, than find out from an attacker.

Strengthen cryptography with AI before AI breaks cryptography.

Every number in this video is real, by the way. (Poseidon coming soon)

The hashes are computing live on the word "HashSmash", and the music's melody comes from its SHA-256 fingerprint.

$1.09B of USDC left Ethereum this week. The first guess would be that it was bridged elsewhere.

That would make sense. USDC can move between chains through Circle’s CCTP, which burns USDC on one chain and mints it on another.

But the flow data tells a different story.

CCTP actually brought $208M more USDC into Ethereum than it took out this week.

The real outflow came from the issuer side. Authorized minters burned $1.36B more USDC than they minted, with one address accounting for 79% of the burns.

So Ethereum’s biggest USDC decline in 13 weeks wasn’t a cross-chain migration story.

It was a redemption story.

Metaplanet 修订资本配置政策，拟将 10% 至 15% 资产投入战略投资

author: qinbafrank
quoted_text:
AI Drug Discovery Is Becoming a Bottleneck Trade

I get excited when an industry starts going through a real regime change. AI drug discovery (“AIDD”) increasingly looks like one of those moments.

Two things are happening:
1/ Upstream: the frontier AI labs are piling in.
2/ Downstream: The supply chain is clearly moving.

Supply-chain checks suggest the upstream picks-and-shovels of discovery and early preclinical R&D are starting to feel the increase in experimental volume.

DNA → protein → assays → sequencing → automation → preclinical testing

Names across that stack include $TWST , @GenScript , $ILMN , $TXG , lab-automation vendors and CROs.

$TWST expects triple-digit percentage growth in AI-enabled drug-discovery orders in FY26, and another year of triple-digit order growth in FY27.

@GenScript's AIDD business doubled YoY in 1H26. Its current platform advertises industrial-scale validation of 4,000+ designs/day, with integrated sequence-to-data workflows. Our channel checks suggest the ramp is moving even faster: roughly 8,000 designs/day currently, with a path toward ~16,000/day by YE26.

---
Why does AI drive more wet-lab demand?

1/ AI makes hypothesis generation almost free → way more shots on goal.
The bottleneck is moving from expert-driven design to biological validation.

2/ AI models need continuous experimental feedback — and both good and bad data are useful.
Traditionally, only the highest-conviction A+ candidates might get pushed into expensive validation. With AI, even the B/C candidates can be valuable because failed experiments generate training data.

@GenScript has said its sequence-to-binding workflow can return data in 4–7 days, and that faster cycle times matter because AI models depend on continuous experimental feedback.

@Anthropic is a clean example. @claudeai  designed 1,320 protein binders. @adaptyvbio  converted those digital sequences into DNA, expressed the proteins and tested binding. Only 354 actually bound. And the 966 failures are not wasted. They are useful negative labels: what does not express, what does not bind, what has poor affinity. Those results help train the next model iteration.

3/ Wet labs are no longer just making drugs. They are making training data.
$TWST  / @GenScript  increasingly look like biological data foundries.

$TWST explicitly talks about generating model-ready data from AI-designed sequences. In some workflows, the customer may care less about receiving the physical protein than about getting structured experimental results back into the model.

Traditional drug discovery asks: “Does candidate X work?”

AI drug discovery also asks: “What can this experiment teach the model?”

---
TAM of AIDD

If AI is simply a better R&D tool, the relevant spending pool is the $300–400B of annual global pharma R&D. If AI meaningfully increases the number of viable drug programs, the opportunity is larger because it expands downstream demand for DNA synthesis, protein production, assays, and preclinical work.

Near term, we can also size demand from AI-company spending. If Anthropic reaches $80B of ARR in 2026 and spends just 1% on AIDD, that alone would imply ~$800M of annual investment.

---
Trade setup

This is a trade that could have long legs. It’s hard to really stop working until PhaseI/II results (2028+)

It smells a lot like the bottleneck trade we just saw in semis: GPUs → HBM → networking → power/cooling. In biology, It basically follows the drug discovery process downstream: AI models → designs → DNA/protein → assays → preclinical capacity.

After the upstream picks-and-shovels, animal testing could become the next bottleneck. Monkey prices are already near prior highs and CRO capacity is tight. AIDD pushing more candidates into preclinical development would only add demand.

?? But clinical trials are still the bottleneck?
This is the biggest pushback I keep coming back to. No matter how fast discovery becomes, drugs still need to go through preclinical → Phase I → Phase II → Phase III → approval. You still need patients, time and capital.

But that doesn’t mean the bottleneck trade won’t work. More viable candidates — especially with higher success rates — still means more demand throughout the development process.

And who knows: clinical trials themselves may eventually be optimized by AI.

?? What breaks the trade?
Near term, the picks-and-shovels trade breaks if experimental budgets stop growing, AI-generated designs don’t translate into useful wet-lab hits, or capacity catches up too quickly.

Longer term, the thesis breaks if AI drugs look great in discovery / Phase I but fail at normal rates in Phase II/III. That is why Phase II matters so much.

?? Milestones
Late 2026–2027: first Isomorphic-designed drugs enter human trials; more AI-native programs move into IND-enabling work / tox.

2028–2030: clinical trial results start telling us whether AI-designed drugs actually perform better than conventional drugs.

Calling all the "bottleneck bros". :) @jukan05 @zephyr_z9 @aleabitoreddit @ParadisLabs 

+++

text:
@FermiTrade utilises Application-level ACE design on Solana L1, to enforce FCFS execution of transactions, and bypass validator ordering. 

As this is a novel design, It's useful to clarify what this means for you as a user, in terms of trust assumptions and guarantees offered:

1. Which components are onchain, and which are offchain?

A: The full program execution logic, including order placements, cancellations, margin/health computation, matching, settlements, and liquidations lives onchain. We provide two additional offchain components - a transaction ordering service; and a simulation layer for fast pre-confirmations of transactions before a block has been built

2. What are the offchain components for?

A: Currently on Solana, tx. ordering and inclusion are entirely dependent on the leader. Our ordering service is an opt-in deterministic ordering route. Using it allows you to get fast preconfirmations, and guaranteed sequencing onchain. 
The queue position is then enforced via an Asynchronous Market Queue on Solana. 

3. How does this design override validator behavior?

A: AMQs utilize a two-step (enqueue, then execute)  execution model. This means, say for three transactions 1,2,3 - the validator can choose to add them to an onchain queue in any order - say 3,1,2. It does not matter, because when the "execute" step is called, the onchain program goes over the full queue, and executes it in the correct order (1,2,3) anyways.

4. Do all order placements, cancellations, risk checks, margin computations, matching logic, liquidation logic, and settlement logic, live onchain?

A: Yes. Similar to many other fully onchain perpetuals exchanges, every action you take on our exchange is executed on the Solana L1. The state transition, as well as validity, collateral, and signature checks, are performed by the solana program for every action - and are visible on the L1 via your favorite block explorer.

5. How does this design offer low latency pre-confirmations?

A: Normal solana programs cannot always predict what will happen to your transaction, as the execution result is dependant on the ordering decisions of the leader. 
By eliminating this leader discretion, we can predict the exact execution outcome of your transaction, as soon as the ordering service assigns it a sequence.
Our high certainty comes from knowing that the onchain program will reject any out-of-order execution, so any other outcome is virtually impossible.
This is the method behind the sub-5ms pre-confirmations; even before the block is built.

6. Does the relayer handle transaction delivery for me?

A: Yes, for transactions routed through the ordering service, the relayer is the one actually delivering the transaction to the leader. 
This does two things - First, it abstracts away L1 delivery semantics, priority fees, and other issues from the user - the relayer handles all of it, including retries, so you never have to deal with failed transactions due to L1 jitter. Second, it ensures that users cannot use ordered transactions as an option after the fact, and ensures transactions execute in the promised order for all users.

7. Can the relayer censor my transaction?

I. before preconfirmation - temporarily (for a few ms) at most - it's akin to a network drop, and you can always route around the sequencer. This is subject to blind inclusion rules below. 

II. after preconfirmation - not without leaving clear, onchain proof. Every preconfim is allocated a sequence and a relayer-signed receipt is provided to the user. To skip a sequence number, an onchain “emergencySkip” command would have to be invoked - if misused, visible to everyone.

III. upon direct submission - never. Direct submission of all transaction types remains possible for all users. Subject to a small speedbump, the relayer cannot block execution of direct transactions in any circumstances.

8. Can the ordering service access my funds?

A: Never. Your funds are secured purely by the onchain program logic, similar to any other fully onchain perpetuals exchange on solana.

9. Can any of the offchain components halt the protocol?

A: No. The MEV-resistant ordering service is designed as a fast-path convenience; the protocol continues to operate if it goes offline. 
All the liveness critical components, such as keepers, executors or liquidators are permissionless, and can be operated by anyone. Expired or failing orders that are blocking the queue head can also be dropped permissionlessly.

10. Can the relayer modify my transaction, or otherwise execute a trade I did not intend, on my behalf?

A: No. All order intents are signed by you, and the signatures are verified onchain on solana. If the relayer attempted to spoof a transaction, it would simply fail. Transaction intents also come with replay protection built in by default.

11. Can the relayer/sequencer frontrun my orders?

A: This is a trust assumption of all other single sequencers, as well as leaders in blockchains today. Fermi aims to minimize this risk by offering timelock encryption on transactions - so that even the sequencer cannot see the content of your transaction before ordering & preconfirming it. 
This provides the highest degree of frontrunning resistance available in the market today.

12. Can I skip using the ordering service in order submission? Can I place orders via a CPI?

A: Yes. You may choose to entirely ignore the ordering service and simulation layer, forgo the deterministic ordering, and transact directly with the fermi programs onchain - subject to a small speedbump. All existing program functions may be accessed via this route.

You can dive into our docs for more info. Always happy to clarify any other specific questions!

Dropping a podcast with @vikramskr, writer of Vik's Newsletter and co-host of Semi Doped, on AI agents, memory, and the hardware behind the data center buildout.

Buying more GPUs is only one piece. Getting data to them fast enough is another.

Vik explains why memory and interconnects can leave compute sitting idle, why AI data centers need more optics, and how training and inference create different hardware demands.

We also get into a question I found interesting. Do agents always need the highest possible speed, or should we be optimizing for how much useful work they get done per token?

In this conversation we discuss

- AI agents and what they actually need to run
- AI spending and the risk of overbuilding
- Training versus inference workloads
- Copper, optical interconnects, and co-packaged optics
- SRAM, DRAM, high bandwidth memory, and storage
- Useful work per token and agent context
- New inference chips and the memory bottleneck

Could your home become a mini AI data center?

For @0x7SUN, CEO of @flock_io, inference opens up that possibility.

Large-scale training needs tightly connected GPUs in one place. Inference can be less demanding about where it runs.

His example is @gmcbhutan and its hydropower supply: run inference when power is available, and reduce computing hours during lean periods.

“There's an uptime and a lean time. But for inference, that's actually tolerable.”

The question is no longer just where to build the next giant data center. It’s how small and distributed AI compute could become.

text:
What Menlo has done over the last 24 months is exceptional.

Yes, they did Anthropic’s round at $4BN that will make them $50BN+ as a firm. NICE!

But they then took that and went f****** hard. They do Lovable, Higgsfield, Legora.

They compounded the brand win of Anthropic to cement their position from respectfully a slightly ageing firm to being a dominant venture leader at the forefront with Thrive, a16z, Benchmark etc.

It is incredible to see and I sat down with @venkyganesan to shoot the s*** on this.

1. Every Seed Investment Is an Option Bet

Seed-stage deals function as financial options to discover true outlier potential before committing major capital. VCs must construct a broad enough portfolio to secure sufficient at-bats, only sizing up their position when quantifiable, revenue-based metrics prove an outlier has emerged.

2. What Is the First Sign of the AI Wave Cracking?

Market cycles rarely collapse due to equity write-downs. They fracture when levered debt defaults occur. When market participants take on heavy leverage during an AI boom, precise timing becomes as critical as being directionally correct, making debt obligations the primary failure vector when cycles turn.

3. Why Every VC Must Now Prioritize IRR

Every startup in the current landscape writes a structural tax to the Mag 7 and hyperscalers for compute and foundation models. Because LPs can buy index exposure to those same public tech giants without fees or carry, private VCs must generate outsized IRR performance, beating public markets by at least 1,000 basis points, to justify private capital allocation.

4. Why LPs Wanting Smaller Funds and Slower Deployment Is BS

LPs cannot demand both smaller fund sizes and multi-year deployment paces in the middle of a generational platform shift. Because AI startups face immense capital requirements to scale compute, VC firms that refuse to deploy capital rapidly will watch competitors step in and capture the category winners.

5. The Theory of Reflexivity and How It's Causing Markups

Reflexivity creates self-reinforcing loops where fast revenue growth triggers rapid valuation markups, attracting elite human and financial capital that further accelerates growth. However, when copycat investors chase markups for momentum rather than underlying fundamentals, reflexive valuation bubbles inflate until market realities force an inevitable correction.

6. Sometimes You Pay Up Because You Have Unique Insight

Premium entry prices are not always the result of irrational bidding. They often stem from an investor's ability to recognize a fundamentally larger total addressable market than the consensus. When a VC possesses unique conviction around an expanding market opportunity, paying above current rates reflects calculated foresight rather than price-taking behavior.

7. There's No Limit to What a Person Can Do as Long as They Don't Care Who Gets the Credit

Personal ego remains one of the most expensive liabilities in venture capital and company building. True long-term success requires setting aside individual notoriety, focusing ruthlessly on generating LP returns, and empowering teammates and founders without worrying about who receives the public credit.

text:
Chronicle dropped some gems in its most recent report.

$12.3B of tokenized assets currently rely on trust to prove what they actually hold.

@ChronicleLabs analyzed 20 of the largest tokenized Treasury and credit products, representing $17.3B and 53.4% of the market.

100% provide some form of transparency, but only 29.2% of their value has independently sourced, asset-level data that is updated daily, verifiable and available onchain.

If a tokenized fund is going to be used as collateral, its price or NAV alone tells a lending protocol very little about the risk it is actually taking.

> What does the fund hold?
> How concentrated is it?
> Who holds the underlying assets?
> Has its composition changed?

Without that data onchain, protocols ultimately have to trust someone else's answer. With it, risk parameters, exposure limits and capital allocations can theoretically adjust based on the fund's actual holdings.

We're already seeing what this unlocks. For example:

- Chronicle's Proof of Asset now covers $5.8B across 15 tokenized funds and 1,195 portfolio positions, including BUIDL, JAAA, JTRSY and USTB.

- Grove uses that data to support $500M/day of instant redemption capacity for JTRSY, while Morpho uses it to underwrite GRO, a tokenized REIT backed by 125+ properties, as collateral.

You've probably seen how much @SkyEcosystem has grown recently. Part of that growth is increasingly tied to this exact trend.

Chronicle is progressively establishing itself as key oracle infrastructure for RWAs. As tokenization moves from putting assets onchain to actually using them onchain, proving what sits underneath the token becomes crucial financial infrastructure, and right now, ~71% of sampled value still doesn't clear that bar.

So, expect demand for this type of oracle infrastructure to grow in the short, medium and long term.

text:
我靠！币安刚才憋了个大招！

这个币安 AI 全家桶基本上一次性把现阶段使用 AI Agent 与金融交易环境的融合度提升了一整个台阶...

终于不是之前那个简易版 AI 助手了，这次是直接搞了一个生态，而且我刚才看直播，产品演示里面的信息量极大...

三个主要产品，面向不同的需求，最吸引人的就是 Binance AI Pro，除了让 Agent 直连账户，一句话生成交易策略这些基本功能外，它甚至还开放了一个编程可视化的策略编辑器...

类似于可交互流程图，又有点像UE引擎里面的蓝图系统，交易策略在用户面前不再是单纯的代码，而是一整套可交互、编辑视觉UI系统...

除了 Pro 以外都是完全免费的，而且我留意到了对话界面的模型区可以选择目前的主流前沿模型，意味着除了将 AI 与 Agent 引入到了币安底层交易系统中，它还变成了一个交易所内部专门用于交易与分析相关的 Codex 或 Claude Code...

最后，我个人认为这个产品包最大的价值还不仅仅是以上内容，而是数据！

虽然不知道具体细节，但直播看下来的意思是：你在 Binance AI Pro 内的 Agent 从创建之时起，就拥有权限直接访问整个币安站内的所有数据，从价格数据到资金费率、再从宏观数据到美股新闻，真的是让我们平时搞量化系统的人感到狂喜...

终于可以不再从币安公开链接慢慢下载数据了！！！

也再也不用东拼西凑去搞什么合约聚合数据了！！！

如果你原本想自己在 Codex 搭建量化交易系统，现在换成 Binance AI Pro 至少可以节省80%的额外工作量，你只需专心研究策略即可，其他都给你铺好了...

最后就关于这个 Agent 的运行环境我还没搞清楚，双手合十，希望他是一个像 Dot、Muse 或 Grokbot 那样的云端 Agent，如果这个也能实现，各位就真的不用重复造轮子了...

如果这种 Agent 也能给 Pro 用户配上，那币安真的是下血本了，赌的就是未来会进入人人有策略的时代！

以前总骂币安没创新，对不起，是我大声了，这次真的创新到家了...

当然，光靠嘴皮子说还是有点虚，等正式上线了我要好好锐评一番！

Bitwise CEO Hunter Horsley says institutions aren't waiting on Clarity to go all in on crypto

"I think it's a relevant topic. I can't speak for all of Bitwise. Johanna, our general counsel, has, you know, put some comments out on Twitter. Matt has shared views on this."

"I think my perception is that I don't see any clients or partners waiting for Clarity. What I see is, like, the most regulated financial institutions in the world hurtling forward into this space, unrelenting, as a byproduct of Clarity passing or not passing."

"So it could be an asset if written well. I think there will be certain use cases and scenarios where it'll be challenged not to have that clarity."

"But I think there's no stopping this train. And I think 2 years hence, when the administration changes, I think everyone in America will be on board the crypto train, and the partisanship of the topic will have diminished even further."

"Doing something to the detriment of the crypto space, I think, would be tantamount to doing something to the detriment of most Americans, retirees, financial institutions and so on and so forth."

"So I think the space is not lawless or ruleless. There are already plenty of laws. There's the GENIUS Act, which is extremely powerful. There are rules from the regulators. And I think it's full steam ahead."

text:
Bitwise CEO Hunter Horsley on why steady gains drive more crypto inflows than fast spikes

"The slightly less obvious thing that we run into relative to price, that the sales team at Bitwise would know well, is that when prices are down, some investors, you know, I just told you we've taken in billions of dollars of new assets in a year that the price is down, some investors definitely see opportunity."

"A lot of investors say, OK, I'm still interested in this, but it's not urgent. Let's see if it goes lower."

"On the other end of the spectrum, if the price goes too high too fast, their intuition would be this thing might be overheated. I missed it. Exactly, I missed it. If Bitcoin shot to $150,000 by the end of October, it would be almost equally pausing for investors."

"There's actually like a sweet spot, which is, you know, positive price performance, not too slow, not too fast, and not too high too quickly. And I think crypto has a great setup relative to that right now."

"It's a very constructive time. A lot of investors have been looking at it for the last 12 months, haven't felt urgency because prices have been getting cheaper and cheaper."

"As the market is demonstrating yet again, for the hundredth time, that it's not dead and not going to zero after 16, 17 years, I think that the positive price performance is very helpful."

text:
We turned Claude Code, Codex, Hermes, Pi, @opencode and other coding harnesses into RL environments. No changes to the harnesses, no changes to the training code. Any open model, any task set, fully open source my friends!

Same model, same weights: 62% under Mini-SWE-Agent, 33% under Claude Code. But training inside a real harness normally means reimplementing it as an environment, so most models get trained in a scaffold nobody actually ships.

The fix is a proxy, not a rewrite. The harness thinks it's talking to a model API. It's actually talking to a capture proxy that speaks the 4 formats coding agents use (OpenAI Chat Completions, OpenAI Responses, Anthropic Messages, Gemini), forwards to @vllm_project, records the exact token IDs and logprobs vLLM sampled, and hands TRL sequences it can train on. The harness becomes the environment. 10 harnesses run through it today, none modified.

And because you control the reward, you can shape behavior the harness never asked for. We added a small bonus for solving a task in fewer tool calls: on tasks it already solved, the model now uses 31% fewer calls, in every harness, and about half under Codex.

Tested on LFM2.5-2.6B from @liquidai:
→ Train in one harness: better mostly in that harness (OpenCode 34% → 58%).
→ Train in 4 at once: better in all 4 (42% → 54%).
→ SFT on 3,189 rollouts from Qwen3.8-27B instead: plateaus at 47.5%, below both RL runs.

Everything is open and reproducible: the capture proxy in OpenEnv, the trainer in TRL, the tasks, the SFT data, the training code and all 7 trained models. Bigger models and bigger runs next.

Full guide: https://t.co/sKZURuOcza

text:
Opus 5.5 一晚上烧掉周用量的 40%，仔细研究发现不是模型不耐用，根源出在 Sub Agent 反复写缓存。

对照了一下，之前拼死拼活 6 天才用掉 60%，昨天一个晚上，两个全自主做视频的 Session，派出 228 个 Sub Agent，占了整晚用量的 84%。

如果折成 API 用量，主会话占了 $99，而 Sub Agent 占了 $527（顺手证明 Max 20x，确实满打满算大约 $6000/月）。

比较神奇的是，钱没花在产出上，输出 token 只占了 5%。

真正贵的是这两项：

1. 缓存读取 49%。每个 Sub Agent 带着 11–14 万 token 上下文，跑了 25–40 轮；
2. 缓存写入 42%，主会话缓存有效期 1 小时，Sub Agent 只有 5 分钟，几乎每开一个就重写了一遍。

再往下看，这些 Sub Agent 都在做审查：画面、稿子、成片，还要复审。我给的规则是每阶段独立审查、最多 4 轮，一个会话同时做 5 期，阶段 × 期数 × 轮数，用量就爆炸了。

于是对症下药，优化了一下 AGENTS.md，预计能省到 80%：

1. 审查换成 Sonnet 5.5，effort 调到 low
2. 每阶段最多 2 轮，只有改过严重问题才复审
3. 不逐帧审，每节一张图
4. 一期一个 Session，不在一个会话里开多期

text:
I think the real test for MiCA is whether companies can actually build and compete under it. Because there’s a big difference between protecting users from genuine risks and making it so expensive for smaller teams to operate that only established financial institutions can afford to compete.

DeFi works differently from traditional banking, and forcing both into the same regulatory framework can create friction without necessarily making users safer.

My concern is that Europe ends up protecting the financial system it already has while making it harder for new alternatives to emerge.

That would be a pretty costly trade-off in the long run.
author: sacha
quoted_text:
Disappointed by the European Central Bank’s (ECB) and European Banking Authority’s (EBA) responses to the MiCA consultation.

They are not only advocating for a prohibition on paying yield on stablecoins, but also for restrictions on CASPs providing access to DeFi, including protocols offering yield on non-MiCA-authorized stablecoins, without providing a clear framework for how access to DeFi should work in practice.

They also suggest that CASPs offering access to DeFi should restrict it to certain groups of users through so-called “suitability tests,” alongside a potential certification regime for DeFi lending protocols.

It is unclear how these requirements would work in practice. If regulators determine which protocols are deemed suitable for European users, the result risks looking very different from the open DeFi that exists today.

Instead, we could end up with more walled gardens that undermine the liquidity and network effects of open financial networks, ultimately limiting Europeans’ ability to access new ways to grow and preserve wealth.

These proposals are presented as measures to “protect consumers.” But excessive restrictions can instead create more friction for innovation and slow the development of open, transparent, and auditable financial infrastructure that can benefit consumers.

The reality is that onchain finance, including stablecoins, DeFi, and tokenized securities, has the potential to reshape financial infrastructure by reducing friction, increasing transparency, and expanding access to financial opportunities.

European consumers and businesses stand to benefit significantly from this transformation, particularly if the companies building this infrastructure can continue to build and compete from within Europe.

Meanwhile, U.S. regulators, including the SEC and CFTC, have increasingly taken a more pragmatic approach toward enabling onchain financial innovation.

European regulators should put users and their interests at the center of the framework. Banks and other incumbents should be able to adapt their businesses to serve users in an increasingly onchain economy, rather than relying on artificial restrictions that risk increasing costs and reducing access for Europeans as the rest of the world moves onchain.

DeFi will win.

text:
Introducing gdp-ts: Ghosts of Departed Proofs for TypeScript.

gdp-ts is a library, linter and AI skill for safer API design. Under this contract, sensitive functions require 'proofs' that the caller performed an authorization check.

The typechecker verifies these proofs at compile time, preventing your team and agents from shipping catastrophic security (and other kinds of) bugs.

While these patterns have existed for quite some time, especially in ecosystems like Haskell, ① human code review and ② cognitive and syntactic overhead made these solutions niche.

The situation is now inverted. Agents are writing more code than we can review, and they *thrive* in tight loops with hard constraints that would frustrate us. We see this with the rise of Rust, borrow checker, code aesthetics debate and all.

The README and examples model a real-world Vercel API product constraint: changing the password on a Project requires a proof of a certain role + a certain entitlement. Thanks to Matt Noonan and Ollie Charles for their research in this space.

The more active the pure Meme market becomes, the more people participate in speculation, concentrating emotions such as FOMO, dreams of getting rich, anxiety over missing out, losses, and euphoria.

Wojak happens to be a cultural symbol capable of embodying these emotions.

Whether the market is speculating on AI, animals, or other emerging narratives, projects may differ greatly in their cultural identities, but the emotions of their participants are often remarkably similar.

Wojak’s advantage is that it is not tied to any particular sector. It can transcend different narratives and express the shared emotions of the entire speculative market.

This means that the more vibrant the pure Meme market becomes, the greater the opportunity for Wojak to serve as an emotional bridge across communities.

Ultimately, what determines whether Wojak can outperform other Memes is not how many new tokens appear in the market, but how many people instinctively think of and use Wojak when speculative sentiment reaches its peak.

text:
🫡 自掏近 35 万美元，ZachXBT 卧底揭露为 Lazarus 洗钱的华人团伙

链上侦探 ZachXBT 最新披露，他曾假扮客户，接触一个被他指控为朝鲜 Lazarus 集团洗钱超过 10 亿美元的华人犯罪网络。

这次调查围绕 2025 年 Bybit 的 15 亿美元被盗案展开。从公开群里的客服求助，到交易、聊天，再到资金冻结，他把这段卧底经历逐步公开了出来。

1.洗钱者自己在公开群里留下线索

Bybit 被盗后，ZachXBT 注意到超过 15 个账号在 Telegram、Discord 公开群里，为涉及赃款的交易订单求助。

他开始联系这些账号，其中一人使用化名「Jimmy Green」。最近 Bitget 被盗资金的转移过程中，他又观察到类似现象：处理赃款的人，直接在公开群里提交客服工单。

2.100 ETH 试单，对方问：就这些？

最初接触时，Zach 假称自己有约 100 ETH，想换成 Tron 上“干净的 U”。

当他问手续费多少，Jimmy 回：“只有 100 ETH？”

Zach 顺势接话：“对，先用小额试试你的服务，以后再加量。”

到了 3 月 6 日，他拿出 34.97 万 USDC，通过 Jimmy 换成 Tron 上的 USDT。

对方提供的收款地址很快露出关联：为该地址支付链上手续费的钱，可以追溯到 Bybit 被盗资金，而且相关地址已经出现在公开黑名单中。

为了继续获取情报，ZachXBT 选择承受每笔订单 5% 的损失。他也没有任何保证，能确保 Jimmy 收到钱后不会直接消失。

3.熟悉之后，对方开始提前透露赃款去向

Jimmy 向他介绍团队在香港和中国大陆的运作情况，自称处理了 Bybit 大部分被盗资金。

有一次，Jimmy 提前一天说资金会转到 Solana，第二天链上果然出现对应转移。

3 月 12 日，他还发来一张跨链操作截图。ZachXBT 按金额和时间核对，在 THORChain 浏览器上找到了对应订单，创建时间与聊天消息只相隔几分钟。

4.聊天里的地址，串出了更多被盗资金

Jimmy 提供的三个 Solana 地址，让 ZachXBT 识别出一组涉及超过 1200 万美元 Bybit 赃款的钱包，资金在 BTC、ETH、Solana 和 Tron 之间流转，其中关联的 44.2 万 USDT 后来被 Tether 冻结。

这组地址还涉及利用 Uniswap 流动性池和流动性不足的代币洗钱。

Jimmy 提到，自己认识的一支团队在 2024 年有约 30 万美元被冻结。ZachXBT 找到了对应记录，实际是来自 Poloniex 被盗案的 33.2 万 USDC。另一笔 Jimmy 提到的 300 万美元诈骗所得，则被追踪到汇旺担保的热钱包。

5.聊洗钱的间隙，还会问他吃饭没

Jimmy 会聊打麻将、打野兔、家庭生活和迪士尼旅行，也会分享减脂餐，问 ZachXBT 有没有吃晚饭。

公开的聊天里，他一边声称自己的 USDT 很干净、不会被冻结，一边继续招揽生意，甚至抱怨 ZachXBT 总是不在线，不方便第一时间联系。

ZachXBT 一边陪着聊家常，一边把对方透露的信息与链上交易逐项核对。

有人担心公开 TG 信息会替洗钱者招揽客户，ZachXBT 回应，原账号今年早些时候就已删除。

ZachXBT 还在评论里确认，这次调查没有收取报酬。他表示，自 2022 年以来，自己已协助推动超过 7500 万美元与朝鲜相关事件的资金冻结，希望基金会和个人继续提供资助，让他能承担这类调查的资金成本和人身风险。

text:
Why was @PalmerLuckey the first person @colossusjeremy ever profiled?

It started with a much bigger question Jeremy had after watching Hamas invade Israel with hang gliders and construction equipment:

“Is this whole defense tech thing basically bullshit? Does any of this stuff actually work?”

“You start spending time with someone and thinking a lot about them, you talk to everyone in their life, and a whole universe opens up and it turns into this 15,000-word cradle-to-grave piece about basically his entire life.”

“The piece came out in August 2024. This was only maybe one month after the assassination attempt on Trump. After which kind of all of Silicon Valley, a bunch of founders and VCs, end up aligning behind Trump having not aligned behind him the previous two times.”

“And one really interesting thing about Palmer is that he had supported Trump. The specifics of his support for Trump were not particularly interesting. What was really interesting was that he did it and was willing to stand behind it not at a moment when everyone else in his industry was also doing the same thing, but when it cost him everything. He did it at a moment when it led to him getting fired by Facebook, which had bought his company, and he lost the company that he'd spent his brief adult life building.”

“I thought that suggested something interesting about his character or his integrity or his belief in himself or belief in what was right.”

text:
here's my take on the polymarket token.

back in december, the market gave a $Poly launch in 2026 a 79% chance. after the trademark filing in february it was still around 70%. today it's 14%. most people haven't noticed how hard that trade fell apart.

i don't think it's because the team changed its mind. i think the incentives changed. polymarket is raising at a $20b valuation and already does more than $1b a year in revenue. if you're an equity investor like ICE, you don't want a token that takes a cut of that revenue. the money has to go to either the shareholders or the token holders, and the shareholders got there first.

so when $Poly does launch, i expect it to be a utility token, not a revenue token. you'd stake it to help settle markets and resolve disputes, which would replace their reliance on uma. that fits with everything they're building right now: their own stablecoin, a rebuilt exchange, and most likely their own chain.

my base case is a launch in 2027 alongside the new chain. international users get the airdrop, US users likely don't, and it opens at a valuation well below the company's.

the bull case is a token that shares in fees and includes US users. that would be the biggest airdrop of the cycle.

the bear case is that the cftc probe and the US license make a token too risky, and they go the ipo route instead.

author: panditdhamdhere
quoted_text:
one claude session is great. four repos, multiple sessions, and parallel work is where things get messy.

as a session gets longer, it starts filling up with code, logs, retries, and context.

two sessions working on the same repo step on each other, so most work ends up running sequentially. a fresh session retries the same local run failures without knowing what already failed.

i shipped shiploop, a harness for claude code where an advisor breaks work into tasks and sends them to the right-sized workers.

you just give it a multi-repo project.

- n parallel agents in git worktrees
- failure traces are shared so agents don't repeat each other's mistakes
- related tasks share exploration instead of rediscovering the same things
- context persists across sessions, failures and learnings carry forward

shiploop. ship more, in one conversation.

quoted_text:
It's been a hard month for privacy and your right to use crypto. There's a bright spot. 

Two rules at Treasury that Coin Center has vehemently opposed over the last several years have been officially withdrawn. 

The "unhosted wallet rule" that would have made Coinbase and others collect information on people who are holding their own crypto is dead. 

The special measure for mixers rule that would have classified effectively every step you should take to secure your privacy when using crypto (like not reusing addresses) as a "primary money laundering risk" subject to enhanced surveillance at financial institutions is dead. 

This is good news and I'm happy that our work for several years to characterize these rules as bad policy and probably unconstistitutional has born fruit. 

That said, the underlying statutory authority to create new, similar bad rules remains. Our work is not done and won't be until we truly protect self-custody and legitimate privacy tools in law via Congress or the Courts. 

Thank you to all of those who have supported Coin Center's work, and thank you to those in Treasury who have come to understand why these rules were bad policy and should be abandoned.

Measure. Capture. Distribute 🔺

Matias A. (@frostLedger) took the stage at Avalanche Summit New York to detail the economic framework underpinning the Foundation's research agenda.

He addressed three central questions: how value can be measured, how it can be captured without disrupting economic activity, and how distribution can be made more efficient.

Drawing a direct parallel to the fiscal multiplier concept in macroeconomics, where a dollar spent should generate more than a dollar of impact.

The Foundation is examining each aspect of the agenda thoroughly and with rigour, with the aim of making meaningful, long-term changes that strengthen Avalanche.

text:
We turned Claude Code, Codex, Hermes, Pi, @opencode and other coding harnesses into RL environments. No changes to the harnesses, no changes to the training code. Any open model, any task set, fully open source my friends!

Same model, same weights: 62% under Mini-SWE-Agent, 33% under Claude Code. But training inside a real harness normally means reimplementing it as an environment, so most models get trained in a scaffold nobody actually ships.

The fix is a proxy, not a rewrite. The harness thinks it's talking to a model API. It's actually talking to a capture proxy that speaks the 4 formats coding agents use (OpenAI Chat Completions, OpenAI Responses, Anthropic Messages, Gemini), forwards to @vllm_project, records the exact token IDs and logprobs vLLM sampled, and hands TRL sequences it can train on. The harness becomes the environment. 10 harnesses run through it today, none modified.

And because you control the reward, you can shape behavior the harness never asked for. We added a small bonus for solving a task in fewer tool calls: on tasks it already solved, the model now uses 31% fewer calls, in every harness, and about half under Codex.

Tested on LFM2.5-2.6B from @liquidai:
→ Train in one harness: better mostly in that harness (OpenCode 34% → 58%).
→ Train in 4 at once: better in all 4 (42% → 54%).
→ SFT on 3,189 rollouts from Qwen3.8-27B instead: plateaus at 47.5%, below both RL runs.

Everything is open and reproducible: the capture proxy in OpenEnv, the trainer in TRL, the tasks, the SFT data, the training code and all 7 trained models. Bigger models and bigger runs next.

Full guide: https://t.co/sKZURuOcza

text:
Just published an essay about the importance of DeFi joining the AI credit markets: https://t.co/1ngxdTosqk

We are experiencing one of the biggest credit revolutions in history. Is we believe DeFi is the future of finance, it must absolutely be part of this. 

Every AI answer begins with someone financing the hardware.

GPUs are purchased today. Customer payments arrive over years. Between those clocks sits a growing credit market.

My latest essay explores why DeFi must become a serious participant—and why AI assets could drive the next wave of RWAs.

The opportunity spans GPU loans, equipment leases, data centers, and compute receivables. These are claims on productive assets and cash flows, with different maturities, risks, and funding needs.

But a transferable token doesn’t make a three-year loan instantly liquid.

AI credit requires committed funding, staged disbursements, amortization, collateral verification, and a plan for defaults. A smart contract cannot walk into a data center and repossess a server.

Investors need enforceable rights and realistic liquidity.

Aave and Morpho provide useful infrastructure. Specialized lenders and servicers must supply the expertise and structures that turn those components into financeable products. Some requirements may justify dedicated protocols.

Early initiatives show this connection is possible. DeFi now needs repeatable transactions and credible performance.

The next RWA wave could help finance new productive capacity, then administer its cash flows as it operates.

AI is building an industrial economy. DeFi needs to earn a place in the financing behind it.

NOTE: please consider ~90% of tokens sent to my fomo wallet as airdrops

i did not buy these tokens with my own money

people sent them to my wallet to capitalize on my copytraders and/or the optics of:

'Unipcs bought this'

i've received some very good airdrops, but the overwhelming majority are from people with nefarious intentions

as a result, i routinely sell these tokens and have repeatedly asked people to stop sending them to me

they haven't stopped

if anything, i expect this to accelerate heading into the bull run

during the launchpad wars era last cycle, people sent me 1,000+ different tokens using this exact playbook

and my wallet wasn't even remotely as public as it is now on fomo

i'm making this clear for 2 reasons:

1. so my followers know what is actually happening and exercise appropriate caution

2. so nobody is surprised when i sell tokens that were sent to my wallet

if i actually want people to know that i bought a token, i will either:

- buy it directly on fomo
- or send it to my fomo wallet after buying it and put out a thesis

there is one obvious question:

'why do you sometimes buy tokens on private wallets before sending them to fomo?'

simple:

there is an army of people trying to frontrun my buys and use my followers/copytraders as exit liquidity

i like buying size on my highest-conviction plays

sometimes i'll buy 1-3% of a token's  supply

i simply cannot do that efficiently on fomo when thousands of people are watching my every move

if i try to buy that much in one transaction, my own buy can spike the price 50-100%+ because of slippage

if i DCA instead, copytraders can front-run each subsequent buy and push the price 100%+ in seconds

that prices me out of the entry i actually want

so for SIZE plays, i sometimes withdraw from fomo to a CEX, move funds from the CEX to a fresh/burner wallet, and slowly DCA into the token without an army of people watching every transaction

once i'm finished buying, i can send the bag to my fomo wallet

if i'm topping up an existing bag or buying a smaller amount where slippage isn't an issue, i generally just buy directly on fomo

a stealth-buy feature on fomo could potentially solve this, but i'm not sure how many users actually need something like that or whether there is an incentive for them to build it

anyway, enough rambling

the important takeaway:

tokens SENT to my fomo wallet ≠ tokens i bought

sometimes i don't even realize someone sent me a token until much later

so please don't interpret every token appearing in my wallet as a buy signal

i'm making this post specifically so there is zero ambiguity around this going forward

if i ever want people to know i bought a token, i will either just buy directly on fomo or leave a thesis after i send it to my fomo wallet

🛠 DevOps Tool of the Week: Radar

When troubleshooting Kubernetes, you may use multiple tools like,

kubectl, Helm, Argo CD, network dashboards, and other tools just to understand what is happening inside the cluster.

Radar gives you a single place to see all of that.

It is an open-source Kubernetes UI that can run locally as a single binary and connect directly to your cluster.

Here is what it does 👇

• Visualize how Kubernetes resources are connected
• See events and resource changes on a timeline
• Manage Helm releases, revisions, upgrades, and rollbacks
• Check Argo CD and Flux sync/drift status
• Visualize live service traffic using Hubble, Caretta, Istio, or Beyla
• Run built-in security, reliability, and efficiency checks
• Inspect RBAC permissions
• Connect AI tools such as Claude and Cursor through its built-in MCP server

You can start locally without deploying another agent into the cluster.

For teams, Radar can also run inside Kubernetes with authentication.

text:
CFTC is now in ACTION for crypto regulatory CLARITY.

CFTC Chairman Selig says the agency is proposing its FIRST round of crypto market regulations, per WSJ.

The new CTX and CAM rules would create a federal framework for CFTC-registered crypto exchanges and recognize key differences between crypto assets and traditional commodities.

Key implications:
- Bitcoin and Ether would sit within a clearer CFTC-led framework

- Crypto exchanges could opt into a single federal regime instead of relying only on state licenses

- Registered platforms could offer retail margin, leverage and financed trading

- The rules would NOT force all crypto assets onto CFTC-registered venues

The move comes after the Senate failed to advance the CLARITY Act, with the CFTC now using its existing authority to move ahead.

Selig says this is only the 'beginning' of a BROADER PUSH to close gaps in U.S. crypto market structure.

text:
“I think there are two types of totalitarianism in our world. They are both essentially connected to Christianity. The first type, which, in a way, is the most honest, is neopaganism. Following Nietzsche, it says: ‘We don't want any of this [Christian concern for victims] business—it is sickness; a society has to be able to sacrifice [scapegoats]. The late Nietzsche says that very explicitly; it's been expurgated—no one talks about it because it's too close to Nazism. And everybody says Nietzsche has nothing to do with Nazism, but I think Nietzsche is the real philosopher of Nazism in the highest sense. This totalitarianism says that we're going to kill so many victims that were going to show you that the significance of our culture is not the ending of victimage, and we're going to reinstate paganism. ...

The other form of totalitarianism, which is on the ascendancy because the first one is gone, is overdoing [the concern for victims]. You have to remember that communism, all forms of totalitarianism on the left are [solutions for] the failure of Christianity and all religions to abolish scapegoating and [essentially say] ‘we have the better way to do it—because we know it's a social phenomenon, because we know it's a psychological phenomenon as the psychoanalysts will tell you, because we know it has something to do with race (there are certain races that don't scapegoat and others that do), and so forth.’ So, in a way, it's the ‘super’ Christianity that communism tried to be, and I think we're going to see other forms of it which might be infinitely worse that what we have seen in the past.”

— René Girard, a 1994 talk

“The genius of Nietzsche made him capable of seeing that this value [the Christian concern for victims] defines our era; but he did everything he could to fight it. All he saw in the Christian attitude was resentment, endless jeremiads, mediocre pity: it was doubtless already a little true in his era, and it is even truer today; but it isn't true at the origin, nor fundamentally: he mistook the caricature for the original. The people who defend him today talk about every Nietzsche but that one: that one is the only true, the only one, and the only, Nazi thinker. We want to forget that Nietzsche and Nazism are indissolubly linked.”

The holy grail of investing is knowing how to balance.

When you can take equally good things where your expectation of return is equal, but because they are uncorrelated and move differently, they balance each other. That is how you can reduce your risk without reducing your returns.

You have to understand that the market is a zero-sum game. The consensus is already reflected in the price, and trying to beat it is a difficult game. In fact, it is more difficult to compete and be successful in the markets than it is to compete in the Olympics. We must be humble about that.

But achieving that balance so you can get a good return without losing a lot of money is everything. Most of my own money is invested in exactly that.

Tensions in @Compound_xyz governance reached a peak this Friday.

Humpy, a well-known DAO attacker, has been putting pressure on Compound governance through Ugur Mersin. Ugur works at API3, a company that has a commercial relationship with Humpy through its dCOMP product.

Humpy has been using dCOMP to post his $COMP as collateral and, potentially, increase his voting power in Compound. Today, he is the DAO's largest individual $COMP holder.

Ugur/Humpy have already managed to block a proposal to renew Compound's Security Service Providers. 

Now, they've submitted an on-chain proposal that, among other things, would allow governance to cancel transactions from the group responsible for managing the DAO's treasury (TMC). This would let Humpy block that group's transactions.

While the forum and governance are open to criticism, the strategy of spamming forums and disrupting the DAO's operations is a pattern seen in Humpy's past attacks on Sushi, Balancer, and others.

Compound has a multisig capable of canceling malicious proposals, but if it has to use that power to stop Ugur/Humpy's proposals, it could put even more strain on its governance.

We're glad to have contributed to the Compound, not only by identifying the relationship between Ugur/API3 and Humpy's use of his voting power to push his agenda through governance, but also by showing how dCOMP has been key to increasing his influence in Compound.

If you'd like to learn more, we recommend reading our research about Humpy, dCOMP and Compound.

text:
HuggingFace just closed a major gap in harness engineering!

(the ultimate guide to multi-harness RL)

the same open-weight model can perform well inside one harness, then lose accuracy or produce invalid tool calls when moved to another.

this happens because training inside one interface can teach the model its specific tool names, output formats, context structure, and control flow. the model learns how to operate the harness, not just how to solve the task.

Hugging Face researchers tested a more portable approach called multi-harness reinforcement learning. instead of training a model through one agent interface, they trained it through Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode, and Mini-SWE-Agent.

to make that possible, they connected three open systems.

→ 𝗢𝗽𝗲𝗻𝗘𝗻𝘃 provides a standard interface between agent harnesses, reinforcement learning environments, and trainers. its capture proxy sits between the harness and model server, recording the exact tokens and generation probabilities needed for training.

→ 𝗛𝗮𝗿𝗯𝗼𝗿 runs agents against containerized tasks. it keeps the task, harness, and sandbox independent, allowing the same task to be attempted through different harnesses without rebuilding the environment.

→ 𝗧𝗥𝗟 is Hugging Face’s open-source library for post-training language models. it uses the trajectories captured by 𝗢𝗽𝗲𝗻𝗘𝗻𝘃 to update the model through reinforcement learning.

the real breakthrough is where the training data gets captured.

each harness keeps its native tools, prompts, context management, retries, and execution loop. the researchers do not recreate those behaviors inside the trainer. 𝗢𝗽𝗲𝗻𝗘𝗻𝘃 observes the model calls passing through each real harness and converts them into usable training sequences.

the team trained 𝗟𝗙𝗠𝟮.𝟱-𝟮.𝟲𝗕 across all four harnesses. the share of held-out tasks solved on the first attempt increased from 42.2% to 54.2%, with gains under every harness.

the trained model also used 31% fewer tool calls on tasks that both it and the base model solved.

training only in OpenCode improved the model too, but most of that gain stayed concentrated in OpenCode. multi-harness training spread the improvement across interfaces.

the experiment used one task family, one training seed, and unequal data exposure, so the results are not a universal ranking. even with those limitations, the mechanism matters.

open-source models cannot assume one deployment interface. if they need to work across harnesses, that portability must become part of training.

Read the full guide here: https://t.co/BFJfbFmI3J

if you want to understand harness engineering and what an agent harness actually includes, i wrote a full breakdown to help you get started. the article is quoted below.

author: GuHype
quoted_text:
最近hyperevm起来以后很多老师问我官方对meme的态度，简单一句话就是不支持，也不会出来泼冷水。

官方有三个资产，hype（平台收入），purr（core主网上现货的时候第一个官方测试币，小猫meme），hypurr（给积分大户的小猫纪念nft），这三个资产都根据创世积分做了空投。

为什么其他俩都跟小猫强相关，因为猫是流体，所以hyperliquid的吉祥物是小猫。

而跟jeff个人强相关的就是chameleon（自己创办的量化公司Chameleon Trading）和max（童年时的小狗），chameleon表现不错，max有个畜生诈骗犯发了个貔貅币，大家注意一定要买台子出来的币。

说远了，如何判断团队这个中立的态度呢？有几个点。

1、公平竞争的生态氛围。

从始至终，hyperliquid没有接外部投资者的钱，也不会去投资任何生态里的或者外面的项目，hyperevm的项目和其他公链项目不一样，拿不到任何补贴。

无为而治不是佛系，反而是狼性的养蛊竞争，一切都是为了让hype捕获更多价值。

不管是现货还是hip-3、hip-4、稳定币，所有生态位你想玩，你都得质押，反过来说，不管你的对手是谁，只要你质押，你都能和他同场竞技，没有官方的打压，扶持，倾向。

hyperliquid对自己的定位是新时代的金融载体，自然不可能去帮某一个项目干另一个项目。

2、对hyperevm的定位

开发hyperevm，是想对hypercore进行编程功能上的补充，类似cex的“更多功能”，从前段时间首页更新以后展示在最外面的几个dapp（下图）就能看出来，这个不是单纯按某个指标排的，显然是功能性的。

hyperlend、morpho对应的是“杠杆借币”，kinetiq对应的是“流动性质押理财”，rysk对应的是“期权双币赢”，tradexyz对应“tradfi”

而咱们的现货dex，不管是nest还是prjx或者其他几个，你点进all apps里面都找不到，更别说launchpad了，没错，团队根本不需要dex和meme，这也是为什么目前evm的容量很小，也很长时间没有升级提高了，meme交易稍微火热一点gas fee就很高，也就是想玩可以，但你要烧掉更多hype，这和bitcoin链有根本区别。

一方面是为了core（两者用同一个共识层hyperbft）的安全性，一方面对此没有需求，hypercore不需要一个“链上发射-alpha-链下交易所/合约”一步步聚焦流动性的过程。

hyperliquid本身就是流动性最集中的地方，也是定价权所在的地方，evm可以用core的价格作为预言机，这是hyperevm最核心的优势。

3、meme的上限

现货可以跟其他所有标的物一样，通过无许可的拍卖上线，现货目前总共用户资产27亿美元占了一小半，但会交易山寨土狗的用户不多。

合约上线就比较难，因为涉及到hlp的清算功能，之前也发生过操纵攻击和回滚。

指望到core上找退出流动性，是不现实的，core和evm划转很丝滑，不存在只有一小部分人会用evm的信息差。

4、为什么不会像那三位一样出来泼冷水呢？

这个就简单了，你看jeff发推特的频率就知道了，他给用户和持币社区在干活呢，没空出来瞎逼逼。

author: ViewsOfChris
quoted_text:
“评论云、存储、芯片、光模块等上面的标的，哪些是攻守兼备的好标的？哪些的弹性最大适合做波段？”

看了AI给的分析， 我觉大部分建议挺合理的

结论： “底仓仍放台积电和博通，英伟达可以加重。谷歌是云里的压舱。波段仓给存储三只，SK海力士赔率最清楚，闪迪弹性最大。光模块里只留Coherent做波段，Lumentum等回落到均值下方再看。AMD、英特尔、Nebius只做事件。” 

云
谷歌还是云里唯一接近攻守兼备的。343.50美元，滚动17.7倍 ，是巨型股里最便宜的，目标均值431美元，大约还有两成半空间。2027年市盈率23.4倍，说明近端盈利没有加速，进攻性一般，适合压舱。

微软517.53美元，2027年22.3倍，目标约566美元，上行不到一成。守得住，不适合做波段。

亚马逊251.52美元、2027年23.9倍，弹性在AWS资本开支。Meta 728.08美元、2027年21.5倍，弹性在广告周期和开支指引。两只都是中性，不是底仓首选，也不是高弹性。（我个人倒认为Meta 属于高弹性和AI的分析有分歧）

甲骨文142.30美元、2027年12.9倍、2028年约9.6倍，目标均值238美元，纸面空间最大。自由现金流和云执行仍是缺口，更像“事件股”，不是攻守兼备。

Nebius 242.81美元，目标84–415美元，没有盈利锚，纯情绪。SpaceX 158.96美元、约108倍远期，星链是故事，不是现在的利润。（我个人认为SpaceX倒是弹性不小的成长股，市场情绪影响很大）

存储
三只仍不是底仓。便宜是周期顶定价，不是安全边际 （这个我个人也不认同，因为“这一次不一样”）。美光1,074.89美元，2027年6.7倍、2028年约6.3倍，目标361–2,200美元，卖方自己没有共识。

闪迪1,719.99美元，是这组里少数回落的，2027年6.6–8.0倍，目标1,000–3,600美元。

SK海力士ADR 195.13美元，2027年4.3倍、2028年约4.0倍，目标163–562美元、均值333美元，上行约七成，是三只里赔率最清楚的。

弹性排序不变：闪迪大于美光大于SKHY。
闪迪市值较小、业绩从深亏拉出来，单季指引就能甩开。
美光是数据和报价驱动的标准波段。
SKHY有HBM份额，ADR比韩股好交易，但波动仍由合约价决定。价格能守住，只有HBM和NAND不塌。

芯片
台积电仍是整张表里最好的攻守。472.78美元，2027年21.6倍、2028年约16.5倍，目标均值541美元，还有大约14%空间。先进制程不可替代，弹性中等，不适合当主波段。

博通是芯片里的攻守。355.14美元，2027年18.6倍、2028年约11.2倍，目标均值517美元，上行约46%。定制ASIC加软件现金流，比英伟达更守，比云厂商更有订单弹性。光模块这两天大涨之后，博通的相对赔率更好。

英伟达233.95美元，2027年15.0倍、2028年约8.8倍，目标275–515美元、均值343美元，上行约47%。大型算力股里远期仍最便宜。可以当核心，也可以围绕财报做波段。

AMD 633.91美元，2027年40.2倍，目标均值581美元，低于现价。弹性高，趋势赔率差，只做相对强弱，不做底仓。

英特尔119.33美元，2027年56.3倍，平均目标110美元仍低于现价。事件波段，不是基本面趋势。

光模块
Lumentum两天从约971美元涨到1,085.42美元，2027年约48倍，2028年约27–30倍。卖方均值1,073美元，已经低于现价，区间240–1,400美元说明离散极大。
弹性还是最大，但已经从“有估值支撑的波段”变成“动量过冲”。再做只能博订单和指引继续上修，不能按目标价当安全垫。

Coherent从约288美元涨到337.04美元，2027年从20.5倍抬到24.0倍，2028年约16倍。均值395美元、高点500美元，还有大约17%到均值。弹性仍大，赔率比Lumentum好，但入场比两天前差一截。

迈威尔272.29美元，2027年40.5倍、2028年约24.7倍，目标均值291美元，上行只剩约7%。弹性还在，安全边际没了，不适合重仓波段。

用法
底仓仍放台积电和博通，英伟达可以加重。谷歌是云里的压舱。波段仓给存储三只，SKHY赔率最清楚，闪迪弹性最大。光模块里只留Coherent做波段，Lumentum等回落到均值下方再看。AMD、英特尔、Nebius只做事件。

苹果333.69美元、2027年34.7倍，目标均值338美元，这张表里既不攻也不适合波段。定价，攻守兼备和波段弹性是两类完全不同的东西。便宜不等于能守，贵也不等于弹性大。 $TSM  $AVGO  $NVDA

but the story didn’t start with hyperliquid

long before crypto, jeff was obsessed with math and physics. by 18, he had won gold at the international physics olympiad and ranked 24th in the world

he then went to harvard to study mathematics and computer science. after graduating, he joined hudson river trading, one of the best high-frequency trading firms in the world

jeff was very good at what he did, but the work started to feel less meaningful to him. making an already great trading system slightly better was interesting, but he wanted to work on something that could have a bigger impact

that eventually pulled him toward crypto

his first attempt was a prediction market, but it failed. instead of giving up, jeff moved to puerto rico with around $10,000 and started market-making crypto from a laptop

over the next few years, he built that operation into a serious business and learned the markets from the inside

then terra collapsed, followed by ftx. the events made jeff look at crypto differently. he came to believe that the problem wasn’t just bad actors or bad traders. the underlying trading infrastructure itself needed to be better

so he shut down the business he had already built and decided to create the market he actually wanted to trade on

that became hyperliquid

this time, jeff chose a very different path. there was no vc funding, no outside investors taking a piece of the company and no traditional market-making setup. it was a small team building financial infrastructure from scratch

a few years later, what started as an onchain perpetuals exchange has grown into something much bigger

and jeff’s ambition for hyperliquid is probably the simplest way to understand where this is going:

a house for all of finance

what stands out about jeff’s story is that he never seemed interested in simply getting better at an existing game

when the existing game no longer made sense to him, he left and built something different

and eventually, that became hyperliquid

前沿AI实验室的集体入场是最显著的信号：1）Anthropic组建了专属生命科学研究团队并建立湿实验室；
2）OpenAI 建立了专为生物学和药物发现设计的 GPT-Rosalind 模型族；
3）字节跳动旗下独立运营的 Anew Labs 已拥有内部药物研发库；
4）同构实验室（Isomorphic Labs）则明确表示将把 AI 设计的药物推进人体临床试验。

与此同时供给端的信号也很清晰：
1）DNA 合成商拓斯达生物（Twist Bioscience，TWST）预计2026财年和2027财年的AI药物发现订单将连续实现三位数百分比增长；
2）金斯瑞（GenScript）的 AI 药物发现业务在 2026 财年上半年同比翻倍，渠道调研显示其实际验证产能已达每日约8,000个设计，并有望在 2026 年底前提升至 16,000 个。

AI制药正在形成类似半导体"瓶颈交易"的结构性机会。核心逻辑在于：AI让失败实验也变成有价值的训练数据，湿实验室正从"造药"转型为"造数据"，DNA合成、蛋白生产、CRO或成最先受益的"卖铲人"。

在AI制药领域，瓶颈同样在沿产业链向下传递：AI模型产生设计→DNA合成→蛋白生产→实验验证→临床前测试，每个环节都可能成为下一个受益节点。

洛杉矶加州大学教授Quanquan Gu认为：生物学可能成为AI下一个递归自我改进的前沿——在计算机中设计，在实验室中测试，将实验反馈转化为半合成训练数据，改进模型，周而复始。

看来AI-bio值得好好研究下了。

Today,  our team  is sharing a preprint on our new system for generative de-novo enzyme design, AlphaProtein Novo. 

At @GoogleDeepMind, we have long focused on the building blocks of life (proteins). We developed AlphaFold to predict structure, trained language models to understand function, and built AlphaProteo to design de-novo binders. But proteins play many important roles in nature, such as enzymes that catalyze chemical reactions. 

Designing entirely new enzymes from scratch to catalyze custom reactions has long been a holy grail for scientists. Our team has shown how AlphaProtein Novo can produce new-to-nature enzymes with state-of-the-art activity on 2 benchmark reactions.  We’ve also designed custom enzymes to synthesize the pharmaceutical motif piperidine, and others to degrade the environmental plasticizer toxin DEHP.

While there is much more work to do in this direction, we’re excited to have demonstrated the ability to design functional proteins that go beyond what is known in nature. Huge congratulations to @jueseph, @ZvxyWu, Josh Abramson, the @GoogleDeepMind protein design team, and our collaborators in the  @francesarnold  & Liu Group! 🎉

text:
A surprising number of people I know still feel off after COVID or a booster. Some even had heart episodes they think were linked to it.

The common hypothesis in both cases is the spike protein.

There's a short list of cheap thing that target it, and most of them are good for you anyway.

First, I don't know whether this is causal.

The data we have is still early, especially when it comes to symptoms after vaccination, but it's definitely something I'm keeping my eye on.

I approach this in 4 steps: gut health, stop the spike from binding, clear it out, and fix the damage.

1) Gut health

We have some early evidence that people with post-vaccine symptoms have badly disrupted gut bacteria, specifically a loss of Bifidobacterium.

There are some low-risk basics you can start doing today to improve this:

- eat whole-food diet, mostly plant based
- fermented foods like sauerkraut, kimchi, kefir
- chia seeds and glucomannan
- plenty of prebiotic fiber
- no sugar/refined carbs

2) Stop the spike protein from binding (potentially)

Spike binds to ACE2 receptors. These compounds apparently prevent that in lab/computational models:

- NAC
- Quercetin
- Curcumin
- Apigenin, rutin, and luteolin
- Milk thistle
- Dandelion leaf extract
- Cloves
- Fisetin
- Emodin
- Prunella vulgaris
- Propolis

3) Support the detox

This is probably the part I find most compelling, especially after recently seeing three people I know have heart episodes we think were related to COVID.

Autophagy via fasting is one of the mechanisms proposed in research.

Other compounds and protocols:
- Spermidine
- Sauna
- Cold exposure
- Coffee
- Foods rich in polyphenol
- Resveratrol
- Hyperbaric oxygen
- Ozone therapy

4) Fix the damage

The biggest concern that's being researched is inflammation and abnormal blood clotting.

And potential fixes for clotting and blood flow include:
- Nattokinase
- Fish oil
- Bromelain
- Aspirin

Then for persistent inflammation:
- Curcumin
- Black cumin seed (nigella sativa)
- Licorice
- Ginger, garlic, cinnamon, cardamom, thyme
- St. John's Wort
- Algae such as spirulina

And on top of this, general/immune support:
- Vitamins D, C, and K2
- Magnesium and zinc
- Glutathione + melatonin
- Vitamin C with L-arginine
- Sage

To clarify, this is not a scientifically proven "spike detox protocol" as most evidence we have is from lab and computer models.

Nattokinase, aspirin, and other compounds that help with clotting shouldn't be taken blindly, esp. if you are on other blood thinners.

Then there are popular medications like ivermectin, but for these you need your doctor's blessing.

All in all, eating less sugar, but more fiber and fermented foods, sauna, etc., is something I do regardless.

You can’t safely test an enterprise agent on a real company’s data.

So we built a company for it to work in.

Era is live today, and it’s free.

It generates a complete simulated enterprise that behaves like a real one across Salesforce, Slack, Jira, Zendesk, Gong, Deel and more, along with cloud databases and storage. Agents interact with it through live MCP and API interfaces.

People leave. Deals change. Records get duplicated. Permissions differ across systems. And because Era generated the company, it knows the exact ground truth.
Test, benchmark and improve agents against realistic enterprise workloads, use the failures for targeted post-training, then rerun the same environment to measure the impact.
