You should be able to use smarter models in your agent.
You should be able to use cheaper models in your agent.
You should be able to use local models in your agent.
You should be able to use a different model for every job.
You should be able to switch models in the middle of a conversation.
You should be able to choose what data your agent has.
You should be able to choose what it remembers and what it forgets.
You should be able to choose what computer your agent runs on.
You should be able to run it on a machine that never touches the internet.
You should be able to run it while your laptop is closed.
You should be able to reach it from the apps you already use.
You should be able to choose how your agent thinks.
You should be able to read the prompt it runs on.
You should be able to see every tool it has, and turn off the ones you don't want.
You should be able to teach it something once and never explain it again.
You should be able to know what it did, and when, and why.
You should be able to export your agent.
You should be able to read the code.
You should be able to change the code.
Your agent should be yours.

author: blknoiz06
quoted_text:
I don't think the tokenization story is well understood - so let's break it down 

Basically - the US Government is in vast, unprecedented amount of debt. And its long term debt is selling off a lot (40%+ over 5 years) - while Gold is up 140%. Gold has crossed US treasuries as the #1 asset held by other Central Banks. 

The buyers for US debt - China, Japan and Europe are stepping away for different reasons. Geopolitical conflict. Currency related. Political difference. 

The government is afraid of running out of buyers for its debt. And it's worried about the liquidity of markets. Historically, this concern is much worse when the Fed is hiking and there's high inflation. As typically the response to unstable debt markets is easing (buying debt). 

Therefore, the US government is very incentivized to allow Stablecoins. Stablecoins hoover up US debt. Tether has different balance sheet behavior than banks and works closely with the US government. 

Stablecoins used to be assumed to be criminal operations and were prosecuted by the USG. Now they're welcomed to Washington DC.  

When you are worried about your reserve currency status, you also want to ensure the dollar is accepted in many places. So stablecoins not only serve as a buyer of US debt, but a promoter of the US dollar globally. 

Enter CBDCs. Europeans see the US government promoting US dollar stablecoins as a matter of foreign policy. Visa and Mastercard going heavy in the space. And see Tether freezing Balances along with the DOJ and say, "We cannot have this. We don't want Trump to be able to use the US dollar in negotiations with us. Therefore we have to digitize our currency" 

Europe and the UK also have fiscal and political problems. So the perverse incentive to digitize their currencies is not just to ensure 'monetary sovereignty' but also to potentially implement wealth taxes, or balance based transaction taxes. This is also the flip side of wide adoption of US dollar stables. We don't call it a CDBC, but its basically an extension of the government. Balances are frequently frozen. Other policies could be implemented under the left.

So rising global debt -> US support of stables -> pressure on Europe to do CBDCs to respond. 

The US is then incentivized to grow the stablecoin market as fast as possible. Stablecoin's usage is primarily driven by speculation. Holding it as collateral for perpetual swaps. Keeping it on exchanges. 

The problem: crypto doesn't have lots of good assets to trade. Bitcoin has been very volatile. Most altcoins collapsed. This slowed the growth of the Stablecoin market, which has basically flatlined year to date. Scott Bessent wanted us to be going at 40-50% CAGR not 0. 

The question then, is how to create appealing speculative markets. The answer: on chain stocks, and prediction markets. 

Big picture, if you want a lot of stablecoin balances. You need to have good things to trade. Over the past 6 months the 2x leveraged Micron ETF traded more than Bitcoin in dollar terms. Trade XYZ launched commodities, and stocks and commands a large % of volume on hyperliquid. Prediction markets are growing fast. 

The losses incurred by retail investors in these markets are substantial. They are allowed for the same reason Casinos are allowed on Native American reservations. Necessary evil due to funding pressure and the geopolitical factors I described above.

This is, at a high level, why we are talking about crypto in the middle of a war with Iran. And why its' consuming the executive department's attention. The US Dollar is ultimately a matter of national security. 

This is true regardless of whether Democrats or Republicans are in power. Both have debt and spending addictions. Both are reliant on the US Dollar. 

But now zoom out: what do you have? You have a bunch of governments adopting digital ledger technology in the middle of a war. Freezing peoples balances. People don't want their balances frozen. They don't want it to be subjected to a wealth tax. 

Enter Z Cash. Over the past 5 years, ZK technology has improved substantially allowing fast, private transactions. Orchard and Halo since 2022 evolved from something Niche to something usable. The EU tried to ban Monero. Exchanges delisted it. Its price increased. 

Z Cash is open source. Vitalik is also prioritizing adoption of ZK technology on ETH. You can move ETH relatively privately on Railgun already - but real private transactions are on the roadmap.

ZK proofs can be accelerated by GPUs. Due to the AI boom, the number of people with access to GPUs and agents capable of accelerating proofs has skyrocketed. Not only can this technology facilitate private transactions but also proofs of reserves that allow trustless accounting for portfolios. This tech is commonly used at crypto exchanges to prove reserves, and algo stables such as Ethena. 

Thus - it's not just that we are set to own a bunch of shielded Z cash, as a base asset. It's that you can swap anything on ETH privately. Including stables. Relatively soon. And you can do so for provable reserves. 

Privacy is incredibly important for large institutions doing financial transactions. They're not concerned with the tax authorities, but rather front running. Slippage. And people hunting their positions or slow moving exits. 

Many big institutions own multiple days of volume in equities that could drop the price 30%+ if the market sniffed out they were selling. And intervene in FX markets, routinely interacting with banks fined billions of dollars for illicitly trading ahead of their flows. 

So a meaningful increase in tokenized trading volume inherently will require privacy. As real institutional counterparties require it. Retail is a great market and is less privacy sensitive, allowing initial growth. But for the big players to enter -- you need that. 

It's not just trading desks that care about privacy. You cannot run corporate treasury functions publicly. People could sniff out that you're doing M&A, or figure out what you're doing -- giving up competitive positioning unnecessarily. At the same time blockchains can offer corporations major cost savings for finance functions. It's estimated - for example, that a properly implemented CBDC could save companies in Germany billions of dollars a year in corporate finance banking fees. 

There are three basic approaches to Privacy. Z cash style. Private, permissionless neutral chain. Canton style: basically segregated databases that interact with each other on chain as little as possible with a permissioned validator set. And private blockchains - which simply deal with the issue by not having a public ledger or bolted on cryptocurrency people are tracking 

The argument for a permissionless neutral chain (aka a cryptocurrency) winning is that 
1. there's no real reason to trust a banking consortium (i.e. what Canton does)
2. governments hate each other and are only doing CBDCs out of geopolitical pressure in a realpolitik environment. we wouldn't be here if Trump wasn't antagonizing Europe and Canada wasn't talking about joining the EU 
3. the tech exists, so why would you want a counterparty in between things if you don't have to 

The world in which crypto loses would be that governments come to an accord about how to do this. China and the US maybe resolve differences. Nationalism subsides. And people say, "You know what, the externalities of all this gambling and absurd crypto shit are not really worth it - we should just have a consortium of nations and corporations for a global CBDC" 

There is another world where crypto loses. The debt problems go away bc we enter an age of productivity and abundance. In my opinion, the reason AI people hate crypto so much natively is that crypto is a bet AGI isn't the economic Hail Mary it's marketed as. 

regardless, we are in neither of those worlds right now. But crypto hasn't done great either. Why? 

The big problem with crypto, from a valuation standpoint, is that it has never been clear how you pay for all the validators or miners without a block subsidy. And the only coherent way that happens is that on-chain volume, swaps, and trading 5-10xes. 

The way that you get there is that high quality assets get tokenized and traded. But probably less understood is that an entire swathe of new assets hit the blockchain, and defi functions like borrowing and looping create carry trade and FX trading opportunities. So rather than pendle looping Ethena, you have looping with RWAs. This already exists to some extent in niche markets like Brazilian credit card debt (looped 28%+ APY) but is relatively tiny. 

Just on this example, you might immediately say "that has huge FX risk", and you'd be right. Which brings a natural demand for FX hedging. Which will hit after you get internationalized RWAs on chain. Which will occur naturally after corporate finance functions hit CBDCs. 

So you have a sort of promethean progression:
0. bitmex and native perp yield 
1. weird crypto yield / credit risk [low quality pre FTX era]
2. ethena (systematized perp yield)
3. defi/aave/ pendle etc (levered yield)
4. on-chain stocks
5. on-chain perps 
6. leveraged stock vs perp yield 
< we are here >
7. private stock trading 
8. institutional lending 
9. direct corporate bond or equity issuance (USD)
10. CBDC facilitated corporate finance (EUR, GBP, NOK)
11. permissionless private fx swaps 
<the promethean explosion>
12. looped international corporate fixed income

Note that the entire time I've talked so far, AI hasn't really been mentioned. AI makes all of this easier. The most concrete example is that the Norgesbank is vibe coding their CBDC with Claude. But more profoundly - eventually agents will be able to trade assets directly on chain. 

investment management is becoming increasingly agentic already, with every major lab launching finance products. And banks rapidly adopting AI across workflows. 

By the time you get to step 9 on the table above, there will likely be investable AI agents. Perhaps in gated jurisdiction. But there will be a new primitive of an agent with a verified balance, and business model that you can buy. The same way you'd buy a stock or subscribe to a vault, or hedge fund. 

I think Step 9 (companies choosing to issue straight on chain) is therefore the most important thing to monitor given the sh1t show with Robinhood's CEO and AMC. Tokenized representations of stocks have major legal risk, and ADRs (American Depository Receipts) as an asset class have quite an ugly history of being banned or depegging (most recently YNDX just straight up went to 0 when Russia went into Ukraine). For you to get really clean on chain stocks, and fixed income that can be effectively looped for yield, you need the credit risk of the actual underlying legal structure to be very low. 

You'll also want to see a proliferation of privacy and ZK accounting products take hold that interact with OTC trades, portfolio swaps, and FX as CBDCs come online. That's the boring bridge to the eventual wild future everyone was envisioning in 2023 where we have a bunch of Accelerando esque corporations existing entirely on chain, compounding capital and investing in their own training

The Track to Financial RSI is paved with Fomo, hyperliquid, gambling on Robinhood and seemingly irresponsible regulatory actions. At least, it seems mad until you consider the alternative. Illiquidity. And currency failure. 

You can complain about Trump's ethics. You can stop Clarity. But the crazy train has already left the station. All aboard! It's not like you have a choice.

The CFTC's concept for exchange-traded spot crypto is legally clever. 

Generally speaking, the agency doesn't have jurisdiction to regulate spot commodity markets. "We regulate cattle futures, not cattle auctions." 

But there is an exception (Section 2(c)(2)(D)) for commodities "entered into, or offered (even if not entered into), on a leveraged or margined basis," which can look very much like futures and so they must be traded on an exchange--unless "actual delivery" of the asset occurs within 28 days. 1/

text:
Austin on why inflation isn't hitting everyone equally: higher rates turned government debt into a payout for people who already own assets

"Think about sort of money at a very macro level. Let's zoom out for a moment on where the particular flows are going. At the government level, you can simplify it to 2 things, which is money that the government is spending and money that the government is taking in."

"Because all of the ways government takes money in, which is through various programs and mostly through taxes, is one side of the ledger. The other side of the ledger is all of the ways in which government spends money, right? Social benefits programs, defense, like, interest service on debt."

"It's just a net inflow and a net outflow, and the differential of those is the amount of increase or reduction in the money supply due to the actions of the government. If we spend $8 trillion and take in $5 trillion, that's a plus $3 trillion, right?"

"All that money does have to come out somewhere. If you look at the variable that's been increasing the fastest as rates have gone up, that's payments on government debt, right? Who holds government debt, it is largely the investing class."

"Why is inflation not hitting everywhere equally, what is going on with the debasement trade? Why do assets continue to run? It's the biggest, positive plus, and where the money is coming into the hands of people who already have brokerage accounts or who are institutional investors, because they're the ones who own the T-bills, right?"

"Your average, 25 year old who just got a job and only has been out there for 3 years and doesn't have savings, probably a negative net worth with student debt, right, does not have a giant pile of T-bills. But your 65 year old mother does."

I've been buying a lot of $ENA over the past few weeks.

A few reasons I'm bullish:

• The last ENA unlock for VCs is happening today. After this, the main supply overhang is gone.

• ENA emissions to bootstrap USDe growth also ended last month.

• Ethena has historically been one of the fastest-growing DeFi protocols during uptrends, as higher funding rates significantly increase the yield it offers. 

• Higher sUSDe yields should drive more TVL and make ENA more attractive as an investments.

• ENA buybacks will be activated once USDe supply surpasses 7.5 billion.

• Ethena has consistently made big announcements over the past few weeks, which helps a lot to maintain the bullish momentum during an uptrend.

• ENA is also seen as an ETH beta play, so if ETH performs well, ENA should also pump.

• Ethena's cryptic message from yesterday likely confirms that a big announcement is coming.

Overall, I think the setup for ENA is great here.

On the flip side, if I were to talk about the things I like less, there are two to keep in mind:

Firstly, if we look at ENA's current FDV and compare it to its revenue (even after its fee switch activates), ENA is clearly overvalued based on its price-to-earnings ratio.

However, I don't think that really matters in a bull market because, as long as its revenue and all its other metrics keep growing, I think Ethena will keep gaining more attention and momentum, and that's the only thing that matters for the token price to go up.

Secondly, ENA is one of the most reflexive crypto assets, and this goes both ways. If BTC nukes, ENA will go down much more. But my thesis assumes that BTC will keep going up for the foreseeable future, and that's why I am also bullish on ENA.

So yeah, this is why I decided to invest in Ethena.

Let's hope it pays off 🤞

text:
Ben Horowitz on what he expects in AI over the next 8 to 12 months.

He thinks the infrastructure for AI is wrong, and it reminds him of the early days of cloud computing. Back then, everyone thought they could put their existing software on the other side of the wire. It didn't work, and everything got rebuilt: storage, networking, operating systems, virtualization, containers.

This is why he expects the same with AI:

1. The workload. A database query is predictable. An AI query could run for a week, and the systems to manage those requests don't exist yet.
2. The chips. Nvidia's GPUs were built for video games. Ben calls them power-hungry and low-yield for what they do today.
3. The models. Training them means sucking down all the data on the internet, and he doubts that is where we end up.

His conclusion: from the model on down, everything is going to change, and there will be a lot of opportunity in that.

Full breakdown here: https://t.co/OvoWHuVAHB

I saw Jeff at a grocery store in Singapore yesterday. I told him how cool it was to meet him in person, but I didn’t want to be a douche and bother him or ask him for photos or anything.

He said, “Oh, like you’re doing now?”

I was taken aback, and all I could say was “Huh?” but he kept cutting me off and going “huh? huh? huh?” and closing his hand shut in front of my face.

I walked away and continued shopping, and I heard him chuckle as I left.

When I got up to the checkout, I saw him trying to walk out of the store with like fifteen Milky Ways in his hands without paying.

The girl at the counter was very nice about it and professional and was like, “Sir, you need to pay for those first.”

At first he kept pretending to be tired and not hear her, but eventually he turned around and brought them to the counter.

When she took one of the bars and started scanning it multiple times, he stopped her and told her she had to scan each one individually “to prevent any electrical infetterence,” then turned around and winked at me. I don’t even think that’s a word.

After she scanned each bar separately and started to tell him the total, he kept interrupting her by yawning really loudly. Then when she asked if he wanted a bag, he just looked at her and said, “Hyperliquid.”

Ram says we're entering the "age of midtwit AGI": more impactful than the computer, nowhere near superintelligent

"So then OpenAI says, wait a minute. We've lost. Anthropic has faster revenue, better revenue growth. Like, the technical staff at Anthropic is the who's who of, like, the NBA dream team. Incredible what they've done."

"So then we have this incident where these agents run amok, and Hugging Face, which is an open source project that no one really cares about because it's open source. There's no one from Hugging Face coming out and talking about this."

"If you're gonna have a target that was run over by these little pushy agents, for a press release event, it would be Hugging Face. This is nothing. It's just a media stunt. That's all it is."

text: Over the past weeks I switched a lot of my Cowork complex work to new Claude Projects (confusingly, it is not the same as the old Projects in Claude, instead, it persistently chats with a dedicated cloud VM). I found it to be much better in most ways, but not clearly documented.
author: emollick
quoted_text:
Hi! I work on Cowork. Probably no surprise, but we want to make our users as powerful as possible with Claude - and you're right that explaining and keeping up with the capabilities is hard. Affected users got both an email and an in-app notice, but I'm grateful for the feedback - I think this change was more surprising to people than I'd like it to be. This one will be a longer explainer, bear with me!

The "old" version of Cowork runs model inference in the cloud, executing tool calls in an Anthropic-provided VM we shipped to your computer. We added the VM for capability, safety, and security reasons - mapping in just the data you explicitly added to your session. People loved what they were able to do with Claude but didn't love the disk, battery, and performance cost of running the VM locally. Also, people didn't love that closing your laptop means the work stops.

The "new" version of Cowork runs model inference and the VM in the cloud. Each session gets its own sandbox, not sharing state with other sessions. When the VM needs something on the users' device (like a file), the desktop app is responsible for that file access tool call. To be clear, Claude will only access files in folders that the user explicitly added to the session, the same way Claude only saw files explicitly added to the VM in the "old" version. Sandboxes are destroyed when the session ends!

We think this solves a lot of problems we've heard about  (like using Cowork from a phone, keeping work running, or getting all the same power without losing battery to the VM) - but we'll keep iterating on new feedback we hear!

I think making solana:pumpCmXqMfrsAkQ5r49WcJnRayYRqmXz6ae8H7H9Dfn the default pair is probably the most obvious next step for Pump.

Look at how this has worked before.

Uniswap v1 made every pool trade through ETH. ETH was the bridge asset between the entire ecosystem.

Virtuals took it even further. Every agent token is paired with VIRTUAL, buys route through VIRTUAL, and they literally describe VIRTUAL as the monetary backbone of the ecosystem. 

Pump is already doing ~$500m+ annualized revenue and using roughly 50% of revenue to buy and burn PUMP. They’ve already bought and burned over $460m worth. 

Now imagine making PUMP the standard pair.

Every new launch needs PUMP liquidity.

Every successful coin creates more demand for PUMP.

More volume creates more Pump revenue.

More revenue creates more PUMP buybacks.

More PUMP gets tied up across LPs while the protocol is simultaneously buying and burning the same asset.

And if PUMP appreciates, the entire ecosystem sitting on PUMP gets wealthier in dollar terms and has more capital to recycle back into coins.

Right now Pump creates the activity but SOL still captures a lot of the monetary premium because most of the ecosystem is SOL denominated.

That feels backwards.

Pump already owns the launchpad.

The obvious next step is making PUMP the reserve asset of the economy it created.

Not PUMP-only.

PUMP-default.

Let SOL/USDC exist, but make the best rewards, incentives and launches gravitate toward PUMP pairs.

If Pump creates the volume, fees and liquidity, PUMP should capture more of the upside.

text:
Only ~5% of tokenized bonds are currently deployed in DeFi.

I think tokenization creates a question for asset managers that doesn't really exist today: how useful is your fund once someone owns it?

I think this will make flexible infrastructure like @chainlink and @aave V4 increasingly valuable.

Historically, asset managers compete on performance, fees, liquidity, distribution and brand. Onchain markets introduce another dimension.

> Can the fund be used as collateral?
> Can investors borrow against it?
> Can it move between venues?
> Can other financial products integrate it?
> Can liquidity remain available 24/7?

Baillie Gifford explicitly says tokenization should make an investment more useful, not simply put the same product on a blockchain. If that thesis is right, DeFi integrations will eventually become a distribution advantage for traditional asset managers.
author: josefabregab
quoted_text:
Baillie Gifford and @Aave Labs just published one of the most interesting reports I've read on tokenization.

The main takeaway: putting assets onchain is no longer the hard part. Making those assets useful is.

There are now ~$38.2B of tokenized RWAs on public blockchains excluding stablecoins, but only ~5% of tokenized bonds are actually being deployed in DeFi. That's the gap the next phase of tokenization needs to close, and one that Aave V4 + Horizon are extremely well positioned to tackle.

Tokenized assets need to:
> become usable as collateral
> move between venues
> access liquidity
> plug into financial markets without giving up the protections institutions require

This is also where Aave Horizon + V4's customizability become extremely relevant.

Instead of selling a tokenized fund position to raise short-term liquidity, an institution can potentially pledge it as collateral and borrow stablecoins against it.

I know I've said this many times, but:

Tokenization gave assets onchain ownership. The next phase gives them onchain utility. This concept will become increasingly popular and increasingly obvious.

I'll be sharing quite a few more posts on this article dissecting each of the most important points.

Credit to @StaniKulechov, @luigidemeo and @LoryKehoe for the contributions to this piece.

quoted_text:
Canton Network vs. Ethereum: What's the Difference?

Ethereum (@ethereum) is a general-purpose public blockchain where transactions and smart contract activity are broadly visible across the network. Validators use proof-of-stake to agree on the chain’s state. 

Canton Network (@CantonNetwork) takes a different approach, focusing on privacy, interoperability, and institutional financial workflows.

Here are the key differences:

(1) Privacy

Ethereum is transparent by design. Addresses, balances, transactions, contract calls, and events can generally be inspected publicly. 

Ethereum is now researching additional privacy technologies, including private reads, private transactions, and zero-knowledge proofs. 

Canton uses sub-transaction-level privacy. Participants only receive the transaction data relevant to them, while sensitive information is shared on a need-to-know basis. 

(2) Network Structure

Ethereum operates as a public blockchain with a shared global state maintained by its network of nodes and validators, plus layer 2 networks that settle back to it.

Canton is designed as a network of networks. Applications can operate across different participant nodes and synchronizers while remaining interoperable, connected through the public Global Synchronizer run by super validators.

(3) Consensus

Ethereum’s proof-of-stake system uses validators to propose and attest to blocks, with validators staking ETH to participate in network security. 

Canton separates transaction validation from transaction ordering and confirmation. The participants involved in a transaction validate the relevant smart contract state, while synchronizers coordinate ordering and commits.

(4) Smart Contracts

Ethereum uses the Ethereum Virtual Machine, allowing developers to deploy programmable smart contracts across a broad public ecosystem. 

Canton uses Daml-based smart contracts and gives applications control over privacy, governance, permissions, and operating policies.

This makes Canton particularly suited to workflows where different institutions need to interact without exposing every transaction to the entire network. 

(5) Main Use Cases

Ethereum has developed into a broad platform for DeFi, NFTs, stablecoins, decentralized applications, and other permissionless applications.

Canton is focused heavily on financial infrastructure, including tokenized assets, payments, institutional markets, and workflows requiring confidentiality.

So, Ethereum emphasizes public verification and permissionless composability, while Canton emphasizes privacy-preserving interoperability between institutions on a public network.

text:
When it comes to big fishes, @TheBigWhale_ got connections.
My review of "Cash That Moves, Cash That Earns: Onchain for Treasurers, Paris Event. 7 notes + 1 tip.

1. The story of the morning was who was in the room. Over 100 people, 66 organisations, and a genuinely new bucket in the audience: corporate treasurers. That is the third wave, after crypto natives and financial institutions.

2. The leading use case is unglamorous and already at volume. Intra-group transfers, especially into emerging markets where the local rail is slow or the FX spread is wide.

3. The economics are real but corridor specific. Europe to Nigeria goes from two or three days to roughly 30 minutes, and one client was paying about 15bp over interbank FX on top.

4. The last mile is still a bank. You can move value on-chain in 30 minutes, then hand it to a correspondent bank to turn into local currency, and that is where they make sure they get paid.

5. Banks will not touch public rails without confidentiality. Amounts are visible by default, so nothing moves until amounts are encrypted and decryption rights are granted to the one party that has to see them.

6. Interoperability is the last structural gap. No treasurer wants to instruct "send on Solana". He wants to instruct an amount in a currency, and today the counterparty often cannot accept the chain he used.

7. The bit nobody has priced: tokenised money market funds give corporate cash one day to one minute liquidity, but rating agencies still prefer cash on the balance sheet. Accounting decides whether treasury may hold it at all.

 Tip:

Credit Rating agencies give less credit to cash trapped in subsidiaries or abroad. Cash held at HQ and moved in seconds when needed strengthens credit rating and enables cheaper borrowings. Value-added here is by an order of magnitude larger than bank fees.

quoted_text:
Doing a bit of a self-experiment.

Goal: use my personal health and travel data to provide personalized diet and exercise recommendations for me, using frontier models but in a way that avoids leaking to them any private information.

Strategy: use a local model (Qwen 3.8 Flash Next) to orchestrate, and use powerful remote models as a tool call to benefit from higher-level thinking and knowledge that the local model does not have.

Three-layer approach to privacy:

Avoid leaking personally identifiable information, or leaking my identity through writing style -> local model writes the queries to the frontier model, not me
Avoid leaking who I am through the payment channel -> zkAPI
Avoid leaking who I am through networking / IP -> Tor

You need all three (and finally we have all three, at least to some extent)

A skill file teaches the local model when and how to construct minimally-data-revealing requests to remote models. Use zkAPI-wrapped-with-Tor as a CLI tool.

And everything works! I got the recommendations back, info from frontier models helped to improve them.

Main deficiencies:

* Tor is really not optimized for request-by-request de-linking, which is the only form of network-layer privacy that really makes sense in today's world (long-running identifiers are too fragile). Probably not private enough, and latency 10-100x higher than it could be, at the same time.
* The skill file's request construction strategies are definitely far from optimal.
* Qwen 3.8 Flash Next is still too slow for comfort. It's comfortably running at 20-30 TPS, but it would only really start to feel fast at 100+
* There is a tradeoff: the more careful you are about what data you give to a remote model, the less it can help you

text:
We are introducing Beam today, a 500b open model that excels in coding, agentic, and scientific workloads.

Beam is very token-efficient, pre-trained from scratch, and scaled with the largest RL run documented openly we are aware of.

Getting here was challenging, rewarding, and personal.

I immigrated to the USA during childhood when my parents got jobs as scientists at PNNL, a national lab located in a rural town in Washington state.

Growing up, I developed an interest in physics because it was grounded in simple principles, was foundational, and had long-term impact.

Physics was the foundational science of the 20th century. The first general computer (ENIAC), the transistor, GPS, and much of modern technology had its roots in physics.

In 2016, during my graduate studies, I noticed the birth of a new foundational science - Artificial Intelligence.

AlphaGo, the superintelligent Go agent developed by DeepMind, had come out and made me feel what was about to come.

A neural network, trained to imitate human players, and then improve itself through trial and error, mastered the most intellectually challenging board game in the world.

What surprised me about AlphaGo is how it was conceptually simple, general, and scalable. The system could in principle improve itself forever, it was just a function of compute.

This is when I became “AGI pilled” as they say.

I switched from physics to AI because I thought this would become the root node science of the 21st century, much like physics was the root node science of the 20th century.

I believe that working on foundational science is not enough on its own. Foundational science must also remain open and widely accessible.

We remember Newton for his contributions to physics, but he was also an alchemist.

Alchemy was done in secret, because the artificial production of gold was deemed lucrative but also dangerous with the potential do destroy entire economies. Newton even wrote his alchemy notebooks in cypher.

On the other hand, Principia was published in the Philosophical Transactions of the Royal Society, the knowledge was made widely available, passed down for generations in what we now call Newton’s laws.

The computer, transistor, GPS were possible to build because physics as a science was open. Openness creates an ecosystem of innovation.

The notion of openness, which is a core tenet of scientific discovery, has also become a guiding principle for how foundational technology gets built and distributed.

The internet was built on open protocols. The most widely used operating systems are open. The field of cybersecurity exists because strong encryption protocols were made open in the 1990s.

Open also means safer. The best defence is a distributed one. Commonly used open source software is robust and battle-tested because it is inspected and patched by a community of developers.

AI is different but also similar to software in many ways, though with a much larger surface area of vulnerabilities. It is impossible for a small group of safety researchers working in secrecy to remediate all of the potential issues regardless of their intentions. It is like entrusting a handful of white blood cells to protect your body.

AI is both foundational as a science and a technology, and the safest way that also ensures the benefits of AI are distributed evenly is by making it open.

I’m excited for what developers and scientists build and learn from this model, and for Beam to play a small part in ensuring that AI is made widely accessible, safe, and beneficial to all.

text:
There’s a weird moment when building something where you realise the prototype has done its job.

For KRYVAN, I think we’re reaching that point.

We’ve been running the economy locally — creating balances, locking $KRVN into games, settling matches, testing refunds and deliberately trying to break the logic.

That environment gave us somewhere safe to make mistakes.

Now the next step is getting much more interesting.

We’re starting the move to Solana Devnet.

That means gradually replacing the things our own backend currently says happened with things we can prove happened onchain.

A player shouldn’t have to trust KRYVAN when it says:

“your tokens were locked.”

There should be a transaction.

Same when an arena settles.

Same when funds move.

Same when something gets burned.

That distinction matters to me.

Otherwise we’ve just built a normal game with a crypto wallet attached to it.

The next phase is about making Solana part of the actual machinery underneath KRYVAN.

I’ll share the wins — and probably some of the things we break along the way.

$KRVN

To me, this shows Hyperliquid is thinking about permissionless markets with accountability built in from day one.

HIP-3 could become a very important piece of the $HYPE ecosystem once it is ready.

Why we built @PermaTell POMP.

I’ve been a @poapxyz collector for years, so hearing that the project was being sunset genuinely hit me. POAPs were never just tokens to me, they were little records of where I had been, the communities I joined, and moments I wanted to remember.

But the idea behind POMP actually goes back even further.

Almost two years ago, while I was helping build the @Weavers_Org Discord community, what later became @OurBazAR, I was sitting in a VC with @SanOfABee and @jasondesante talking about an idea:

What would better POAPs look like if they were built on @ArweaveEco?

Permanent artwork and metadata. Community-owned memories. Collectibles that didn’t depend on a platform staying alive forever.

That conversation stuck with me.

When the POAP sunset news came, a few community members helped revive that old idea, @rc_julin1889 and @Maximio79, and it became the foundation for what we’re now building as POMP: Proof of Memory Protocol inside PermaTell.

Today, communities can create POMPs for Spaces, IRL events, music drops, hackathons, calls, and shared moments. They’re created as Atomic Assets on Arweave, can be claimed by the people who were there, and can even unlock unique 1/1 tradable collectibles.

POMP wasn’t created because we wanted another NFT platform.

It was created because memories deserve infrastructure built to last.

And in a strange way, the idea started in a Discord VC years before we knew we would actually build it.

text:
GM all. First weekly update from Base Batches!
I’ll be sharing what we’re learning as we build @Tribeca_xyz on @base. What it’s like working with the team, and a few lessons I’ve learned that I think will be useful for founders that are still early-stage like us.

1. Base Batches W1
We started with a rundown of the program: founder AMAs, fundraising support, and resources across the Base ecosystem. Pretty much what you’d expect from an accelerator.
The highlight was an hour with Jesse, where we got to ask questions and hear his vision for Base. Base’s plans for tokenized stocks are ambitious, and as more stocks come onchain, sustaining deep liquidity across a growing number of markets could prove challenging for AMMs. That’s where we see an opportunity to contribute with @tribeca_xyz.

2. Collaboration
You can tell the Base team put a lot of thought into bringing this cohort together. Many of us are building complementary products, and bouncing ideas around has already helped us see how they could fit together and where we can help each other grow. Spoke with the founders of @get_grow_app  and @contavcbr (amazing founders & product. go check them out!). We’re already exploring how Tribeca could serve as a trading layer for what they’re building. Still very early, but excited to see where these conversations go and chat w the other BB teams.

3. Support
Support is funny when you’re building. It’s hardest to find when you need it most. Then you get some traction, and suddenly everyone wants to help.
That’s why having the Base team in our corner while we’re still pre-product means so much. Not a lot of ecosystems(especially one as a big as base) are willing to truly be in the trenches and help teams go from 0 to 1, so if you’re building on Base, keep going. We’ve seen firsthand the effort the team is putting into helping its builders get off the ground.

4. Don’t build in a vacuum.
This applies to whatever you’re building.
“Heads down, just build” is useful advice, but it’s easy to spend months building without asking who needs your product or where it fits. Look up once in a while. Talk to other founders, learn what’s missing, and figure out where you can contribute.
I’ve personally benefited a lot from the resources @base offers early founders. Reaching out has helped me meet some of the most incredibly down-to-earth people in the community. If you’re building, it’s definitely worth your time getting involved and exploring the support available. Attention and resources aren’t evenly distributed, and a good product alone doesn’t guarantee success. Understanding the ecosystem and building relationships are a huge contributing part of building a company too. I’m also happy to help any founders looking to get involved and feel free to reach out!

Lots of exciting updates coming from Base Batches 004 so be sure to follow @tribeca_xyz and the rest of the teams to stay in the loop. See y’all next week!

text:
The bridge data changes the interpretation of Ethereum’s $1.09B USDC decline.

If users were simply moving USDC to other chains, CCTP should have been net negative on Ethereum.

Instead, it was +$208M.

The actual gap came from issuer-side activity, where burns exceeded mints by $1.36B.

That makes the latest supply drop much more about redemptions than migration.
author: Covalent_HQ
quoted_text:
$1.09B of USDC left Ethereum this week. The first guess would be that it was bridged elsewhere.

That would make sense. USDC can move between chains through Circle’s CCTP, which burns USDC on one chain and mints it on another.

But the flow data tells a different story.

CCTP actually brought $208M more USDC into Ethereum than it took out this week.

The real outflow came from the issuer side. Authorized minters burned $1.36B more USDC than they minted, with one address accounting for 79% of the burns.

So Ethereum’s biggest USDC decline in 13 weeks wasn’t a cross-chain migration story.

It was a redemption story.

最近把 $virtual 、 solana:7VertkgF9KLhxxJXHX6uaWuoYZTP9LdGj2bWmVXVpump 、 robinhood:0x18e674231a58c239dc7daedcffe15ec3a24cff5c 、 $Claus 和  ethereum:0x7987f03462200b3d8a072e02c89a8a41dcb124ee  放在一起看，感觉这条叙事开始有意思了：AI 不光能发帖、管钱包，还能参与一个币的交易规则。🤔

这几个项目，做的其实是不同层面的事。

Virtuals 偏向把 AI agent 做成币，强制配对， solana:7VertkgF9KLhxxJXHX6uaWuoYZTP9LdGj2bWmVXVpump  更进一步，给每个币配一个脑子和金库，用交易手续费养它，让它发内容、空投、回购。但池子怎么交易，还是按 Pump 的规则来。

robinhood:0x18e674231a58c239dc7daedcffe15ec3a24cff5c  做的是交易规则：发币时选好功能，积木搭建，上线后焊死，创建者和平台都不能随便改。

⭐️ $Claus  最有意思的地方，是币不用重发，池子不用重建，后面的规则还能继续变。

比如根据天气调整手续费里多少拿去回购、多少拿去加池。名字也能改，持有人手里的币还是原来那个地址。以前想加新玩法，往往得发个新币；现在可以在原来的币上继续做。

不过得分清楚：能改规则，不代表 AI 已经可以随心所欲地创造金融产品。目前改规则的钥匙还在项目钱包手里，借贷、杠杆这些也还是后续方向。
👉这个权限让它有想象力，也意味着你得信任掌握钥匙的人。

再看 ethereum:0x7987f03462200b3d8a072e02c89a8a41dcb124ee ，逻辑就从“哪个实验会火”，变成了“这些实验从谁的工厂里出来”。

这里说的是 Programmable 的平台币  ethereum:0x7987f03462200b3d8a072e02c89a8a41dcb124ee， $Claus  就是通过 Programmable 的以太坊发射路由部署的。

Claus 自己收的那笔约 2% 项目费，拿去养 Claus；V4 吃的是另外一层平台过路费。费用在 ETH 收，V4 在 Robinhood 链上，实际有没有买回来、烧掉多少，还得看执行记录。

所以我看这两个的兴趣点很明确：

$Claus  值得看，是因为它把“一个币上线之后还能怎么进化”做成了具体实验。

ethereum:0x7987f03462200b3d8a072e02c89a8a41dcb124ee  值得看，是因为如果这类实验越来越多，它有机会持续收过路费，且做一个高质量 HookV4+AI 发射工厂。

text:
Replicate Mulvaney, lever equity.

@choffstein’ s ledger for copying SG Trend is about 145bp a year of savings, minus alpha leakage he illustrates at 108bp. That leaves roughly 37bp on his own example. We agree with the costs. We would copy a different target.

SG Trend is trend diluted to a volatility an investment committee can hold. At that size it only partly delivers what the allocation is for: making money when equities fall and doing ‘fine’ when they rise. 

Mulvaney Global Markets is the undiluted version. The IASG card from early 2024 shows 36 vol, a 0.63 Sharpe, -0.14 correlation to the S&P and a -45% worst drawdown, at 2 and 20.

Per unit of trend, that 2% is the cheaper management fee. It is 5.6bp per point of vol, and the 1.20% average only matches that on a program running above 21.6 vol. The 20% incentive fee is above the 13% average and is paid only on profits. Less capital carries the same hedge, and the capital released goes into levered equity. 

The P&L is not smooth. The hedge becomes something you try to make money on.

The target has already been replicated in public. Concretum's rules-based replica uses 6-month breakouts on 39 futures and reports 0.84 to 0.85 correlation to his monthly returns. On Corey's own formula that fit leaks about 3.8% a year at 36 vol, close to 10bp per point of vol. 2024 was cocoa, more than 4x the next market in that replica, and a replicator that drops softs misses it. Which market prints the fat tail changes every year, and over a long horizon it averages out.

The diluted version wins the mandate because of career risk. 

Concretum counts the fund underwater in about 82% of months, which is hard to defend as a line item, so allocators pay managers to carry that risk for them. The fee is the price of that outsourcing, and the allocation is a local optimum at the allocator level.

Slow trend leaves levered equity exposed to gaps. That is the job of volatility strategies built to make money in gaps, which is what we run.

We still could not run our flagship at 36 vol. We need to sleep at night, so it optimizes for drawdown protection over max growth, and tokenization lets us put other risk profiles in their own vaults. We see the irony. 

The real mystery of finance is how Mulvaney still has hair (asking for a friend @CliffordAsness 🫡)

As for Polymarket Perps and Entropy, I think we'll hear some kind of announcement from Shayne at Token2049 related to their perp DEX. Polymarket and the team obviously want to capture their share of the perp DEX market

It could be some major partnerships, updates to the perp DEX, or even the launch of a points program

The main thing I took away from all this drama is that I no longer have any desire to use Entropy, because we'll probably see the same farming machine there that we saw with Polymarket

In this conflict of interest between perp DEXs, the devs will come out on top and the airdrop farmers will take the L

One of the quants I really respect is Lynn000333. Today he said that after Variational, he doesn't plan to participate in anything else, and his main bet is holding $BTC and $VAR into 2027

My position is pretty similar. You can see me publicly explaining why I'm skipping a lot of perp DEXs, including ones that look like gems such as Arcus and Entropy. I just think the perp DEX meta is heavily overheated, and more and more questionable characters are showing up among the devs. I think we're going to see a lot of disappointed people in this meta in 2027-2028

You already know which perp DEXs I use. You can look through my X and see them. I use them organically, without going overboard. I'm not interested in intentionally farming anything right now

quoted_text:
聊聊怎么赚钱？ #美股 #Bitcoin #ETH
包含美股、加密（涉及现货、合约、MEME等等）

前沿：其实原本这我写了一大段话，但还是删了，因为感觉有点说教的味道。
知道小伙伴不太听，直接聊怎么赚钱才是小伙伴们最想看的。

先说 #Bitcoin 的趋势、波段机会，我知道小伙伴想听MEME  妖币 以及合约的高收益赚钱策略，放心后面会讲到

一、#Bitcoin 的趋势、波段机会（最好结合图查看）

1️⃣ 趋势机会，就是单边主升浪上涨

特征：经历过高价筹码换低价筹码，至少1-2个月；

恐慌情绪完全消散，没有新会产生恐慌情绪的事件预期发生；

利好事件预期发生且会实际发生；
以上缺一不可。

例如，23年Q4，加息最疯狂阶段过去，BTC 现货ETF预期通过并且实际通过，筹码也经过换手，符合

24年Q4，暂停加息，首次降息发生，总统大选，川普支持加密，筹码同样经过换手，符合

25年4-10月，关税告一段落，降息发生等，筹码仍经过换手，符合

以上均带来了BTC单边主升浪上涨行情。不仅K线走势上均直接走出了底部震荡区间，利好事件也实际发生，带动资金的情绪。这就是趋势机会。

当下，筹码确实经过了2月-8月的换手

但恐慌情绪还未消散，因为油价高企，不仅没有降息，还加息了，甚至后续还有加息预期，降息预期不知道在何时

故 虽然冲破585-82的底部震荡区间，但前景恐慌情绪仍在，所以也看到拉升到87还是又打回接近82附近的位置，仍需看宏观利率、地缘层面的走向。

2️⃣波段机会，就是主升浪上涨之前和之后

主升浪上涨之前也就是底部震荡区间，这种在经历过约2-4万美金幅度大跌之后，需要高价筹码换低价筹码，需要开启以月为单位的震荡。因为不可能一直跌。

这就是波段机会，即使觉得看不上这点收益，耐心上车做好均价等待主升浪上涨机会也是可以的。

然后主升浪上后就是高位震荡区间，这种在经历几万美金幅度的拉升之后，需要低价筹码换高价筹码，一般也会开启以月为单位的震荡。因为不可能一直涨。

总要派发低价筹码的，同时新的利空情绪也在酝酿并诞生。不管是高位波段还是主升浪上涨机会把握后，也要及时卖出。不然就会经历利空情绪滋生带来的大幅下跌。

（当然不看K线，就是拿住，那完全看个人）

就此大饼的机会讲完

延伸：#ETH  #BNB #SOL #OKB 等市值靠前的主流项目（注意我说的是加密主流项目，不是指山寨，因为风险不一样）

其实都看大饼的脸色。机会同理，这里就不再一一赘述，细心的小伙伴们可以自己拉长K线走势对比去研究即可。

二、美股的波段机会

美股是风险市场的优质市场，相对其他的市场来说，美股，尤其是核心重股，可称之为简单模式。
如图，美股股票总市值排名，数据来源：https://t.co/OuROkgVFWy

哪些是核心重股？
市值至少3,000亿美金以上，ai科技股，或者近期炒作热点。

如美股七姐妹 英伟达 谷歌 苹果等，一般上市很多年，赶上宏观宽松周期一直拉，然后略微回调歇一歇继续拉升

如新开盘上市 SPCX 高位市值开盘，腰斩左右洗盘，然后继续回升，根据宏观周期和产品进展波动

如炒作热点，闪迪，月线一直拉一直拉，还比如之前的PLTR

主要特征：流动性好，加上美股熔断机制，极短时间快速上下波动，这就是波段机会，因为跌的话，可能跌不了多少，但会一直拉升。

注意⚠️ 宏观层面黑天鹅如经济衰退、加息周期开启等避免下风险即可。这种风险一般出现的时机不多，近6年以来就是20年312，24年85，而今年加息都加了一次，结果都没怎么跌，甚至还涨了。

当然这种黑天鹅出现就是黄金坑。

论波动幅度和大饼比起来，以上提及的美股核心重股更适合投资稳定性偏好者。

对，可能小伙伴马上想到这也更适合低倍大资金合约交易，这是后文要提到的。

三、合约机会

1️⃣加密市场

大饼 、ETH 、BNB等前排市值主流币，什么阶段做什么方向。
相信看过上文，对于合约多空应该也能想得到。

单边主升浪上涨阶段，适合逢低多

一番主升浪上涨过后，不可能一直涨，来到高位震荡阶段，此时得转换思维。因为利好兑现了，情绪也到了过热阶段，此时适合逢高空。

当一轮大跌（幅度2-4万美金）过后，高价筹码换低价筹码，来到底部震荡区间，前期适合逢高空，后期适合逢低多。

因为前期经过大跌，恐慌情绪还未消散，利空可能还有，筹码换手频繁，大事件利好预期没有这么快，涨不上去的。

而后期则要转换思维。因为恐慌情绪消散接近尾声，利好事件预期滋生，筹码换手也结束，一旦事件利好，资金就会推动。

本质上比拼是资金的厚度和认知、心态的耐心。无非怕的就是选错方向。

做短线，吃到就走了。不用赘述。

做长线，即使方向选错，举个实际的例子

前面大饼在6万美金附近，选择多，爆仓位置拉到3万甚至2万以下，然后就是熬时间，无非就是计算费率成本和耐力、资金使用率，或者可以选择分仓拉低均价处理。

所以小伙伴，熬不熬得住看个人。

ETH等其他市值前列的主流币也同理，毕竟主要看BTC的脸色。

然后非主流币：山寨、妖币这些

其实还是我前面说的那个本质问题。但山寨也好，妖币也好，庄的强控性更大，费率更夸张。

试想一下，庄控制高达90%以上的筹码，你觉得在合约上，你玩的过庄吗？

我知道这个更刺激，赚钱更快，但亏钱也快。
故，我个人介意，这种标的，遇上了，玩玩现货能吃一口的话得了。

2️⃣美股市场

能看到这里的小伙伴应该能想到美股核心重股的合约机会的

本质因为流动性好，比如 #SPCX 闪迪 #PLTR 英伟达 等等

适合的策略就是逢低做多，即使位置没有选很好，也不用担心被套很久。且费率也不高，跟油价单子的费率比起来，美股的就很友好

尽可能少做空，因为可能你不知道高的位置在哪，一旦被套就很难受。

而且在宏观层面利于宽松环境、产品发布、主要创始人、机构等发文，可能股价就会上去的。

个人建议可选择1-3个长时间学习，然后去做。

我自己前面就做过英伟达、SPCX的。

四、MEME

高市值MEME满足的条件

1️⃣ 有超高热度，比如在某一语文区有很大流量，比如被知名大佬站台
2️⃣BTC上涨，情绪贪婪时，才能刺激整体用户的情绪，提升投资偏好

缺一不可，比如近期牛来，之前的币安人生，否则是不太可能有高市值、上大所预期的。
没有高市值预期的话，就是提供流动性的。

玩MEME能赚钱且能踩中的本质是拥有足够多的子弹。

不要去拼运气，对于大资金的小伙伴来说，可能可以，但资金不多的小伙伴，一旦真正的机会来了，没有留在牌桌上会是很痛苦的。

写在最后

看到这里的小伙伴可能吐槽，来币圈是赚10个点50个点的嘛？是要10X、20X啊

当下能满足吃到 10X 20X，只可能是MEME 或者妖币，或者妖币合约

而刚好这几类也是高风险的。

假设小资金靠冲MEME想资产增值，那么500刀或者1,000刀，或者3,000、5,000冲一次，
那手里的资金可以冲几次？

如果失去留在牌桌的机会呢？不如老老实实做大饼等主流项目、美股等核心重股的趋势机会或者波段行情。

如果你想从0-1，我个人觉得越应该玩主流币种、核心重股，拿赚到的钱苟着等待时机，再去捕捉高风险高收益的机会。赢了你不就到1了嘛?

输了你也还在牌桌上，怕啥。

其实我刚进圈那会也跟很多小伙伴们一样，拿着小十万块钱，想博一个机会，变成小一百万，但你的运气有多少？别人有运气，那是别人的啊。

当你已经是1，想从1-2，也更应该求稳，有没有想过当你是1的时候，去大饼里去美股里吃10个点，而且没有什么风险，这两个不至于归零吧

你的10个点可能只需要几天，最多1个月，但可能就是别人一年的收入啊。

当然我知道小伙伴们会贪。吃了10个点就想吃20个点。是吧

这就像做生意，不是比谁赚得多，而是比谁活得长。

能看到这里的小伙伴，我相信你多少会有在交易上的一些新认识。

其实每一个点拆开能讲的内容还有很多。我自己就是按照我说的去做交易的。以后也会多分享此类文字

如果觉得看完有帮助，有疑问，欢迎留言探讨，也欢迎一键三连，谢谢大家。

Crypto’s next adoption wave starts when you don’t have to explain how to use it.

@litocoen

“I think today is the time where the mobile UX is finally at a point where you can really onboard a normie without having to explain anything.

Obviously, mobile apps existed in crypto before, like Binance or Coinbase. But I’m talking purely about non-custodial crypto here, which is much harder to abstract away for all kinds of reasons.

And so that is not the case anymore.

You mentioned FOMO. I think it’s crazy how, once you see a product that is really well constructed from a UX point of view, how quickly it can actually scale to a million, two million users.

When there’s no barrier to entry anymore, it just spreads like wildfire. One person tells the other, ‘Use this. You can trade and make money.’

Maybe in our case, it will be, ‘Use this. You can spend with a card and get cashback. Or put your money there regardless of where you are in the world, and you’ll earn some earn rate that is higher than your local bank.’

So once you have a form factor that is really intuitive, mobile apps can spread in a very viral way that a desktop app like Rabby will just never.”

Host:

“Yeah, totally agree. And not to harp on this too long, but I would say I was the case that you had to win over for mobile, because I’m this desktop-only guy for life with crypto.

I never thought I’d do serious crypto on a mobile app, but I’ve completely pivoted that stance.

I think there’s a huge inflection point for crypto adoption because you need to be able to get customers when they’re commuting to work on the bus, or they’re walking, or doing something where they’re carrying their phone. They’re away from desktop.

You’ve just opened the aperture for way more user interaction, and I do think it’s going to be huge.

We’re already seeing it.”

text:
Here's a LlamaAI prompt to find protocols that have growing revenue and steady or declining P/S ratios.

Use it as one of your free 5 daily prompts:

Find token-backed protocols whose protocol revenue is growing faster than their market cap, so they are getting cheaper on P/S, and label each one as sustained or breaking out. Use protocol revenue (not gross fees). Rank the protocols and show P/S for each. P/S is mcap ÷ annualized revenue.

Universe: Protocols with a token and both mcap and revenue data. Exclude chains, stablecoin issuers, CEX-linked tokens, and protocols whose revenue is mainly incentive-driven. ⚙️ Floors: mcap ≥ $25M and 30-day revenue ≥ $250K.

Growth signals:

1.Revenue over the last 30 days vs the prior 30 days must be positive.
2.P/S is compressing: it is lower now than 30 days ago because revenue grew faster than mcap. Show the 30-day P/S change.
3.Classify each protocol as one of:
Sustained: revenue up in each of the last 3 completed months, and 90-day revenue up.
Breaking out: 30-day revenue growth well above its 90-day trend after a flat or declining stretch.
⚙️ Quality checks:
Show absolute revenue next to every % change, and flag base effects from small revenue.
Check whether one day makes up more than ~30% of the 30-day total. If it does, show growth with and without that day.
Separate organic revenue from one-offs and incentive-driven revenue, and say what evidence you used.

Output:
A top-15 table with these columns: protocol, mcap, 30d revenue, 30d revenue change, 90d revenue change, P/S, 30d P/S change, label (sustained or breaking out).
A scatter chart of revenue growth vs P/S.
For each name, one line on the thesis (what is driving revenue) and one line on the main risk.

State every filter you applied. Name notable protocols the screen dropped and why: below the floors, no token, missing mcap or revenue data, or incentive-driven

quoted_text:
what's gonna be your reaction when someone explains "AI on a blockchain" to you for the very first time?

you probably won't take them seriously and maybe even laugh it off right? 

same.

because it's usually vague. just a chatbot with a token attached.

well, @BaranosAI is the first one where i actually sat down and thought, wait, this might actually be it.

read through the whitepaper and the quote below got me:

"verification proves this is the result produced by model M on input X under policy P. it does not prove that the model's statement is factually true, unbiased, safe, or wise."

you see, most projects in this space would never put that sentence in their own paper.

it's basically admitting "our AI can still be wrong."

and that's exactly why i believe it.

because that's the honest version of what's actually solvable right now.

you can't make an AI always correct.

you can make it so nobody can quietly change the question after you've already committed money to the answer.

quite a number of AI-on-chain projects will tell you "trust our AI" because it's perfect, right?

baranos is basically saying "stop trusting us. verify it yourself"

those are completely different products with the same label.

interestingly, they have a two-mode design: confirmation and replay.

they didn't build some slow, expensive, fully-onchain-every-time system.

they built the cheap, fast version for the 99% of jobs that go fine, and kept a heavier, fully onchain fallback for the moment someone actually disputes a result.

and the @fogo choice makes sense once you think about why they're building on fogo.

an AI answer that takes ten minutes to settle isn't very useful for anything time-sensitive like a market resolving, a covenant check, or a liquidation trigger.

if the chain can't settle disputes in roughly a minute, the whole "verifiable" part becomes a nice idea that nobody actually uses because it's too slow 🤷

what i actually believe, not hope, believe, is this:

the chains and products that win the AI era aren't necessarily the ones with the smartest model.

they're the ones that solve the trust problem around the model.

anyone can plug in a good LLM.

almost nobody has built the infrastructure to make that LLM's answer something a smart contract can safely depend on without just taking someone's word for it.

that's what baranos is actually building for.

still early, and it needs the public testing they talk about in their own roadmap.

i'm not pretending this is proven at scale yet.

but the thesis is sound, and the architecture actually matches the thesis instead of just gesturing at it.

text:
Story time.

A few weeks ago, everyone wanted a piece of the Robinhood ecosystem. Now the charts are down, the timeline is miserable, and people are calling it finished.

Robinhood put stocks onchain, and LONG caught on, pairing tokens with stock tokens, like AI against NVDA. Meanwhile, the high-volume launchpad PONS and Robinhood meme CASHCAT ran first. Memecoin culture had just started meeting real stocks.

Early buyers made money, screenshots spread, and new money poured into Robinhood Chain, BNB Chain and Solana.

But that money had plenty of places to go. Early holders took profits. Platforms collected fees. Bots took their cut. Others rotated into the next thing. Some insiders sold into latecomers. And in a thin market, a little selling can reprice the entire onchain ecosystem.

Then the psychology flips. After enough losses, people sell rallies and stop trusting launches. Weaker confidence means fewer buyers, and the chart starts writing the story.

So what changed underneath the chart? Robinhood has nearly 30 million funded customers, and Vlad has talked about taking stock tokens from around 200 to the thousands.

This is where LONG gets more interesting. With LONG 500, new stock-paired pools send a share of their stock-token fees to $AI's treasury. If stock tokens grow into the thousands, that's a lot of potential new pairs. The projects still have to capture it.

One drawdown doesn't settle the story either. POPCAT fell about 70% in early 2024, then went far above that peak. BONK, PEPE and WIF came back from big drawdowns too. Plenty of tokens never recover, so that's not a forecast.

I'm watching for stronger BTC and ETH, buyers absorbing the selling, and charts starting to turn.

The first wave of excitement has faded while the opportunity keeps building.

text:
AI Drug Discovery Is Becoming a Bottleneck Trade

I get excited when an industry starts going through a real regime change. AI drug discovery (“AIDD”) increasingly looks like one of those moments.

Two things are happening:
1/ Upstream: the frontier AI labs are piling in.
2/ Downstream: The supply chain is clearly moving.

Supply-chain checks suggest the upstream picks-and-shovels of discovery and early preclinical R&D are starting to feel the increase in experimental volume.

DNA → protein → assays → sequencing → automation → preclinical testing

Names across that stack include $TWST , @GenScript , $ILMN , $TXG , lab-automation vendors and CROs.

$TWST expects triple-digit percentage growth in AI-enabled drug-discovery orders in FY26, and another year of triple-digit order growth in FY27.

@GenScript's AIDD business doubled YoY in 1H26. Its current platform advertises industrial-scale validation of 4,000+ designs/day, with integrated sequence-to-data workflows. Our channel checks suggest the ramp is moving even faster: roughly 8,000 designs/day currently, with a path toward ~16,000/day by YE26.

---
Why does AI drive more wet-lab demand?

1/ AI makes hypothesis generation almost free → way more shots on goal.
The bottleneck is moving from expert-driven design to biological validation.

2/ AI models need continuous experimental feedback — and both good and bad data are useful.
Traditionally, only the highest-conviction A+ candidates might get pushed into expensive validation. With AI, even the B/C candidates can be valuable because failed experiments generate training data.

@GenScript has said its sequence-to-binding workflow can return data in 4–7 days, and that faster cycle times matter because AI models depend on continuous experimental feedback.

@Anthropic is a clean example. @claudeai  designed 1,320 protein binders. @adaptyvbio  converted those digital sequences into DNA, expressed the proteins and tested binding. Only 354 actually bound. And the 966 failures are not wasted. They are useful negative labels: what does not express, what does not bind, what has poor affinity. Those results help train the next model iteration.

3/ Wet labs are no longer just making drugs. They are making training data.
$TWST  / @GenScript  increasingly look like biological data foundries.

$TWST explicitly talks about generating model-ready data from AI-designed sequences. In some workflows, the customer may care less about receiving the physical protein than about getting structured experimental results back into the model.

Traditional drug discovery asks: “Does candidate X work?”

AI drug discovery also asks: “What can this experiment teach the model?”

---
TAM of AIDD

If AI is simply a better R&D tool, the relevant spending pool is the $300–400B of annual global pharma R&D. If AI meaningfully increases the number of viable drug programs, the opportunity is larger because it expands downstream demand for DNA synthesis, protein production, assays, and preclinical work.

Near term, we can also size demand from AI-company spending. If Anthropic reaches $80B of ARR in 2026 and spends just 1% on AIDD, that alone would imply ~$800M of annual investment.

---
Trade setup

This is a trade that could have long legs. It’s hard to really stop working until PhaseI/II results (2028+)

It smells a lot like the bottleneck trade we just saw in semis: GPUs → HBM → networking → power/cooling. In biology, It basically follows the drug discovery process downstream: AI models → designs → DNA/protein → assays → preclinical capacity.

After the upstream picks-and-shovels, animal testing could become the next bottleneck. Monkey prices are already near prior highs and CRO capacity is tight. AIDD pushing more candidates into preclinical development would only add demand.

?? But clinical trials are still the bottleneck?
This is the biggest pushback I keep coming back to. No matter how fast discovery becomes, drugs still need to go through preclinical → Phase I → Phase II → Phase III → approval. You still need patients, time and capital.

But that doesn’t mean the bottleneck trade won’t work. More viable candidates — especially with higher success rates — still means more demand throughout the development process.

And who knows: clinical trials themselves may eventually be optimized by AI.

?? What breaks the trade?
Near term, the picks-and-shovels trade breaks if experimental budgets stop growing, AI-generated designs don’t translate into useful wet-lab hits, or capacity catches up too quickly.

Longer term, the thesis breaks if AI drugs look great in discovery / Phase I but fail at normal rates in Phase II/III. That is why Phase II matters so much.

?? Milestones
Late 2026–2027: first Isomorphic-designed drugs enter human trials; more AI-native programs move into IND-enabling work / tox.

2028–2030: clinical trial results start telling us whether AI-designed drugs actually perform better than conventional drugs.

Calling all the "bottleneck bros". :) @jukan05 @zephyr_z9 @aleabitoreddit @ParadisLabs 

+++
More comprehensive analysis: https://t.co/vaTuiyyYB6

加密安全调查员 @zachxbt 发布重磅推文，曝光了他亲自作为“卧底”深入朝鲜黑客（DPRK）洗钱网络的完整过程。

通过数月的诱敌深入与链上交叉比对，不仅锁定了 Bybit 被盗案的关键资金链路，还一举牵出了 Poloniex 攻击案与汇旺担保（Huione Guarantee）的黑产网络！

🧵 以下为调查的核心线索与惊人细节整理：

1️⃣ 诱敌深入：从微额交易到锁定“核心洗钱人”

黑钱源头露馅：洗钱中介 Jimmy Green 向 ZachXBT 提供了收款地址（0xbaa5...）。ZachXBT 追查其 Gas 费来源地址（0xcbc84...），发现该地址直接源自 Bybit 黑客攻击资金，已被标记为黑名单。

小额建立信任：为了不打草惊蛇，ZachXBT 自掏腰包与对方进行了多笔微额交易。

洗钱团伙自爆：Jimmy Green 在聊天中夸口称他们是“中国最大的专业混币隔离与防冻结团队”，并透露“老外（朝鲜黑客）最近让我们放假 10 天”。

2️⃣ 预判路径与链上“抓包”闭环

预告洗钱路径：Jimmy Green 在聊天中提前透露了朝鲜资金的跨链路线（如 BTC 跨链转回 Solana），第二天链上数据精准印证了其说法。

实况截图被“抓包”：2025 年 3 月 12 日，Jimmy Green 发送了一张自己正在操作跨链 Swap（BTC 转 ETH）的截图。ZachXBT 迅速在 THORChain 浏览器上根据金额和时间戳匹配到了具体的交易哈希（81a85130b...），形成了无法反驳的链上锁死证据！

承兑商分发机制：Jimmy Green 宣称 Bybit 案中近 15 亿美元的 ETH 几乎都由其团队洗掉，并透露他们通过将“脏 U”分散给下线承兑商（Acceptors）来规避冻结。

3️⃣ 链上图谱：一石激起千层浪

Bybit 资金流向：TRM 资金链路图显示，Bybit 盗款经多层中间地址分流后，通过 THORChain 跨链为 1.192 BTC，汇入 Jimmy Green 控制的地址并流入 THORSWAP。

Solana 资金池与冻结：根据对方提供的 Solana 地址，ZachXBT 追踪到超过 1200 万美元的 Bybit 盗款在多链（BTC/ETH/SOL/TRX）间流转，并协助 Tether 成功冻结了其中的 44.2 万 USDT。

牵出更多黑产事件：

· Poloniex 盗案：Jimmy Green 提及有团队被冻结的 33.2 万 USDC，链上追查确认直接源自 2023 年 11 月的 Poloniex 攻击案。
· 汇旺担保（Huione）：其提及帮另一客户洗钱 300 万美元，资金链直接指向已被制裁的汇旺担保热钱包。

4️⃣ 人设破绽与高昂的“卧底代价”

洗钱者的日常：Jimmy Green 在聊天中展示了极度割裂的生活——一边聊着帮朝鲜黑客和诈骗犯洗钱，一边分享打麻将、吃枪杀野味（野兔/野禽）、吃减脂餐、去迪士尼，以及靠翻译软件打出蹩脚英文。甚至还吐槽“朋友发 NFT 卖给日本人杀猪”。

真正的风险与成本：ZachXBT 坦言，为了完成这次卧底，他亲自垫付了 34.97 万美元，每笔交易承受 5% 的损耗。他不仅面临对方随时卷款跑路的风险，还要承受直接与犯罪集团交涉的人身安全威胁。

💡 总结：链上安全不仅是冷冰冰的数据比对，更是惊心动魄的心理博弈。ZachXBT 用极大的个人风险和资金成本，再次为整个 Web3 行业绘制出了一幅清晰的黑产洗钱全景图。

quoted_text:
Opus 5.5 一晚上烧掉周用量的 40%，仔细研究发现不是模型不耐用，根源出在 Sub Agent 反复写缓存。

对照了一下，之前拼死拼活 6 天才用掉 60%，昨天一个晚上，两个全自主做视频的 Session，派出 228 个 Sub Agent，占了整晚用量的 84%。

如果折成 API 用量，主会话占了 $99，而 Sub Agent 占了 $527（顺手证明 Max 20x，确实满打满算大约 $6000/月）。

比较神奇的是，钱没花在产出上，输出 token 只占了 5%。

真正贵的是这两项：

1. 缓存读取 49%。每个 Sub Agent 带着 11–14 万 token 上下文，跑了 25–40 轮；
2. 缓存写入 42%，主会话缓存有效期 1 小时，Sub Agent 只有 5 分钟，几乎每开一个就重写了一遍。

再往下看，这些 Sub Agent 都在做审查：画面、稿子、成片，还要复审。我给的规则是每阶段独立审查、最多 4 轮，一个会话同时做 5 期，阶段 × 期数 × 轮数，用量就爆炸了。

于是对症下药，优化了一下 AGENTS.md，预计能省到 80%：

1. 审查换成 Sonnet 5.5，effort 调到 low
2. 每阶段最多 2 轮，只有改过严重问题才复审
3. 不逐帧审，每节一张图
4. 一期一个 Session，不在一个会话里开多期

你有哪些好用的 token 优化技巧？欢迎分享出来👏

author: bread_
quoted_text:
Derive spent V2 building a specialized chain for sophisticated derivatives. V3 takes a different approach

the execution environment becomes specialized, while Ethereum becomes the settlement and verification layer. that distinction matters as Derivatives need speed

risk calculations, pricing and matching cannot wait for every individual state transition to be processed on L1. so V3 pushes the heavy execution into a zkVM, generates proofs of the resulting state, and lets Ethereum verify the outcome.

the result is an interesting separation of responsibilities:

- fast execution where the market needs it

- cryptographic verification where trust matters

- Ethereum settlement underneath it all

that gives @DeriveXYZ a much stronger foundation for composability. if the state of a derivatives market can be verified against Ethereum, the market becomes easier to integrate with the rest of DeFi

Wallets can interact with it, Vaults can build on it && Structured products can settle against it

Agents can potentially use it as a financial execution layer. other applications don’t necessarily need to become their own derivatives venue

they can build on the infrastructure underneath. that’s the part i personally think gets overlooked when people describe V3 as simply “moving Derive back to Ethereum.”

the interesting shift is architectural

-V2 specialized the chain

-V3 specializes the execution

Ethereum provides the settlement layer

and ZK proofs connect the two:)

if Derive can execute increasingly sophisticated financial logic while anchoring the resulting state to Ethereum, the addressable market becomes much larger than the users on https://t.co/zCo1Y9YLfq

the frontend becomes one distribution channel

the protocol becomes the infrastructure

that’s a much more interesting bet

text:
Uniswap approved our hook 🦄🌲

Uniswap Labs reviewed the Twigpine Wrap Hook and approved it for routing.

In plain words: when you buy $TWIG on Uniswap, the router can now use the main GITLAWB pool, which is about 40x deeper than the TWIG/WETH pool. That means more TWIG for the same ETH.

What's a hook?
A small contract attached to a Uniswap pool. It changes how swaps in that pool work.

Ours does one thing. It swaps TWIG ↔ GITLAWB at exactly 1:1 with a 0% fee, by wrapping or unwrapping. It has no owner, and nobody can change it.

Why it matters:
Until now, a TWIG buy on most apps went through the small TWIG/WETH pool (~$11K liquidity). In our tests, buys of 0.1 to 1 ETH got 10–16% fewer TWIG than the route through the hook.

Now Uniswap can do the deep route in one swap:
ETH → GITLAWB in the main pool (~$490K liquidity) → TWIG at 1:1 through the hook.

Selling works the same way, in reverse.

author: 0xMerp
quoted_text:
credits is an artwork about belief

each credit was created from a private payment - an $8 transaction on x money

each transaction id, originally visible only to sender and recipient, was converted to a sha-256 hash to create an artwork made of four 8x8 printing plates in cmyk (cyan, magenta, yellow and black)

the transaction id and settlement timestamp became public source data for the onchain artwork

the x money transaction settlement time (in seconds) determined which plates print - there are 15 different possible combinations of cmyk, so this process repeats 4 x per minute

if the original transaction id contained an 8, the resulting artwork metadata keeps track of each

the rarity calculation considers the color combination, the number of active pixels, the space they occupy after the plates shift, the number of 8s in the transaction id, and the registration of the plates

these qualities are measured against the completed collection and translated into a credit rating between 80 and 800

the rating measures those traits - it cannot account for every reason someone might value an image

the rating is fixed - the price is whatever someone is willing to pay

80 credits can be burned to create a statement

the collector chooses which credits to use and how to arrange them - their individual ratings are added together, and their colors become the material of the new artwork

a statement can take different visual forms without changing its rating

statements can also be overprinted - one is burned into another, combining their ink, ratings and histories

balance is the proposed next form

under this design, a statement can be permanently surrendered for its rating in divisible erc-20 tokens - one point becomes one balance

the statement is locked rather than destroyed - its artwork and history remain, but it can no longer be transferred

its quantity and color composition can move independently

each receiving wallet gets one non-transferable erc-721 artwork

the artwork stays with the wallet and reads its current balance of the transferable erc-20 token

the tokens move - the artwork updates

if the wallet holds nothing, the artwork remains and displays zero

when balances meet, their colors mix in proportion to the amounts received - when they split, each part carries a share of that mixture

the colors preserve an aggregate ancestry, not a traceable list of individual credits or statements

exchange custody can mix them further - a buyer may receive the exchange’s mixture rather than the particular colors a seller deposited

someone who never owned a credit or a statement can inherit their colors

credits, statements and balances can exist at the same time

some people keep the individual marks, some compose them into pages, and some surrender the page for something they can divide and exchange

others may simply prefer the balance artwork

composition reduces the number of surviving credits, overprinting reduces the number of surviving statements, and surrender moves statements out of circulation while releasing their accumulated rating as balance

the appetite for liquidity becomes one of the forces shaping all three collections

but making something divisible does not mean someone will want to buy it - actual liquidity still requires buyers and funded markets

balance offers divisibility, not a promise of demand

the market becomes a medium - its activity changes the distribution of the work, and when trading stops, that distribution remains

the price can disappear, the artwork cannot

text:
JUST IN: Scientists estimate there will be over 23,200,000 new launchpads created within the next year!

There are currently 400 cryptocurrencies valued above $50M market cap. Each of these deserves their own themed launchpad.

You can assume that on each of these launchpads, there will be another 400 launchpads launched:

400 * 400 = 160,000

On top of that, some builders might want to create forks (L3s) of the main launchpads (L1s) or of the launchpads launched (L2s) on the launchpads (L4s).

Being conservative, we can just multiply 160,000 by 10 to get us to 1.6M launchpads created.

Keep in mind that crypto is developing at an extremely fast rate though. We'll probably have another 1000 coins reach a valuation above $50M market cap this cycle, (1000 * 1000 = 1 million * 10 = 10 million additional new launchpads).

On top of that, you have to remember that hooks will only continue to gain more mindshare this cycle, so there will probably be a separate hook launchpad for every other launchpad created:

(1.6M + 10M) * 2 = 23.2M new launchpads

text:
of all the takes that age terribly, “dont put ads in a consumer product” is probably the one that’s most guaranteed to make you look sanctimonious and self-righteous in retrospect. every single great consumer internet product and platform with >1bn users delivers some form of ad unit, because that’s how you scale a product to the largest group of people possible. ads are, quite literally, why we can have nice things.

and so it shouldn’t have been a surprise that back in jan / feb the following things happened 1) openai announced they were rolling out ads to subsidize their enormous base of free users 2) a bunch of people tried to paint this as a bad thing. now, with the benefit of ~240 days of hindsight, we can audit just how ridiculous this kneejerk reaction was.

as of august, oai has ~$1bn in arr for their ad product. in this podcast recorded for the 7th edition of the top 100 consumer ai apps leaderboard, i sat down with @omooretweets, author of the bi-yearly report, and @joshelman, to discuss why ads remain such an important part of the consumer experience, and why subscriptions can only take us so far. some takeaways:

- the subscription market is a peculiar slice of the consumer market. olivia's yipit panel suggests around 4.5% of US consumers pay for an ai subscription, and spending is concentrated in people using it to build, create, and get work done.
-a founder who needs every user to pay has a strong reason to keep building for that audience (a rather circumscribed group of people who value saving time over spending it). advertising creates room to serve people with different interests and willingness to pay. developers / creators who view ai as a way to get leverage over their lives is an important group of paying subscribers, but a smaller cohort compared with people who view ai solely as a source of information or mild entertainment for now.
- josh pointed out that ai companies can become afraid of growing too fast because every new user brings meaningful expense (this explains why, for example, meta seems to be pushing muse a little less aggressively than a product like threads, which cost far less marginally to serve to users). but as inference gets cheaper, ads and transaction fees can support more of the experiences people might want to try.
- josh found its ads useful while planning a trip. olivia thinks the context people supply could make the advertising more effective. that creates a product-design opportunity: help someone find what they want, with the sponsorship made overt and a clear value add.
- a valuable audience doesn't have to be everyone. olivia points to openevidence's early success with advertising among doctors. specialized ai products can gather audiences whose shared needs are useful to particular businesses. there is room for companies with much more focused purposes than a general assistant.

i think this is why the ads question matters beyond oai’s revenue. the business model helps determine who gets products built for them. ads are what enable ai to get built for everyone.

text:
关于 @OKX 即将推出的代币化股票交易平台 (Tokenized Securities Venue, TSV)，这是你需要知道的 16 个细节：

1/ 公司主体叫 OKXICE LLC，ICE 和 OKX USA 各持股 50%

2/ 这个 TSV 基于 X Layer 构建，以 OKB 作为 gas

3/ 这个 TSV 是用 Uniswap v4 和「需许可」的 Hook 建立股票代币 AMM，可 7×24 小时交易，价格由 x * y = k 决定，不是传统订单薄

4/ 「需许可」的意思是，散户、机构和做市商要参与交易和成为 LP，都得经过 KYC 和 AML 审查，钱包里会获得一个不可转移的 SBT。每一笔交易、转账、添加 LP 等活动，智能合约都会检查 SBT；如果用户出现制裁、可疑活动、监管要求等情况，OKXICE 可以撤回/销毁 SBT，并把钱包踢出白名单。

5/ 首批支持的股票有 60 多支，我们耳熟能详的英伟达、特斯达、微软、谷歌、苹果、SpaceX、亚马逊这些... 肯定都在里面了。这些股票可以跟 USDC, USDT, USDG 组成交易对。

6/ 这些股票都不是合成资产，必须有 1:1 的美国正规上市股票 (NMS Stock) 支撑。并且享有普通股持有人一样的权益，包括经济权益、股息、投票权、合并/拆分同步等

7/ 这些股票在 Uniswap V4 上可以 7×24 小时交易，价格完全由 AMM Pool 决定。周末纳斯达克、纽交所没有价格时，Uniswap 里仍然有价格。

8/ 但如果正股因为退市、熔断等因素停牌时，Uniswap 这边也必须停止交易。

9/ 用户的资产始终是自托管的，OKXICE 不托管用户资产。因此交易也是完全链上结算，没有清算所。

10/ 只支持现货，要买 1 万美元的 TSLA token，就必须有 1 万美元的稳定币。不支持保证金、借款等杠杆手段。

11/ 既然是在链上，所以任何通过 KYC 持有 SBT 的人都可以提供流动性成为 LP，参与做市。100% 的池子手续费都会给 LP，OKXICE 不收取。OKXICE 会对每一笔成交另外收取服务费。

12/ 因为是「需许可」的，所以除非被列入了白名单，否则第三方智能合约无法与 OKXICE TSV 智能合约集成或访问它们。

13/ 还有一个很大的悬念：负责股票托管 + 代币铸造 / 赎回 + 权利映射的这个「发行方」(Tokenizer) 到底是谁，是 OKXICE 自己，还是另外的公司，目前不确定。

14/ 如果未来 Tokenizer 同意、另一个交易平台满足 SEC 的要求，这些代币股票也可以在 OKXICE TSV 之外的平台进行交易。这是标准之争，长期看很重要。现在市场上已经有 Ondo, xStocks, bStocks, Coinbase Tokenized Stocks, Robinhood Stock Tokens 这些股票代币发行通道 / 标准，如何整合他们之间的流动性，未来会是一个问题。

15/ OKXICE TSV 已经收到 Cerebras Systems Inc. (CBRS) 的发行人异议通知，这就牵扯出另一个问题，如果更多上市公司明确反对自己的股票被代币化，会怎样？

16/ SEC 给 TSV 设定了一个单只股票每天允许成交的上限。第二次及以后超量成效，该股票会在 TSV 上停牌 3 个月。也就是说，SEC 允许实验链上证券交易，但规模必须足够小。如果反复突破实验规模限制，SEC 就让这个标的强制冷却三个月。

整体感受就是，OKX 这次的做法跟其它几家 CEX 不一样，它是把股票、稳定币、DeFi、自托管和传统证券交易所，全部有机地连接到了一起，而不是简单地「代币化」，非常牛 👍 @star_okx 

如果这套模式跑通，区块链行业争夺的就不再只是几万亿美元的加密资产交易市场，而是开始进入数十万亿美元传统证券资产的交易与结算基础设施。

SEC 在实验的是，DeFi LP 能不能合法成为美国证券市场的流动性提供者，如果最终跑通，意味着普通人也可以真正成为证券市场的做市商，这个意义也是非常巨大的

text:
灰度：比特币涨幅高度集中于少数交易日，保持离场亦存在机会成本

灰度研究主管 Zach Pandl 发文表示，过去三年，比特币累计回报率约为 225%，同期纳斯达克指数回报率为 109%。但比特币的上涨并未均匀分布，少数表现最强的交易日对长期回报贡献较大，增加了投资者把握入场时机的难度。

数据显示，若剔除比特币表现最好的 5 个交易日，其三年累计回报率将由 225% 降至 95%；剔除最佳 10 个交易日后，回报率降至 27%；若错过最佳 15 个交易日，三年回报将转为亏损 11%。相比之下，纳斯达克的回报分布较为均衡，剔除最佳 15 个交易日后，累计回报率由 109% 降至 21%。

灰度表示，在此期间，不到 0.5% 的交易日贡献的涨幅，就足以在剔除后令比特币累计回报减少一半以上。对于具有高回报和高波动特征的资产，保持离场同样存在机会成本；由于最佳交易日难以可靠预测，等待波动下降或市场前景更加清晰时，部分价格重估可能已经完成。
