quoted_text:
What Menlo has done over the last 24 months is exceptional.

Yes, they did Anthropic’s round at $4BN that will make them $50BN+ as a firm. NICE!

But they then took that and went f****** hard. They do Lovable, Higgsfield, Legora.

They compounded the brand win of Anthropic to cement their position from respectfully a slightly ageing firm to being a dominant venture leader at the forefront with Thrive, a16z, Benchmark etc.

It is incredible to see and I sat down with @venkyganesan to shoot the s*** on this.

1. Every Seed Investment Is an Option Bet

Seed-stage deals function as financial options to discover true outlier potential before committing major capital. VCs must construct a broad enough portfolio to secure sufficient at-bats, only sizing up their position when quantifiable, revenue-based metrics prove an outlier has emerged.

2. What Is the First Sign of the AI Wave Cracking?

Market cycles rarely collapse due to equity write-downs. They fracture when levered debt defaults occur. When market participants take on heavy leverage during an AI boom, precise timing becomes as critical as being directionally correct, making debt obligations the primary failure vector when cycles turn.

3. Why Every VC Must Now Prioritize IRR

Every startup in the current landscape writes a structural tax to the Mag 7 and hyperscalers for compute and foundation models. Because LPs can buy index exposure to those same public tech giants without fees or carry, private VCs must generate outsized IRR performance, beating public markets by at least 1,000 basis points, to justify private capital allocation.

4. Why LPs Wanting Smaller Funds and Slower Deployment Is BS

LPs cannot demand both smaller fund sizes and multi-year deployment paces in the middle of a generational platform shift. Because AI startups face immense capital requirements to scale compute, VC firms that refuse to deploy capital rapidly will watch competitors step in and capture the category winners.

5. The Theory of Reflexivity and How It's Causing Markups

Reflexivity creates self-reinforcing loops where fast revenue growth triggers rapid valuation markups, attracting elite human and financial capital that further accelerates growth. However, when copycat investors chase markups for momentum rather than underlying fundamentals, reflexive valuation bubbles inflate until market realities force an inevitable correction.

6. Sometimes You Pay Up Because You Have Unique Insight

Premium entry prices are not always the result of irrational bidding. They often stem from an investor's ability to recognize a fundamentally larger total addressable market than the consensus. When a VC possesses unique conviction around an expanding market opportunity, paying above current rates reflects calculated foresight rather than price-taking behavior.

7. There's No Limit to What a Person Can Do as Long as They Don't Care Who Gets the Credit

Personal ego remains one of the most expensive liabilities in venture capital and company building. True long-term success requires setting aside individual notoriety, focusing ruthlessly on generating LP returns, and empowering teammates and founders without worrying about who receives the public credit.

Solana’s next titan is being built in plain sight, and I don’t think most people have caught on yet.

The past couple of weeks at @solomon_labs have been pretty incredible. We’ve launched solana:USDvUSpnhCr9yBgj3UyVrD239HRUv4RsHwH2FxsWuMk publicly and started putting real capital and partnerships behind something I’ve been excited about since joining: your dollar should be productive without you having to change how you use it.

A quick look at where we stand:

• USDv launched on Solana through @sunrise, with $5M+ entering circulation in its first hour.
• Three independent security audits are complete, including the latest review by @zenith256.
• @Raydium committed an initial $1M of treasury capital and is becoming USDv’s primary liquidity venue, with support for USDv pairs across its markets and launchpads.
• @onrefinance has already allocated $1M to USDv as part of the collateral backing ONyc.
• @MetaDAOProject will convert up to $2M of treasury USDC into USDv.
• @orogoldapp announced GOLD/USDv pools, bringing productive dollars into onchain gold liquidity.

For a dollar that only launched publicly last week, that is a hell of a starting point.

These announcements are the opening steps in relationships we’re continuing to build. There are deeper ties forming with Raydium, OnRe, Sunrise and our other partners, with a lot more we want to accomplish together. The initial allocations and markets give us somewhere to start, and I’m excited to share more as that work develops.

It’s worth understanding why these teams are choosing USDv, because the same benefit applies to your own dollars.

Opt in once and eligible USDv balances can earn while remaining liquid and usable across supported wallets, LP positions and integrations. The dollar side of a liquidity pool can earn alongside swap fees. Treasury capital can stay available while producing rewards. You don’t need to stake, wrap or lock your dollars to participate.

Teams are already putting millions behind that proposition. I think the appetite for productive assets is going to become much more obvious as people see what this means for the positions they already hold.
And that opportunity extends well beyond USDv.

The Solomon Platform lets issuers program an asset’s economics and rules, track who is entitled to what as it moves through different contexts, and route those economics where they belong. USDv demonstrates what that can do for dollars. The same infrastructure can support other productive assets, including tokenized stocks with dividends to distribute.

The network we’re building around USDv gives us a way to help those assets grow as well. Relationships with liquidity venues, applications and asset issuers can create distribution for future assets using Solomon, giving them access to an ecosystem we’re already working to connect.

Seeing that take shape with some of the biggest teams on Solana, this early, is a huge part of why I’m excited about where we’re headed.

If you’re holding idle USDC or USDT, take a look at USDv. Swap into USDv, opt in to rewards, and put those dollars to work.

I have dug through over 7,000+ arrest records in the state of North Carolina over the past 2 weeks.

What I found was so shocking, I had a hard time believing it myself...

It appears major fraud is taking place in arrest records where Black offenders are labelled White.

I didn't come across this once or twice.

It appears that a few HUNDRED Black offenders are being labelled as White.

The option to pick "BLACK" exists and is used frequently in arrest records...

...but it seems they are purposely choosing the label of "WHITE AFRICAN" or "WHITE CAUCASIAN" to identify someone who is clearly a "BLACK" person.

This is massive fraud.
author: mattvanswol

text:
The video shows real NC jail records (e.g. Mecklenburg) with Black-appearing people coded Race W + Ethnicity AFR (or CAU), including same-person flips from B. Black is an available option.

This does not prove deliberate "massive fraud" at scale. Large mugshot/record studies find Black-White swaps rare and roughly symmetric (impact ~1%). Main misclassification is Hispanics as White per NC/federal coding rules. Official NC arrest data still shows Blacks ~46% of arrestees. Likely entry errors or system quirks, not a coordinated plot.

text:
TLDR is Derive v3 is Lighter, but for options. 

"Deposits" into the app are still functionally bridging, but because it's not general purpose there isn't a perceived migration to a totally separate execution environment (which it is). 

This is a bullish rebrand of the term imo, and actually gives a glimpse into how the Ethereum roadmap plays out.

→ Ethereum is a liquidity hub
→ Appchains link into it

This creates less of a perceived vamp on Ethereum mainnet, but it's the ~same outcome for $ETH unfortunately (your offloading the valuable part [execution]).

Very bullish for the apps tho — they get access to Ethereum liquidity, are still perceived as "Ethereum" apps, can do things like allow for Ethereum defi positions/yield as collateral, and keep all the fees/good UX by performing off chain execution.

A few more of these appchain infinity stones and Ethereum has a full slate. Should probably do a launchpad + dex combo appchain next.
author: dcfgod
quoted_text:
Derive spent V2 building a specialized chain for sophisticated derivatives. V3 takes a different approach

the execution environment becomes specialized, while Ethereum becomes the settlement and verification layer. that distinction matters as Derivatives need speed

risk calculations, pricing and matching cannot wait for every individual state transition to be processed on L1. so V3 pushes the heavy execution into a zkVM, generates proofs of the resulting state, and lets Ethereum verify the outcome.

the result is an interesting separation of responsibilities:

- fast execution where the market needs it

- cryptographic verification where trust matters

- Ethereum settlement underneath it all

that gives @DeriveXYZ a much stronger foundation for composability. if the state of a derivatives market can be verified against Ethereum, the market becomes easier to integrate with the rest of DeFi

Wallets can interact with it, Vaults can build on it && Structured products can settle against it

Agents can potentially use it as a financial execution layer. other applications don’t necessarily need to become their own derivatives venue

they can build on the infrastructure underneath. that’s the part i personally think gets overlooked when people describe V3 as simply “moving Derive back to Ethereum.”

the interesting shift is architectural

-V2 specialized the chain

-V3 specializes the execution

Ethereum provides the settlement layer

and ZK proofs connect the two:)

if Derive can execute increasingly sophisticated financial logic while anchoring the resulting state to Ethereum, the addressable market becomes much larger than the users on https://t.co/zCo1Y9YLfq

the frontend becomes one distribution channel

the protocol becomes the infrastructure

that’s a much more interesting bet

Derive Simplified

text:
September was an absolute blur, looking back on it we actually shipped a bunch of cool updates, and finally cracked a few big milestones (10m volume, 2m OI) 🚢

Bullet Liquidity Provider (BLP) was finally opened to public deposits, and the $300k cap filled the same day. We've extensively tested the strategy for 3 months and it's been overall profitable, with a 2.37 Sharpe and ~100% APY on the last 30 days annualised. Deposit caps will be opening up again this week, keep notis on 🔔

Speed. We benchmarked end-to-end execution against other perp venues. Bullet came in at ~8ms, ahead of Lighter and HL (Nado just recently improved their p50 a lot to ~7ms, congrats to them, we will get you back xd). Our matching engine runs at ~250µs, and most of the remaining time goes to the network, and there's a lot we have flagged to improve still. Thankfully still have the lowest p999 (tail latency) of any DEX by a factor of 4x.

Collateral. You can now post SOL and jitoSOL as margin, meaning no hassle to sell your beloved bags to stables. We built the jitoSOL integration with @jito_sol, so your collateral keeps earning staking yield while you trade.

New Markets. We listed RAY, BNC, UNI and NEAR, and PUMP and DOGE go live tomorrow. We also automated most of our listing pipeline, so a new market now takes us about 15 minutes end to end. Expect a lot more of them, and quickly. People under-appreciate the operational burden of exchange listings, and we've spent a bunch of time seeing how it can largely be automated. We're aiming to list 2 new markets every week.

Liquidity. Most majors (BTC/ETH/SOL) are now consistently 0.1-0.5bps wide at the top of the book (!!), which is testament to why we've been hell bent on building the fastest execution stack on the market. @AphelionTrading  is now providing very competitive liquidity on Bullet. They were the highest-volume onchain market maker on Solana from last cycle, and true friends and legends that I am grateful to be working with again.

Fees. We cut trading fees across every tier, and volume picked in accordance. We are going to continue experimenting with fee structures that reduce friction to onboarding for new traders evaluating our product, our goal being to provide the best cost for the average perps consumer (spread + fees).

Affiliates. More than 100 affiliates have signed up since we launched the program. Form linked below.

Product. We shipped subaccounts, isolated margin, and vault infrastructure that lets anyone launch and run their own vault.

text:
AI 创业这三年最可能集体做错的一件事，是太迷信「帮人省时间」了。

a16z 昨天刚发了第七版 Top 100 Consumer AI Apps。他们把消费互联网分成 15 个大类，其中 9 个品类，到现在连一个进入 AI Top 100 的产品都没有。

这 9 个是：

Streaming、Social、Dating、Gaming、Travel、Retail、Finance、Real Estate、Jobs。

基本把过去两代消费互联网最肥的地方列了一遍。

Netflix、YouTube、TikTok、Tinder、Roblox、Airbnb、Amazon、Zillow、LinkedIn……这些公司能长这么大，核心需求很多都和「效率」没什么关系。用户打开它们，本来就是为了把时间花掉。

「大多数人没那么想节省时间，他们是在找怎么花掉时间。」

这也解释了现在 AI 面对消费者的一个挺奇怪的结构。

美国已经有接近一半的人用过 AI，但只有 4.5% 的消费者在为 ChatGPT、Gemini 或 Claude 这样的个人 AI 订阅付费。更夸张的是，付费用户里最顶上的 1%，平均一个月能在 AI 上花 903 美元；中位数只有 25 美元。

现在这套 AI 产品，实际上还是一群开发者、创作者和效率狂人在消费。

大家做 Coding、Research、PPT、写作、视频生成、自动化，全都在研究怎么把原来一小时的事压到十分钟。

但普通人的一天并没有因此突然多出八小时工作需求。

我反而越来越觉得，下一波真正大的 Consumer AI，未必会继续从「帮你做完一件事」里出来。

它可能更像 TikTok、游戏、约会软件或者社交网络。用户没有任务，也没有 Prompt，甚至没想着自己需要 AI，但就是愿意每天在里面待两个小时。

AI 已经证明自己能帮人工作了。

接下来更难、也可能更值钱的问题，是怎么让人愿意把时间花在 AI 上。

The token originated from a real event that happened very recently. Its account name uses the scientific name of the plague bacterium and is specifically dedicated to tracking related developments.

In early October 2026, a 28-year-old female laboratory technician at the Research Institute for Plague Control of Siberia and the Far East in Russia’s Irkutsk region died. She was reportedly hospitalized around September 29 and died from “pneumonia of unknown etiology” during the night of October 1–2.

The institute primarily researches plague and other dangerous pathogens. Local independent media and some Russian reports claimed that she may have been infected at work after breaking a test tube containing Yersinia pestis around September 25. However, Russia’s health regulator, Rospotrebnadzor, and the governor of Irkutsk publicly denied this: tests did not detect a pathogen in her samples that was linked to her work, the institute reported no incident involving pathogenic microorganisms, and officials classified the case as “pneumonia of unknown etiology,” while stating that the local epidemiological situation remained stable.

Neighboring countries such as Kazakhstan reportedly strengthened border controls. International media including CNN, The Guardian, and NBC have also reported on the case, but all emphasized the official denial of any connection to a laboratory pathogen and that the diagnosis has not yet been confirmed.

text:
Last week I had a night terror, throwing myself off the bed and bloodying up my back, sides and arms.  

I dreamt that I was on a runaway train and jumped off in a panic.  

I had night terrors years ago but they'd stopped. They were a significant problem in my life as I'd frequently seriously injure myself. I ended up in the hospital once from it. 

I did some research and it seems that they coincide with sleep deprivation. Happening 1-3 hours after sleep onset. 

This makes sense why I had one: I spent five days at 7,000 ft while also missing my bedtime for consecutive days for social events. Going from sea level to altitude creates acute sleep disruption. Full acclimation happens over several weeks. 

People mistakenly think that bad dreams happen in REM but during REM your brain chemically paralyzes your muscular system so you can't act out. 

Night terrors happen during deep slow wave sleep (stage n3) when your muscles aren't paralyzed, putting you at risk of doing something dangerous with your body, like I did.

text:
A decent amount of agent adoption and deployment is bottlenecked by being able to test, tune, and optimize agents on “real” work environments. The files agents need to access, the CRM environments, email, and more.

It’s impossible to know how agents are performing if you don’t understand how well they’re executing on your evals and how they’ll perform in the future with a model change or workflow upgrade. Every enterprise has to do this 1 by 1 right now, which is obviously slow and tedious.

Every enterprise is going to have someone managing evals, infrastructure for building and running evals and simulated environments, and more. Huge space.
author: levie
quoted_text:
You can’t safely test an enterprise agent on a real company’s data.

So we built a company for it to work in.

Era is live today, and it’s free.

It generates a complete simulated enterprise that behaves like a real one across Salesforce, Slack, Jira, Zendesk, Gong, Deel and more, along with cloud databases and storage. Agents interact with it through live MCP and API interfaces.

People leave. Deals change. Records get duplicated. Permissions differ across systems. And because Era generated the company, it knows the exact ground truth.
Test, benchmark and improve agents against realistic enterprise workloads, use the failures for targeted post-training, then rerun the same environment to measure the impact.

Huge thanks to our research partners @NVIDIA, @Decart, @Composio, @openlayerco, @Deel, @Eragon and @Plurai, with more coming soon.

quoted_text:
AI Drug Discovery Is Becoming a Bottleneck Trade

I get excited when an industry starts going through a real regime change. AI drug discovery (“AIDD”) increasingly looks like one of those moments.

Two things are happening:
1/ Upstream: the frontier AI labs are piling in.
2/ Downstream: The supply chain is clearly moving.

Supply-chain checks suggest the upstream picks-and-shovels of discovery and early preclinical R&D are starting to feel the increase in experimental volume.

DNA → protein → assays → sequencing → automation → preclinical testing

Names across that stack include $TWST , @GenScript , $ILMN , $TXG , lab-automation vendors and CROs.

$TWST expects triple-digit percentage growth in AI-enabled drug-discovery orders in FY26, and another year of triple-digit order growth in FY27.

@GenScript's AIDD business doubled YoY in 1H26. Its current platform advertises industrial-scale validation of 4,000+ designs/day, with integrated sequence-to-data workflows. Our channel checks suggest the ramp is moving even faster: roughly 8,000 designs/day currently, with a path toward ~16,000/day by YE26.

---
Why does AI drive more wet-lab demand?

1/ AI makes hypothesis generation almost free → way more shots on goal.
The bottleneck is moving from expert-driven design to biological validation.

2/ AI models need continuous experimental feedback — and both good and bad data are useful.
Traditionally, only the highest-conviction A+ candidates might get pushed into expensive validation. With AI, even the B/C candidates can be valuable because failed experiments generate training data.

@GenScript has said its sequence-to-binding workflow can return data in 4–7 days, and that faster cycle times matter because AI models depend on continuous experimental feedback.

@Anthropic is a clean example. @claudeai  designed 1,320 protein binders. @adaptyvbio  converted those digital sequences into DNA, expressed the proteins and tested binding. Only 354 actually bound. And the 966 failures are not wasted. They are useful negative labels: what does not express, what does not bind, what has poor affinity. Those results help train the next model iteration.

3/ Wet labs are no longer just making drugs. They are making training data.
$TWST  / @GenScript  increasingly look like biological data foundries.

$TWST explicitly talks about generating model-ready data from AI-designed sequences. In some workflows, the customer may care less about receiving the physical protein than about getting structured experimental results back into the model.

Traditional drug discovery asks: “Does candidate X work?”

AI drug discovery also asks: “What can this experiment teach the model?”

---
TAM of AIDD

If AI is simply a better R&D tool, the relevant spending pool is the $300–400B of annual global pharma R&D. If AI meaningfully increases the number of viable drug programs, the opportunity is larger because it expands downstream demand for DNA synthesis, protein production, assays, and preclinical work.

Near term, we can also size demand from AI-company spending. If Anthropic reaches $80B of ARR in 2026 and spends just 1% on AIDD, that alone would imply ~$800M of annual investment.

---
Trade setup

This is a trade that could have long legs. It’s hard to really stop working until PhaseI/II results (2028+)

It smells a lot like the bottleneck trade we just saw in semis: GPUs → HBM → networking → power/cooling. In biology, It basically follows the drug discovery process downstream: AI models → designs → DNA/protein → assays → preclinical capacity.

After the upstream picks-and-shovels, animal testing could become the next bottleneck. Monkey prices are already near prior highs and CRO capacity is tight. AIDD pushing more candidates into preclinical development would only add demand.

?? But clinical trials are still the bottleneck?
This is the biggest pushback I keep coming back to. No matter how fast discovery becomes, drugs still need to go through preclinical → Phase I → Phase II → Phase III → approval. You still need patients, time and capital.

But that doesn’t mean the bottleneck trade won’t work. More viable candidates — especially with higher success rates — still means more demand throughout the development process.

And who knows: clinical trials themselves may eventually be optimized by AI.

?? What breaks the trade?
Near term, the picks-and-shovels trade breaks if experimental budgets stop growing, AI-generated designs don’t translate into useful wet-lab hits, or capacity catches up too quickly.

Longer term, the thesis breaks if AI drugs look great in discovery / Phase I but fail at normal rates in Phase II/III. That is why Phase II matters so much.

?? Milestones
Late 2026–2027: first Isomorphic-designed drugs enter human trials; more AI-native programs move into IND-enabling work / tox.

2028–2030: clinical trial results start telling us whether AI-designed drugs actually perform better than conventional drugs.

Calling all the "bottleneck bros". :) @jukan05 @zephyr_z9 @aleabitoreddit @ParadisLabs 

+++

author: cremieuxrecueil
quoted_text:
Are prediction markets biased by white men? Republicans? Young people?

Dartmouth professor Eric Zitzewitz analyzed 145 years of election prediction market data, spanning multiple exchanges and countries. His findings:

• No systematic evidence of political bias across different eras, countries, and offices.
• No systematic evidence of pricing bias based on candidates’ race, gender, or age in the recent elections studied.
• Traders weren’t always representative of the voting population, yet that didn’t translate into systematic bias in election forecasts.

The paper points to a powerful mechanism: people who spot a mispriced outcome have a financial incentive to correct it. Even if some participants trade on personal preferences, informed traders keep prices grounded in reality.

Open competition incentivizes research, challenges consensus, and gives the best ideas a chance to surface. People are rewarded for being right, regardless of their background or preferences.

The paper does find some pricing biases, including slight overpricing of longshots and underpricing of favorites. Its central finding on election markets remains: no systematic evidence of political or demographic bias.

In an increasingly polarized world, these markets give us something valuable: an impartial source of information shaped by people with an incentive to get it right.

A token launch platform built on Solana and powered by Orca DEX.

Traditional memecoin launches on Solana typically require completing a bonding curve first and then migrating to a DEX to create a liquidity pool. This can create issues such as opaque liquidity, migration risks, and limited fee distribution.

POD’s approach is different: users enter the name, ticker, and image, select a trading pair, and can create a real Orca Whirlpool pool in about one minute, with locked liquidity available for trading from the very first block.

The fixed fee is 2%, with 80% going to the creator side and 20% going to the platform. Creators can choose different “modules” to determine how their 80% is used.

For example:

Harbor: Send the fees directly to themselves or their team.
Undertow: Buy back and burn the token.
Reef: Deepen the locked liquidity pool.
Cargo: Use the fees to purchase tokenized stocks and distribute them to holders.

The platform currently supports pairing with SOL, USDC, ORCA, as well as hundreds of tokenized stocks.

Platform-related revenue is used to buy back and burn POD.

All tokens launched on the platform are permanently linked to POD. Cargo uses trading fees to purchase tokenized stocks and periodically airdrops them according to predefined rules to POD holders and holders of the corresponding Cargo token.

Chad: "By a 2/3 majority."

Taylor: "Okay. So why couldn't you do that in any case where, let's say, the majority of funds on a certain route are known to be directly stolen funds? What you did for THORFi, right? You take an interim action and then you do whatever you want to do."

"But even if it still was around, you want the protocol to turn off its entire system and all the trading that it does, and the source of revenue and income, for 1 to 2 weeks every time some external exchange or external thing gets hacked."

text:
$CLAUS was still around a $4M market cap when we analyzed it yesterday afternoon, and it later ran to nearly $14M.

0x1b54e762aa34cf6e28e9c082f2848e28e45da6b8 

But I don’t think this move happened because there was any single event significant enough to fundamentally change the project.

Instead, I think the market is starting to understand CLAUS’s real thesis:

Hook v4 + AI.

A lot of people simply view CLAUS as an “AI meme + Uniswap v4 Hook,” but I think that undersells what it is.

Uniswap v4 Hook gives CLAUS a “body” that can continuously change its trading rules and economic mechanisms.

CLAUS can use the Hook to experiment with buybacks, burns, auto-liquidity, weather-based allocation, and other mechanisms, rather than deploying a token once and having its rules remain essentially fixed.

AI is the other layer.

I still wouldn’t describe CLAUS as a fully autonomous AI agent. A more accurate way to think about it is:

AI is the Brain / Character, while the Hook is the Body / Execution.

In other words, the point of AI isn’t simply to post or chat. Theoretically, it can generate new ideas, which can then be turned into actual on-chain behavior through the token’s Hook.

So what CLAUS is really trying to prove isn’t any individual mechanism like the weather burn or Arena.

It’s this:

Can a token continue evolving after launch without having to launch a new token every time?

That’s what I think the market is starting to reprice.

Yesterday, the market was mainly betting on:

AI meme + Uniswap v4 Hook + programmable token.

Now it’s starting to bet on something bigger:

Can CLAUS become a programmable asset that continuously generates new mechanisms, new use cases, and new narratives?

Those are two completely different valuation frameworks.

Secondly, I think the fundamentals have strengthened, but not nearly enough to justify the magnitude of the price move.

What has improved is execution.

Over the past few days, CLAUS has actually deployed or experimented with buyback/burn, auto-liquidity, weather-based allocation, Fomo buybacks, and other mechanisms.

So it has already proven that this isn’t just a concept. The Hook can actually be continuously modified and used to change the token’s on-chain behavior.

But economic value has not been proven yet.

The amount of supply burned is still limited, while fees are primarily being used for burns, liquidity, and the project’s own mechanisms.

So:

Execution ≠ Economic Value.

And $13M does not prove that CLAUS is worth $13M.

Its valuation is still largely driven by:

attention + narrative + speculation + future optionality.

I don’t think the next major upside catalyst is simply another new gimmick.

It’s the next Hook that actually changes what the token can do.

For example:

prediction markets

lending

leverage
or other new economic mechanisms
These are currently only potential directions, so I wouldn’t price them in as existing fundamentals yet.
The bigger catalyst would be:

AI going from narrative to execution.

Right now, human developers are still upgrading the Hook, while AI is primarily part of CLAUS’s identity and narrative.

If we eventually see something like:

AI research → propose a mechanism → validate it → deploy the Hook → iterate based on on-chain results

that would be a completely different thesis.

Because at that point, AI wouldn’t just be CLAUS’s avatar.

It would actually start participating in the evolution of the token’s economic rules.

So there are really only three things I’m watching now:

First, what the next Hook actually ships.

I’m not interested in what gets announced on X. I want to see what actually goes live.

Second, whether the new mechanism gets real usage.

Does it generate new volume, fees, user behavior, and on-chain data?

Third, whether a real loop starts to form:

mechanism upgrade → real usage → data feedback → next upgrade.

If that loop can keep running, the CLAUS thesis gets stronger and stronger.

Because then it’s no longer just an AI meme.

It’s trying to become a programmable token that can continuously evolve.

But if what follows is simply:

AI narrative → new gimmick → attention → attention decay

then CLAUS will eventually fall back into the valuation framework of a normal meme.

So I’m slightly more positive than I was yesterday.

Not because the price went up.

But because the market is starting to shift from:

“This is an interesting gimmick.”

to:“This system might actually be able to keep evolving.”

The key from here is whether the project can continue to actually ship those evolutions and make them change real on-chain behavior.

Hook v4 determines whether CLAUS can change.
AI determines why it should change.

What the market is really betting on now is whether these two layers can eventually form a token that continuously evolves on its own.

And from here, the product is the thing that matters most.

Chart: https://t.co/DSZEsmVzDq
author: cfm_sol
quoted_text:
What I think is really worth looking at about this move in $CLAUS isn’t that it’s being hyped as another AI Meme, but that this thing is actually starting to “move.”

0x1b54e762aa34cf6e28e9c082f2848e28e45da6b8 

CLAUS’s original Thesis was already different from that of a typical Meme.

It treats the Token as the body, and the Uniswap v4 Hook as a brain that can be continuously rewritten.

In other words, once the token is launched, its rules aren’t completely locked in.

New code can continue to be added to the Hook, trading rules can be modified, and mechanisms can be added, replaced, or even removed.

So the bet isn’t really on any single feature. It’s on whether an existing Token can continuously gain new capabilities without changing its CA.

That is no longer just something imagined in a whitepaper.

CLAUS’s official Journal has already documented a series of Hook updates, starting with price movement restrictions, then trading fee distribution, buyback & burn, liquidity management, and now dynamically adjusting the burn / liquidity split based on London’s weather.

So I think the real catalyst behind the market’s renewed attention on CLAUS isn’t any single KOL call.

It’s that the market is starting to see that this thing can actually keep changing itself.

The most interesting experiment right now is London decides the split.

CLAUS charges a 2% project fee on every buy and sell, with 0.50% of that determined by the weather at London Heathrow.

When it rains:
0.35% → buyback & burn
0.15% → liquidity

When it’s dry:
0.15% → buyback & burn
0.35% → liquidity

The weather data comes from NOAA Heathrow observations, is then signed by IMD, and finally the Hook adjusts the allocation based on that data.
What I find interesting here isn’t the “weather Meme.”

It’s that for the first time, it actually connects:real-world data → Oracle → Smart Contract → Token economics

That’s also why I wouldn’t simply categorize CLAUS as an AI Meme.

A lot of AI Meme narratives are basically, “AI will be able to do many things in the future.”

CLAUS’s story is more specific:The Token itself can continuously gain new rules.

And CLAUS is no longer just demonstrating the concept.

Right now, the 2% trading fee is used for project operations, buyback, burn, and liquidity; 0.25% goes to buyback & burn, 0.25% goes to liquidity, and another 0.15% goes toward FounderClaus’s Fomo wallet buyback.

CLAUS has even previously used trading fees to pay 176.25 USDC for Surplus inference, while explicitly recording that the LP principal was not touched.

That means it’s already starting to form a real loop:Trading → Fee → Capital → New experiments / Buyback / Burn / Liquidity

Of course, it’s still a long way from being mature.

The existence of these mechanisms doesn’t mean they’ve already formed a strong economic flywheel.

Ultimately, what matters is whether trading volume can remain sustainable, whether fees can remain sustainable, and whether that capital can continuously produce new functions that actually matter.

Looking at the chart, I actually think the current position is more interesting than simply looking at its historical move.

CLAUS is currently around $4.09M market cap, with an all-time high of around $5.42M.

More interestingly, the average cost of the top 10 buyers is around $1.40M, while the average cost of the top 10 sellers is around $2.69M.

So at around $4M, this is no longer the cost basis of the earliest group. The market has already gone through a significant round of holder rotation.

And with roughly $3.1M in 24h volume, the level of attention and trading activity relative to its current market cap is still quite high.

So I wouldn’t simply look at CLAUS as a “$4M low-cap Meme” anymore.

The market is already starting to price in its mechanism innovation.

I think people buying CLAUS right now are really betting on two things.

First, whether it can become the most recognizable ticker within the emerging evolvable Token narrative.

Second, whether this Hook architecture can continue producing genuinely interesting experiments.

If it’s just weather today, burn tomorrow, and another gimmick the day after, the market will absorb that very quickly.

But if new financial mechanisms actually emerge, and each upgrade brings real trading activity, fees, or new user behavior, then CLAUS becomes something very different.

It would no longer just be a Meme with a lot of mechanisms. It would be testing a new way of designing Tokens.

So I think the upside catalysts from here are pretty clear:Whether CLAUS can continue producing new, verifiable Hooks that generate real economic activity.

Especially if the next stage introduces a feature that is easy for the market to understand while meaningfully expanding its use cases, CLAUS could be repriced again.

Because at a $4M valuation, the market is still essentially buying the possibility that “this experiment might work.”

If it starts proving that:Upgrade → Usage → Trading → Fee → New Function

can become a self-sustaining loop, then what the market is paying for is no longer just Meme premium.

But the risks are also very clear.

CLAUS’s biggest selling point is that its Hooks can be upgraded, and that is also its biggest risk.

Because the rules can be modified, it isn’t as straightforward as a completely immutable Meme.

So ultimately, the question the market needs to answer is very simple:Is every upgrade increasing the value of the Token, or increasing the uncertainty for holders?

If it’s the former, CLAUS’s valuation ceiling can keep moving higher.

If future Hooks are only being used to manufacture new narratives without generating real trading or usage, the market will eventually reclassify it as a very clever Meme experiment.

So my current view on CLAUS is simple:The fundamentals are getting stronger.

Not because it suddenly has another AI label, but because the original “Token + evolvable Hook” concept is now backed by continuous real experiments, fee usage, and mechanism iteration.

But for the market cap to keep moving higher from here, it doesn’t need more concepts.

It needs the next upgrade to prove that this thing is actually more valuable than it was before.

That’s what I think the real upside catalyst for CLAUS is from here.

text:
The difference between @Chainlink CRE and Fulcrum is important.

CRE gives developers and institutions the infrastructure to build custom workflows connecting blockchains, data, APIs and existing systems.

Fulcrum takes that infrastructure and turns it into a ready-made solution for a specific financial market: institutional financing.

For example, a bank could theoretically use CRE to build its own workflow for collateral verification, pricing, settlement and cross-chain transfers.

Fulcrum packages that into a reusable financing workflow, combining CRE for orchestration, CCIP for cross-chain settlement and Data Streams for collateral pricing.

I think we'll see much more of this from Chainlink.

CRE becomes the underlying orchestration layer, while products like Fulcrum package Chainlink's infrastructure into solutions institutions can actually adopt for specific financial workflows.

Correction: buying $MORPHO today is a bet that the fee switch eventually turns on AND that its customer base is inelastic to it.

The second part matters just as much as the first.

Morpho currently has a 0% take rate and recorded ~$46M in negative earnings since Q4 2024. Borrowers paid ~$177M in interest over the last four completed quarters, but that economic activity currently flows to lenders rather than the protocol.

Governance can eventually capture up to 25% of borrower interest on individual markets. The problem is that this isn't free money.

Every dollar @Morpho captures is a dollar that no longer goes to suppliers. Turning on fees therefore doesn't just monetize the existing product, it changes its economics for the users who helped Morpho scale in the first place.

So the $MORPHO thesis isn't simply:
0% take rate → fee switch → revenue

It's:
0% take rate → build massive liquidity/distribution → introduce fees → hope enough liquidity stays that the revenue captured outweighs whatever activity leaves

That's why fee elasticity might eventually become one of the most important metrics for $MORPHO.

The fee switch gives the protocol monetization optionality. Whether users tolerate it determines how valuable that optionality actually is.x-

author: PLAYTR0N
quoted_text:
Amazon shutting down consumer agent access (now both Muse and Instinct) is both completely rational and a big mistake

They have plausible reasons: 

1. Advertising accounts for ~10% of Amazon revenue, but an estimated 50-60% of operating profit because it's so high margin. People purchasing via agents = fewer consumer eyeballs to monetize

2. Amazon knows from experience how dangerous it is to give another platform a lever to ramp up / down your distribution 👀 They've done this to many retailers themselves

3. They are in a very good spot re: near-term defensibility - with ~250M Prime subs (who are habituated to buying on Amazon) + a massive logistics and distribution network that you can't vibe code

However, this logic is short-sighted (IMO). Agents are inevitable, especially for the kind of purchases people make on Amazon (low consideration, frequent, fairly urgent or recurring). 

I don't think Amazon is going to come out with a first-class consumer agent on their own...and in the meantime, why anger your valuable users and make them even consider alternatives? 

It's almost never a good idea to be on the wrong side of innovation. I'd much rather see them continue to greenlight agent traffic (it's pretty minimal now!) and work on adjusting to an agent-first world in the meantime.

text:
说人话就是 CFTC 准备给让美国散户加杠杆买币的交易所制定一套专门的监管规则。

比如，用户自己有 1,000 美元，通过平台融资买了 3,000 美元的币。这类业务涉及谁借钱、谁保管币、亏损怎么处理、客户资金会不会被挪用，CFTC 想把这些责任明确下来。

对交易所来说，就是想向美国散户提供这类服务，就要满足相应注册条件，保护客户资金，审查上币风险，接受监管。

其中，CAM 是平台的注册和运营规则，CTX 是相关交易的规则。

对用户来说，方案要解决的是平台可以提供杠杆服务，但必须承担相应的客户保护责任，不能只有交易功能，没有资金和风控约束。

所以，这次主要针对散户杠杆、保证金和融资买币业务。
author: PhyrexNi
quoted_text:
CFTC 拟推加密交易所新规，聚焦散户杠杆交易与客户资产保护

CFTC 在 10月5日 公布了一套加密资产监管方案，准备为向美国散户提供杠杆、保证金或者融资买币服务的交易所建立专门的联邦注册和监管规则。

A. 加密资产市场

对交易所来说，未来可以申请一种叫“加密资产市场”的注册资格，在满足条件后按照统一的联邦规则经营相关业务。平台可以开展哪些服务，客户资金怎么保管，上币需要做哪些审查，都将有更具体的要求。

这次准备推进两套配套规则：

1. CTX 负责明确哪些交易受到监管，以及怎样才算把币真正交付给用户。

2. CAM 负责规定交易所如何注册和运营。

普通现货平台仍可主要按照州级制度经营，希望进一步提供散户杠杆和融资交易的平台，则需要满足相应的联邦注册要求。CFTC 也明确表示，要强制所有加密现货交易所统一注册仍然需要国会授权。

B. 客户资产保护

CFTC 正在考虑要求相关交易通过受监管的中介机构处理，由这些机构承担客户账户、资金隔离、资本和风险披露等责任，同时落实身份核验和反洗钱要求。对于使用汇总账户保管客户资产的平台，还考虑加入储备证明义务。

C. 上币审核

代币集中在多少人手里，团队什么时候解锁，是否存在程序化增发或者回购，这些都可能成为判断代币是否容易被操纵的重要因素。对平台来说，这意味着上币之后也需要持续关注相关风险。

D. 实际交付

现行法律对 28 天内完成实际交付的交易设有例外，CFTC 准备明确，把币转到用户自己的外部非托管钱包，通常可以满足这一条件。币是否真正进入用户控制的钱包，会直接影响相关交易适用哪套规则。

目前这份文件还处于制定规则前的征求意见阶段，意见期从刊登《联邦公报》之日起计算 60 天，具体要求和实施时间仍待后续确定。另外，CAM 主要针对上述零售加密交易，平台如果还要经营期货、期权或掉期，仍需要适用现有的衍生品监管框架。

머니플로우 ’26.10.6

SK하이닉스: 코스피 발목 좀 잡을게
소부장, 기판: 호랑이 없는 골에 여우가 왕할게

2차전지: 코스닥 파티한다길래 우리도 날뛸게
코스닥: 나 좀 신날게
코스피: 먼 산 바라볼게

한국 연휴동안 미장, 일장 모두 상승마감 했었음.
나스닥은 어제 1% 넘게 오르며 종가 기준 신고가 갱신.
SOX는 0.3%도 못오르며 메모리는 또 약했던 미국장
미국도 결국 반도체 중에서 메모리 빼고 AI 플랫폼쪽만 강세.

유가는 $89인데 미10년물은 5.31%까지 급등했던 시장.
금리가 높아서 기술주 약세일줄 알았는데 나스닥 신고가 갱신.
금리 부담보다 AI 실적 기대와 모멘텀 기대가 더 컸던 모양새.

국장도 갭은 띄었으나 코스피는 7천피를 못지키고 있는 모습.
코스피는 -0.5%, 코스닥은 2.4%로 최근 훨씬 강세를 보임.
프리마켓 머니플로우에서 얘기한 소부장 강세가 더 두드러짐.
코스피만 보고 국장 망했다고 섣불리 결론 내리면 안됨.

삼성전자 약보합, SK하이닉스 2%대 하락하며 발목을 잡는중.
코스피 대형주는 코스피 중소형주가 오히려 플러스로 강세임.
최근 글로벌 시장 강세의 온기를 받아먹는 쪽은 따로있단 얘기

반도체 중에서도 기판과 소부장은 오히려 더 강해지는 모습임.
삼성전기 6%대, 심텍 8%, 이수페타시스 9%, LG이노텍 10%.
주성엔지니어링은 16%대로 급등하며 거래대금도 크게 붙음.
반도체가 끝났다기보다는 돈이 흐르면서 순환매가 도는 중. 

목요일엔 삼성전자 잠정실적이 예정되어 있고, 게다가 만기일.
만기일에 맞춰서 반도체 ETF 리밸런싱 얘기까지 나오고 있음.
ETF 7개(합산 AUM 18조)의 리밸런싱 매매가 만기일에 집중.
삼성전자 비중 초과로 약 2,100억을 매도가 나올 예정이라 함.
해당 매도만큼 주변 소부장 종목으로 매수세가 기대되는 상황.

금융권 해킹 수사 소식에 보안주도 강세를 보이는 모습.
하지만 프리마켓 대비해서는 그 기세가 많이 줄어든 양상.
시장 주도주가 따로 있다보니 테마주는 메리트가 덜하기 때문.

AI 인프라에서는 LG전자가 냉각장비 수주 뉴스로 6%대 상승.
AIDC인프라 중 원전, 전력기기는 대미투자 노이즈로 약세.
그 와중에 LG전자가 개별 뉴스로 강세를 보임.

HLB도 리보세라닙 FDA실사 뉴스로 급등하며 그룹주가 들썩.
담관암 허가 이후 리보세라닙 간암 치료제까지 기대감이 붙음.
HLB제약, HLB바이오스텝 등 일부 그룹주는 상한가까지 도달
소부장을 도와서 코스닥을 끌어올리는 중.

2차전지도 급등하며 코스닥 강세에 불을 붙이는 중.
전고체 뉴스와 미국 데이터센터 ESS 뉴스가 동시에 나옴.
2차전지도 에코프로비엠 9%, 삼성SDI 6%대 강세.

우주테마는 프리마켓 상승률을 정규장에서 많이 토해냄.
앞서 말했듯이 코스닥이 강하다고 테마주가 같이 강한게 아님
주도 섹터가 있는 시장에서 테마주의 메리트가 떨어지는 상황.

시장을 상방으로 열어두긴 했는데 코스닥만 이렇게 갈줄이야.
전자닉스가 쉬어가는 동안 순환매 돌면서 시장이 고루 상승중.
결국 코스피가 올라갈려면 큼직한 애들이 움직여야한다.

목요일엔 삼성전자 잠정실적, 옵션만기, ETF 리밸런싱 
그리고 목요일 새벽엔 FOMC 의사록, 금요일엔 한글날 휴장.
거래일도 적은데 굵직한 한방들이 기다리고 있는 장.

매매를 쉬더라도 시장에서 뭐가 강한지는 계속 체크해야함.
매매를 쉰다는게 손놓고 노는거랑은 다르다는 얘기임.

코스피만 보면 답답한데 코스닥만 보면 꽤 신나는 상황임.
다들 계좌에서 어떻게 체감하고 있는지 한 번 얘기해보자.

text:
就在今天对于以太坊重要程度仅次于The Merge的Glamsterdam升级将正式完成测试网激活，以太坊也正式将一只脚迈入并行区块链时代。以太坊历史上经历了20次升级，其中最重要的是在2022年的The Merge让以太坊从POW彻底转向了POS，改变了以太坊的经济模型，当然大家对于2024年通过L2扩容的Dencun升级更熟悉，但是随着L2群魔乱舞九子夺嫡以及Vitalik亲自推翻了这一路线，终结了周天子分封天下诸侯的历史，要打造秦王大一统帝国，以太坊主网自己的扩容成了重中之重，而这次Glamsterdam则相当于是给以太坊重新换了一套发动机。

在前些年并行区块链概念被誉为以太坊杀手的核心原因，是包括以太坊在内绝大多数区块链只能A→B→C→D的依次执行交易，所以为了提高性能，只能以牺牲去中心化为代价减少节点数量。

之所以ABCD不能同时跑的原因是因为以太坊的交易之间可能本身就存在一部分依赖关系，节点并不知道几个交易之间是不是可以同时执行，于是只能非常笨重原始的一个个执行。

这次升级引入了EIP-7928名为Block Level Access Lists，简称BAL，它把每一个区块都提前记录到底访问了哪些账户，哪些存储空间，最后变成了什么状态，然后客户端节点就可以提前获知到每一笔交易之间是否存在依赖关系，于是就可以把那些不存在依赖的交易同时执行，而根据历史数据回测，以太坊大约70%的交易都不存在依赖关系。

但是BAL也有一个副作用就是会产生额外的数据传播和存储的成本，所以这次的Glamsterdam是打了一套组合拳，除了BAL外还叠加了ePBS。

EIP-7732名为Enshrined Proposer Builder Separation，简称ePBS，解决了谁负责提出区块、谁又负责构建区块的历史遗留问题，其中Proposer提议者负责决定今天轮到哪个验证者出块，Builder构建者负责从成千上万笔交易里选出来最赚钱的一组放进区块中。

但是这个过程中并没有规定构建者怎么给提议者报价，于是行业自己又搞出来了一大堆角色，包括MEV、中转器等等这些“小商小贩”们来做协调，导致现在一个区块的诞生要经过验证者→MEV→中转器→构建者→执行验证，这里面大量的关系并不属于以太坊共识层本身，以太坊最核心的出块过程中间居然插进来了一大堆协议之外的东西，导致提议者在收到一个区块后必须要在非常短的时间窗口内完成传播、执行和验证。

如果能把这些都塞进以太坊的共识层，就可以延长这个时间窗口不用那么紧张。

ePBS让构建者先提前承诺准备好了出块的资源，然后再给到提议者确认好，这两方达成协议确保这次出块该准备的东西都提前准备好了，那剩下对区块的的传播、执行和验证过程就不需要再手忙脚乱的进行。

所以ePBS可以扩大区块，从而一定程度解决刚才说到的BAL导致数据增长的问题。

总之这次以太坊的Glamsterdam升级，进一步加强了主网的速度和性能，L2们的扩容历史使命也将彻底终结。

text:
Amazon shutting down consumer agent access (now both Muse and Instinct) is both completely rational and a big mistake

They have plausible reasons: 

1. Advertising accounts for ~10% of Amazon revenue, but an estimated 50-60% of operating profit because it's so high margin. People purchasing via agents = fewer consumer eyeballs to monetize

2. Amazon knows from experience how dangerous it is to give another platform a lever to ramp up / down your distribution 👀 They've done this to many retailers themselves

3. They are in a very good spot re: near-term defensibility - with ~250M Prime subs (who are habituated to buying on Amazon) + a massive logistics and distribution network that you can't vibe code

However, this logic is short-sighted (IMO). Agents are inevitable, especially for the kind of purchases people make on Amazon (low consideration, frequent, fairly urgent or recurring). 

I don't think Amazon is going to come out with a first-class consumer agent on their own...and in the meantime, why anger your valuable users and make them even consider alternatives? 

It's almost never a good idea to be on the wrong side of innovation. I'd much rather see them continue to greenlight agent traffic (it's pretty minimal now!) and work on adjusting to an agent-first world in the meantime.

text:
Depending on whether prediction markets are favoring Republicans or Democrats, everyone seems to have an opinion that they are biased one way.

In reality, this Dartmouth study, dating all the back to 1880 finds no systematic evidence of political or demographic bias.

For most prediction market traders, this probably doesn’t come as a surprise, but I would encourage everyone to read this study and give their thoughts.
author: MarcHochstein
quoted_text:
Are prediction markets biased by white men? Republicans? Young people?

Dartmouth professor Eric Zitzewitz analyzed 145 years of election prediction market data, spanning multiple exchanges and countries. His findings:

• No systematic evidence of political bias across different eras, countries, and offices.
• No systematic evidence of pricing bias based on candidates’ race, gender, or age in the recent elections studied.
• Traders weren’t always representative of the voting population, yet that didn’t translate into systematic bias in election forecasts.

The paper points to a powerful mechanism: people who spot a mispriced outcome have a financial incentive to correct it. Even if some participants trade on personal preferences, informed traders keep prices grounded in reality.

Open competition incentivizes research, challenges consensus, and gives the best ideas a chance to surface. People are rewarded for being right, regardless of their background or preferences.

The paper does find some pricing biases, including slight overpricing of longshots and underpricing of favorites. Its central finding on election markets remains: no systematic evidence of political or demographic bias.

In an increasingly polarized world, these markets give us something valuable: an impartial source of information shaped by people with an incentive to get it right.

text:
CFTC 拟推加密交易所新规，聚焦散户杠杆交易与客户资产保护

CFTC 在 10月5日 公布了一套加密资产监管方案，准备为向美国散户提供杠杆、保证金或者融资买币服务的交易所建立专门的联邦注册和监管规则。

A. 加密资产市场

对交易所来说，未来可以申请一种叫“加密资产市场”的注册资格，在满足条件后按照统一的联邦规则经营相关业务。平台可以开展哪些服务，客户资金怎么保管，上币需要做哪些审查，都将有更具体的要求。

这次准备推进两套配套规则：

1. CTX 负责明确哪些交易受到监管，以及怎样才算把币真正交付给用户。

2. CAM 负责规定交易所如何注册和运营。

普通现货平台仍可主要按照州级制度经营，希望进一步提供散户杠杆和融资交易的平台，则需要满足相应的联邦注册要求。CFTC 也明确表示，要强制所有加密现货交易所统一注册仍然需要国会授权。

B. 客户资产保护

CFTC 正在考虑要求相关交易通过受监管的中介机构处理，由这些机构承担客户账户、资金隔离、资本和风险披露等责任，同时落实身份核验和反洗钱要求。对于使用汇总账户保管客户资产的平台，还考虑加入储备证明义务。

C. 上币审核

代币集中在多少人手里，团队什么时候解锁，是否存在程序化增发或者回购，这些都可能成为判断代币是否容易被操纵的重要因素。对平台来说，这意味着上币之后也需要持续关注相关风险。

D. 实际交付

现行法律对 28 天内完成实际交付的交易设有例外，CFTC 准备明确，把币转到用户自己的外部非托管钱包，通常可以满足这一条件。币是否真正进入用户控制的钱包，会直接影响相关交易适用哪套规则。

目前这份文件还处于制定规则前的征求意见阶段，意见期从刊登《联邦公报》之日起计算 60 天，具体要求和实施时间仍待后续确定。另外，CAM 主要针对上述零售加密交易，平台如果还要经营期货、期权或掉期，仍需要适用现有的衍生品监管框架。

author: PhyrexNi
quoted_text:
SEC 放宽加密资产托管规则，基金和投资顾问可以自己托管加密资产

SEC 昨天放出了新的加密资产托管规则提案，投资顾问和受监管基金在满足条件的情况下，可以自己托管加密资产。

现在很多机构想配置一些新的加密资产，最大的问题是有没有符合现行规则的托管机构愿意托管。SEC 自己也承认，新资产出现以后，合规托管服务可能跟不上，直接限制了投资顾问提供相关策略，也限制了基金配置这些资产。

按照新的提案，如果确实找不到合适的托管机构，投资顾问可以自己保管客户的加密资产，但要求也很具体：

1. 要证明自己有托管能力。

2. 要有私钥管理制度。

3. 每笔转账至少两个人共同授权。

4. 不同客户的资产需要单独地址保存。

5. 定期检查网络安全。

6. 每年接受独立会计师的内部控制审查。

另外，SEC 也准备正式允许符合条件的州特许信托公司托管基金和客户的加密资产。投资顾问和基金需要确认这些机构有州监管授权、有完整的资产保护制度，并且客户资产必须和托管公司的自有资产分开。

另外未来符合条件的链上记录，可以直接满足部分监管记录保存要求。

这意味着 SEC 已经开始把区块链本身纳入传统金融机构可以正式使用的基础设施，而不只是把它当成一个需要单独监管的东西。

当然，这现在还只是提案，正式落地前还有 60 天公众意见期。但方向已经很清楚了，美国正在加速让基金、投资顾问和托管机构更顺畅地进入加密货币市场。

text:
南华早报主编：中国正大力囤积黄金，其背后有着更大的目标——人民币国际化。上海负责合约定价，香港负责离岸金库保管，构建一条以黄金为支撑的货币国际化路径。

香港的角色发生了结构性转变，从一个简单的门户变成了国家推进金融安全和货币国际化的关键环节。

作为无可争议的全球贸易超级大国，中国力劝其他国家以人民币结算交易，却无意放松资本管制。但要让其他国家像持有美元或欧元一样持有人民币，外国央行必须确信人民币能够保值，并且可以兑换成有形抵押品。黄金和离岸人民币市场应运而生。

美国主导的对俄制裁给北京敲响了警钟，现在增加黄金储备已成为一种结构性需求。中国通过逐步以实物黄金替代美元资产，表明其国家资产负债表背后有庞大的、中性的“硬资产”支撑。这增强了外国，特别是西方以外的全球南方国家，对持有人民币计价债务或贸易顺差的信心。

历史上，黄金交易、定价和实物清算一直集中在伦敦和纽约。伦敦黄金市场仍占据全球每日交易量的70%以上，但上海黄金交易所的份额已上升至16%。更重要的是，上海黄金交易所主导着全球实物黄金交易，包括实物交割和金库保管。

中国还在上海黄金交易所推出了人民币计价黄金合约，并扩建了香港的离岸金库。这使得贸易伙伴，特别是金砖国家和中东石油出口国，能够接受人民币支付其商品，并立即在香港将其兑换成实物黄金，然后运回本国。这一被称为“黄金可兑换性”的过程，大大降低了中国贸易伙伴接受人民币的风险。

未来几十年，香港能否继续保持国际金融中心的地位，取决于能否为国家发展离岸人民币和黄金业务。如果能成为连接全球南方国家的黄金桥梁，香港的地位将得到无可撼动。

author: Mercy_okx
quoted_text:
能成为行业领军者，远见弥足重要

刚刚 OKX NOW 上
@star_okx  和  @VitalikButerin  两位刚刚的发言

看看两位都聊了什么

@star_okx 这边

1/ 我们做了 13 年，从加密现货交易所起家，一路扩到衍生品、Web3 钱包、支付和多资产交易，现在做代币化资产

2/ 我给 OKX 定的新位置是面向下一代用户的全场景金融科技服务，就四件事：存钱、全球支付、一站式投资、AI 驱动的财富增值

3/ 这批人不太可能再走进传统银行网点，这是我们整套愿景的底座

4/ 我的判断前提是互联网、加密、AI 正在融合，一起重建金融

5/ 传统金融的毛病是几十年没变的基建配不上实时数字世界，低收入人群跨境汇款成本接近 10%，服务也做不到 24 小时

6/ 我把行业分成五个阶段：极客实验、机构关注、DeFi 和 ICO 实验、合规建设、2025 年之后的主流化

7/ 做全球金融服务，光有技术不够，真正的门槛是信任、监管、治理和本地问责

8/ 牌照和监管资格我们覆盖了美国、欧洲、阿联酋、新加坡、澳洲、巴西、土耳其等主要市场

9/ 我们是最早一批把储备金证明做成常态化透明机制的交易所，这件事后来成了行业标准

10/ 全球独立审计我交给了德勤，为的是把加密技术和全球金融机构的标准对齐

11/ 加密和传统金融长期被说成对立，我不同意，这个对立正在消失

12/ 我们的股东名单里有 ICE 和纽交所、渣打银行、Ripple、Circle，覆盖交易所、银行、支付、量化

13/ 两边的互补很清楚：加密给的是 24/7 基建、可编程的钱、全球结算、自托管，传统金融给的是巨额流动性、监管经验、机构信任

14/ 在我们内部，AI 已经不是概念，是核心基建，我们自建了内部 AI 平台

15/ 95% 的工程功能发布流程实质由 AI 完成，工程师只负责审查、测试和最终批准

16/ 接下来 AI 要接手三件事：24 小时智能客服、实时反欺诈干预、把各地区不同的监管要求做成统一执行的合规

17/ 上个月我们在大模型服务上的支出到了 1000 万美元，AI 已经跑到规模化工业使用这一步

@VitalikButerin 这边

1/ 我这场讲的都是正在发生、但还没成熟的技术趋势

2/ 我认为零知识证明两年内会成熟，以后用户不用披露完整隐私信息，就能证明资产和身份的合规性

3/ AI 既是这行最大的机会也是最大的风险，它能加速安全建设，也能反过来发现系统漏洞、发动大规模攻击

4/ AI agent 会成为新的交互层，取代传统前端界面，成为操作区块链的主要方式

5/ 这层变化会消掉大部分 UI 层的安全风险，同时带来一批 AI 安全的新问题

6/ 未来的安全是全栈的，从链协议、应用层一直到最底层的芯片和硬件

7/ 硬件钱包会演化成通用的安全设备

8/ 以前我们说 not your keys, not your coins，很快要变成 not your silicon, not your...

9/ 区块链这行是全球数字技术迭代的最前线，我们行业今天遇到的问题，很快会变成整个互联网的普遍问题

10/ 两年后链上交易更便宜、更私密，不再只是支付

11/ 两年后的对手方大多数是机器人，甚至应用代码也由 AI 生成，机器人可以直接在链上发起报价

12/ 技术已经把信息民主化了，金融还没有

13/ 加密带来 24 小时运转、可编程的钱、全球结算和自托管，传统金融带来巨额流动性和监管经验

text:
加密一级、二级市场越来越难做，核心问题是太多项目方不以做好产品为目的，而是以收割为目的。比如@opinionlabsxyz，预测赛道又怎样。韭菜在被割了无数次之后，也不会再轻易听项目方画大饼了。

模因以前几十亿美元市值都有人追，后来几亿美元、几千万美元，到现在有些项目只有百万美元市值韭菜也不愿上车，这并不全是流动性问题，而是韭菜悟了，韭菜不愿充当流动性和接盘侠了。

未来一级、二级的机会在哪里？我认为还是在那些真正想把产品做好的团队身上。看产品有没有人用、靠什么赚钱，还要看项目赚到的钱，跟持币者有什么关系。有真实需求、有盈利能力，代币也有实实在在的用途或回馈机制，再结合合理的估值和筹码结构，才值得投。
author: FLS_OTC
quoted_text: 加密一级市场为什么快死了，我们曾作为最活跃的投资机构之一，这十年感受最明显问题，第一个是叙事破灭了，从白皮书到机构背书到TVL刷量，基本市场不再买单。第二个是供给失衡，现在出现数以万计项目，优秀项目跑出来难度极大。第三个是1➕3解锁机制，基本是定向杀死VC，让项目，MM和交易所先跑，第四是上币成本，现在一级项目为什么需要高估值和大融资，主要是几个龙头交易所上线，平均成本需要千万美金。虽然VC问题也很多，但没有大量VC支持一级市场，市场只剩下专业发币集团和MEME币活跃。一级市场是加密创新的重要来源，需要行业龙头真正的去buliding方向，比如币安上币筛选方式改进，按照现在模式，当年V神的ETH来了也上不了币安。其次是彻底废除1➕3解锁机制，VC承担了最大风险，应该不背负最差的解锁条款，项目成功或失败根本不是VC决定的。最后是加密项目需要回到真正的营收和回购，美股那么多年持续繁荣，最重要的是业绩增长和督促回馈股东利益，这才是行业龙头们应该做的事情，让市场二级投资者真正找到优质项目。

text:
$Agency went from a $2M market cap all the way to $30M, and then fell back to $7.5M.

7VertkgF9KLhxxJXHX6uaWuoYZTP9LdGj2bWmVXVpump 

I think what really matters now isn’t the market cap, but whether the product data has also collapsed.

First, let’s look at the data officially released 5 hours ago:

4,168 coins / 9,637 on-chain actions / $528K+ deployed / $207K buybacks / $123K holder rewards

And now the data on the official website has become:

4,271 coins / 35 minds / 522 programs / $936K fees / 645 actions today

In other words, while the token’s market cap has been getting crushed from the highs, the product data is actually continuing to grow.

So for now, I wouldn’t interpret this pullback as a deterioration in fundamentals.

More accurately, I think the attention premium that the market previously assigned at $30M has been stripped away.

In my previous post, I argued that the market was initially betting on:

AI agent + launchpad + autonomous token economy

Now, what actually needs to be proven is:

Can these AI minds continuously create economic activity?

The most valuable part of AGENCY isn’t that it can launch thousands of coins in a day.

It’s:AI mind → manages its own token → executes buybacks / rewards / experiments → generates trading activity and fees → continues operating

If this loop works, AGENCY could eventually become more than an AI launchpad.

It could become an economic network made up of thousands of AI-controlled tokens.

That’s the Thesis I think is actually worth trading in the next phase.

So I’m only watching three major upside catalysts from here:

1. Fees continuing to grow

Fees have already reached $936K.

Now the question is whether this number can continue accelerating.

2. AI mind behavior proving to have economic value

It’s not enough that “AI can operate on its own.”

The question is whether its decisions can actually generate higher volume, fees, retention, or better token performance.

3. A real killer agent / killer coin emerging

If one AI mind can make its own decisions, manage its token, and eventually produce a genuinely successful case, that would be much more important than simply launching another 1,000 coins.

Because it would directly prove:

AI minds aren’t just a gimmick — they can actually create economic activity.

But the biggest risk is also pretty simple:

4,271 coins can easily turn into a huge quantity of tokens with extremely short lifecycles.

If the model eventually becomes:

launch → attention → volume → death

then AGENCY is ultimately just a more sophisticated launchpad.

If it becomes:AI mind → continuous decisions → real trading → fees → reinvestment → new growth

then that’s when it becomes a true AI economic network.

On the price side, AGENCY is currently around $7.52M, which is already a very deep retracement from its $30.8M ATH.

But I wouldn’t automatically call it cheap just because it has fallen 75%.

What matters more now is whether $7M can become a new consensus zone.

If the product data continues growing while the market cap stays around $5–10M for an extended period, that’s when we could start seeing a meaningful fundamental / valuation gap.

On the other hand, if fees, actions, and active minds all start declining together, then this isn’t just a valuation reset anymore — it means product growth itself is starting to peak.

So the real thing to watch in AGENCY’s next phase isn’t how many more coins it can launch.

It’s whether the AI minds can turn those coins into sustainable economic activity.

That’s what will determine whether AGENCY is an AI launchpad or an AI economic network.

quoted_text:
My current view on $Agency is that its fundamentals are clearly stronger than they were during the first wave, and the change has moved from a “concept upgrade” to the “product starting to generate its own data.” 

7VertkgF9KLhxxJXHX6uaWuoYZTP9LdGj2bWmVXVpump 

But the real upside catalyst for AGENCY’s next move is no longer telling the AI Launchpad story again. It’s whether the platform can prove that these Minds can generate sustained economic activity.

In the first wave, the market was essentially buying a very new concept: every Token can have its own Mind.

You choose a model, give it a Token, and it can observe the market, research information, set tasks, manage its Treasury, reward holders, and even create content on its own.

Back then, the market was buying the potential of the “AI Launchpad” concept.

But now I think the more important thing to look at is that Agency has started letting these Minds actually run.

From what the website currently shows, Minds are no longer just AI chatbots attached to Tokens. They are continuously executing Research, Strategy, Treasury, Rewards, Programs, and other activities.

You can also see from the screenshots that a large number of Minds are running in real time, and the platform has started publicly displaying data such as Minds Awake, Fees Earned, Programs Live, and Made Today.

This means Agency is moving from “giving a Token an AI” toward “giving a Token continuously running economic behavior.”

I think that is where the fundamentals have actually changed.

And Agency’s product is also clearly more complete than it was during the first wave.

The easiest thing to understand before was AI token launches.

Now you can see Minds doing Research, managing Treasuries, executing Buyback / Burn, DCA, Rewards, Quests, Contests, and different types of programs.

It has even started adding AI Influencers, and I think this is quite important.

If a Mind is simply a bot sitting behind a Token, there isn’t that much separating it from a normal AI agent.

But once a Mind starts having its own identity, content, and public behavior, it starts moving from being a “backend tool for a Token” to becoming an entity that can attract attention on its own.

If it eventually forms a loop like:Mind → Content → Attention → Community → Trading → Treasury

then Agency has a much larger upside than a simple Launchpad.

Another change I think is more important than during the first wave is that Agency’s value capture is becoming increasingly clear.

Under Agency’s economic model, trading fees generated by Coins on the platform are distributed between the Coin Treasury, Mind credits, and Agency itself depending on the stage.

Once trading volume passes a certain threshold, 15% goes to the Agency platform for Buyback & Burn of AGENCY.

So in theory:

More Coins on Agency → More Trading Activity → More Platform Fees → More AGENCY Buybacks

That’s the part that actually makes me willing to give the fundamentals more credit.

But I wouldn’t say this flywheel has already been proven.

Because having an economic model and having an economic model that generates meaningful value are two different things.

What still needs to be proven is:

How long do these Coins actually survive?

Can the Minds continue running?

Can platform fees keep growing after the FOMO phase ends?

And can Buyback/Burn ultimately create meaningful value capture for AGENCY?

So I think the market’s bet on AGENCY has already started to change from the first wave.

The first wave was more like betting:

“AI + Launchpad could become something very big.”

Now the bet is becoming:

“Can these AI-native Tokens actually develop their own economic activity?”

That’s also why I don’t care that much about how many new features Agency adds.

More features don’t automatically mean more value.

What I want to see is whether there are actually successful examples emerging.

For example, if an Agency-native Coin stays active for a long period, its Mind continues doing Research, managing its Treasury, producing content, executing strategies, and the Coin itself actually develops trading activity and a community.

If examples like that start appearing, Agency’s valuation logic changes significantly.

Because at that point, it is no longer proving:

“We can use AI to help you launch a Token.”

It is proving:

“We can actually make a Token run on its own.”

That proof is worth much more.

So I think AGENCY’s upside catalysts from here are pretty clear.

It’s not about another round of AI narrative.

It’s about whether three things can continue moving higher:

Platform revenue, continuously active Minds, and Agency-native Coins that actually break out and survive.

Especially after the first wave of FOMO is over, if platform fees, Mind activity, and actual economic activity can continue growing, that will be an important validation.

Because it would mean Agency didn’t lose its value when the first wave of sentiment faded.

Instead, it has entered a more important phase:

from price discovery to product validation.

If it can eventually create a loop like:

Coin → Mind → Behavior → Trading → Fee → Treasury → Buyback → More Minds

then AGENCY’s valuation will no longer just be the valuation of an AI Launchpad.

It could start being valued as AI-native Token infrastructure.

That’s the part of Agency I think is most worth watching right now.

交易所是 OKX 的起点，但绝不是终点。

quoted_text: 加密一级市场为什么快死了，我们曾作为最活跃的投资机构之一，这十年感受最明显问题，第一个是叙事破灭了，从白皮书到机构背书到TVL刷量，基本市场不再买单。第二个是供给失衡，现在出现数以万计项目，优秀项目跑出来难度极大。第三个是1➕3解锁机制，基本是定向杀死VC，让项目，MM和交易所先跑，第四是上币成本，现在一级项目为什么需要高估值和大融资，主要是几个龙头交易所上线，平均成本需要千万美金。虽然VC问题也很多，但没有大量VC支持一级市场，市场只剩下专业发币集团和MEME币活跃。一级市场是加密创新的重要来源，需要行业龙头真正的去buliding方向，比如币安上币筛选方式改进，按照现在模式，当年V神的ETH来了也上不了币安。其次是彻底废除1➕3解锁机制，VC承担了最大风险，应该不背负最差的解锁条款，项目成功或失败根本不是VC决定的。最后是加密项目需要回到真正的营收和回购，美股那么多年持续繁荣，最重要的是业绩增长和督促回馈股东利益，这才是行业龙头们应该做的事情，让市场二级投资者真正找到优质项目。

text:
我如何筛选perpdex的年度项目，HYPE/LIT/VAR都能在车上，最近又为什么在@popdex_ 上交易。

首先筛选的前提其实很简单，就是要真的在链上。

不管是Hyperliquid还是Lighter，成功的关键都是链上的订单簿撮合。

就算做RFQ模式的Variational没有订单簿，流动性来自链下，也把结算全部放在链上。

链下撮合的perpdex，你可以用，但要明白，其本质和cex没有区别。

其次，要跑出来就得有技术或分配机制上的创新。

hyperliquid是链上原生订单簿的开山祖师，随后的lighter免交易费，Variational滑点低。

而popdex在这两方面都符合条件，融资3000万美元，由Foresight Ventures孵化，有实力，做的是纯链上撮合。

创新的点，主要是价值分配上的，理念是把交易员创造的价值返还给平台的使用者，而不是补贴资本家。

很多dex看起来交易量不错，实际上是建立在负债上，用户为了拿积分，主动付手续费/清算费去买币，就是变相ICO我说白了。

popdex不搞积分PUA，关于价值捕获和分配，也有独特的理解。

在市场波动清算剧烈的情况下，很多dex社区会有分化。持币人和产品用户之间往往会有矛盾。在清算中，持币人是受益的，收入提高了嘛；但用户很多是亏损的，有怨气。

协议为了缓解这一点，一般是学cex的思路，搞质押平台币获得手续费等折扣权益，来促使用户和持币社区之间的转化和融合。

popdex的路径显然不同，目前已完成 4 轮现金奖励发放给交易员，最新一期单地址最高超过 8000刀，也不要求用户质押平台币就可以减免手续费。

试一下popdex，你会发现交易可以很单纯，交易量达标了就是VIP，每旬能收到现金奖励： https://t.co/O3YzeZH1vt

author: PLAYTR0N
quoted_text:
Amazon shutting down consumer agent access (now both Muse and Instinct) is both completely rational and a big mistake

They have plausible reasons: 

1. Advertising accounts for ~10% of Amazon revenue, but an estimated 50-60% of operating profit because it's so high margin. People purchasing via agents = fewer consumer eyeballs to monetize

2. Amazon knows from experience how dangerous it is to give another platform a lever to ramp up / down your distribution 👀 They've done this to many retailers themselves

3. They are in a very good spot re: near-term defensibility - with ~250M Prime subs (who are habituated to buying on Amazon) + a massive logistics and distribution network that you can't vibe code

However, this logic is short-sighted (IMO). Agents are inevitable, especially for the kind of purchases people make on Amazon (low consideration, frequent, fairly urgent or recurring). 

I don't think Amazon is going to come out with a first-class consumer agent on their own...and in the meantime, why anger your valuable users and make them even consider alternatives? 

It's almost never a good idea to be on the wrong side of innovation. I'd much rather see them continue to greenlight agent traffic (it's pretty minimal now!) and work on adjusting to an agent-first world in the meantime.

text:
聊聊怎么赚钱？ #美股 #Bitcoin #ETH
包含美股、加密（涉及现货、合约、MEME等等）

前沿：其实原本这我写了一大段话，但还是删了，因为感觉有点说教的味道。
知道小伙伴不太听，直接聊怎么赚钱才是小伙伴们最想看的。

先说 #Bitcoin 的趋势、波段机会，我知道小伙伴想听MEME  妖币 以及合约的高收益赚钱策略，放心后面会讲到

一、#Bitcoin 的趋势、波段机会（最好结合图查看）

1️⃣ 趋势机会，就是单边主升浪上涨

特征：经历过高价筹码换低价筹码，至少1-2个月；

恐慌情绪完全消散，没有新会产生恐慌情绪的事件预期发生；

利好事件预期发生且会实际发生；
以上缺一不可。

例如，23年Q4，加息最疯狂阶段过去，BTC 现货ETF预期通过并且实际通过，筹码也经过换手，符合

24年Q4，暂停加息，首次降息发生，总统大选，川普支持加密，筹码同样经过换手，符合

25年4-10月，关税告一段落，降息发生等，筹码仍经过换手，符合

以上均带来了BTC单边主升浪上涨行情。不仅K线走势上均直接走出了底部震荡区间，利好事件也实际发生，带动资金的情绪。这就是趋势机会。

当下，筹码确实经过了2月-8月的换手

但恐慌情绪还未消散，因为油价高企，不仅没有降息，还加息了，甚至后续还有加息预期，降息预期不知道在何时

故 虽然冲破585-82的底部震荡区间，但前景恐慌情绪仍在，所以也看到拉升到87还是又打回接近82附近的位置，仍需看宏观利率、地缘层面的走向。

2️⃣波段机会，就是主升浪上涨之前和之后

主升浪上涨之前也就是底部震荡区间，这种在经历过约2-4万美金幅度大跌之后，需要高价筹码换低价筹码，需要开启以月为单位的震荡。因为不可能一直跌。

这就是波段机会，即使觉得看不上这点收益，耐心上车做好均价等待主升浪上涨机会也是可以的。

然后主升浪上后就是高位震荡区间，这种在经历几万美金幅度的拉升之后，需要低价筹码换高价筹码，一般也会开启以月为单位的震荡。因为不可能一直涨。

总要派发低价筹码的，同时新的利空情绪也在酝酿并诞生。不管是高位波段还是主升浪上涨机会把握后，也要及时卖出。不然就会经历利空情绪滋生带来的大幅下跌。

（当然不看K线，就是拿住，那完全看个人）

就此大饼的机会讲完

延伸：#ETH  #BNB #SOL #OKB 等市值靠前的主流项目（注意我说的是加密主流项目，不是指山寨，因为风险不一样）

其实都看大饼的脸色。机会同理，这里就不再一一赘述，细心的小伙伴们可以自己拉长K线走势对比去研究即可。

二、美股的波段机会

美股是风险市场的优质市场，相对其他的市场来说，美股，尤其是核心重股，可称之为简单模式。
如图，美股股票总市值排名，数据来源：https://t.co/OuROkgVFWy

哪些是核心重股？
市值至少3,000亿美金以上，ai科技股，或者近期炒作热点。

如美股七姐妹 英伟达 谷歌 苹果等，一般上市很多年，赶上宏观宽松周期一直拉，然后略微回调歇一歇继续拉升

如新开盘上市 SPCX 高位市值开盘，腰斩左右洗盘，然后继续回升，根据宏观周期和产品进展波动

如炒作热点，闪迪，月线一直拉一直拉，还比如之前的PLTR

主要特征：流动性好，加上美股熔断机制，极短时间快速上下波动，这就是波段机会，因为跌的话，可能跌不了多少，但会一直拉升。

注意⚠️ 宏观层面黑天鹅如经济衰退、加息周期开启等避免下风险即可。这种风险一般出现的时机不多，近6年以来就是20年312，24年85，而今年加息都加了一次，结果都没怎么跌，甚至还涨了。

当然这种黑天鹅出现就是黄金坑。

论波动幅度和大饼比起来，以上提及的美股核心重股更适合投资稳定性偏好者。

对，可能小伙伴马上想到这也更适合低倍大资金合约交易，这是后文要提到的。

三、合约机会

1️⃣加密市场

大饼 、ETH 、BNB等前排市值主流币，什么阶段做什么方向。
相信看过上文，对于合约多空应该也能想得到。

单边主升浪上涨阶段，适合逢低多

一番主升浪上涨过后，不可能一直涨，来到高位震荡阶段，此时得转换思维。因为利好兑现了，情绪也到了过热阶段，此时适合逢高空。

当一轮大跌（幅度2-4万美金）过后，高价筹码换低价筹码，来到底部震荡区间，前期适合逢高空，后期适合逢低多。

因为前期经过大跌，恐慌情绪还未消散，利空可能还有，筹码换手频繁，大事件利好预期没有这么快，涨不上去的。

而后期则要转换思维。因为恐慌情绪消散接近尾声，利好事件预期滋生，筹码换手也结束，一旦事件利好，资金就会推动。

本质上比拼是资金的厚度和认知、心态的耐心。无非怕的就是选错方向。

做短线，吃到就走了。不用赘述。

做长线，即使方向选错，举个实际的例子

前面大饼在6万美金附近，选择多，爆仓位置拉到3万甚至2万以下，然后就是熬时间，无非就是计算费率成本和耐力、资金使用率，或者可以选择分仓拉低均价处理。

所以小伙伴，熬不熬得住看个人。

ETH等其他市值前列的主流币也同理，毕竟主要看BTC的脸色。

然后非主流币：山寨、妖币这些

其实还是我前面说的那个本质问题。但山寨也好，妖币也好，庄的强控性更大，费率更夸张。

试想一下，庄控制高达90%以上的筹码，你觉得在合约上，你玩的过庄吗？

我知道这个更刺激，赚钱更快，但亏钱也快。
故，我个人介意，这种标的，遇上了，玩玩现货能吃一口的话得了。

2️⃣美股市场

能看到这里的小伙伴应该能想到美股核心重股的合约机会的

本质因为流动性好，比如 #SPCX 闪迪 #PLTR 英伟达 等等

适合的策略就是逢低做多，即使位置没有选很好，也不用担心被套很久。且费率也不高，跟油价单子的费率比起来，美股的就很友好

尽可能少做空，因为可能你不知道高的位置在哪，一旦被套就很难受。

而且在宏观层面利于宽松环境、产品发布、主要创始人、机构等发文，可能股价就会上去的。

个人建议可选择1-3个长时间学习，然后去做。

我自己前面就做过英伟达、SPCX的。

四、MEME

高市值MEME满足的条件

1️⃣ 有超高热度，比如在某一语文区有很大流量，比如被知名大佬站台
2️⃣BTC上涨，情绪贪婪时，才能刺激整体用户的情绪，提升投资偏好

缺一不可，比如近期牛来，之前的币安人生，否则是不太可能有高市值、上大所预期的。
没有高市值预期的话，就是提供流动性的。

玩MEME能赚钱且能踩中的本质是拥有足够多的子弹。

不要去拼运气，对于大资金的小伙伴来说，可能可以，但资金不多的小伙伴，一旦真正的机会来了，没有留在牌桌上会是很痛苦的。

写在最后

看到这里的小伙伴可能吐槽，来币圈是赚10个点50个点的嘛？是要10X、20X啊

当下能满足吃到 10X 20X，只可能是MEME 或者妖币，或者妖币合约

而刚好这几类也是高风险的。

假设小资金靠冲MEME想资产增值，那么500刀或者1,000刀，或者3,000、5,000冲一次，
那手里的资金可以冲几次？

如果失去留在牌桌的机会呢？不如老老实实做大饼等主流项目、美股等核心重股的趋势机会或者波段行情。

如果你想从0-1，我个人觉得越应该玩主流币种、核心重股，拿赚到的钱苟着等待时机，再去捕捉高风险高收益的机会。赢了你不就到1了嘛?

输了你也还在牌桌上，怕啥。

其实我刚进圈那会也跟很多小伙伴们一样，拿着小十万块钱，想博一个机会，变成小一百万，但你的运气有多少？别人有运气，那是别人的啊。

当你已经是1，想从1-2，也更应该求稳，有没有想过当你是1的时候，去大饼里去美股里吃10个点，而且没有什么风险，这两个不至于归零吧

你的10个点可能只需要几天，最多1个月，但可能就是别人一年的收入啊。

当然我知道小伙伴们会贪。吃了10个点就想吃20个点。是吧

这就像做生意，不是比谁赚得多，而是比谁活得长。

能看到这里的小伙伴，我相信你多少会有在交易上的一些新认识。

其实每一个点拆开能讲的内容还有很多。我自己就是按照我说的去做交易的。以后也会多分享此类文字

如果觉得看完有帮助，有疑问，欢迎留言探讨，也欢迎一键三连，谢谢大家。

text:
Muse的竞品Instinct（刚刚估值达到了100亿美金），在小范围推出了群聊功能，早期访问用户可以将Instinct添加到群聊中。一个新的Instinct加入并为整个群组工作。 

-主要解决多人活动，需要多方协调的问题。

主要做一些场景是：
- 与朋友规划周末旅行，包括日期和到达时间 
- 与室友协调后勤 
- 一旦门票开售就抢票，然后分摊费用并发送给每个人 
- 运行幻想联赛，保持排名，解决规则争议，并提醒每个人设置他们的阵容 
- 整理拼车时间表 - 根据每个人的日程安排出谁每天开车 
- 组织感恩节，跟踪谁带什么并订购购物清单  群聊对本能来说是新领域，我们投入了很多精力来正确设置权限。以

下是其工作方式： 
- 你的个人本能在与群组的本能连接前会询问。你选择信任哪些群组，并可以随时移除信任。 
- 群组的本能无法直接访问你的个人账户。你的本能在分享信息或采取行动前会检查你的权限。 
- 如果有人新加入群组，你的本能的所有待处理回复都会被保留，直到你授予它与扩展群组分享的权限。  群聊对我们所有早期访问用户可用，并将很快向所有人推出。要加入此版本的早期访问，请让你的本能把你加入列表。

其实这个方向，chatgpt/元宝也推出过，最终没有了下文。chatgpt/元宝当时感觉只能在群聊里问问问题，互动下，Instinct可以更近一步，帮着用户协调后进行行动。这个多人协调想做好，也非常不容易。

这个群聊AI方向，之前就有创业公司在做，之前一个从 Google 出来、专门做群聊 AI 的人 David Petrou，他做的公司叫 Continua。他在 Google 待了 17 年多，是 Google Goggles 和 Google Glass 的创始团队成员。2023 年初离职创业，专门把 AI agent 放进群聊：SMS、iMessage、Discord 里加一个号码或账号，就能帮忙设提醒、发起投票、写进日历、整理待办。2025 年 8 月宣布 800 万美元种子轮，GV 领投，Bessemer 跟投，天使里还有 Jeff Dean。

quoted_text:
Instinct in group chats

Starting today, early access users can add Instinct to group chats. A new Instinct joins and works for the whole group.

Making plans with friends usually turns into a frustrating back-and-forth over times and places. With Instinct in the group, you can explore options together, agree on a plan and get it done, all in one thread. Your friends don't even need Instinct to join in.

A few things it’s good at:
- Planning a weekend trip with friends, including dates and arrival times
- Coordinating logistics with a roommate
- Getting tickets as soon as they go on sale, then splitting the cost and sending one to everyone
- Running a fantasy league, keeping standings, settling rules disputes, and reminding everyone to set their lineups
- Sorting out carpool schedules - works out who’s driving each day from everyone’s schedules
- Organizing Thanksgiving, keeping track of who’s bringing what and ordering the shopping list

Group chats are new territory for Instinct, and we put a lot of care into getting the permissions right. Here’s how it works:
- Your personal Instinct asks before connecting with the group’s Instinct. You choose which groups to trust and can remove trust at any time.
- The group’s Instinct has no direct access to your personal accounts. Your Instinct checks your permissions before sharing information or taking action.
- If someone new joins the group, all pending replies from your Instinct are held until you grant it permission to share with the expanded group.

Group chats are available to all of our early access users, and will be rolling out to everyone soon. To join early access for this release, ask your Instinct to put you on the list.

Great work with @GajanNagaraj @anuda_w and @saagarwashere
